items.title: From Commitment to Institutionalization: Healthcare Organization Leaders’ Perspectives on Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging in Southern California — A Qualitative Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Public health and health-oriented non-profit organizations increasingly implement diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging (DEIB) initiatives to strengthen organizational culture and reduce health inequities. However, translating DEIB commitments into sustainable, structural change remains a significant challenge. Existing literature offers limited insight into how organizational leaders distinguish between symbolic and transformative implementation strategies. This qualitative study explored leaders' and facilitators' perspectives on DEIB institutionalization. Methods Using a qualitative study design, semi-structured virtual interviews were conducted with 15 organizational leaders and DEIB facilitators across nine public health and health-oriented non-profit organizations in Southern California, USA. Participants were selected based on leadership roles or direct DEIB implementation experience. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis, guided by Inclusive Leadership Theory and Systems Theory. Trustworthiness was established through member checking, reflexive journaling, and audit trails. Results Five primary themes emerged: (1) leadership commitment as the central driver; (2) systemic integration over isolated initiatives; (3) authentic community engagement; (4) robust accountability and measurement; and (5) adaptive leadership resilience. Importantly, participants distinguished between performative DEIB – marked by symbolic actions and superficial structural change – and restorative DEIB, an approach focused on repairing historical inequities, rebuilding trust, fostering belonging, and embedding equity into governance, policies, and daily practice. Conclusions Achieving meaningful DEIB requires moving beyond representation and compliance toward organization-wide transformation. We propose restorative DEIB as an emerging conceptual framework to shift healthcare organizations from symbolic commitment to sustained systems change. This framework provides a practical pathway for embedding equity into organizational culture, decision-making, and continuous improvement, ultimately supporting workforce inclusion and equitable outcomes.

items.title: Latent profiles of subsequent fertility pressure and their association with intention to have another child among parous women in China: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Subsequent fertility pressure may reflect interacting social determinants, including household resources, employment conditions, access to childcare, health concerns, and family expectations. This study aimed to identify latent profiles of subsequent fertility pressure, examine factors associated with profile membership, and compare intention to have another child across profiles. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted from March to July 2025. Parous women of reproductive age were recruited from 21 provinces and autonomous regions and four municipalities in China using convenience sampling guided by prespecified demographic strata. Participants completed a general information questionnaire, the Subsequent Fertility Pressure Scale for Women of Childbearing Age, and a single-item measure of intention to have another child. Latent profile analysis identified pressure profiles. Multinomial logistic regression examined factors associated with profile membership, and the Kruskal-Wallis H test compared fertility intention across profiles. Results Among 2,123 participants, the median fertility-pressure score was 117.00 (IQR 103.00-133.00). Three profiles were identified: moderate pressure with prominent health impairment and childcare pressure (15.50%), moderately high pressure with a multidimensional pattern (62.41%), and high pressure with prominent child growth and development pressure (22.09%). items.title: Characteristics of HIV-1 molecular transmission networks among older men, their spouses, and female sex workers in Southwest China.
items.abstract: Objective The rising incidence of HIV-1 infection in older adults is a challenge in China. We have previously reported a close transmission connection between older men and female sex workers (FSWs). This study aimed to characterize the transmission network and explore the potential transmission directions among older men, their spouses, and FSWs. Methods Participants with HIV-1, including older men, their female spouses, and FSWs, were recruited from Guigang City, Guangxi, China. Sanger-derived HIV-1 pol sequences were used for transmission network construction. Conjugal pairs within the largest cluster and the associated FSWs were subjected to next-generation sequencing (NGS) to infer transmission direction via Phyloscanner. Results A total of 726 HIV pol sequences were obtained by Sanger sequencing, including 595 older men, 88 female spouses, and 43 FSWs. Seven HIV-1 subtypes were identified, with CRF01_AE being the predominant subtype (75.8%, 550/726). Overall, 70.5% (512/726) participants were clustered in transmission networks; 63.9% (327/512) of them belonged to clusters with older men, their spouses, and FSWs. NGS and transmission inference were performed for 30 individuals, revealing 12 source-recipient pairs: three from FSWs to older men, three from older men to spouses, three from spouses to older men, and the remaining three were same-sex pairs. Conclusion This exploratory study identifies transmission networks among older men, their spouses, and FSWs, and provides preliminary evidence for putative transmission directions. We propose a study strategy combining Sanger sequencing and NGS for population-level identification of HIV-1 transmitters, which helps determine local epidemic drivers and inform targeted interventions.

items.title: Human–AI Divergence in Ego-Centric Action Recognition Under Spatial and Spatiotemporal Manipulations
items.abstract: Abstract Humans consistently outperform state-of-the-art AI models in action recognition, particularly in challenging real-world conditions involving low resolution, occlusion, and visual clutter.e those utilised by humans Understanding the sources of this performance gap is essential for developing more robust and human-aligned models. In this paper, we present a large-scale human AI comparative study of egocentric action recognition using human-defined Minimal Identifiable Recognition Crops (MIRCs), defined as the smallest spatial or spatiotemporal regions sufficient for reliable human recognition. We used our previously introduced, Epic-ReduAct, a systematically spatially reduced and temporally scrambled dataset derived from 36 EPIC-KITCHENS videos, spanning multiple spatial reduction levels and temporal conditions. Recognition performance is evaluated using over 3,000 human participants, Side4Video, and Qwen 3.5 9B models. Our analysis combines quantitative metrics, Average Reduction Rate and Recognition Gap, with qualitative analyses of spatial (high-, mid-, and low-level visual features) and spatiotemporal factors, including a categorisation of actions into Low Temporal Actions (LTA) and High Temporal Actions (HTA). Results show that human performance exhibits sharp declines when transitioning from MIRCs to sub-MIRCs, reflecting a strong reliance on sparse, semantically critical cues such as hand object interactions. In contrast, the model degrades more gradually and often relies on contextual and mid- to low-level features, sometimes even exhibiting increased confidence under spatial reduction. Temporally, humans remain robust to scrambling when key spatial cues are preserved, whereas the model often shows insensitivity to temporal disruption, revealing class-dependent temporal sensitivities. Overall, our findings demonstrate that strong benchmark performance can obscure fundamental human AI misalignment and highlight limitations in current spatial and spatiotemporal representations, suggesting concrete directions for more efficient and human-aligned action recognition systems.

items.title: The Psychology of Prompting and Behavioral AI Design: Cognitive, Motivational, and Behavioral Foundations of Human–AI Interaction
items.abstract: The rapid integration of large language models (LLMs) into everyday activities, education, professional practice, and decision-making has transformed natural language into an increasingly important medium of human–computer interaction. Although prompt engineering is commonly approached as a technical process of optimizing instructions for artificial intelligence systems, its effectiveness also depends on psychological processes involving cognition, motivation, metacognition, trust, communication, and behavioral regulation. At the same time, the behavioral characteristics of AI interfaces influence how users formulate goals, interpret generated information, distribute cognitive effort, evaluate recommendations, and maintain independent judgment. This article introduces an interdisciplinary conceptual framework integrating the psychology of prompting with behavioral artificial intelligence design. Drawing on cognitive psychology, self determination theory, behavioral science, human–computer interaction, and emerging research on human–AI collaboration, the article examines prompting as a psychologically mediated form of cognitive and behavioral coordination. Six interconnected dimensions are proposed: cognitive representation and goal formulation, metacognitive regulation, behavioral activation and motivation, trust calibration, psychological autonomy, and adaptive interaction design. Particular attention is devoted to the reciprocal relationship between human instructions and AI-generated responses, through which interaction patterns may influence users' cognitive strategies, expectations, perceived competence, and subsequent behavior. The article proposes the Psychological Prompting and Behavioral Design (PPBD) Framework, identifies practical principles for designing psychologically informed prompts and AI interfaces, and develops testable propositions for future empirical investigations. Ethical challenges, including automation bias, anthropomorphism, persuasive manipulation, excessive reassurance, and cognitive dependency, are considered. The central argument is that effective prompting should be evaluated not only by the immediate quality of AI-generated outputs but also by its consequences for human understanding, decision making, self-regulation, competence development, and long-term autonomy

items.title: The Psychology of Human–AI Interaction Design: A Conceptual Framework for Cognitive, Metacognitive, Emotional, and Behavioral Alignment
items.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence has transformed human–computer interaction from predominantly instrumental exchanges into increasingly conversational, adaptive, and cognitively integrated forms of collaboration. Contemporary AI systems can participate in activities traditionally associated with human cognition, including reasoning support, knowledge synthesis, planning, creative ideation, and decision assistance. However, the effectiveness of human–AI interaction cannot be adequately evaluated through computational performance, usability, or task completion alone. It also depends on the psychological mechanisms through which individuals interpret, trust, regulate, and incorporate artificial intelligence into their cognitive and behavioral activities. This conceptual paper examines the psychological foundations of human–AI interaction design and proposes an integrative framework for developing AI environments that support human cognition, metacognitive regulation, emotional well-being, autonomy, and sustainable competence. Drawing on cognitive psychology, social psychology, motivational theory, human–computer interaction, and research on automation, the paper identifies seven interconnected design dimensions: cognitive compatibility, metacognitive scaffolding, calibrated trust, relational transparency, autonomy preserving delegation, psychological safety, and developmental sustainability. The proposed Psychologically Informed Human–AI Interaction Design (PI-HAID) framework conceptualizes interaction quality as a dynamic relationship among individual characteristics, task demands, system behavior, and interface-mediated psychological processes. It further distinguishes immediate task performance from long-term cognitive and psychological outcomes, arguing that successful interaction design should optimize not only what humans accomplish with AI but also what they understand, retain, control, and become capable of accomplishing independently. Practical design principles, operational indicators, and testable research propositions are developed to support future empirical investigation. The paper positions psychological design as a foundational component of responsible human–AI systems and identifies opportunities for interdisciplinary research connecting psychological science, AI engineering, interaction design, and human development

items.title: Cognitive Biases in Prompt Engineering: Psychological Mechanisms, Human–AI Feedback Loops, and a Framework for Bias Aware Interaction with Large Language Models
items.abstract: Prompt engineering is commonly conceptualized as the systematic design and refinement of instructions that guide the behavior of large language models (LLMs). However, the effectiveness and reliability of prompting depend not only on linguistic structure and technical characteristics but also on the cognitive processes of the humans who formulate, interpret, and evaluate prompts. Human reasoning is influenced by cognitive biases, including confirmation bias, anchoring, framing effects, availability bias, overconfidence, and automation bias. These mechanisms can shape the assumptions embedded in prompts, the selection of information presented to artificial intelligence, the interpretation of generated responses, and subsequent decisions about accepting or modifying outputs. This article proposes a psychologically informed conceptual framework for understanding cognitive biases throughout the prompt engineering process. It distinguishes biases originating in human cognition from prompt-induced response effects and systematic characteristics of language-model behavior. Particular attention is given to reciprocal human–AI feedback loops in which initial expectations influence prompt construction, model responses reinforce those expectations, and repeated interactions may increase perceived confidence without corresponding improvements in evidential accuracy. Building upon research in cognitive psychology, human–automation interaction, and prompt sensitivity, the article introduces Bias-Aware Prompt Engineering (BAPE) as a proposed framework for reducing epistemically undesirable bias through explicit assumption identification, alternative hypothesis generation, controlled prompt variation, independent verification, and metacognitive monitoring. Practical examples, operational indicators, and testable research hypotheses are presented. The central argument is that effective prompt engineering should be evaluated not merely by the coherence, usefulness, or persuasiveness of generated responses, but by the extent to which the interaction supports accurate reasoning, epistemic calibration, intellectual autonomy, and accountable human judgment

items.title: Exploration Before Representation: What Do Machine Learning Models Do in Science?
items.abstract: Philosophy of machine learning frequently frames what machine learning models do in science in target-oriented terms. This paper argues that this framing misses a significant modeling function: across many stages of scientific practice, machine learning models are used primarily for exploration, with target-oriented, representational assessment deferred. I develop a framework for exploratory machine learning models, characterizing them by their functional role in carving and exploring spaces of theoretical/experimental possibilities under target indeterminacy. I then propose robustness, calibration, and downstream investigative yield as primary evaluation criteria. I further argue that such workflows can warrant theoretically constrained modal claims and support how-possible inferences.

items.title: Not so dead after all: Young stars in the massive lenticular NGC 3115
items.abstract: Massive early-type galaxies (ETGs) host old, metal-rich stellar populations that formed rapidly in the high-z Universe, ostensibly earning themselves the moniker `red-and-dead'. To study their properties, most works have focused on optical wavelengths. When studied under the ultraviolet (UV) lens, however, a different picture emerges: a sub-one-per-cent mass fraction of young stars is revealed from detailed spectroscopic analysis. We aim to measure the mass fraction of young stars in NGC,3115, a local massive isolated lenticular. Unlike in previous UV studies, which focused on massive ellipticals, we attempt to understand the spatial distribution of this young component in a lenticular galaxy. This is a strong test of the ubiquity of this component. Using SOAR/Goodman spectra down to the atmosphere cut-off, we employed line-strength fitting to uncover this hidden population. We used a parametrised star formation history given by a single model representing the bulk stellar population plus a young component modelled with constant star formation over the last 1 Gyr . Using ultranest , we found the posterior distributions of age, metallicity, Mg/Fe , and the young stellar mass fraction. Using the mismatch in the U-band indices across the different spatial extractions, we measured how the young stellar population mass fraction varies within the galaxy. We find that the gradient peaks at 0.69^ +0.09 _ -0.15 % in the centre, decreasing to zero at around 1 kpc galactocentric distances. We find that the kinematic and morphological structures correlate with the presence of this young component, which dominates in the pressure-supported region. We interpret these findings as residual star formation in the centre of NGC,3115 likely fuelled by internal processes (e.g. recycled material from past generations of stars). To further strengthen this detection, we also compared models of other UV-bright stellar sources (e.g. metal-rich extreme horizontal branch and metal-poor contributions) that could mimic a young stellar population. We find that these models result in worse fits and unphysically high mass fractions and thus cannot explain the observed mismatch. The presence of young stars in old, `red-and-dead' galaxies, therefore, seems to be more common than previously expected. The fact that they are being found in a wider population of galaxies and exhibit similar gradients further indicates that residual star formation is apparently a common feature in massive ETGs of any type. Measuring this residual star formation can help place constraints on the physical processes governing the baryon cycle in ETGs.

items.title: Optical linear polarization of the Be--X-ray pulsar binary LS V +44 17
items.abstract: We present the optical BVR polarization measurements for the Be--X-ray pulsar binary łsv from its giant outburst in early 2023 and subsequently over three years. We detect a significant polarization of ≈1.1--2.1%, which includes the interstellar contribution. Polarization evolves significantly with time since the outburst. The interstellar polarization was found to be ≈2.5--2.9%. The obtained intrinsic optical polarization of łsv after correction is between 0.5--1.7%, perpendicular to the interstellar polarization direction. We considered various plausible sources of optical polarization and inferred scattering in the Be decretion disk to be the most dominant source based on time and spectral evolution. The changing intrinsic PA with time hints at a plausible precession of the Be disk.

items.title: Co-creating a quality management system: development, implementation and lessons learned from a mixed-method action case study in a regional hospital.
items.abstract: Purpose Despite achieving an external accreditation label in 2018, an acute-care hospital in Flanders (Belgium) questioned why quality improvement was not sustainably embedded in daily practices. Contemporary quality paradigms emphasise co-creation with patients, kin and professionals, yet empirical evidence on how hospitals can operationalise co-creation within quality management systems (QMSs) remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to longitudinally explore and describe, over a four-year period, how a co-created QMS was developed and implemented in a regional acute-care hospital, and to identify the lessons learned throughout the co-creation process. Design/methodology/approach A four-year mixed-method action case study (June 2019-April 2023) using participatory and insider action research was conducted. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, focus groups, direct field observation and validated surveys assessing stakeholder (patients, kin and professionals) experiences and organisational QMS maturity. Findings The co-creation processes unfolded eight phases: contracting, exploring perceptions of the QMS, defining challenges, establishing and implementing quality projects, involving stakeholders, developing new quality visions, assessing QMS maturity and continuous follow-up. Four mechanisms were critical for success: broad stakeholder involvement, systematic integration of quantitative and qualitative data, committed leadership across organisational levels and the translation of a co-created quality vision into practice through iterative feedback loops and organisational follow-up. Practical implications The eight-phase co-creation approach provides a replicable pathway for hospitals seeking to embed co-creation in their QMS. Insights from this case informed the development of the Flanders Quality Model, currently implemented in 25 hospitals, demonstrating the broader applicability of the approach beyond the single case. Originality/value This study offers a detailed longitudinal description of how co-creation was operationalised within a hospital-wide QMS. By identifying eight interrelated development phases and elucidating the contributions of patients, kin, professionals, managers and researchers throughout the process, the study offers empirical insights into how co-creation can be operationalised in healthcare quality management. Furthermore, it highlights key conditions that supported its implementation over time, including broad stakeholder engagement, committed leadership, the integration of multiple data sources and continuous organisational learning.

items.title: Retinopathy of prematurity among infants in East Africa: a systematic review and Meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Aim To evaluate the pooled magnitude of retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) among infants' populations in East Africa. Methods A literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, Scopus, and African Journals Online to identify studies from East African published up to August 2025 that reported the magnitude of ROP and its associated factors. The quality of the included cohort and cross-sectional studies was assessed using a modified Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. A random-effects Meta-analysis was used to estimate the pooled magnitude of ROP and adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for associated factors, with results presented using 95% confidence intervals (CI). Heterogeneity among studies was assessed using the I ² statistic, and subgroup analysis and meta-regression were performed to explore its sources. Publication bias was assessed using funnel plots and Egger's regression test. Results A total of 11 studies were included. The pooled magnitude of ROP in East Africa was 18% (95%CI: 13%-24%, I 2 =95.77%). The Meta-analysis result showed that infants who received oxygen therapy (pooled OR=4.61, 95%CI: 1.88-7.33), neonates with birth weight less than 1500 g (pooled OR=5.82, 95%CI: 2.89-8.75), and respiratory distress syndrome (pooled OR=3.92, 95%CI: 2.54-5.29) were factors associated with ROP. Conclusion ROP is a significant public health concern in East Africa, affecting nearly one in five preterm infants. Policymakers and healthcare providers should prioritize evidence-based interventions targeting the prevention and early detection of ROP to mitigate its long-term impact on childhood blindness.

items.title: A Multidimensional Framework for Assessing the Direct and Indirect Effects of Urbanization on Avian Breeding Fitness: Integrating Environmental Factors, Food Resources, and Citizen Science for Species Conservation in Urban Landscapes
items.abstract: Urbanization is one of the defining issues of the Anthropocene, leading to dramatic transformation of land-cover patterns all around the Earth. This transformation has detrimental effects on global biodiversity and threatens the carrying capacity of our ecosystems. Three key environmental issues are associated with urbanization. First, urbanization affects ecosystem functioning and, particularly where it becomes more intense, it often results in reduced species richness and abundance. Second, the urban heat-island effect (UHI) and sensory pollutants such as noise pollution and artificial light at night (ALAN) cause detrimental effects on wildlife by advancing breeding dates, impairing communication and reducing breeding fitness. Third, urbanization can also imply a reduction in available food resources that is commonly perceived as the main constraint to breeding fitness for urban organisms — usually referred to as the food limitation hypothesis. The overall aims of this study were therefore to investigate how these different factors directly and indirectly interact, and their relative importance in shaping the fitness of wild organisms. The Barn Swallow Hirundo rustica is a perfect model species to study these questions. This human commensal is one of the few species that has coexisted with humans for thousands of years, and in China it is regarded as a symbol of good luck. It is also an aerial insectivore that benefits farmlands and croplands and controls urban pest populations, and its diet overlaps with many other insectivores, making the results applicable to a wide range of urban species. Moreover, Barn Swallow populations and other aerial insectivores are experiencing steep declines all around the world. Investigating the current status of Barn Swallow rural and urban populations, its interactions with humans, and deepening our understanding on the consequences of increased urbanization, are thus top research priorities. Here, I first developed a multidimensional framework to act as a theoretical foundation for understanding how different facets of the urban ecosystem interact to affect bird breeding fitness. In my first field project, I collected Barn Swallow breeding data regarding laying dates, clutch size, number of hatchling and fledgling, hatching and fledging success, and insect biomass at the colony level, quantifying environmental variables and dietary composition for active nests (N=53) at the nest and colony level. The results showed that urbanization and laying behavior were directly related to insect abundance, phenological mismatch and diet of Barn Swallows while UHI was indirectly related to phenological mismatch and diet. Finally, direct negative effects of insect diets (e.g., flies) on fledging success of Barn Swallows, and indirect positive effects on fledging success of later laying date were recorded. In the second field project, I used Barn Swallow nesting locations from a nationwide citizen science as well as associated environmental variables at the site and landscape levels. This study revealed that UHI effects at the site scale, and ALAN and road simplicity at the landscape scale were positively associated with Barn Swallow nest abundance while building year had a negative impact on Barn Swallow nests. Overall, results suggest Barn Swallow can respond to these mixed effects at multiple spatial scales and efficiently adapt to various environmental conditions across the urbanized landscape. The studies presented in this thesis demonstrated that adopting a multidimensional framework in urban ecology can lead to a comprehensive understanding of both direct and indirect, as well as positive and negative effects of urbanization and environmental factors on species’ habitat selection and breeding parameters. Utilizing a multidimensional framework also enables us to plan and design urban environments in order to minimize the adverse impacts of urbanization for both biodiversity and people.

items.title: From Burden to Breakthrough: A Roadmap to Disentangle Fatigue in Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
items.abstract: Despite observed benefits of current treatments, several burdensome symptoms persist in people living with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). Fatigue is consistently indicated as a top unmet need by the SMA community. Historically ascribed as an inevitable consequence of underlying muscle weakness, fatigue is now recognized as central to the lived SMA experience, and several efforts have been made to better characterize it. As in other disorders, the study of fatigue in SMA is complicated by inconsistencies in terminology and nomenclature, a challenge compounded by the heterogeneous language patients use to describe their experiences. Without shared language and conceptual frameworks, progress toward an improved understanding of fatigue has been impeded. Critical to this aim is distinguishing between related but distinct constructs: perceived fatigue, a subjective multidimensional experience, and fatigability, a measurable decline in motor output or sustained activity. Both are prominent in SMA, but their biological causes remain unclear. Here, we draw on available evidence and the perspectives of experts, community stakeholders, caregivers, and patients to propose a uniform, collaboratively developed methodology that aims to advance SMA fatigue research and clinical management. This review outlines a roadmap to enhance identification of biological mechanisms and harmonize assessment tools, ultimately leading to a breakthrough in the treatment of fatigue. This iterative process is likely to extend beyond SMA and yield similar benefits in related neuromuscular conditions.

items.title: Associations Between Sexual Goals, Relationship Satisfaction, and Conflict Among Couples Affected by Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder.
items.abstract: Engaging in sex to pursue approach goals (e.g., intimacy), is linked with greater relationship satisfaction, whereas avoidance goals (e.g., preventing partner disappointment) relate to lower satisfaction and higher conflict. Compared to those without sexual difficulties, individuals with Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder (SIAD) report fewer approach and more avoidance goals, with potential implications for their relationship quality. To examine bidirectional associations between partner-focused sexual goals and relationship satisfaction and conflict, individuals with SIAD and their partners ( N = 263 couples) completed validated measures at baseline and 6 months later. Guided by the actor-partner interdependence model, structural equation models revealed that higher approach goals among individuals with SIAD were associated with greater concurrent relationship satisfaction. In contrast, partners' higher avoidance goals were associated with lower concurrent satisfaction and higher conflict for both couple members. Prospective associations indicated that sexual goals did not predict 6-month outcomes, or vice versa, except that those individuals with SIAD who reported higher baseline relationship satisfaction reported lower avoidance goals 6 months later. Findings highlight that sexual goals mostly relate to proximal experiences of relationship quality in couples facing SIAD, suggesting that promoting approach and reducing avoidance goals may be linked to more favorable outcomes in their sexual relationships.

items.title: Early Treatment with Oral Pirfenidone Improves Bladder Function after Contusive Spinal Cord Injury in Mice.
items.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) disrupts innervation to the lower urinary tract, resulting in bladder dysfunction that predisposes to urinary infections and renal impairment. While inflammation is central to bladder pathology after SCI, the molecular events linking acute to chronic remodeling are poorly defined. We hypothesized that early treatment with pirfenidone, an anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic drug, would attenuate bladder pathology after SCI. Adult female C57BL/6J mice underwent contusive SCI or sham laminectomy, and bladders were collected at 2, 7, 16, and 45 days later. SCI induced bladder hypertrophy, edema, hemorrhage, neutrophil infiltration, cell proliferation and loss of voiding function in the first 48 hours. Transcriptomic profiling at this timepoint was characterized by activation of inflammatory and cytokine pathways including TNF-α, IL-6, the complement cascade, and TGFβ. Although bladder function partially recovered by day 7, inflammatory pathways persisted and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling programs emerged. By day 16, robust activation of ECM-remodeling pathways was evident in all bladders. Treatment with pirfenidone during the acute inflammatory phase (day 2-7) reduced bladder hypertrophy and suppressed expression of pro-fibrotic, inflammatory, and neuroplasticity-associated genes including Bdnf and Chrm2 that encodes muscarinic receptor 2 (M2). Mechanistically, pirfenidone attenuated TGFb signaling as shown by downregulation of phosphoSmad2 protein in whole bladders and decreased M2 receptor expression in the urothelium. These molecular changes correlated with improved function in pirfenidone-treated mice as shown by fewer voiding events with larger urine volumes up until 45 days after SCI. Early treatment with pirfenidone limits inflammation and fibrosis, normalizes neural signaling, and improves bladder function after SCI.

items.title: Growth Differentiation Factor 15 as a Body-Brain Stress Signal in Major Depression and Insulin Resistance.
items.abstract: Objective Major depressive disorder (MDD) is linked to insulin resistance, which is associated with increased risk, chronicity, and poor treatment response in depression. Growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15), a stress-induced cytokine linking peripheral to central energy metabolism, may mediate this link, but its role in MDD is unclear. The authors assessed associations of MDD and insulin resistance with GDF15; links between GDF15, symptoms, and stress; and whether baseline GDF15 levels predict symptom persistence. Methods In this preregistered secondary analysis, 190 participants with MDD and 183 control participants provided blood, underwent interviews, and completed questionnaires. GDF15 values were log-transformed and analyzed with linear models. The association between GDF15 and depression severity was validated in an independent cohort of medication-free MDD patients (N=168). Results Both MDD diagnosis and insulin resistance were significantly associated with elevated GDF15 (adjusted for age and sex). Across all participants, elevated GDF15 was significantly associated with greater depressive severity, childhood trauma, and perceived stress. In stratified analyses, the association with depression severity and perceived stress was significant only in healthy control subjects. In MDD patients, baseline GDF15 was associated with persistence of symptoms across time. In the second independent sample of medication-free MDD patients, depression severity was significantly associated with GDF15. Conclusions GDF15 is elevated in MDD and insulin resistance, indicating convergent stress-energy pathway activation, and in MDD higher GDF15 predicted symptom persistence. These findings position GDF15 as a mechanistic biomarker at the interface of psychiatric and metabolic health and reinforce the need for integrated care of metabolic and mental health.

items.title: Late-onset Alzheimer's Disease Pathologies in a Novel hAβ/ApoE4 Mouse Line.
items.abstract: Most Alzheimer's disease (AD) cases are late-onset and sporadic, yet existing mouse models predominantly reflect familial, autosomal-dominant forms. To address this gap, we present the first characterisation of hAβ/ApoE4 mice, which carry a humanised amyloid-beta (Aβ) sequence knocked into the endogenous amyloid precursor protein (APP) locus and a human apolipoprotein E4 (ApoE4) allele replacing murine ApoE, in the context of age-associated AD phenotypes. We aged hAβ/ApoE4 mice of both sexes to 12 months and assessed AD-relevant pathologies including cognition, spine loss, neurodegeneration, neuroinflammation and Aβ deposition. At 12 months, hAβ/ApoE4 mice exhibited spatial memory deficits in the Barnes maze as well as modestly reduced apical dendritic spine density without hippocampal neuronal loss. This model offers a platform for introducing environmental stressors and co-morbidities and establishes a reference point for the development of next-generation sporadic AD models.

items.title: Neuroprotective effects of the petroleum ether fraction of Teucrium polium in free and lipid nanoparticle formulations on cognitive deficits and oxidative stress in an ICV-STZ-induced Alzheimer's-like rat model.
items.abstract: Background Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline, oxidative stress, and neuronal loss. Current pharmacological treatments provide only partial symptomatic relief. This study investigated the neuroprotective effects of the petroleum ether fraction of Teucrium polium (T. polium), administered in both free and lipid nanoparticle formulations (T. polium-LNP), in a rat model of AD-like pathology induced by intracerebroventricular streptozotocin (ICV-STZ). Methods Adult male Wistar rats were divided into five groups: Control, ICV-STZ, ICV-STZ + Memantine, ICV-STZ + T. polium, and ICV-STZ + T. polium-LNP. Cognitive function was assessed using the Morris water maze (MWM) and novel object recognition (NOR) tests. Serum oxidative stress markers-including malondialdehyde (MDA), total antioxidant capacity (TAC), and superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity-were measured. Hippocampal CA1 histopathology and hippocampal mRNA expression of Bax, Bcl-2, and p53 were also evaluated. Results The ICV-STZ-induced AD-like model was associated with memory impairment, increased serum MDA levels, reduced TAC levels and SOD activity, and hippocampal CA1 neuronal damage, accompanied by increased Bax and p53 expression and decreased Bcl-2 expression. Treatment with T. polium and T. polium-LNP improved cognitive performance, particularly spatial memory in the MWM, and attenuated several pathological changes. Both treatments reduced serum MDA levels and decreased CA1 neuronal degeneration. Conclusion In this experimental AD-like rat model, both formulations of T. polium were associated with improvements in cognitive performance, serum oxidative status markers, and hippocampal tissue changes. Although T. polium-LNP showed numerically greater effects on several outcomes, direct comparisons between the free T. polium extract and T. polium-LNP were statistically significant only for CA1 neuronal damage. Further mechanistic and long-term studies are needed to clarify the potential relevance of these findings to AD-related neuroprotection.

items.title: Males and females integrate paternal predation cues through distinct early-life gene expression trajectories.
items.abstract: Environmental conditions experienced by parents can alter offspring phenotypes, with increasing evidence that parental cues have sex-specific intergenerational effects on sons and daughters. A key mechanistic step of such intergenerational plasticity involves the integration of parentally transmitted cues by early developing offspring through changes in gene regulatory processes. Sex-specific intergenerational effects may therefore arise if male and female embryos have divergent gene regulatory responses to shared parental cues - a process that could mitigate the severity of intersex conflicts associated with intergenerational inheritance. Using three-spine stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus), we exposed fathers to predation risk and tested whether paternal cues are differentially integrated by male and female offspring by measuring gene regulatory responses across four stages spanning embryonic and early larval development. Consistent with sex-specific integration of parental cues, we found that paternal predation risk had sex-specific effects on gene expression across all stages of early development. Male gene expression responses to paternal predation risk were dominated by epigenetic processes, including DNA demethylation, whereas female responses were enriched for genes involved in transcriptional coregulation as well as neural and visual processes. ∼39% of genes responding to paternal predation cues in males were located on non-recombining regions of sex chromosomes, compared with only ∼1.6% of differentially reacting genes in females, suggesting that sex chromosome-associated genomic regions may contribute to sex-specific integration of shared parental cues. Altogether, our results demonstrate that sons and daughters integrate cues from fathers through distinct gene regulatory pathways, potentially facilitating the development and evolution of sex-specific phenotypes.

items.title: Contrasting host infection strategies predict cercarial behavioural responses to humic substances.
items.abstract: Parasite transmission depends on free-living infective stages locating susceptible hosts within a limited time window. For trematodes, host-search behaviour is shaped by host ecology and environmental cues, yet the effects of environmental change on these behaviours remain poorly understood. We compared the cercarial behaviour of two common marine trematodes, Cryptocotyle lingua (fish host) and Himasthla elongata (blue mussel host), using automated tracking, dimensionality reduction and hidden Markov model. The species occupied distinct movement-phenotype spaces consistent with different host-search strategies: C. lingua showed sparse, fast, relatively linear movement interspersed with prolonged quiescence, whereas H. elongata exhibited slower, highly tortuous trajectories and frequent switching between roaming and dwelling states. Exposure to environmentally relevant humic substances induced species-specific behavioural plasticity, reducing activity in C. lingua while increasing turning and reshaping behavioural state dynamics in H. elongata. Waterborne cues in host-conditioned water interacted with humic substances to further reorganise movement patterns. These findings identify humic substances as active modulators of parasite behaviour and suggest that behavioural state architecture links environmental change to parasite transmission in coastal ecosystems.

items.title: Effects of electron beam and Cesium-137 irradiation on Cochliomyia macellaria.
items.abstract: The New World Screwworm Cochliomyia hominivorax (Diptera: Calliphoridae) is an obligate parasite that causes myiasis of endothermic hosts. The agricultural costs incurred by infestations can amount to billions of dollars in losses annually. This species was eradicated from the United States and Central America utilizing the Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) with radioactive isotopes such as Cobalt-60 (Co-60) or Cesium-137 (Cs-137) as the radiation source. Electron beam (eBeam) is a possible alternative ionizing radiation technology for SIT that is safer and potentially less expensive. This study investigated the effects of both eBeam and Cs-137-based gamma radiation technologies on the lifespan and fertility of Cochliomyia macellaria, the sister species of C. hominivorax. Late-stage pupae of C. macellaria were exposed to either high-energy electron beam (HEEB) or Cs-137 radiation. Treated pupae were allowed to develop to adulthood and were utilized in biological assays. Results indicated that neither eBeam nor Cs-137 treatments affected eclosion rates. Both eBeam and Cs-137 treatments of >40 Gy significantly decreased ovarian development. Induced sterility assays indicated that both eBeam and Cs-137 treatments reduce male fertility, resulting in reduced counts of viable offspring. Longevity data suggest a possible hormetic effect: eBeam treatments may extend adult fly lifespan compared to controls, whereas Cs-137 treatments appeared to negatively impact lifespan. These results suggest that eBeam treatments can induce sterility in C. macellaria-treated flies, with limited negative effect on other fitness traits. These results support eBeam technology as a potential alternative ionizing radiation source for SIT applications.

items.title: Introduction to the Special Issue on Operational Psychology.
items.abstract: Operational psychology applies psychological theory and research methods to understand how human factors influence readiness, performance, and learning in safety-critical military and civilian operations. The seven studies in this special issue demonstrate how psychological processes contribute to mission success in domains including military aviation, law enforcement, fire and rescue operations, and municipal public safety. Across these contexts, operational outcomes depend not only on technical expertise but also on interpersonal, emotional, ethical, and organizational factors. The findings collectively underscore the need for enhanced training, professionalization, and cross-domain research at the individual, team, and organizational levels to support resilient responses to critical events.

items.title: Composite scores as a measure of cyclic vomiting syndrome burden: Preliminary validation in children.
items.abstract: Cyclic vomiting syndrome (CVS) is a debilitating, episodic vomiting disorder. There are no validated outcome surveys quantifying the burden of CVS episodes. Recent data demonstrate that specific parameters such as episode timing, duration, and associated symptoms are key to diagnosing pediatric CVS. It is unclear if these specific parameters alone or in combination relate to the disabling nature of CVS. This study aimed to evaluate the strength of various CVS composite scores based on episode parameters compared to individual parameters in relationship to a proxy index of disability. Secondary analysis of data from 38 patients aged 3-18 years presenting with episodic vomiting at Children's Wisconsin hospital with a formal CVS diagnosis, including a migraine-associated CVS (mCVS) subgroup (n = 21), were analyzed. Patients and caregivers completed surveys on specific symptoms during vomiting episodes and the pediatric migraine disability assessment (PedMIDAS) tool as index of CVS-related disability burden. Pearson correlations were computed between PedMIDAS disability scores and seven different CVS composite scores including the following parameters of episodes: frequency (F), duration (D), nausea severity (Sn), headache pain severity (Sh), and abdominal pain severity (Sa). For both CVS and mCVS, each composite score was more strongly associated with PedMIDAS than any individual parameter. For CVS patients, the F*D*Sn and F*D*Sn*Sa composite scores showed the strongest disability association (r = 0.628, p < 0.001 and r = 0.654, p < 0.001, respectively). For mCVS, the F*D*Sh composite score had the strongest association with disability (r = 0.731, p < 0.001). This study provides preliminary validation of a pediatric CVS burden scale based on an index of disability. Composite scores that include several individual episode parameters have stronger associations with disability than any individual parameters alone.

items.title: Nanobiomaterial Immunoengineering of Cold Tumors: Overcoming Barriers to Enable Therapeutic Response.
items.abstract: Immunologically "cold" tumors are unresponsive to immune checkpoint blockade and adoptive cell therapies. Thisunresponsiveness has been attributed to factors such as limited antigen presentation, abnormal vasculature, metabolic constraints, suppressive myeloid and regulatory networks, and the exclusion of effector lymphocytes. Engineered nanobiomaterials have recently emerged as versatile immunoengineering platforms capable of modulating these barriers within the tumor microenvironment (TME). This narrative review summarizes recent preclinical and early clinical advances demonstrating how rationally designed nanobiomaterials can induce immunogenic cell death, activate innate immune sensing pathways, remodel immunosuppressive TMEs, enhance dendritic cell priming, and promote T-cell infiltration and memory formation. Through these mechanisms, nanobiomaterials have the capacity to reprogram cold tumors into immunotherapy-responsive microenvironments. The present study also evaluates the translational potential of nano-enabled immunotherapies and then discusses the current challenges related to targeting specificity, safety, and scalability. Finally, we highlight future directions focused on mechanism-driven design, integration with cell-based immunotherapies, and the incorporation of clinically relevant immune profiling strategies to improve therapeutic outcomes.

items.title: Do You See Me How I See Myself-and Does It Matter? Parent-Child Agreement on Symptom Ratings after Mild Traumatic Brain Injury and Its Association with Recovery: An A-CAP Study.
items.abstract: Current methods for diagnosing and monitoring recovery of pediatric mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) rely heavily on both self-report and parent-proxy symptom inventories. Yet little is known about parent-child agreement and the clinical relevance of (dis)agreement on symptom inventories commonly used in pediatric mTBI. The current study thus aimed to (1) quantify parent-child agreement on an mTBI symptom inventory; (2) investigate which sociodemographic, clinical, psychosocial, and study-related factors are associated with agreement; and (3) finally explore whether early parent-child difference in symptom report is associated with symptom reporting over time. We conducted a secondary analysis of data collected from the Advancing Concussion Assessment in Pediatrics (A-CAP) study, a large-scale prospective longitudinal cohort study. Participants were children between ages 8 and 16.99 years with mTBI (n = 633) or orthopedic injury (OI; n = 334). Parent-child dyads completed symptom ratings using the Health and Behavior Inventory (HBI; cognitive and somatic symptom subscales) weekly or biweekly over the first 6 months post-injury and completed a series of questionnaires assessing sociodemographic, clinical, and psychosocial variables. Parent-child agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Bland-Altman (BA) plots. Two ordinary least squares linear regression models were used to assess factors associated with parent-child directional differences (i.e., parent minus child rating scores) on cognitive and somatic ratings. To investigate whether parent-child directional differences were associated with symptom trajectories, four generalized least squares models were used, with parent-reported cognitive and somatic and child-reported cognitive and somatic symptoms as the outcomes. Parent-child agreement was moderate for both cognitive (ICC = 0.67) and somatic (ICC = 0.65) symptoms. Visual inspection of BA plots showed somewhat better agreement for somatic symptoms. Number of days post-injury, sex, race, and parent-reported pre-injury report of symptoms, but not group (mTBI vs OI), were associated with cognitive and somatic parent-child difference scores. Parent-child differences early after injury were associated with both parent (χ2(3) = 38.11, p < 0.001) and child (χ2(3) = 27.16, p < 0.001) cognitive and parent (χ2(3) = 11.11, p = 0.011) and child (χ2(3) = 42.36, p < 0.001) somatic symptom trajectories. Parent-child agreement on the HBI is consistent with the broader psychopathology and health literature. Factors such as time since injury, sex, race, and pre-injury symptoms may be particularly important for understanding parent-child agreement on the HBI. Early disagreement, especially for cognitive symptoms, was relevant to later recovery trajectories, with dyads "coming together" over time. Findings highlight the importance of multi-informant assessment after mTBI.

items.title: Arts-based involvement is associated with positive perceptions of dementia in Singapore: an item-level perspective.
items.abstract: Background Arts-based programmes have shown promise in enhancing perceptions towards dementia, but research on such initiatives is scarce in the Asia-Pacific region. We investigated how involvement in an arts-based programme designed for persons living with dementia in Singapore is associated with attitudes towards dementia. Methods A cross-sectional survey design was employed with 75 community members aged 19 to 68 ( M = 42.07, SD = 13.77) with three levels of involvement in the programme: low involvement, high involvement, and newly inducted community members. Participants rated items on the Approaches to Dementia Questionnaire and Dementia Attitudes Scale. Quantitative data were analysed in R software. Results Compared to community members with low involvement and those who are newly inducted, participants with high involvement reported significantly higher hope (η p 2 = .18) and personhood (η p 2 = .17). Arts-based involvement was positively associated with hope (r s = .40, p s = .32, p = .005), and knowledge (r s = .28, p = .014), but not comfort (r s = .07, p = .528). Item-level analyses revealed that high involvement in the programme was associated with greater endorsement of flexible routine (η p 2 = 0.09), hope (η p 2 = .14), independent decision-making (η p 2 = .12), and the importance of conversations (η p 2 = .52). Conclusions Involvement in arts-based programmes is associated with viewing persons living with dementia through a more empowering lens - recognising their capacity for independent decision-making, valuing meaningful conversations, endorsing that dementia care need not be overly regimented, and holding greater hope for their dignity.

items.title: First-hand Alcohol-Related Harms in Hong Kong University Dormitories: A Serial Cross-sectional Study Comparing the Normative, Social Unrest, and COVID-19 Pandemic Periods.
items.abstract: Between September 2018 and June 2021, we conducted serial cross-sectional surveys of university dormitory residents in Hong Kong (n = 2659). Drinking behaviors and first-hand harms were examined across a normative period, time of protests, and the COVID-19 pandemic. Drinking levels remained steady between the normative and protest periods but increased during the pandemic, and the proportions reporting drinking-related harms were 57.1%, 53.9%, and 62.5%, respectively. Binge drinking was associated with high first-hand harms across 3 periods (adjusted odds ratio [AOR]: 3.46-5.76). Having a drinking roommate was also correlated with harms during the normative period (AOR = 1.66). During the protests, underage drinking history and university location were associated with high first-hand harms (AOR: 1.69 and 1.82). During the COVID-19 pandemic, weekend dormitory residence and low alcohol-related knowledge were significant factors (AOR: 2.78 and 2.85). The findings indicate the need for context-specific alcohol harm reduction strategies in East Asian university dormitories.

items.title: Ethical and emotional complexity of verbal autopsy implementation in South Africa: a preliminary trauma-informed practice framework.
items.abstract: Verbal autopsy (VA) is used in mortality surveillance and civil registration where deaths lack medical certification. Its ethical, emotional, and cultural challenges are recognised, but less is known about implementer experiences and organisational responses. To examine ethical and emotional challenges among those implementing and supervising VA across settings, identify available supports, and develop a preliminary trauma-informed practice framework. We interviewed 13 VA implementers: 8 interviewers and 5 in supervisory, coordination or related roles, across three rural and urban South African Population Research Infrastructure Network (SAPRIN) nodes. Rapid qualitative analysis explored experiences and supports across roles and sites. Interviewers described repeated exposure to grief and traumatic deaths, guilt about prompting distress among bereaved respondents, and emotional impacts that extended into personal lives. Participants reported ethical tensions when they were unable to address bereaved households' needs and divergent views on respondent compensation. Supervisors described emotional demands arising from previous frontline experience together with responsibilities for supporting teams. Supports ranged from informal peer and supervisory discussions to structured debriefing and counselling with varied views on availability and adequacy. Drawing on implementer experiences and trauma-informed principles, we developed a preliminary framework outlining actions and organisational responsibilities to support VA implementers' wellbeing and the safe, respectful conduct of interviews with bereaved respondents. The ethical and emotional demands of VA warrant organisational responses to support interviewer and supervisor wellbeing, alongside measures to protect bereaved respondents and ensure respectful interviewing. The framework requires refinement with bereaved respondents and communities, and testing in other settings.

items.title: Scoping Review of the National Surgical Plans of Small Island Nations.
items.abstract: The Lancet Commission on Global Surgery (LCoGS) report in 2015 established surgical care as an integral part of public health and critical for the achievement of universal health coverage. This review aims to assess the gap that exists by evaluating the presence and or absence of formal surgical plans and the integration of global surgical indicators into national health frameworks of Small Island Development States (SIDS). The review employed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) framework for scoping reviews and was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) Checklist. A targeted search of both published and gray literature to find national health policy documents from the 39 SIDS was performed. Titles, executive summaries, and full document reviews were searched for any form of surgical component and reporting of the six LCoGS indicators. Twenty-eight documents were found for analysis. Of the 28 national plans, 11 were from the Caribbean, 13 from the Pacific and 4 from the Atlantic, Indian Ocean, and South China Sea (AIS). The median publication date was 2019 (2010-2026). Only three countries had National Surgical Obstetric and Anesthesia Plans (NSOAPs), all from the Pacific region. Twenty-three included general National Strategic Plans (NSP), one National Development Plan (NDP) and one other plan. 64% (Caribbean 7/11, Pacific 9/13 and AIS 2/4) reported inclusion of surgical components. At least one LCoGS indicator inclusion was reported by 20 (71%). Planning for safe and affordable surgical, obstetric and anesthesia care remains poorly developed across the SIDS with only 3 countries having developed a standalone NSOAP. Closing this gap requires context specific plans applying WHO's 6 health system building blocks through expanded universal health coverage for surgical and anesthesia services, formalized referral partnerships, and greater recognition of allied health workers.

items.title: Voices of the volunteer health workforce: exploring motivations and systemic barriers among community health workers in Pader District, Uganda.
items.abstract: Community health workers (CHWs) are essential to primary healthcare delivery in low-resource and post-conflict settings, yet limited evidence describes factors associated with sustained engagement among volunteer CHWs. To explore CHWs' motivations for joining and remaining in a volunteer program, their aspirations and perceived public health impact, and the challenges and coping strategies shaping engagement in Pader District, Northern Uganda. We conducted semi-structured interviews with CHWs (n = 11) across six sub-counties in July 2024, purposively sampled for gender, geography, and experience. Interviews were conducted in English and Acholi, transcribed, translated, and analyzed using qualitative descriptive analysis informed by interpretative phenomenological analysis. After themes were finalized, Social Cognitive Theory and Self-Determination Theory were applied as interpretive lenses to map findings to behavioral mechanisms and propose implementation strategies. Participants were 8 men and 3 women aged 29-49 years, with 6 months to 8 years of program involvement. CHWs joined out of altruism and lived experiences, alongside extrinsic motivators such as community recognition and hopes for future training. They described roles as trusted educators and providers, with perceived improvements in early care-seeking and community trust. Major barriers included supply shortages, transportation limitations, limited supervision, and gender-based legitimacy challenges. CHWs coped through peer support, informal learning, and encouragement from friends and family. CHWs in post-conflict Northern Uganda demonstrate strong commitment and perceived public health impact, but persistent system constraints threaten sustained engagement. A theory-informed, hypothesis-generating conceptual model and implementation mapping propose candidate strategies to strengthen CHW programs in similar settings.

items.title: Satisfaction with hospital-based outpatient rehabilitation in people with Parkinson's disease and its association with life satisfaction and health-related quality of life: a longitudinal national register study.
items.abstract: To examine satisfaction with hospital-based outpatient rehabilitation and its association with life satisfaction and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in people with Parkinson's disease, and whether sex and age affect possible associations. A longitudinal national register study. Methods: Data from the Swedish register for rehabilitation medicine included 173 individuals with Parkinson's disease. Self-reported questionnaires were collected at admission, discharge, and 1-year follow-up. Associations between satisfaction with rehabilitation received (register-based questionnaire) and life satisfaction (Life Satisfaction Questionnaire, LiSat-11 global item) and HRQoL (EuroQol 5 dimensions questionnaire, EQ5D) were examined using regression analyses. Over 82% of the participants were satisfied with the outpatient rehabilitation on discharge. High satisfaction with several aspects of rehabilitation was associated with higher scores on LiSat-11 and EQ-5D at discharge, whereas few associations were observed at the 1-year follow-up. Men and older adults (> 69 years) demonstrated broader associations than women and younger adults. Greater satisfaction with hospital-based outpatient rehabilitation was associated with higher life satisfaction and HRQoL on discharge, whereas these associations were less evident at the 1-year follow-up. Assessing patients' experiences of rehabilitation and patient-reported outcome measures may provide complementary perspectives when evaluating and developing rehabilitation in people with Parkinson's disease.

items.title: Real-world effectiveness and safety of eptinezumab in migraine prevention.
items.abstract: Eptinezumab is the only anti-calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) monoclonal antibody administered intravenously for migraine prevention. Randomized trials have shown efficacy in episodic and chronic migraine, including after previous preventive failures, but strict eligibility criteria limit their generalizability to routine care. This review summarizes the pharmacology and pivotal trials of eptinezumab and examines real-world studies of its effectiveness and safety, identified through a PubMed search up to October 2026. Particular attention is given to patients with previous anti-CGRP antibody failure, medication overuse and cardiovascular disease, and to the limitations of the available evidence. Real-world cohorts confirm a rapid onset and a clinically relevant benefit in broader and more refractory populations, with mostly mild and transient adverse events, although hypersensitivity reactions during infusion deserve attention. Effect sizes vary widely and are likely inflated by analyses restricted to patients who remain on treatment. Previous response to an antibody may predict benefit better than previous failure. Priorities are controlled switching studies, predictors of response and prospective evidence on when to judge treatment and whom to escalate to 300 mg.

items.title: Hypophosphatemia in Pediatric Diabetic Ketoacidosis: Incidence, Determinants, and Clinical Impact in a Tertiary Emergency and Intensive Care Cohort.
items.abstract: Serum phosphate levels commonly decline during treatment of pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), but the determinants and clinical implications of hypophosphatemia remain incompletely defined. We aimed to determine its incidence, predictors, and clinical impact during pediatric DKA. In this retrospective study, 116 DKA episodes managed in a tertiary pediatric emergency department and intensive care unit between January 2022 and June 2025 were analyzed. Demographic characteristics, admission biochemical parameters, and clinical outcomes were recorded. Hypophosphatemia was defined according to age-specific reference ranges. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of hypophosphatemia, while length of hospital stay was assessed using multivariable linear regression of log-transformed values. Hypophosphatemia occurred in 72/116 episodes (62.1%). Compared with those without hypophosphatemia, affected patients had lower admission pH (7.03±0.13 vs. 7.12±0.17; P=0.002), bicarbonate (7.8±2.4 vs. 9.8±3.3 mEq/L; P<0.001), and potassium levels (4.43±0.96 vs. 4.81±0.66 mEq/L; P=0.024). Hyponatremia and hypokalemia were more frequent, whereas hyperkalemia was less common (all P<0.05). Lower admission pH (OR: 0.008, 95% CI: 0.000-0.219; P=0.004) and lower baseline phosphate concentration (OR: 0.67, 95% CI: 0.47-0.97; P=0.031) independently predicted hypophosphatemia. Although hospitalization was longer in the hypophosphatemia group (85.3±75.2 vs. 56.2±36.4 h; P=0.018), hypophosphatemia was not independently associated with length of stay. Higher admission pH independently predicted shorter hospitalization (β=-0.957, P=0.026). Baseline phosphate positively correlated with nadir phosphate during treatment (r=0.303, P<0.001). Hypophosphatemia is common during pediatric DKA and is closely associated with the severity of metabolic acidosis at presentation. However, it does not independently affect hospitalization duration, suggesting that it primarily reflects disease severity rather than independently determining short-term outcomes.

items.title: Redefining the Self in Adolescent and Young Adult Survivors of Childhood Cancer: Identity Attributes From a Qualitative Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Although survival rates in childhood cancer have improved substantially, survivorship remains a complex and ongoing process marked by identity reconstruction, shaped by developmental transitions, late effects, and the contested meanings of being a "survivor." To synthesize qualitative evidence on how adolescents and young adults (AYAs) who survived childhood cancer construct their identities and the meanings they attribute to being a "survivor." Systematic searches were conducted using the SPIDER framework. Eligible studies were original qualitative research exploring identity among AYAs diagnosed with cancer during childhood or adolescence who had completed treatment. Publications in English, Portuguese, or Spanish were included. Methodological quality of included studies was assessed using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Qualitative Research, and data were analyzed through thematic synthesis. Fourteen studies were included. Two analytical themes, each supported by 2 descriptive themes, were identified: (1) Identity Configurations and Self-Redefinition, reflecting ambivalence in adopting the "survivor" identity, and (2) The Dual Imprint of Identity, describing the coexistence of personal growth and persistent late effects. Social recognition also shaped identity construction. Identity in childhood cancer survivorship is characterized by ambivalence and a dual imprint of growth and limitation. Survivorship is experienced as an ongoing presence rather than a completed phase. Nursing care should incorporate identity-sensitive approaches that support reflection, self-expression, and recognition of individual strengths. Addressing identity in survivorship can promote psychosocial adjustment, autonomy, and long-term well-being among AYAs, reinforcing the need for person-centered oncology nursing care.

items.title: Cardiovascular Disease Prevention in Emerging Adults: A Narrative Review of Hypertension Knowledge, Cardiovascular Risk Perception, Self-Efficacy, and Life's Essential 8 Behaviors.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, making early prevention a public health priority. Emerging adulthood (18-29 years) is a critical period for establishing lifelong cardiovascular health behaviors, yet adherence to the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) health behaviors remains suboptimal among this population. To synthesize evidence on hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge, cardiovascular risk perception, self-efficacy, and LE8 health behaviors among emerging adults within the Health Belief Model. A narrative review was conducted using PubMed, CINAHL, Web of Science, APA PsycINFO, and Google Scholar. English-language publications (2000-November 2025) examining hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge, cardiovascular risk perception, self-efficacy, or LE8 health behaviors were reviewed. Findings were synthesized using a Health Belief Model-guided narrative approach. Thirty-nine studies were included. Hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge alone appeared insufficient to promote sustained engagement in LE8 health behaviors. Emerging adults frequently underestimated their cardiovascular risk despite modifiable risk factors. Self-efficacy may facilitate the translation of cardiovascular risk awareness and motivation into healthy behaviors. The synthesis informed a proposed HBM-guided framework in which knowledge may inform cardiovascular risk perception, risk perception may strengthen motivation for preventive action, and self-efficacy may facilitate healthy eating, physical activity, nicotine avoidance, and adequate sleep. These proposed relationships require empirical testing. Cardiovascular disease prevention among emerging adults requires more than education. Interventions should strengthen cardiovascular risk perception and self-efficacy while addressing social and structural barriers. The proposed framework provides a theory-informed foundation for cardiovascular nursing practice, future research, and intervention development.

items.title: Beyond age and ovarian reserve: a prospective study exploring inflammatory and cycle-specific biomarkers to enhance IVF outcome prediction.
items.abstract: Conventional predictors such as age and AFC fail to fully explain the substantial inter-individual variability in in vitro fertilization outcomes. This prospective exploratory study investigated whether integrating systemic and local inflammatory biomarkers-specifically calprotectin measured in plasma and follicular fluid-with conventional clinical parameters improves the prediction of cumulative clinical pregnancy. We prospectively enrolled consecutive patients undergoing in vitro fertilization and analyzed 75 completed cycles in which all retrieved oocytes and resulting embryos were used. Calprotectin concentrations were quantified in plasma and follicular fluid collected at oocyte retrieval. We evaluated associations with cumulative clinical pregnancy using univariable and multivariable logistic regression. Predictive models obtained were internally validated using a bootstrapping procedure to estimate optimism-corrected discrimination. Age and antral follicle count confirmed their established predictive roles, whereas calprotectin concentrations alone showed no significant association with cumulative pregnancy. In multivariable models, follicular fluid calprotectin showed a negative trend with pregnancy probability, whereas plasma calprotectin showed the opposite trend. Combining age, antral follicle count, and inflammatory parameters yielded strong discriminative performance; after bootstrap correction, the optimism-corrected area under the curve reached 0.862 for the peri-retrieval model and 0.841 for the post-fertilization model. Heatmap visualizations highlighted distinct risk patterns across age strata and inflammatory profiles. Integrating local and systemic inflammatory biomarkers with conventional clinical predictors provides complementary insights into in vitro fertilization success, suggesting that local microenvironmental stress and systemic immune activation exert divergent effects on reproductive potential. These exploratory, hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in larger, prospective cohorts. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06872294. Registered 20 March 2025.

items.title: Serum lipidomic remodeling associated with MASLD in Alström syndrome: comparison with BMI-matched obesity.
items.abstract: Alström syndrome (ALMS) is an ultra-rare monogenic ciliopathy with early-onset metabolic dysfunction and a high burden of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). However, the metabolic and lipidomic features of MASLD in ALMS remain poorly defined. We conducted a cross-sectional case-control study including patients with ALMS, BMI z-score-matched obesity controls, and healthy controls. Clinical phenotyping, metabolomics, lipidomics, network analysis, regression, and Random Forest analysis were integrated to characterize MASLD-associated lipid remodeling and prioritize candidate lipid signatures. Ninety-four participants were included: 30 with ALMS, 33 obesity controls, and 31 healthy controls. MASLD assessments were available for 83 participants (24 with ALMS, 30 obesity controls, and 29 healthy controls). MASLD was present in 75.0% (18/24) of patients with ALMS versus 23.3% (7/30) of obesity controls, despite comparable obesity severity. Lipidomic analyses revealed coordinated remodeling. Ether-linked phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidylethanolamine species were predominantly inversely associated with MASLD, whereas diacylglycerols, phosphatidic acids, and triglycerides showed positive associations. Integrated analyses further prioritized candidate lipid signatures for future validation. ALMS-associated MASLD is characterized by distinct structural lipid remodeling beyond obesity alone, particularly depletion of ether-linked phospholipids and enrichment of glycerolipid intermediates. These candidate lipid signatures warrant independent validation and mechanistic investigation in ALMS and broader MASLD populations.

items.title: Clinical and hematological characterization and carrier status awareness in a colombian cohort of sickle cell trait: a multicenter study.
items.abstract: Sickle cell trait (SCT) has traditionally been categorized as a benign carrier state; however, isolated reports and case series have nonetheless described rare complications overlapping with those seen in sickle cell disease (HbSS). The strength and consistency of these associations remain incompletely characterized. In this context, public health institutions like the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) have emphasized the need to expand research on SCT. To characterize the clinical and hematological profile of HbAS carriers compared with HbAA individuals and to assess carrier status awareness within a Colombian cohort. A descriptive and analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 400 adult volunteers from the Pacific and Atlantic Afro-descendant regions. Genotypes were confirmed via high-precision liquid chromatography (HPLC) and rs334 SNP sequencing. Clinical data were retrieved through structured interviews and medical record reviews. Hematological parameters and comorbidities were compared between HbAS and HbAA individuals using robust statistical analysis. A significant genotype unawareness was identified, with 45.9% (95%CI: 37.3%-54.8%; n = 56/122) of HbAS carriers being uninformed of their status prior to screening. Serious clinical events were documented predominantly in the HbAS group: Osteomyelitis and atypical diaphyseal femoral osteonecrosis occurred only in carriers (3.3% vs. 0.0%, Fisher´s exact p = 0.016). Neurovascular events; showed a higher prevalence in heterozygous individuals (5.7% vs. 0.9%, p = 0.013). The vast majority of HbAS carriers presented at the time of this project, percentage of HbS 36-40%. Regarding hematological parameters, HbAS individuals exhibited lower mean levels of RDW (12.2 ± 0.7% vs. 13.4 ± 1.3%, p = 0.017), platelets (260 ± 56.4 × 109/L vs. 308.2 ± 95.8 × 109/L, p = 0.003), and white blood cell count (6.1 ± 1.5 × 109/L vs. 7.4 ± 1.8 × 109/L, p = 0.026) compared to non-carrier individuals (HbAA). These findings suggest that HbAS may not be uniformly benign, as uncommon but clinically notable vaso-occlusive and osteonecrotic events were observed in a minority of carriers, alongside statistically detectable but subclinical hematological differences and a substantial gap in genotype awareness. Given the cross-sectional design and the small number of severe events, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to clarify their clinical significance and to inform screening and monitoring strategies in high-prevalence populations.
