items.title: Bogong moths navigate with a light-dependent geomagnetic inclination compass
items.abstract: Abstract Bogong moths ( Agrotis infusa ) migrate biannually up to 1,000 km between their breeding areas and geographically restricted aestivation sites in the Australian Alps 1,2 . These moths navigate towards their distant goal using the stars as a compass 3 but navigate correctly even when the stars are obscured by clouds 3 , suggesting that their magnetic sense 4 probably harnesses the Earth’s magnetic field as a compass. However, the nature of this compass, and of the magnetic sense underlying it, remains unknown. Here we show that Bogong moths, tethered in a flight arena under a full-spectrum randomized starry night sky, navigate in their inherited migratory direction using the geomagnetic field alone. If the geomagnetic field is turned by 180°, or if inclination is inverted, moths fly in the opposite direction. If polarity is inverted, moths fail to turn. Furthermore, if violet–blue light (380 nm < λ < 500 nm) is removed from the illumination spectrum, or if tethered moths are exposed to weak broadband radiofrequency fields (150 kHz to 60 MHz), magnetic orientation is abolished. Our results indicate that Bogong moths use the geomagnetic field as an inclination compass for long-distance navigation at night and possess a light-dependent radical-pair-based magnetic sense 5 .

items.title: Clustering constraints on super-early galaxy formation scenarios
items.abstract: The unexpectedly high abundance of bright, blue, super-early galaxies (z≳ 10) has challenged most pre-JWST models of early galaxy formation and motivated a wide range of proposed explanations. We systematically investigated whether galaxy clustering can distinguish among representative scenarios that reproduce the observed UV luminosity function. Using the Shin-Uchuu dark-matter-only simulation, we populated z≈ 11 halos with galaxies according to solutions based on the absence of dust attenuation, feedback-free bursts, bursty star formation, and primordial black hole models. For each model, we predicted the galaxy bias for flux-limited samples at different thresholds in the -20 < < -16 magnitude range. All models predict similar bias values (b≈ 7) for faint galaxies (̊m M_ i) ii) iii) iv) M_ UV ̊m UV ≈ -16), but diverge at ̊m M_ ̊m UV łesssim -18, as the underlying halo-mass to ̊m M_ ̊m UV relations differ significantly. In particular, the primordial black hole scenario predicts an almost luminosity-independent bias, whereas the other models generally predict an increasing bias with luminosity, reaching b≈ 13 for ̊m M_ ̊m UV ≈ -19. items.title: The first 3D magnetohydrodynamic core-collapse progenitors. II. Rotation, magnetic-field amplification, and magnetic topology
items.abstract: The most energetic core-collapse supernovae are thought to arise from rapidly rotating, magnetised progenitors. However, the three-dimensional pre-collapse structure of their angular momentum and magnetic fields remains poorly constrained, limiting the realism of magnetorotational core-collapse simulations. We aim to investigate the angular-momentum distribution, magnetic-field amplification and magnetic topology of physically consistent three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic pre-supernova progenitors from the stellar core to the helium shell. This second paper focuses on the rotational and magnetic properties of the models introduced in . Griffiths2026PaperI We used to evolve two compact Wolf--Rayet progenitors, computed with the stellar-evolution codes and through the final minutes before core collapse. The initial magnetic-field strengths were derived from the one-dimensional stellar-evolution prescriptions in radiative regions and then evolved self-consistently in three dimensions. Our models suggest that the rotation profile near the inner core can depart from a purely shellular distribution and reorganise itself towards a more cylindrical structure. In convective regions, hydrodynamic Reynolds stresses drive the flow towards an approximately constant specific-angular-momentum profile, corresponding to an average rotation profile close to Ω∝ ̌arpi^ -2 (̌arpi denotes the cylindrical radius). Maxwell stresses oppose this tendency but are not strong enough in our models to restore rigid rotation. Convective regions amplify seed magnetic fields, transported from neighbouring radiative layers, producing saturated fields with comparable toroidal and poloidal components and a topology containing substantial small-scale power. As a result, regions that are magnetically disconnected in the original one-dimensional stellar-evolution description become magnetically linked in the multi-dimensional models. Together with , these models represent the first three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic pre-supernova progenitors of this kind, which are suitable for subsequent collapse and explosion calculations. Griffiths2026PaperI Multi-dimensional evolution can substantially modify both the angular-momentum distribution and magnetic topology of pre-collapse progenitors. They provide a physically motivated basis for constructing more realistic initial conditions for magnetorotational core-collapse simulations and for improving prescriptions of magneto-convective angular-momentum transport in late stellar evolution.

items.title: Forward Modeling of Spectral-line Polarization for Weak Magnetic Field Imaging
items.abstract: Abstract Measurements of interplanetary magnetic fields rely mainly on spacecraft observations that provide in situ sampling and cannot directly reveal global magnetic structures. In addition, the Zeeman effect is generally too weak to image weak interplanetary magnetic fields. Here, we investigate the suitability of spectral-line polarization for spatially resolved imaging of weak magnetic fields, focusing on the Na I D lines in Mercury’s magnetosphere. We calculate the spectral-line polarization produced by anisotropic solar radiation and modified by the magnetic field orientation. Using a three-dimensional forward-imaging model of Mercury’s magnetosphere, we generate synthetic maps of Na I D–line intensity and linear polarization. The resulting polarization maps trace the large-scale magnetospheric magnetic field geometry, demonstrating the potential of Na I D–line polarimetric imaging to constrain the spatial structure of Mercury’s magnetosphere. We further show that, with a 1.8 m telescope, Na I D–line linear-polarization imaging of Mercury’s magnetosphere at a spatial resolution of 2″ is feasible with an exposure time of approximately 10 minutes.

items.title: Matrix-free inversion framework for weak lensing mass mapping and its application to DES Y3 data
items.abstract: Weak gravitational lensing mass mapping offers a direct probe of the matter distribution. Accurate reconstruction of mass maps from masked shear catalogs remains challenging due to survey boundaries and spatially varying noise. In AKRA 2.0, we addressed the mask problem on the curved sky by constructing and inverting the normal-equation matrix $\mathbf{H}\ensuremath{\equiv}{\mathbf{A}}^{\mathrm{T}}{\mathbf{N}}^{\ensuremath{-}1}\mathbf{A}$ explicitly, necessitating a split-scale strategy that reconstructed different angular scales independently to reach high resolution. Here we present AKRA 3.0, in which $\mathbf{H}$ is treated as a linear operator and the normal equations are solved by the conjugate gradient method. This reformulation reduces the memory requirement from $\mathcal{O}({N}^{2})$ to $\mathcal{O}(N)$ and the inversion cost from $\mathcal{O}({N}^{3})$ to $\mathcal{O}({N}_{\mathrm{iter}}{N}^{3/2}),N\ensuremath{\sim}{\ensuremath{\ell}}_{\mathrm{max}}^{2}$ for full-sky (SHT-based) operations. Such optimizations render high-resolution full-sky reconstruction tractable for Stage III and Stage IV surveys. Applying AKRA 3.0 to the DES Y3 METACALIBRATION catalog, we produce the highest-resolution convergence map of this dataset to date at HEALPix ${N}_{\text{nside}}=2048$ without imposing a cosmological signal prior. We validate the map reconstruction and its auto and cross-power responses using end-to-end simulations with known input fields and present a preliminary power-spectrum analysis of the DES Y3 maps. The reconstructed $E$-mode convergence map will be made publicly available to facilitate future cosmological studies.

items.title: Detecting classical nova-like explosions with LISA
items.abstract: Abstract Gravitational waves from close binary white dwarfs will form the bulk of measurements obtained by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). Previous studies have highlighted the importance of including the effects of steady-state mass transfer in waveform models as many individually resolvable white dwarf binaries will be interacting during the LISA observation window. However, few studies have considered the effect of novae on gravitational wave observations and parameter estimations. We fill in this gap by analyzing the detectability of novae in these systems and the biases in physical parameters when these bursts are not considered. We model a nova burst as a rapid loss of mass from the accretor that suddenly shifts the gravitational wave frequency. We analytically predict the signal-to-noise ratios for direct detection of the nova and where bias from mismodeling becomes greater than the statistical uncertainty. We also consider comparison of two halves of future LISA data to detect bursts in a model agnostic way. Our work has implications for identifying and classifying individual nova events as well as constraining the galactic nova rate throughout the entire galaxy, a challenging task for optical surveys.

items.title: Statistical field theory for weak gravitational lensing
items.abstract: Standard weak-lensing calculations treat lensing as a linear remapping of the matter field along the line of sight. We instead formulate lensing as a stochastic field theory for the Sachs optical scalars, driven by random Ricci-focusing and Weyl-shearing fields. With convergence and shear expressed linearly in the Sachs-scalar fluctuations, the resulting path integral generates a diagrammatic expansion for their n -point correlation functions, organized into linear response, nonlinear propagation, and driving-field cumulants. The conventional calculation emerges as the lowest-order, linear-propagation limit. Beyond it, nonlinear Sachs evolution couples to driving-field non-Gaussianity, mixing the matter cumulant hierarchy into the lensing hierarchy. A selection rule governs the couplings: an n -point observable receives a direct contribution from the n -point driving-field cumulant, and its leading hierarchy-mixing correction from the ( n + 1 )-point cumulant via one nonlinear Sachs interaction, with higher cumulants entering only at higher order. The two-point function, for instance, receives corrections from three-point cumulants of Ricci focusing and Weyl shearing through nonlinear Sachs evolution. Rather than a restrictive approximation scheme, the formalism is a paradigm shift: a unified framework naturally accommodating path corrections, higher-order matter statistics, stochasticity, and small-scale effects.

items.title: Spatiotemporal evolution of the current filamentation instability in relativistic beam-plasma systems: Higher-order spatial correction and the role of the initial seed perturbation
items.abstract: The spatio-temporal evolution of the current filamentation instability in a relativistic beam--plasma system is studied analytically and with two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations. A partial differential equation for the transverse vector potential is derived for a sharp-front relativistic beam entering cold, unmagnetized plasma, including a second-order spatial derivative term that governs the spatial growth near the beam front. The equation is solved analytically for constant, linearly growing, and oscillatory initial noise when this term is neglected, and numerically when it is included, as no closed-form solution then exists. For constant initial noise, the numerical solution reproduces the simulated magnetic-field structure, unlike the analytical solution without the term. This shows that the longitudinal field modulation is intrinsic to the instability, present even for a noise with constant amplitudes. The noise profile as well can influence the spatial-temporal evolution of the instability, which we discuss further considering linearly growing and oscillatory noise. The field grows spatially behind the beam front and saturates at a length $L_{\mathrm{sat}}\propto(v_{0b}+2)v_{0b}/γ_{0b}^{3}$, where $v_{0b}$ and $γ_{0b}$ are the beam velocity and Lorentz factor, beyond which growth is purely temporal. The saturation length increases linearly in time at a constant rate $\mathrm{d}L_{\mathrm{sat}}/\mathrm{d}τ\approx0.42\,c$, matching the analytical estimate. The temporal growth rate remains unchanged, so the term modifies the spatial transport of the instability rather than its local amplification. For beam velocities above $0.6c$, the model deviates from the simulations as oblique modes and nonlinear filament dynamics outside the single-mode treatment become important.

items.title: Non-spherical cows: Introducing the asphericity parameter as a measure of accretion geometry
items.abstract: The outer regions of galactic haloes represent the bridge connecting internal processes within the galaxy to the larger surrounding cosmic web. The gas in this bridge region is shaped by the competing processes of cold inflows from the web and hot ejecta from feedback of supernovae or an active galactic nucleus. Similarly, the gas around galaxy clusters characterizes the balance between inflows and outflows. To study this connection, we introduce a new parameter for quantifying the geometrical configuration of the flow field connecting structures to the cosmic web, the asphericity parameter. This inflow asphericity is based on a spherical harmonics decomposition of the inflow at the virial boundary of the halo. It can be computed using both the linear and the logarithmic inflow field. To validate this parameter, we apply it to both an extensive toy model set and to simulated haloes from the Magneticum simulations. We find the linear asphericity to be a tracer of the total power of the non-spherical inflow and the total anisotropy. On the other hand, the logarithmic asphericity traces the covering fraction of inflows at the surface and is highly sensitive to regions with zero inflow (regions that are dominated by outflow). Thus the asphericity of the flow field is a powerful tool to simultaneously study the geometry of in- and outflows in numerical simulations.

items.title: Hybrid Simulations of Proton Acceleration at Oblique High- β Shocks
items.abstract: Abstract Collisionless shocks in the intracluster and intergalactic media (ICM/IGM) are expected to energize both electrons and ions. While electron acceleration is revealed by prominent radio emission, γ -ray emission from hadronic interactions remains undetected, suggesting that high- β (ratio of thermal to magnetic pressure), low-Mach-number shocks cannot accelerate protons efficiently. We present three-dimensional hybrid simulations of quasi-perpendicular shocks with sonic Mach numbers M s ∼ 3.4–17.5, focusing primarily on high- β conditions representative of cluster environments and including several lower- β comparison runs. We find that weak shocks with M s ≲ 5 are consistently inefficient, with ε CR ≲ 0.1%, while inefficient cases can persist to substantially higher M s depending on M A and β . In contrast, stronger shocks ( M s ≳ 10) develop clear power-law tails with slopes q ∼ 4.0 and reach ε CR ∼ 3%. These results suggest that weak, oblique ICM shocks are generally unlikely to accelerate protons efficiently. However, reducing ϑ B n to ∼45 ∘ leads to substantially higher acceleration efficiencies, indicating that magnetic obliquity plays a critical role in determining proton acceleration. Our findings provide a microphysical framework for interpreting radio relic observations, whose polarization suggests that electrons are accelerated at oblique shocks, and the absence of cluster γ -ray detections.

items.title: Depth-reduced quantum simulation of Lindbladian dynamics via adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression
items.abstract: Abstract Quantum simulation of open quantum systems in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era is hindered by the non-unitary nature of dissipative dynamics and the limited quantum resources available on near-term quantum processors, namely restricted qubit counts and noise-limited circuit depths. In this work, we propose an efficient quantum algorithm for simulating Lindbladian dynamics on NISQ devices. For open quantum systems with Pauli dissipations, we first derive a compact and stable mixed-unitary adjoint channel that approximates the target dissipative dynamics and enables ancilla-free implementation through trajectory sampling. To further reduce the circuit depth required for implementing the sampled trajectories, we introduce an adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression framework. In this framework, a depth-adaptive parameterized quantum circuit is trained to approximate repeated Hamiltonian simulation operators, which are then used to replace repeated unitary segments appearing in the sampled trajectories. Importantly, the training procedure can also be performed without auxiliary qubits. Numerical simulations of the dissipative quantum X Y model and the interacting disordered X X Z chain demonstrate the accuracy and reduced execution gate counts of the proposed algorithm. Our results provide a practical route toward ancilla-free and depth-reduced simulation of open quantum systems on near-term quantum hardware.

items.title: Parameter estimation on LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA O4a binary merger triggers with subsolar mass components
items.abstract: The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration has reported the results for searches for sub-solar mass components in compact binary coalescence during observing run O4a. No detection candidates were identified, but the most significant seven triggers were reported. We present the results of Bayesian parameter inference on these triggers. Five of the triggers show agreement between the Bayesian parameter estimation and the search pipeline trigger. Our results show that three of the triggers may contain a possible sub-solar mass component. Parameter estimation indicates that the other two events, if real, would be neutron star - black hole binaries. The remaining two triggers do not provide informative parameter estimation. We also study three O4a compact binary coalescence triggers, and one O3 trigger, that have been noted by three other groups, and our parameter estimation indicates that three of these may contain a sub-solar mass component. We study the data quality associated with these triggers. Finally, we discuss the challenges for parameter estimation on compact binary coalescence events containing a sub-solar mass component: long signal duration, possible small chirp masses, possible small mass ratios, and data quality issues over potentially hundreds of seconds of data.

items.title: Black bounces to traversable wormholes from pure gravity in four and higher dimensions
items.abstract: Abstract This article derives generic static and spherically symmetric spacetimes --- most notably wormholes and black bounces --- as vacuum solutions of metric gravitational theories in four and higher dimensions. To this end, I extend previous results on quasi-topological gravities to encompass cases in which the metric depends on two arbitrary functions of one variable --- instead of the usual single function. I then explain how, given (almost) any spherically symmetric metric, one can reverse engineer a well-defined theory having such a metric as solution. I apply these results to three paradigmatic examples, including the Simpson--Visser black bounce, to showcase the versatility of this method, as well as its limitations. Moreover, I consider the coupling to a Vaidya-like matter source, so as to generate time-varying solutions and investigate what kind of dynamical evolution these theories can account for.

items.title: Astrophysical constraints on hadron-quark crossover in hybrid neutron stars
items.abstract: We investigate astrophysical constraints on hybrid neutron-star equations of state constructed by combining an extended linear sigma model description of quark matter with several representative hadronic equations of state through a smooth hadron-quark crossover. Four different hadronic models are examined in order to explore the model dependence of the resulting hybrid equations of state. After imposing stability, causality, perturbative QCD matching, tidal deformability, and maximum-mass constraints, only the eLSM+GMSR(BSK16) construction remains fully consistent with current astrophysical observations. The surviving parametrizations are further constrained using Bayesian inference based on NICER mass-radius measurements and the GW170817 gravitational-wave event. The posterior distributions favor a broad hadron-quark crossover occurring at relatively high baryon densities, while the formation of extended pure quark cores is strongly disfavored. Instead, the current observations favor neutron stars containing an extended mixed hadron-quark transition region. We also investigate the implications of the inferred maximum-mass distribution for the secondary object of GW190814 and find that, within the present model and adopted observational constraints, its interpretation as a neutron star is unlikely.

items.title: Dark energy in the w − c s 2 plane
items.abstract: We introduce a unified framework for dark energy diagnostics based on the joint phase space of the equation of state w and the sound speed c s 2 . This w - c s 2 plane provides a minimal extension beyond background cosmology, capturing both the expansion and perturbative properties within a single representation. Building on this, we then define the microphysical flow parameter ℱ = d c s 2 / d w , which encodes the dynamical relation between background evolution and perturbative response. We derive a direct connection between ℱ 0 (the present-day value of ℱ ), H 0 , and σ 8 . We show that the microphysical flow parameter enables a hierarchy of increasingly stringent consistency tests that significantly reduce the viable dark energy theory space. We further demonstrate how trajectories in the w - c s 2 plane distinguish models that are nearly degenerate at the level of w ( a ) , including canonical quintessence, Chaplygin gas models, and noncanonical scalar field realizations. This provides a compact phenomenological bridge between dark energy microphysics and future perturbation-sensitive observations, making ℱ 0 a useful discriminator of the kinetic structure which is underlying cosmic acceleration.

items.title: BilbyFlow : User-friendly Neural Posterior Estimation for Gravitational-wave Astronomy
items.abstract: Abstract Bayesian inference plays a central role in the new field of gravitational-wave astronomy. However, traditional Bayesian inference with stochastic samplers is computationally expensive, taking hours to days per event. Transformative changes are therefore required to enable the science of next-generation observatories whose event rates and signal-to-noise ratios will increase significantly over the current generation. Recent work has shown that neural posterior estimation (NPE) is a promising path forward. A neural net is trained to approximate the posterior distribution of gravitational-wave parameters, allowing generation of reweighted posterior samples in a fraction of the time required by stochastic samplers. In this work, we introduce BilbyFlow , which harnesses the power of NPE in the popular Bilby code suite. We use BilbyFlow to analyze a subset of 38 high-mass events from the third LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog (GWTC-3). For 29 events (76%), we obtained an importance-sampling efficiency > 1%, allowing us to produce reliable posterior distributions within 3 minutes to 1.5 hr. For the other events, with importance-sampling efficiency ≪ 1%, the runtime can be as long as 35 hr. We achieve a median importance-sampling efficiency of 7%, which is roughly comparable to the DINGO package. We aim to significantly improve this efficiency with further development to make the runtime more reliably O ( min ) . BilbyFlow is open source and pip installable.

items.title: Properties of neutron stars with hyperons within a generalized relativistic approach
items.abstract: In this work, we study the effects of $Λ$-hyperons on neutron star properties employing a generalized relativistic framework for the equation of state (EOS). Different choices for defining the hyperonic couplings with different levels of parametric freedom are discussed. In all models, the predicted NS maximum masses are reduced compared with the purely nucleonic composition as expected. In the case of relating hyperonic couplings via $SU(6)$-symmetry arguments to the nucleonic ones, we find that NS radii for intermediate mass stars are shifted to higher values compared with purely nucleonic stars, in agreement with the existing literature. However, allowing for more freedom for the hyperonic couplings, the effect is strongly reduced, and the distributions in the NS mass-radius plane of models with and without hyperons become very close. We have also investigated how different nucleonic density functionals influence the hyperon matter composition and neutron star properties.

items.title: Probing the details of relativistic electrons with multifrequency observations of M87 black hole
items.abstract: Abstract Beginning in March 2026, the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) conducted a two-month observing campaign aimed at obtaining the first time-resolved sequence of images of the black hole M87* at the center of the Virgo A galaxy. The primary objectives of this campaign are to constrain black hole spin and investigate the temporal variability of the magnetic field and plasma properties within the horizon-scale jet-launching region. In this work, we present theoretical predictions for the spectral index maps expected from these observations. Our predictions are based on Magnetically Arrested Disk simulations performed with the EBHLIGHT code and post-processed using the IPOLE general relativistic ray-tracing code. We investigate the temporal evolution of the spectral index for a range of electron distribution models and five black hole spin values. The analysis includes both frequency bands currently present within the EHT and neighboring frequencies proposed for future array extensions. In addition to extending previous studies to a broader frequency range, our work systematically investigates the time variability of the predicted spectral index maps. In purely thermal electron models, temporal variability of the spectral index maps closely traces variations in magnetic field strength and electron temperature near the event horizon. By contrast, models incorporating a non-thermal electron population exhibit weaker spectral index variability, owing to the contribution of a power-law component with a fixed spectral slope. Our numerical results are consistent with theoretical expectations. Finally, a comparison with the recently measured integrated spectral index of M87* enables us to place preliminary constraints on model parameters.

items.title: A Multimission Detection Framework for High-energy Transients: Application to a 13 yr Fermi/GBM and Swift/BAT Sample
items.abstract: Abstract The detection of faint high-energy transients is becoming increasingly important in time-domain and multimessenger astronomy, particularly for identifying electromagnetic counterparts to binary neutron star mergers, high-energy neutrino events, and other weak transient phenomena. At present, the sensitivity of gamma-ray and hard X-ray searches is often limited by the detection threshold of individual instruments, leaving a population of faint transients inaccessible to single-mission analyses. To address this limitation, we develop a joint detection framework that combines trigger information from multiple detectors and assigns each candidate a joint association probability, p joint , as a function of the individual detector signal-to-noise ratios. We apply this framework to archival Fermi/GBM and Swift/BAT rates data from 2013 to 2025. The method effectively separates coincident signals from accidental background associations, suppressing inconsistent coincidences while enhancing the significance of faint events observed by both instruments. We find that, under optimal conditions, a two-mission search can increase the accessible volume for short gamma-ray bursts by up to 60%. This framework provides a practical foundation for generalized multimission searches, enabling more sensitive exploration of the faint high-energy transient sky and improving the prospects for future multimessenger discoveries.

items.title: PEARLS: NuSTAR and XMM-Newton Extragalactic Survey of the JWST North Ecliptic Pole Time-domain Field V: Unraveling X-Ray Spectral Variability
items.abstract: Abstract As one of the first deep time-domain surveys in the hard X-ray band, the NuSTAR campaign in the JWST North Ecliptic Pole Time Domain Field (NEP-TDF) offers a prime opportunity to measure variability in a faint population of active galactic nuclei (AGN) in the medium- to high-redshift Universe. In the X-ray band, AGN variability is generally caused by changes in the brightness of the corona ( F int variability) or changes in the column density of obscuring material near the supermassive black hole (SMBH; N H variability). Broadband spectroscopy (∼0.5–24 keV) is required to reliably disentangle these two phenomena. With simultaneous NuSTAR and XMM-Newton coverage—as well as 1.8 Ms of Chandra monitoring—the X-ray surveys in the NEP-TDF are ideally situated for this purpose. This work presents the first spectral modeling of the 52 NuSTAR-identified sources discovered in the latter half of the campaign, as well as a spectroscopic variability study of the entire 112-source NuSTAR NEP-TDF catalog. Seven variable candidates are identified. We find that ≳1000 total counts split across many (≳10) epochs are needed in order to detect variability. Additionally, variable sources are compared to the survey sensitivity in order to inform population synthesis models of how variations can affect the detectability of faint AGN, which dominate the SMBH accretion history. Lastly, the timescale of N H variability is investigated as a probe for the obscurer location. Significant variability is slightly more common on >100 day timescales, suggesting that the torus may have only slight dominance in driving N H variability in faint AGN.

items.title: Exploring PSR J0901-4046 as an Ultraslowly Rotating Neutron Star versus a White Dwarf
items.abstract: Abstract The source PSR J0901-4046 shows a very long rotational period of ≈75.88 s. In fact, its long period suggests that it could be a white dwarf. We examine the properties of the source and compare the outcomes under the hypotheses of the source being a highly magnetized white dwarf (B-WD) and neutron star. We find that assuming it to be a B-WD with a surface field ∼10 10 G explains many properties, including its storage/rotational energy, in turn, explaining luminosity. On the contrary, the neutron-star-based idea, particularly if examined under the conventional spin down mechanism, requires an unusually high surface magnetic field ≳10 14 G, even exceeding 10 16 G, depending on the obliquity angle and emission mechanism. The source also sits very close to AR Sco, a white dwarf pulsar, in the period and period-derivative plane. We suggest that the source is a B-WD. Along with AR Sco, the source being a B-WD constrains the death line model. The B-WD hypothesis alleviates the necessity of an unusually high magnetic field hindering pair production for PSR J0901-4046 under the neutron star hypothesis. We argue that some rotation-powered pulsars with extreme properties may possibly be white dwarfs rather than neutron stars.

items.title: Composition-controlled cut-off-resonance coupling and polarization-selective wave propagation in a four-component magnetized plasma
items.abstract: Abstract This study deals with the propagation of circularly polarized electromagnetic waves in magnetized multicomponent plasmas composed of electrons, deuterium positive ions (D + ), hydrogen negative ions (H − ), and oxygen negative ions (O − ). Based on the cold-fluid approach combined with Maxwell’s equations, the dielectric functions of right-hand circularly polarized (RCP) and left-hand circularly polarized (LCP) waves are obtained analytically. The numerical values of the cut-off frequencies, the reflection, transmission, and absorption coefficients for a finite multicomponent plasma slab are found using electromagnetic boundary conditions. Due to the presence of two kinds of negative ions, three cut-off frequencies of the RCP waves and the propagation and stop bands related to the negative-ion and electron cyclotron resonances are found. In turn, the LCP wave has only one cut-off-controlled propagation boundary. The effects of negative-ion concentrations of hydrogen and oxygen, magnetic field strength, slab thickness, and frequency are studied. Increase in the concentration of the H − ions leads to a shift in cut-off frequencies, changes in the widths of propagation and stop bands, decrease in the gap between the RCP and LCP cut-offs, and improvement of the low-frequency transparency when both RCP and LCP modes are propagating. A remarkable effect is a tendency of the second RCP cut-off towards the H − cyclotron resonance that results in the cut-off-resonance coincidence with an enhancement in absorption of the light negative ions. The cut-off-resonance proximity produces enhanced electromagnetic absorption associated with the resonant response of the light negative-ion population, indicating enhanced wave-ion coupling. The results provide a fluid-level basis for controlling frequency-selective electromagnetic energy deposition in multicomponent plasmas and show how negative-ion composition can tune polarization-dependent propagation and electromagnetic power deposition in the present model. It can be used in plasma diagnostics, ionospheric wave propagation, plasma electromagnetic filters, tunable polarization devices, and ion-selective heating.

items.title: By Land or By Sea: Ecology in a Foreign (Scot)Land
items.abstract: Biology has taken me from studying coastal mangrove ecosystems in South Florida to surveying ancient temperate rainforests in the Scottish Highlands. In this talk, I'll share the windy path that connected those two very different worlds and the unconventional experiences that shaped my path toward a career in ecology. I'll discuss how undergraduate research opened the door to scientific discovery, why I chose to spend two years traveling across the United States after graduation before pursuing graduate school, and what ultimately led me across the Atlantic to the University of Edinburgh. Along the way, I'll introduce my current dissertation research on Scotland's Atlantic temperate rainforests, where I study how herbivore impacts influence communities of rare rainforest lichens, remarkable organisms that serve as important indicators of forest health. This presentation will focus on the many paths a career in biology can take. I'll share what it's like to conduct ecological fieldwork in Scotland, the realities of graduate school abroad, and the lessons I've learned about embracing uncertainty, seeking opportunities, and following your curiosity. Whether your interests lie on land, beneath the sea, or somewhere above or in between, I hope this talk demonstrates that the path to your goals doesn't have to be a straight line. About the presenter Joe Dubner is an MSc student in Ecology, Evolution and Biodiversity at the University of Edinburgh and an aquarist at Scotland's National Aquarium. He earned dual Bachelor of Science degrees in Biology and Marine Biology from Nova Southeastern University in 2023, where he was also a Razor's Edge Research Scholar. Through RER, he conducted undergraduate research in marine biogeochemistry under Dr. Tyler Cyronak. During his undergraduate studies, Joe served as President of the Nature Club, chaired the Sustainability Club's Climate Change Committee, and was actively involved in science outreach and environmental initiatives. After graduating, Joe spent two years traveling throughout the United States as a professional petsitter and tutor, an unconventional experience that reinforced his passion for wildlife, conservation, and exploring new environments. In 2025, he moved to Scotland to continue his education at the University of Edinburgh. His current research focuses on Atlantic temperate rainforests, investigating how herbivore impacts influence epiphytic lichen communities in Scotland's internationally important rainforest ecosystems. Joe hopes to continue to ultimately build a career as a university professor, combining ecological research, teaching, and mentorship. The path there is not a straight line, and it doesn't have to be.

items.title: Compassionate technology in teacher education: Advancing connection, care, and digital wellbeing in a digital society
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies into teacher education has transformed teaching, learning, and professional preparation worldwide. While these innovations have enhanced accessibility, personalisation, collaboration, and instructional efficiency, they have also intensified concerns regarding techno-stress, digital fatigue, emotional disengagement, ethical dilemmas, and diminished human connection. These challenges highlight the need for educational approaches that balance technological advancement with compassion, inclusion, and digital wellbeing. This conceptual paper proposes a Human-Centred Framework for Digital Wellbeing in Teacher Education, developed through a critical synthesis of contemporary literature on compassionate pedagogy, ethical AI, digital wellbeing, inclusive education, and human-centred learning. The framework comprises five interconnected dimensions: Human-Centred AI Integration, Emotional and Psychological Wellbeing, Compassionate Pedagogical Practices, Inclusive and Equitable Digital Learning, and Ethical and Mindful Technology Engagement. Collectively, these dimensions position technology as a means of strengthening empathy, meaningful relationships, equity, and sustainable learning rather than merely improving efficiency. The paper discusses implications for teacher education curricula, digital pedagogy, institutional policy, and professional learning. It argues that preparing future teachers for AI-enabled classrooms requires not only digital competence but also the capacity to create ethical, inclusive, and compassionate learning environments that promote human flourishing in an increasingly digital society.

items.title: Patterns, outcomes and predictors of severe hospital course among people in prison admitted for poisoning in northwest Iran: a retrospective analytical cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Purpose People in prison may be at heightened risk of poisoning and overdose because of substance use, psychiatric morbidity and the stresses of incarceration. This study aims to describe the demographic, toxicological and clinical characteristics of people in prison who required hospital admission for poisoning in northwest Iran. Design/methodology/approach A retrospective cross-sectional review was conducted using hospital records of all people in prison admitted to the poisoning service of Taleghani Hospital, Urmia, Iran, from 12 January 2017 to 31 December 2020. Demographic variables, poisoning agent, route and intentionality of exposure, psychiatric history, previous poisoning-related admission, intensive care unit admission, length of stay and treatment outcome were summarised descriptively. Findings The study included 276 admissions. Most patients were male (98.2%), and the mean age was 35.05 ± 10.43 years. Opioids (30.0% of recorded substances), benzodiazepines (21.0%) and stimulants (17.0%) were the leading recorded agents. Oral exposure was most common (84.1%), and 66.7% of episodes were documented as intentional. Psychiatric history was recorded in 47.8%, previous poisoning-related admission in 54.7% and ICU admission in 15.6%. Most patients were discharged (94.2%); in-hospital mortality was 2.2%. Research limitations/implications This was a single-centre retrospective study based on hospital records, which may have involved incomplete documentation and limited generalisability. The small number of deaths limited mortality-specific modelling. Findings should be interpreted as exploratory and require validation in larger multicentre studies. Practical implications The findings support structured clinical risk assessment at admission, closer monitoring of patients with decreased consciousness, supervised medication access in correctional settings and routine psychiatric and substance-use assessment after poisoning. Strengthened communication between hospitals and prison health services may help reduce recurrent poisoning and improve continuity of care. Social implications Poisoning among people in prison represents an important public health and social concern. Improving prevention, timely identification and continuity of care may help reduce avoidable harm and support better health outcomes for this vulnerable population. Originality/value This study adds regional evidence on hospital-treated poisoning among people in prison and extends the descriptive thesis data set with exploratory outcome analysis. The findings highlight the need for integrated prison mental health, substance-use, medication-safety and emergency transfer pathways.

items.title: Electrophysiological Markers in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Enhancing Sudden Cardiac Death Risk Prediction with Index of Cardiac Electrophysiological Balance and Its Corrected Variant.
items.abstract: Background Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is characterized by asymmetric left ventricular hypertrophy and myocardial fibrosis, which significantly increases the risk of sudden cardiac death (SCD). Existing risk stratification models are limited in predicting SCD risk in patients within the "gray zone"-those with intermediate risk. This study investigates the prognostic utility of the Index of Cardiac Electrophysiological Balance (ICEB) and its corrected variant (ICEBc) in predicting ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) in HCM. To evaluate the predictive value of ICEB and ICEBc for Life-Threatening Arrhythmias (LTA) and non-sustained ventricular tachycardia (NSVT) in HCM and compare their performance with traditional repolarization parameters and the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) SCD Risk Score. Methods A retrospective observational study was conducted at a single center, including 127 HCM patients categorized into 3 groups: LTA (n = 45), NSVT (n = 29), and control (n = 53). Electrocardiographic parameters, including ICEB, ICEBc, Tp-e interval, Tp-e/QTc ratio, and QRS-T angle were measured. Multiple logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of VAs. Results The ICEB and ICEBc were significantly lower in LTA and NSVT groups compared to the control group (P Conclusion The ICEB and ICEBc are robust markers of repolarization heterogeneity and effective predictors of VAs in HCM patients. Their integration into existing risk stratification models could enhance predictive accuracy, particularly for gray zone patients.

items.title: A Latent Variable Perspective on EEG Measures of Attentional Control
items.abstract: Attentional control is a core cognitive function, yet there is still a significant debate revolving around its definition, factorial structure and underlying neural mechanisms. Research in this domain has largely developed along two largely disconnected traditions. Psychometric approaches assess individual differences using latent-variable models (e.g., structural equation modeling, confirmatory factor analysis), while cognitive neuroscience focuses on group-level behavioral and neural effects. This raises a critical question: can neural measures robust at the group level validly capture stable individual differences? Or more specifically, can some of the principles and analytical methods adopted in individual-differences research be directly applied to neural correlates of attentional control? The current study aims to address this question. Electroencephalogram data were recorded from participants as they completed four attentional control paradigms: a change detection task, the go/no-go task, the Simon task, and the Stroop task. From each task, we extracted the P3 component and a data-driven decoding accuracy measure as indices of conflict processing and tested whether these neural measures load onto a common latent factor of attentional control. Results revealed weak and largely non-significant correlations. Structural-equation modeling provided no evidence for a common latent factor, despite robust within-task effects at the group level reflected both in the behavioral and the EEG parameters. These findings suggest that EEG components may lack the construct validity needed to reliably capture individual differences in attentional control.

items.title: Subtractive and Divisive Methods for Isolating Neural Oscillations From Broadband Activity Yield Different, Even Conflicting, Power Estimates
items.abstract: Understanding the role of oscillatory brain activity in cognition is a key objective in cognitive neuroscience. However, quantifying the power of narrowband neural oscillations is made challenging by the presence of non-oscillatory broadband activity in the signal. Recently, there has been a proliferation of methods designed to separate oscillatory from non-oscillatory (aperiodic) signals. To perform this separation, these methods must model the relationship between oscillatory and aperiodic components. Crucially, however, such methods rarely explicitly clarify whether they assume that this relationship is additive or multiplicative, an issue compounded by the common use of log-transformed data (i.e., subtraction in log space is equivalent to division in linear space). Here, we show the importance of justifying which assumption about component relations is applied. Using simulated power spectra with additive oscillatory and aperiodic components, we illustrate that methods that assume a multiplicative model, such as the popular specparam (formerly fooof) toolbox, systematically mis-estimate oscillatory activity in ways that can obscure real oscillatory differences between conditions, or even reverse their sign, creating an illusory effect. We then demonstrate these effects in two complementary empirical datasets: (a) a cross-sectional, between-subjects analysis of age-related differences in alpha power, showing how separation approaches impact effect size and detectability; and (b) a within-subjects analysis of pre-stimulus changes in alpha power in a detection task, showing how switching between approaches can greatly reduce the evidence for an effect, leading to different conclusions. These results highlight that researchers must explicitly report and justify assumptions about aperiodic and oscillatory signal combination, as these assumptions have implications not only for analyses of oscillatory activity and resultant conclusions, but also for integration of results across reports (which may implicitly employ different assumptions), and ultimately for the development of theories regarding electrophysiological features and their putative relations to cognition.

items.title: From Pipeline Automation to Scientific Discovery: A Multi-Layer Agent-Driven Bioinformatics Framework
items.abstract: Abstract AI-driven bioinformatics is undergoing a multi-layer evolution from script automation to autonomous scientific discovery. We present a three-layer agent-driven framework spanning this complete spectrum. Layer 1 (Foundation Validation) benchmarks three OpenClaw agents—DESeq2 differential expression, GO/KEGG enrichment, and variant calling—against standard pipelines on TCGA liver cancer and E. coli genomic data, achieving near-perfect padj correlation (r ~ 1.0), >90% pathway overlap, and 95.8% variant concordance. Layer 2 (Domain Tool) presents CRISPR Agent, a multi-layer pipeline integrating Cas-OFFinder candidate discovery, multi-backend off-target scoring (mm_only/CFD/MIT), genomic context annotation, and end-to-end report synthesis, validated on GUIDE-seq/CIRCLE-seq/CHANGE-seq benchmarks. Layer 3 (Scientific Discovery) introduces SciOS, a ten-agent autonomous discovery system governed by a five-gate FORUM review chain (Plan-Execute-Audit-Synthesize-Ratify). Deployed across three single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets (457,000 cells, 154,000 spatial spots), SciOS produced three findings: (i) effector genes encoding ion channels, synaptic adhesion, and axon guidance proteins are significantly more conserved across cortical regions than transcription factor identity genes (P = 1.2 x 10^-16, d = 1.27)—a genuinely novel discovery inverting the standard neuroscience hierarchy; (ii) APOE expression is spatially coupled to oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (r = 0.673) but not mature oligodendrocytes (r = 0.136) in the human entorhinal cortex; and (iii) independent pseudobulk validation of CALB1/SOX6 dopamine neuron depletion in Parkinson's disease. The framework's Critic agent mandated average confidence reductions of -0.06 across all claims, while a Literature agent corrected a directional error introduced by autonomous analysis without domain context. These three layers collectively define an evolution from "doing" to "designing" to "discovering," establishing a methodological foundation for fully autonomous scientific discovery systems.

items.title: Adolescent social isolation and re-socialization increases alcohol intake and aversion-resistant drinking in male and female rats.
items.abstract: Rationale Adverse experiences during adolescence, especially social isolation, increases risk for alcohol use disorders (AUDs). Previous rodent studies of adolescent social isolation (ASI) encompassed all stages of adolescence and/or maintained isolation into adulthood, limiting identification of vulnerable stages of adolescence. Utilizing males only, or combining the sexes, also may have contributed to contradictory findings. Objectives Investigate social isolation restricted to discrete adolescent stages in combination with re-socialization and then persistent alcohol drinking. Determine whether adolescent isolation during specific developmental time periods, with or without subsequent re-socialization, leads to increased alcohol drinking in males or females. Methods Male and female Wistar rats underwent one of six housing conditions: (1) isolation from postnatal day (P)21-42 followed by re-socialization (ASIR-Early), (2) isolation from P42-63 followed by re-socialization (ASIR-Late), or (3) continuous isolation from P21 onward (ASI), or (4​-6) one of three appropriate control treatments. Alcohol-related behaviors were assessed in adulthood using intermittent-access two-bottle choice drinking (IAP), limited daily access (LDA-20) procedures, quinine-adulterated aversion-resistant drinking (ARD), and alcohol re-exposure following prolonged abstinence. Results In general, ASIR-Early and ASI elevated alcohol drinking in males and females, when compared to contemporary controls, during IAP, LDA-20, ARD, and after prolonged withdrawal, while ASIR-Late had largely similar effects as control conditions. However, for females, only ASI led to greater ARD at the highest quinine dose and also increased alcohol drinking after prolonged withdrawal. In contrast, for males, ASIR-Early and ASI had largely similar enhancement of alcohol drinking. Conclusions Under these conditions, isolation housing that encompassed the early adolescent period produced enduring increases in alcohol-related behaviors, with re-socialization perhaps more protective in females against ARD and elevated intake after abstinence. These results inform future studies that will investigate neural mechanisms underlying ASI-induced enhancement of alcohol drinking.

items.title: Pediatric nondysraphic intramedullary spinal cord lipomas: surgical burden, reoperations, and long-term outcomes.
items.abstract: Objective Spinal cord lipomas without spinal dysraphism are rare tumors but can cause substantial neurological deficits. Resection is particularly challenging owing to tight tumor-cord interface and there is no clear consensus regarding the management in the pediatric population. Therefore, we review our experience treating a cohort of pediatric patients with intramedullary lipomas. Methods A database of pediatric patients surgically treated for intramedullary spinal cord tumors at a large comprehensive cancer center and affiliated children's hospital was reviewed between 2012 and 2025. Cases with a confirmed histology of lipoma were included. Demographic, surgical, and outcome data were collected. Results Seven patients were identified with spinal cord lipomas, with a median age of 9 years. All tumors spanned the cervical cord. Symptoms included pain, paresthesias, numbness, weakness, and bowel/bladder dysfunction. Five patients required repeat surgeries for hardware failure, repeat debulking, cerebrospinal fluid leak, and scoliosis repair. Two patients had long-term tumor progression. Conclusions Surgical decision-making in pediatric intramedullary lipomas needs to balance maximal safe resection with the risk of iatrogenic deficits. Patients should be counseled about the significant risks and need for lifelong monitoring. In our series, reoperations were frequent and included both disease-related (repeat debulking/detethering) and treatment-related (CSF leak, deformity, and hardware complications). Early intervention before patients develop debilitating symptoms may help maximize long-term neurological outcomes.

items.title: Competition Indices and Environmental Variables Weakly Improve Predictions of Natural Population Fluctuations on Independent Data
items.abstract: The debate about the relative importance of interspecific competition and environmental factors in annual population fluctuations has persisted in ecology for many decades. Ecologists face the challenge of determining the extent to which interspecific competition and environmental factors impact population growth rates. We assess the predictive ability of models with and without interspecific competition and environmental covariates to predict population size one year beyond the model-building data. For 11 of 14 datasets a model with interspecific competition and/or environmental factors make better mean ‘absolute’ prediction error. However, none of the models with interspecific competition and/or environmental variables make predictions that are statistically significantly superior to the random walk model. Overall, in about 60% of the sites, models with interspecific competition and environmental variables show performance worse than the random walk baseline model on independent data. We conclude that there is weak evidence that incorporating interspecific competition and/or environmental covariates leads to improved model predictive ability. A thorough assessment of the relative importance of interspecific competition and environmental factors in annual population fluctuations will require evaluating the predictive power of a broader range of models that incorporate ecology of species traits at each generational time.

items.title: Spatial distribution and uncertainty assessment of heavy metals in coastal groundwater of northern Hainan Island using sequential Gaussian simulation.
items.abstract: Heavy metal contamination in coastal aquifers has attracted increasing attention, yet probabilistic characterization of spatial uncertainty remains limited. This study investigated the coastal aquifer of northern Hainan Island using 315 sampling locations. Sequential Gaussian simulation (SGS) was applied to characterize the spatial heterogeneity, prediction uncertainty, and threshold exceedance probabilities of Fe, Mn, As, and Pb, and was compared with ordinary kriging (OK). Mean concentrations followed the order Fe > Mn > As > Pb. Mn had the highest exceedance percentage among the measured samples (26.35%), followed by Fe (2.54%), As (1.59%), and Pb (1.59%). Spatially, Mn and Pb concentrations generally increased from coastal to inland areas. Mn formed an extensive high-concentration zone in the central-southern region, whereas As formed a relatively continuous high-concentration belt along the northern coast. OK and SGS produced highly consistent regional trends, but SGS better preserved local spatial variability and reduced the smoothing effect of OK. The SGS simulation standard deviations showed that uncertainty for Mn was concentrated in the southern region, whereas high uncertainty for As occurred in the northeastern coastal area. Threshold exceedance probability analysis identified a continuous high-risk belt for Mn in the southern region, where probabilities exceeded 0.6 and locally approached 1.0. Mn was therefore the contaminant requiring the highest management priority. Overall, SGS extends conventional concentration interpolation into a probabilistic risk-zoning approach and supports refined identification and management of heavy metal contamination risks in coastal groundwater.

items.title: No effect of post-meiotic sperm aging on male fertility in a species with finite sperm production.
items.abstract: Post-meiotic sperm aging occurs when mature sperm cells are stored in the male reproductive tract before mating. In most species, males produce sperm throughout their life, thereby partially mitigating sperm aging by replenishing their sperm supply. By contrast, sperm production is finite in some species, preventing aging sperm to be replaced by new gametes. Finite sperm production is therefore predicted to impose strong selective pressure to minimize post-meiotic sperm aging. In this study, we tested this prediction by investigating post-meiotic sperm aging in a species with finite sperm production and pre-mating sperm storage in males, the buff-tailed bumblebee (Bombus terrestris). We adopted an integrative multi-level approach combining high-throughput flow cytometry, dual-type DNA methylation profiling, and untargeted proteomics. We identified molecular and cellular hallmarks of aging in sperm cells during male storage, including reduced sperm viability, elevated oxidative stress, increased DNA damage, and altered DNA methylation and proteomic profiles. However, these changes were modest in magnitude. Accordingly, neither male fertility nor reproductive fitness declined with age: males (hence, sperm) of different ages achieved similar mating success and sired colonies that did not differ in foundation success, productivity, composition, or lifespan, indicating that post-meiotic sperm aging has no significant impact on male reproductive performance. Together, our results support the prediction that finite sperm production is associated with limited post-meiotic sperm aging. More broadly, they challenge the assumption that advancing paternal age inevitably compromises reproductive function and highlight the importance of life history in shaping reproductive aging.

items.title: The Curse of Dimensionality: How Does it Affect Dynamical Systems Research in Clinical Psychology?
items.abstract: The dynamical systems approach is gaining attention across many subfields of clinical psychology. Although the systems are assumed to involve many variables, theoretical and methodological work in this field often relies on low-dimensional stability landscapes, creating potential mismatches. In this article, I discuss how high-dimensional stability landscapes may challenge intuitions derived from low-dimensional landscapes, put forward a potential solution based on sufficient low-dimensional descriptions, and propose a future research agenda centered on dimensionality reduction approaches that emphasize preserving information about stability and transitions.

items.title: Estimating the replicability of psychology experiments after an initial failure to replicate
items.abstract: When a replication fails, scientists have to decide whether to make a second attempt or move on.Psychology researchers who attempt to replicate studies often face this decision, given the empiricalrate of replication success in psychology, which is lower than desired. Here, we report 17 re-replicationsof experiments for which an original replication had failed. In 5/17 of these “rescue” projects (29%),the “rescue” study mostly or fully replicated the original results, albeit with a smaller effect size;in the other 12, the second replication was also judged to have failed. We speculate that successfulrescue projects were due to larger sample sizes or methodological changes such as attention checks. Inthe absence of obvious weaknesses in a failed replication study’s sample or procedure, however, it maybe most efficient to stop pursuing an effect after a single failed replication.

items.title: Recipient-Focused Hallucinations in AI-Generated Professor Outreach Emails: A Pilot Factorial Evaluation of Grounding and Verification
items.abstract: Abstract Background : LLMs increasingly draft personalized academic outreach, which depends on describing a real professor's research. Unsupported claims about a recipient's topics, methods, or findings misrepresent their scholarly work. Methods : In an offline pilot, a 2 × 2 design varied whether the writer received a publication evidence packet during drafting and whether a verifier revised the draft afterwards (conditions A–D). We generated 96 emails for 12 professors across three fields, decomposed them into 360 atomic research claims, and labelled each against the professor's evidence packet with an automatic (LLM) evaluator. All primary estimates are pilot estimates from automatic labels, not human-verified measurements. Reliability was assessed against a blinded 36-claim human-labeled subset (10% of claims) and a second automatic evaluator from a third model family. Results : Under the primary evaluator, the closed-book baseline (A) had a Severe Error Rate (SER) of 0.344 (21/61 claims; exact 95% CI 0.227–0.477). Grounding the writer (B) produced no severe errors in 90 judged claims (0.000, CI 0.000–0.040) and raised Supported Personalization Density (SPD) from 0.65 to 1.71 supported claims per 100 words. Verify-only (C) left 1 severe error in 50 claims (0.020; SPD 1.04); grounded-plus-verified (D) produced none (0/87) at the highest specificity (1.76). Interpretation and limits: Primary-evaluator agreement with the human annotator was only fair (Cohen’s κ = 0.33, CI 0.16–0.49). The evaluator was too lenient in 14 of 16 disagreements, suggesting that the automatic severe-error rates may underestimate error prevalence. However, the small human-labelled subset does not establish the magnitude or direction of bias across the complete dataset. The zeros are evaluator-specific: a second evaluator relabelling the same claims found 10 severe errors in B and 4 in D, closed-book 0.455 - a large reduction under grounding, not elimination. And 17 of the 21 closed-book severe errors came from the four psychology professors; excluding that field, closed-book SER falls to 0.095. Both automatic evaluators reported lower pooled severe-error rates for grounded conditions than for ungrounded conditions. Grounding during drafting also showed a lower observed pooled SER than post-generation verification alone. Conclusion : Verified publication evidence sharply reduced severe misrepresentation - to zero under the primary evaluator, roughly four-fold under the second - while making emails more specific, and outperformed correcting drafts afterwards. Grounding, not correction alone, is the more promising safeguard; establishing the effect size needs human labelling at scale and a validated judge.

items.title: Behavior–emotion decoupling as micro-level spatial injustice: Why urban villages morphology fails to heal marginalised groups in China
items.abstract: Abstract Urban villages host tens of millions of rural-to-urban migrants in Chinese cities, yet their dense, fragmented morphology is widely assumed to erode residents' mental health (Wu, 2016). Drawing on spatial justice theory and environmental psychology, this study asks whether urban villages morphology shapes healing environments differently for marginalised groups versus indigenous residents.Using Kuidong Village (Xuzhou, China) as a case study, we integrate Baidu POI and heatmap data, SegNet-based street view segmentation, behavioral observation, and a seven-dimension emotion survey (N = 162) into a multi-group mediation framework linking spatial configuration, daily behavior, and emotional perception. We identify systematic behavior–emotion decoupling among migrants: their activity patterns respond to spatial form, yet no behavior produces emotional returns. All three mediation pathways (enclosure via necessity to depression, greenery via spontaneity to safety, and permeability via sociality to relaxation) fail for migrants while remaining significant for indigenous residents. Healing resources thereby remain visible yet unusable. We interpret this decoupling as a form of micro-level spatial injustice, extending spatial justice theory from the macro distribution of resources to micro psychological pathways. We accordingly propose differentiated spatial interventions to restore migrants' behavior–emotion linkage, transforming urban villages from mere dwelling spaces into healing places.

items.title: Sensitivity to Physical Activity Predicts Daily Physical Activity Levels in People with Chronic Musculoskeletal Pain.
items.abstract: Objective This study investigated whether Sensitivity to Physical Activity (SPA, a measure of changes in pain responses to standardized physical tasks) predicts self-report and objective physical activity levels in individuals with chronic musculoskeletal (MSK) pain. We also examined whether SPA offers predictive value in activity levels beyond psychological factors and quantitative sensory testing (QST). Methods Sixty-one participants with chronic MSK pain completed a standardized SPA lifting task, psychological questionnaires (Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia, Pain Catastrophizing Scale), and QST (pressure pain thresholds, temporal summation of pain). Participants wore an accelerometer for up to nine days to objectively measure physical activity. Self-reported activity was assessed using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire. Hierarchical regression analyses were conducted to evaluate the predictive value of SPA, psychological, and QST measures on physical activity outcomes. Results SPA significantly predicted objectively measured daily physical activity levels, explaining unique variance in both average daily steps (ΔR²=11.6%, P=0.005) and time spent performing moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (ΔR²=6.1%, P=0.030), after controlling for age and pain levels. SPA was not associated with self-reported physical activity. Neither psychological factors nor QST measures significantly predicted objective or subjective activity levels. Discussion Lifting-based SPA emerged as a unique predictor of real-world physical activity in individuals with chronic MSK pain, outperforming traditional psychological and sensory predictors. These findings support the potential of SPA as a biopsychosocial marker for physical inactivity and the importance of objective activity monitoring in rehabilitation planning.

items.title: Gender differences regarding body image-related aspects in the general population during the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted daily routines, physical activity, eating behaviors, and social interactions, all of which may have influenced body image. Previous research suggests that body image concerns differ by gender and may be particularly pronounced among sexual and gender minority (SGM) individuals, who face unique challenges due to internalized appearance ideals and societal stigma. This systematic review examined gender differences in body image-related concerns in the general adult population during the pandemic. Supported by: German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (01KX2121). Methods This systematic review was preregistered (PROSPERO CRD42023421727) and conducted according to PRESS, PRISMA guidelines. Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, PsycINFO were searched for original studies published January 2019-July 2024. Studies were eligible if they 1) examined body image-related outcomes during the COVID-19 pandemic and reported gender-specific analyses in non-clinical adult populations. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross-Sectional Studies. Studies were narratively summarized according to body image-related constructs assessed and the reported gender-specific findings. Results Sixteen studies comprising 9,813 participants were included. Across most studies, women reported greater body dissatisfaction, weight and shape concerns, body shame and guilt, and dysmorphic concerns than men. Men generally reported lower body dissatisfaction and higher body satisfaction and were more likely to perceive their bodies as slimmer or more athletic. However, three studies found no significant gender differences, and one study reported higher body dissatisfaction among men. Longitudinal evidence suggested increases in body dissatisfaction among men over the course of the pandemic, whereas weight concerns decreased among women over time. One study found higher levels of weight- and body-related shame and guilt among gender minority participants compared with cisgender men, while another study reported no association between sexual orientation and body appreciation. Conclusions Women generally reported greater body image-related concerns than men during the COVID-19 pandemic, although findings were not entirely consistent across studies. Evidence regarding SGM individuals remains limited due to their underrepresentation in the literature. Additional longitudinal and gender diverse research is needed to better understand body image changes during public health crises and to inform targeted prevention and intervention.

items.title: Estimating the replicability of psychology experiments after an initial failure to replicate
items.abstract: When a replication fails, scientists have to decide whether to make a second attempt or move on.Psychology researchers who attempt to replicate studies often face this decision, given the empiricalrate of replication success in psychology, which is lower than desired. Here, we report 17 re-replicationsof experiments for which an original replication had failed. In 5/17 of these “rescue” projects (29%),the “rescue” study mostly or fully replicated the original results, albeit with a smaller effect size;in the other 12, the second replication was also judged to have failed. We speculate that successfulrescue projects were due to larger sample sizes or methodological changes such as attention checks. Inthe absence of obvious weaknesses in a failed replication study’s sample or procedure, however, it maybe most efficient to stop pursuing an effect after a single failed replication.

items.title: Prevalence and associated risk factors of malaria in Ethiopia: An umbrella review
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Malaria is a major public health problem globally, particularly in Africa. Ethiopia is among the sub-Saharan African countries where malaria is a major cause of morbidity and mortality. Therefore, comprehensive evidence on the pooled prevalence of malaria had a valuable role in minimizing its burden. Objective: This review aimed to assess the nationwide prevalence and associated risk factors of malaria. Methods: Potential papers were searched systematically in Web of Science, PubMed, Science Direct databases, and Google Scholar search engine. A total of eleven relevant articles on prevalence and associated factors of malaria were identified for final umbrella review. Microsoft Excel with separate sheets for prevalence and associated factors of malaria were used to extract data. Extracted data was analyzed using STATA software version 17.0. A sensitivity analysis was performed to determine the role of each study in the final findings. The presence of publication bias was assessed by using Egger’s test and funnel plot. Trim and fill analysis was implemented to obtain a bias-adjusted effect estimate. Heterogeneity across studies was checked by Inverse of variance statistics; if I 2 value ≥50%, significant heterogeneity was considered and subgroup analysis was implemented. Results: A total of 45,597 studies were identified by the systematic search. Among these articles 11 studies were included for this umbrella review. The pooled prevalence of malaria in this review was 14.93 % (95% CI: 9.88-19.99). In addition, the pooled prevalence of P. falciparum and P. vivax were 17.79 % (95% CI: 0.93-34.95) and 9.68 % (95% CI: 1.44-17.91), respectively. The subgroup analysis based on number of studies (P=0.00) and number of sample size (P=0.01) showed significant differences in the pooled prevalence of malaria. On the other hand, the subgroup analysis based on number of sample size showed significant differences in the pooled prevalence of P. vivax (P=0.04). Among the associated risk factors, the use of insecticide-treated bed nets, indoor residual spraying, stagnant water, health education, staying outside at night, and mosquito breeding places were all statistically significant risk variables for the incidence of malaria. Conclusions: This umbrella review showed that malaria is prevalent in Ethiopia. The observed rise in malaria prevalence highlights the need for improved infection control techniques and surveillance systems for reducing malaria burden and transmission in Ethiopia. Furthermore, joint efforts at the local and national levels are needed to address the factors that contribute to malaria and reduce its impact on public health.

items.title: Burden and Trends of Antimicrobial Resistance Among Major Clinical Bacterial Pathogens in Bangladesh (2019–2024): A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a severe global public health threat, particularly in low- and middle-income countries like Bangladesh, where factors such as unregulated antibiotic use, weak surveillance, and inadequate healthcare infrastructure exacerbate the problem. A unified, up-to-date assessment of recent resistance trends is crucial to guide effective public health interventions and optimize clinical decision-making. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the prevalence and antimicrobial resistance patterns of major clinical bacterial pathogens in Bangladesh between 2019 and 2024. The analysis followed PRISMA guidelines, with data sourced from PubMed, Google Scholar, ResearchGate, and DOAJ. A random-effects model was employed to synthesize data from 30 eligible studies encompassing over 270,000 clinical specimens, providing estimates for the pooled prevalence and resistance patterns of eight major bacterial pathogens. Median resistance (MR) and interquartile ranges (IQR) were also calculated to determine resistance levels for each pathogen–antibiotic pair. The findings revealed that Gram-negative bacteria were most prevalent, with Escherichia coli (12%), Klebsiella spp. (8%), and Pseudomonas spp. (7%) as the most common pathogens. Alarmingly high antibiotic resistance rates were observed across all species, particularly in Enterococcus spp. (70%), Pseudomonas spp. (56%), Acinetobacter spp. (53%), E. coli (46%), Proteus spp. (44%), Staphylococcus aureus (43%), Klebsiella spp. (41%), and Enterobacter spp. (40%). Resistance was notably high for conventional antibiotics such as β-lactams, cephalosporins, and fluoroquinolones, while concerning levels of resistance were also detected against last-resort antibiotics including carbapenems, colistin, and certain aminoglycosides. These findings highlight the urgent need for national antimicrobial stewardship programs, enhanced surveillance, and coordinated public health strategies to mitigate the escalating threat of AMR.

items.title: Prospective integration of Physician Associates into primary care in India: a multistakeholder qualitative study
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Physician Associates (PAs) in India have worked mainly in specialty hospitals. The 2025 national competency-based PA curriculum gives greater weight to community and primary care, but little is known about how the people who would supervise, employ or fund PAs decide where a PA post is justified. We aimed to explore how stakeholders view the integration of PAs into primary care in India. Methods: We conducted 23 semi-structured interviews between July and August 2026 with purposively recruited stakeholders in policy and regulation, PA education and practice, clinical and health-system leadership, and public health and workforce organisation. We used reflexive thematic analysis, followed by cross-stakeholder interpretation and a secondary reading informed by the updated Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research. Results: Participants described how PAs could contribute to initial assessment, communication, referral and follow-up. They judged a specific post by six conditions: (1) an improvement to the patient pathway, not only redistributed tasks; (2) workable clinical accountability; (3) acceptance negotiated with colleagues and patients; (4) fit with local staffing and need; (5) readiness shown in placements and assessment; and (6) funded posts with career progression. Views differed by service setting and by the decision being considered, and we did not identify a consistent split by occupation. Only one participant had direct experience of a PA in primary care; most accounts were prospective. Conclusions: Stakeholders saw a PA’s possible clinical usefulness as separate from the case for creating a particular post. Before a post is created, planners, educators and employers can check six things: whether it would improve a defined patient pathway, how it compares with other staffing options, whether delegated care is accountable, whether the role is understood, whether graduates are ready, and whether the post can be funded and sustained. These findings can guide service evaluation. They do not show whether PAs are effective.
