items.title: Public Acceptability of Self-Payment for Community Pharmacists' Services: A National Online Survey
items.abstract: Background: The traditional business model for sustaining United States (U.S.) community pharmacies has relied on income generated by product sales. A fee-for-service model could help alleviate insufficient profit by monetizing conventionally free pharmacy services if patients are willing to pay out-of-pocket. Objectives This study evaluated public acceptability of out-of-pocket payment for community pharmacist-provided services, variation in payment acceptability across services, and assessed whether payment acceptability differed by respondent characteristics and trust constructs. Methods This study represents a cross-sectional online survey of U.S. adults conducted during spring 2026 using a non-probability sampling approach. Primary outcomes were binary stated payment-acceptability judgments for a variety of pharmacist and health services. The survey used a between-subjects randomized payment-framing design, where participants were assigned to either a stated-price condition or an any-payment condition. Secondary outcomes included trust designations and participant demographic characteristics. Results A total of 1069 respondents completed the survey. A $20 fee was viewed more favorably than a general "any amount of money" fee. In the $20 stated-price condition, agreement was highest for osteoporosis screening (75.8%) and travel-related vaccines (69.0%), and lowest for antibiotic use consultation (23.9%) and wound care (32.1%). Older respondents and Hispanic respondents were less likely to view payment as acceptable, whereas men and respondents with greater pharmacist trust were more likely to view payment as acceptable. Conclusion Although patients historically have received many community pharmacy services at no cost, this study demonstrates that the concept of self-payment ifor certain services is considered acceptable, especially for services not typically provided.

items.title: Improving respiratory virus forecasts by capturing the effects of school holidays, public holidays and seasonal changes in transmission
items.abstract: Respiratory viruses impose a substantial burden of morbidity and mortality globally, and models that forecast this burden are widely used to support public health decision-making. However, the public health utility of these forecasts can be limited by poor predictive accuracy. In this work, we show how capturing the effects of school holidays, public holidays and seasonal changes in transmission can improve respiratory virus forecasting performance. We construct a Bayesian renewal model where the effective reproduction number R(t) is composed of log-additive components including school and public holiday effects and an annually-periodic Gaussian process. The model also allows for the relative rate of reporting to vary with school and public holidays. We use this model to forecast respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza and SARS-CoV-2 case incidence across a 28-day horizon over five jurisdictions in Australia. Applied to the 2025 winter season, our forecasts outperform a random-walk baseline forecast across all settings. We find that the inclusion of holiday and seasonal transmission effects improved forecasting performance across the three pathogens. We show that the school holidays are associated with population-wide reductions in R(t) on the order of 5-15% but are generally not associated with changes in reporting. Collectively, our results provide support for the inclusion of holiday and seasonal effects in future respiratory virus forecasting models.

items.title: Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis Rates Among High-Risk Populations in Brazil: An Analysis from 2001 to 2021
items.abstract: Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR-TB) represents a global public health threat, with a rising prevalence, particularly among vulnerable populations. This cross-sectional study analyzed MDR-TB notifications in Brazil from 2001 to 2021, using data from DATASUS, and stratified by periods and risk groups (HIV-positive individuals, smokers, drug users, healthcare workers, incarcerated individuals, and people experiencing homelessness). Descriptive analyses and parametric statistical tests (ANOVA and Tukey, p less than 0.05) were applied. A significant increase in cases was observed across all groups, especially between 2017 and 2021, with growth ranging from 294% to 574% depending on the population. Factors such as treatment abandonment, coinfection, social vulnerability, and occupational exposure were key determinants for MDR-TB dissemination. The findings indicate that current public health policies are insufficient, highlighting the urgent need for targeted prevention strategies, therapeutic follow-up, and control measures for high-risk populations.

items.title: Prevalence and Trends of Unmet Need for Family Planning in West Africa: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Background Unmet need for family planning remains a major public health challenge in West Africa, where low contraceptive use continues to contribute to unintended pregnancies and adverse reproductive health outcomes. Although several country-specific studies have been conducted, evidence remains fragmented, limiting regional estimates and informed policy decisions. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of unmet need for family planning, including unmet need for spacing and limiting, and to explore country-level variations across West Africa. Methods This systematic review and meta-analysis followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261361984). PubMed, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies published between 2000 and 2025. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed study quality using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using random effect model with Freeman–Tukey transformation. Heterogeneity was quantified with I² statistics, and sensitivity analyses were performed. Due to limited studies, spacing and limiting unmet need were synthesized descriptively. Results Eleven studies involving 51,991 women met the inclusion criteria. The pooled prevalence of unmet need for family planning in West Africa was 41.1% (95% CI: 30.5–52.1%; I² = 99.6%). Country-specific prevalence was highest in Benin (47.0%), followed by Ghana (34.5%). Six studies (n = 8,327) reported unmet need for spacing and limiting, with pooled prevalence estimates of 19.2% and 13.9%, respectively. Ghana recorded the highest prevalence of both unmet need for spacing (19.6%) and limiting (16.0%). Unmet need for spacing increased after 2016, while unmet need for limiting demonstrated fluctuating but generally increasing trends. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the findings, and no evidence of publication bias was observed. Conclusions Unmet need for family planning remains a significant reproductive health challenge across West Africa, with substantial variation between countries and a predominance of unmet need for spacing. These findings emphasize the need for sustained context-specific strategies to improve equitable access to family planning services and support progress toward improved reproductive health outcomes in the region.

items.title: Comparing Countries Is Not Following Them: When Can a Cross-National Well-Being Decomposition Describe Change?
items.abstract: Abstract Subjective well-being is increasingly proposed as a headline indicator for tracking progress. The World Happiness Report divides each country's life evaluation into parts attributed to six factors, using coefficients estimated across countries, and the parts are often read as explaining why a country's well-being has changed. This paper asks when that reading is justified and states three conditions. The factors must relate to life evaluation within countries as they do between them (structural equivalence), the relationships must be stable over time (temporal invariance), and the published series must come from one model and one set of data throughout (measurement continuity). A probe with the report's public files for 2019 to 2025 shows that the third condition fails by construction. Each year of the published series comes from a different edition, with its own coefficients, benchmarks and data sources, and the income and health series break between editions. Rebuilt on one set of coefficients and consistent income and life expectancy data, the series shows within-country slopes for income and social support at least as large as their pooled cross-country slopes, although the income difference is not statistically significant, while the within-country slope for freedom is a quarter to a third of the pooled slope. Within-country slopes also differ between the two halves of the period. The decomposition is a defensible account of differences between countries but, as published, not an account of change. The paper proposes reporting practices, including for progress dashboards, that would support a dynamic reading.

items.title: Geographic heterogeneity of recorded public diabetes care in Paraguay: a nationwide ecological study with Bayesian spatial analysis across harmonised administrative areas, 2023–2025
items.abstract: Abstract Background Routine administrative records are increasingly mapped for health surveillance, but boundary changes, population composition and place-of-care attribution complicate interpretation. We examined the geography of recorded public diabetes care in Paraguay and the contribution of demographic standardisation, spatial dependence statistics, Bayesian disease mapping and cluster detection. Methods Nationwide ecological analysis of annual counts of people attended for diabetes (ICD-10 E10–E14) in outpatient services of the Ministry of Public Health, 2023–2025. The 263 current districts were aggregated to 246 polygons of the 2012 open cartography. Expected counts were indirectly standardised for sex and age with district projections and the 2022 census; crude normalisation was a sensitivity analysis. We applied empirical Bayes Moran statistics, Kulldorff's scan statistic and BYM2 models, including a referral-hospital adjustment. Results We analysed 510,221 records (26.7 per 1000 population annually); from 15 years of age, rates in women were 1.6–1.9 times those in men. Standardisation changed expected counts by factors of 0.68–1.94 and reduced the empirical Bayes Moran's I from 0.39 to 0.11 (p = 0.005); one local Moran cluster remained after false discovery rate control. The BYM2 latent standard deviation was 0.47 (95% credible interval 0.42–0.55) and the spatial mixing parameter 0.56 (0.21–0.86). Fifty-seven areas, mainly in the south-centre of the Eastern Region and often departmental capitals, had a posterior probability ≥ 0.80 of a standardised ratio above 1.25, and 64, notably in the Chaco, along the Brazilian border and around Asunción, of a ratio below 0.80. Areas with a referral hospital had higher recorded use (relative ratio 1.42; 1.21–1.64), but adjustment changed the pattern little. Annual rankings were stable (Spearman 0.77–0.88). Every candidate scan cluster reached the minimum Monte Carlo p-value. Conclusions Recorded public diabetes care in Paraguay is geographically heterogeneous, but much of the regional structure of crude rates reflects population sex and age composition. Because events are attributed to the place of care, standardised patterns describe service activity, not prevalence, coverage or unmet need. Demographic standardisation should precede spatial inference on routine data; with large counts, Bayesian models add uncertainty-based classification more than smoothing, and scan p-values discriminate poorly.

items.title: GS-ECG: a generalist–specialist approach to structural heart disease prediction from electrocardiograms
items.abstract: Abstract Structural heart disease (SHD) often goes undiagnosed, and echocardiography, the standard test, cannot be offered to every patient promptly. AI analysis of routine electrocardiograms (ECGs) could help prioritize who is scanned first. ECG foundation models promise broad applicability across ECG tasks, but SHD abnormalities are novel targets, defined by echocardiography and outside the labels on which these models were pretrained, so how best to use them is unclear. Rather than adapting the foundation model to these targets, we propose GS-ECG, a synergistic generalist–specialist approach that keeps it frozen and pairs it with a compact specialist, DGRNet, trained on novel SHD targets. In this setup, the generalist summarizes each recording in long-context features, while DGRNet focuses on SHD-specific waveform morphology at beat-level resolution, with a receptive field of about two cardiac cycles per feature. We evaluated GS-ECG in two health systems: MIMIC-IV-Ext-SHD (49,229 patients), a new public benchmark, and the EchoNext-Mini Dataset (36,286 patients). Full fine-tuning of the foundation model improved mean AUPRC by only 1.3–3.6% over freezing it, whereas DGRNet alone exceeded fine-tuning by 6.1–6.4%. Combining the frozen generalist with DGRNet in GS-ECG performed best, exceeding fine-tuning by 8.1% in both datasets while training 4.9% as many parameters; its composite SHD AUROC was 0.825 and 0.839. Against the published EchoNext-Mini Model on its own dataset, GS-ECG found 17–25% more patients with aortic stenosis, mitral regurgitation or tricuspid regurgitation among the top 5% ranked for echocardiography. Pairing frozen foundation models with purpose-built specialists offers an efficient route to clinical targets that lie beyond pretraining labels.

items.title: Community-Partnered Research to Improve Newborn Screening Awareness and Follow-up in a High-Infant-Mortality Setting.
items.abstract: Newborn screening (NBS) is a public health program that tests infants for rare but treatable congenital, metabolic, and genetic disorders shortly after birth, creating an opportunity for early intervention that can prevent death and reduce long-term morbidity. Although NBS is often framed as a health equity success, research has shown persistent disparities in the timeliness of diagnosis and treatment following abnormal results. This concern is especially urgent in Cleveland, Ohio, where infant mortality rates exceed state and national benchmarks. In partnership with First Year Cleveland, an organization dedicated to lowering infant mortality rates, we launched a community-partnered pilot. Our goal is to identify actionable, systems-level opportunities to strengthen NBS follow-up by engaging home-visiting perinatal professionals as trusted messengers and implementation partners. We convened stakeholder meetings to build shared understandings of NBS and to elicit frontline perspectives; insights from the initial session were used to co-develop a survey distributed via snowball sampling to home-visiting professionals serving pregnant people and newborns across Cuyahoga County (January 22-March 17, 2025; N=80). Findings showed strong endorsement for family education about NBS (89%), ideally by the third trimester (71%), alongside substantial workforce knowledge gaps, with most respondents reporting no formal training about NBS (71%). Stakeholders emphasized the need for clearer role delineation, generally viewing physicians as the primary source of NBS education while positioning home-visiting professionals as a complementary, secondary source who can reinforce messages and support care navigation. These preliminary findings are shaping a roadmap for meaningful change that combines continued research expansion into additional communities with immediate capacity-building for the home-visitation workforce.

items.title: A prospective, comparative cohort analysis of influenza antibody waning in Michigan and Hong Kong during periods of low influenza circulation.
items.abstract: Background Reduced influenza transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic prompted concern about waning of population immunity that could lead to subsequent surges in circulation. We compared longitudinal influenza antibody titers in Michigan and Hong Kong, two regions with reduced influenza transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods In two prospective cohort studies (HIVE, Michigan; EPI-HK, Hong Kong), we analyzed longitudinal serum samples collected from 2020 through 2023 from participants without influenza infection or vaccination. Sera were tested using hemagglutination inhibition assays (HAI) and microneutralization (MN) against vaccine strains. Two-year fold changes in titers were estimated using multivariable power-law models adjusted for age and baseline titer. Results We analyzed 173 sera from 57 HIVE participants and 259 sera from 60 EPI-HK participants. Initial HAI geometric mean titers ranged from 12.3-123.4 in HIVE and 6.3-40.9 in EPI-HK. Among those with >1:40 baseline titers in HIVE, fold-change estimates indicated waning for H1N1 strains, including A/Brisbane (0.70 [95% CI: 0.56,0.86]), A/Idaho (0.40 [0.32,0.50]), and A/Michigan (0.43 [0.34,0.52]), while H3N2 and influenza B showed minimal or no waning. In EPI-HK, fold-change estimates demonstrated heterogeneous patterns by strain for H1N1, and waning for selected H3N2 strains, including A/Cambodia (0.44 [0.29,0.65]) and A/Singapore (0.48 [0.33,0.69]). MN results were consistent with HAI findings. Conclusion Influenza antibody responses during the pandemic showed heterogeneous, strain-specific changes rather than uniform decline. These findings suggest that population immunity was maintained for many strains despite reduced viral circulation, with waning occurring in particular strains and varying by population.

items.title: Frequent snacking, caries risk, and preventive care delivery in US dental school clinics: A BigMouth data repository study.
items.abstract: Background This study examined the associations between frequent snacking, caries risk classification, clinical indicators of caries, and preventive care delivery among adult dental patients. Methods Data from 9 institutions participating in the BigMouth Dental Data Repository (UTHealth Houston) were reviewed. Adult patients who underwent oral examinations from July 1, 2022, through August 22, 2023, were included. Frequent snacking was defined as frequent or prolonged intake of sugary foods or drinks between meals per the American Dental Association caries risk assessment form, or as more than 3 between-meal snacks per day per the Consortium for Oral Health-Related Informatics questionnaire. Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, gender, race or ethnicity, and examination type. Results Among 8,067 adult patients with complete dietary questionnaires, 2,429 (30.1%) reported frequent snacking. Frequent snackers were significantly more likely to be classified as high or extreme caries risk than nonfrequent snackers (91.1% vs 81.3%; adjusted odds ratio, 2.39; 95% CI, 2.03 to 2.82; P Conclusions Frequent snacking was strongly associated with an elevated caries risk and clinical disease indicators, yet preventive care was not consistently aligned with this behavioral risk. Practical implications There is a gap between dietary risk identification and preventive care implementation in academic dental clinics, underscoring the need for improved integration of dietary counseling.

items.title: Trial Endpoints for Endemic Mycoses: Consensus Recommendations by the Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium and European Confederation of Medical Mycology.
items.abstract: Background Endemic mycoses, caused by Blastomyces, Coccidioides, Emergomyces, Histoplasma, Paracoccidioides, Sporothrix, and Talaromyces marneffei, represent an important global health challenge. Expanding endemic regions, climatic change, improved diagnostics, increased disease awareness, and an increasing at-risk population have contributed to rising case numbers. These infections affect both immunocompetent and immunocompromised hosts and exhibit marked clinical heterogeneity. Current treatment response guidance, established by the Mycoses Study Group and the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer in 2008, are primarily tailored for invasive yeast and mold infections and are inadequate for endemic mycoses due to their complexity and heterogeneity. Methods An international, multidisciplinary expert panel convened through the Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium and the European Confederation of Medical Mycology to develop consensus guidance for treatment response assessment in endemic mycoses. The process included a structured literature review, expert discussion, regulatory consultation, patient input, and public comment, culminating in consensus-based response criteria. Results The proposed guidance response criteria encompass clinical, mycologic, and radiologic assessments. Conclusions The new criteria aim to improve the accuracy and standardize the assessment of treatment response, enabling comparison and pooling results across clinical trials while addressing the unique challenges posed by these diverse pathogens.

items.title: Trial Endpoints for Aspergillus and Rare Molds: Consensus Recommendations by the Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium and the European Confederation of Medical Mycology.
items.abstract: Background Invasive mold disease (IMD) remains a substantial cause of patient morbidity and mortality. Aspergillosis and mucormycosis remain the predominant infections encountered, although rare molds continue to emerge as important pathogens. Improvement in patient outcomes has been the result of progress in risk stratification, diagnostics, supportive care, antifungal therapy, and/or prophylaxis, yet substantial challenges remain, requiring the development of novel treatment strategies. Clinical trials evaluating treatment response are currently based on consensus criteria published in 2008. However, advances in clinical mycology and the broadening variety of mold diseases in clinical trials necessitate a revision of these criteria to ensure that adjudication of patient outcomes accurately captures responses to therapeutic intervention. Methods To tackle this task, an international expert panel nominated by the European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium (MSGERC) was convened. Results The panel produced updated consensus guidance for assessing treatment responses and defining study outcomes in clinical trials of IMD in both adults and children. Conclusions Along with guidance, potential pitfalls in assessing outcome, such as discordant clinical, radiologic, and/or mycologic data and areas for future research are discussed.

items.title: Trial Endpoints for Candidemia and Invasive Candidiasis: Consensus Recommendations by the Mycoses Study Group Education & Research Consortium and European Confederation of Medical Mycology.
items.abstract: Invasive candidiasis (IC) remains the most common invasive mycosis world-wide, responsible for a wide range of infections that can range from superficial mucosal infections to life-threatening systemic diseases. Clinical trials of antifungal agents for IC are pivotal to its management. Therapeutic responses in these trials are currently based on consensus criteria initially presented by the Mycoses Study Group (MSG) and the European Organization for Research and the Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) in 2008. These 2008 definitions originally described by Segal et al are still employed by both investigators and regulatory agencies when evaluating antifungal drug efficacy and patient outcomes. However, advances in clinical mycology, the change in epidemiology of Candida infections due to the increase in non-albicans Candida species, and the increase in newer antifungal agents currently under development require a revision of these criteria to ensure appropriate and standardized adjudication of patient outcomes and to accurately capture responses to newer therapeutic regimens and modern interventions. Therefore, the European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium (MSGERC) have decided to revise the criteria to be used for future studies.

items.title: Developmental age determines DNA damage response dynamics and tumor susceptibility following irradiation in the small intestine of ApcMin/+ mice.
items.abstract: Purpose Epidemiological studies have demonstrated that age at exposure is a critical modifier of radiation-induced cancer risk, with higher susceptibility observed in children. However, the underlying cellular mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we aimed to examine the effects of age at exposure on radiation-induced tumorigenesis in a mouse model and to investigate age-dependent differences in DNA damage responses, including double-strand break repair kinetics and apoptosis. Materials and methods The effects of age at exposure on radiation-induced tumorigenesis were investigated in C3H/He (C3H) × C57BL/6 (B6)-F1 Apc Min/+ mice. Mutational events in tumor tissues were characterized using loss of heterozygosity (LOH) analysis. Radiation-induced DNA damage responses were evaluated by quantifying γH2AX and 53BP1 foci in intestinal crypts. Apoptosis was assessed by morphological analysis and cleaved caspase-3 staining of apoptotic bodies. Results Tumor burden was at its peak in mice irradiated at 2 weeks of age (infants), whereas irradiation at 4 weeks or older did not result in a significant increase compared with non-irradiated controls. LOH analysis of tumor tissues indicated deletion including the Apc locus as a mutational signature associated with radiation; frequency of deletion-type mutational events was correlated with increased susceptibility to tumorigenesis. Radiation increased 53BP1 foci in the crypts of both infant and adult mice; however, prolonged persistence of these foci was observed specifically in infant crypts. Similar trends were not observed for γH2AX foci. In addition, radiation-induced apoptosis was significantly lower in infant intestinal crypts compared with those in adults. Conclusion Our findings demonstrate that infancy is associated with increased susceptibility to radiation-induced tumorigenesis in C3H/B6-F1 Apc Min/+ mice and that age-dependent sensitivity is associated with dynamics of DNA damage signaling and apoptotic kinetics. This study provides mechanistic insights into age-dependent radiation sensitivity and highlights the importance of DNA damage response processes in determining cancer risk.

items.title: Maternal adiponectin restores cholinergic vasodilation in mesenteric arteries from adult mice exposed to obesity in utero.
items.abstract: Maternal obesity increases the risk of cardiovascular and metabolic disease in the offspring during childhood and adult life. Pregnant women and mice with obesity have lower circulating levels of adiponectin (ADN) than normal weight controls. ADN is an adipokine that regulates energy metabolism, vascular function, and placental function. We hypothesized that offspring of obese dams have impaired resistance artery vasodilation, which could be prevented by late-pregnancy normalization of circulating ADN concentrations. Adult female mice were fed either a control or obesogenic diet and mated with control diet-fed males. Control dams received a continuous infusion of phosphate saline buffer (PBS) during late pregnancy whereas obese females received either PBS or ADN. After weaning, offspring were fed a control diet. Mesenteric arteries (MsA) were dissected from adult offspring and mounted in a wire myograph. MsA responses to the vasoconstrictors phenylephrine or endothelin-1 were not different between groups. However, the vasodilatory responses to acetylcholine were reduced in offspring from obese dams as compared to control-fed dams. Furthermore, ADN supplementation during pregnancy restored the MsA cholinergic vasodilatory responses in offspring from obese dams. The reduced vasodilatory response to acetylcholine in MsA from offspring of obese dams was mediated by a decrease in prostaglandin signaling. Vasodilation induced by bradykinin or by activation of AMP-activated protein kinase did not differ with maternal obesity or ADN treatment, whereas vasodilation to sodium nitroprusside was reduced by ADN treatment. These observations suggest that normalizing circulating ADN in pregnancies with maternal obesity prevents in-utero programming of cholinergic dysfunction in the offspring.

items.title: Machine learning-based proteomics analysis identified 23 protein biomarkers for enhanced risk prediction of myocardial infarction in Chinese and Europeans.
items.abstract: Background Advances in proteomics assays enable measurement of thousands of plasma proteins, which could facilitate machine learning-based approaches to enhance risk prediction of disease. Methods We measured plasma levels of >9500 proteins among 4000 Chinese adults (1937 myocardial infarction [MI] cases and 2026 subcohort), using both Olink Explore (2923 proteins) and SomaScan (6597 proteins) platforms. Protein-based risk prediction models were constructed, using conventional and machine learning approaches, with model performance assessed via discrimination (C-statistic), classification (net reclassification index; NRI) and calibration. Protein scores were compared and combined with conventional risk factors and polygenic scores (PGS), and externally validated in 37,187 Europeans (630 MI cases) in UK Biobank. Findings Overall, 451 Olink and 530 SomaScan proteins were significantly associated (5% false discovery rate) with MI risk after adjustment for conventional risk factors. The protein prediction models based on Olink, SomaScan, or both platforms combined, outperformed conventional risk factors and PGS using discrimination, classification and calibration. The protein score using 23 Boruta-selected (Olink/SomaScan: 11/12) proteins yielded a 3.3-fold difference in 10-year cumulative incidence of MI between the top and bottom 20% risk groups (3.6 [95%CI: 3.1-4.1] vs 1.1 [0.9-1.2] per 100), compared with 2.5-fold (2.5 [2.2-2.9] vs 1.0 [0.9-1.2]) and 1.5-fold (1.9 [1.6-2.1] vs 1.3 [1.1-1.4]) differences for conventional and PGS, respectively. Adding this protein score to conventional risk factors increased C-statistics from 0.846 (0.829-0.862) to 0.864 (0.849-0.879), yielding an NRI of 72%. External validation in 37,187 participants in UK Biobank by adding 23 Boruta-selected proteins to conventional risk factors yielded comparable improvement in C-statistics for MI (from 0.710 [0.688-0.731] to 0.733 [0.710-0.756]) and 45% improvement in NRI (NRI 45%). Conclusions Machine learning identified subsets of proteins for improved MI risk prediction beyond conventional risk factors and PGS, showing the potential for developing small panel proteomics assays to improve disease risk prediction.

items.title: Relationship Between Spectacle Refractive Status, Tactical Firing Stages, and Individual Weapon Qualification Performance in U.S. Army Soldiers.
items.abstract: Introduction Vision is a critical component of military readiness, yet nearly 25% of U.S. service members require spectacle correction. This study quantitatively investigated the impact of spectacle-corrected refractive error, particularly myopia, alongside modern operational variables (assisted night fire, Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear [CBRN] protective mask, and optical assistance) on individual weapon qualification performance. Materials and methods This retrospective study analyzed 292,436 marksmanship records from 220,539 active-duty U.S. Army Soldiers (March 2019-March 2020). Weapon qualification scores for the M16/M4 rifle/carbine (n = 245,273), combat pistol (n = 34,222), and M249 Automatic Rifle (M249AR, n = 12,941) were extracted from the Digital Training Management System (DTMS) and coupled with spectacle prescriptions from the Spectacle Request Transmission System (SRTS). GLM ANCOVA, controlling for age and gender, evaluated associations between marksmanship performance and 7 refractive conditions and firing stages. Results For the rifle/carbine platform, the "No Spectacle" cohort achieved the highest scores compared to all male spectacle cohorts and female moderate-to-high myopia cohorts (P Conclusions Spectacle dependence, particularly for moderate-to-high myopia, represents a significant marksmanship liability. On precision rifles, optics and night-vision devices act as coupled performance multipliers while CBRN degrade scores because of cheek-weld interference. Conversely, handguns and automatic weapons bypass these physical restrictions.

items.title: Aqua Steps: A Feasibility Study of a new Aquatic Exercise Therapy Intervention for Falls Prevention in Older Adults.
items.abstract: Importance One-third of people ≥65 years old fall at least once each year. Falls cause major deteriorations in physical and mental health and have high economic costs. Aquatic exercise may reduce falls, but research on older adults at high falls risk is sparse. Objective The objective was to assess the feasibility and acceptability of a new aquatic exercise intervention (Aqua Steps) and explore preliminary evidence on its effectiveness for older adults at high falls risk. Design A feasibility study for the Aqua Steps intervention, with secondary outcome assessments at baseline, end of intervention, and 6 months after end of intervention. A second group undertook an established pre-existing land-based program for falls prevention (Steady Steps). Setting The settings were swimming pools and exercise halls. Participants Participants were 101 older adults at high falls risk. Interventions Both the aquatic and land-based group participants undertook 60 minutes of supervised exercise therapy per week, for 16 weeks. Main outcomes and measures Primary outcomes, based on Aqua Steps feasibility, included recruitment, retention, and adverse events. The following secondary outcomes were also explored to identify preliminary evidence of improvements: falls; functional, strength, and balance tests; and patient-reported outcomes. Results The Aqua Steps intervention exceeded comfortably all feasibility targets set for progression to a large-scale trial; recruitment took 1 month, the program had 88% retention and 90% adherence, and there were no accidents or severe adverse events. After the intervention, falls, fallers, and frequent fallers were reduced by 38%, 36%, and 58%, respectively. There were statistically significant improvements, which were maintained at follow-up, on all functional (22%-70%) and strength (10%-80%) tests, falls efficacy (11%), and balance confidence (8%). In the Steady Steps group, there was a reduction in falls and fallers/frequent fallers (29%-35%) and significant improvements in functional tests (8%-30%) and falls efficacy (7%). Conclusions Aqua Steps had very high feasibility and acceptability and was popular and safe. There was preliminary evidence for improvements in falls and risk factors for falls. Relevance Such positive effects could have a significant impact on people's lives. The findings can inform the design of a large-scale follow-up definitive trial to confirm and generalize findings and to shape future policy on exercise for falls prevention.

items.title: Landscape of HTLV-1 in vitro diagnostic tests.
items.abstract: The extent of regulatory-approved assays for in vitro diagnostics of human T-lymphotropic virus 1 (HTLV-1) remains largely undocumented. This study aimed to map the current landscape of HTLV-1 diagnostics in 13 countries to support the development of World Health Organization guidelines and aid countries in building effective public health responses. Through a review of regulatory records and consultations with government officials, we identified 25 screening assays and three confirmatory tests. While most assays used serum or plasma, two enzyme immunoassays in Brazil were approved for antibody detection in dried blood spots. Only Japan had registered a rapid diagnostic test, which is based on immunochromatography. Screening assays generally had good performance, with both high sensitivity (range: 97.8%-100%) and specificity (range: 99.4%-100%). Assays using dried blood spots also had good performance with 96%-100% sensitivity and 98.7%-99.4% specificity. Three confirmatory, antibody-based tests were identified, but no molecular diagnostic tests were registered. The number of registered screening assays per country varied widely (range: 0-15), revealing a fragmentation and inconsistency in the global market. To foster an effective public health response, expanding access to and uptake of HTLV-1 testing services using accurate and quality-assured products is a priority.

items.title: Effect of Sociodemographic Factors on Cochlear Implant Follow-Up and Hearing Outcomes in Adults.
items.abstract: Objective To evaluate associations between sociodemographic factors, postoperative audiometric rehabilitation follow-up, and hearing outcomes after cochlear implantation in adults. Study design Retrospective cohort study of adults evaluated for cochlear implant candidacy between January 1, 2018 and December 31, 2022 who underwent surgery prior to December 10, 2024. Setting Three tertiary care centers within a single city. Methods Linear regression models, multinominal linear regression, and linear mixed-effects models evaluated the relationship between sociodemographic variables and the number of audiometric rehabilitation follow-up visits attended within 1 year of device activation (primary outcome) and the change in consonant-nucleus-consonant word recognition score from preoperative baseline to 1-year postactivation (secondary outcome). Results Among 292 patients (median age 70; 46% male; 88% White), 345 implanted ears were included with a median of 4 audiology visits. Medicaid coverage was associated with higher visit rates versus private insurance (rate ratio 1.44 [1.13-1.83], P = .003). Older patients were more likely to attend their scheduled visits while single individuals had higher odds of greater‑than‑expected visit frequency (odds ratio 2.89 [1.46-5.71], P = .002). In 102 implanted ears with 12-month consonant-nucleus-consonant scores, public insurance and non-White race were associated with smaller consonant-nucleus-consonant score improvement while the number of visits attended was not associated with consonant-nucleus-consonant scores. Conclusions Public insurance, being single, and older age were associated with deviations from typical audiometric rehabilitation utilization patterns. Consideration of patients' sociodemographic context is an important factor that can be used to personalize and tailor post-cochlear implantation rehabilitation.

items.title: Molecular characterization of Blastocystis in wild Tibetan macaques (Macaca thibetana) and evidence of isolation by distance in subtype ST3.
items.abstract: Macaca thibetana is an endemic primate in China. This study represents the first molecular investigation of the prevalence and subtypes of Blastocystis in wild M. thibetana in China, examining the relationship between geographic distance and Blastocystis genetic differentiation, while accounting for host species. A total of 264 fecal samples were collected from three populations in China (Mount Emei, Erlang, and Gongga) across seasons. The small subunit ribosomal RNA (SSU rRNA) gene of Blastocystis was amplified, and genetic analyses were performed using reference sequences from 14 countries and 17 host species. Blastocystis was detected in 35.2% (93/264) of the samples, with the highest prevalence (56.3%) in Emei, followed by Gongga (28.6%), and Erlang (21.5%). Seasonal variation in prevalence was observed across populations (Emei: 83.3% in summer, Erlang: 69.2% in autumn, and Gongga: 87.5% in winter), indicating no consistent seasonal pattern. Three zoonotic subtypes (ST1-ST3) and ST39 were identified. Phylogenetic analysis revealed no clear clustering of Blastocystis sequences by host species or broad geographic scales (countries or continents). However, a significant association between genetic and geographic distances was detected for ST3 (r = 0.638, p = 0.0014), and this association remained significant after controlling for host species. This suggests that geographic distance is associated with ST3 genetic variation among macaque populations in China. Additionally, the high prevalence of zoonotic subtypes indicates a potential for zoonotic exposure in the human-wildlife interface, necessitating targeted public health monitoring in the studied areas.

items.title: Application of geospatial technologies in mental health research: A scoping review of progress and future directions.
items.abstract: While geospatial technologies in psychiatric epidemiology have advanced, the literature remains fragmented. Guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), we reviewed English-language research in Scopus and Web of Science published between 1982 and 2024. We included 114 studies applying geospatial tools for public health research on mental health outcomes, all of which were published between 2012 and 2024. Findings indicate a significant transition from static, area-based descriptive mapping toward dynamic computational mental health epidemiology. Key advancements include artificial intelligence (AI)-based street-view assessments and Global Positioning System (GPS) mobile sensing to address the Uncertain Geographic Context Problem (UGCoP), a spatial exposure misclassification issue. However, critical gaps persists: physical environment are extensively mapped, whereas dynamic social interactions are largely unexplored. The focus remains heavily skewed toward clinical pathology, rendering positive adaptation under-researched. Additionally, research is predominantly conducted in high-income countries and specific middle-income nations like China, leaving populations in the Global South largely underrepresented. To advance the field, future research must prioritize longitudinal designs to establish robust causal relationships. Investigating positive psychological constructs is essential to shift the focus from merely mitigating pathology to actively promoting resilience. Furthermore, developing standardized environmental indices is critical to ensure cross-study comparability and translate spatial data into actionable public health and spatial planning policies. Crucially, there is an urgent need to address geographic disparities by expanding research within the Global South and translating geospatial insights into actionable policies that foster mental health equity and build resilient communities.

items.title: Toward a Healthier Future Through Obesity Prevention and Care: The JAMA Summit Report on Obesity.
items.abstract: Importance Obesity is one of the most difficult challenges of the modern era, affecting more than 1 billion people worldwide. Nearly half of US adults and 1 in 5 US children meet the medical definition of having obesity, with major consequences for cardiometabolic, kidney, hepatic, pulmonary, musculoskeletal, reproductive, oncologic, and mental health. Obesity also carries social and economic harms through stigma, discrimination, and bias. Observations Drivers of the obesity epidemic include changes in food production and consumption accompanied by social, economic, and technological shifts that reduce food preparation, disrupt sleep, and decrease physical activity. The burden of these changes is not equally distributed, with higher obesity prevalence among socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. Current prevention measures include nutrition standards, food and menu labeling, school meal policies, sugar-sweetened beverage taxes, community-based lifestyle programs, and public assistance efforts. The impact of these approaches has been inadequate. Contemporary clinical management recognizes obesity as a chronic disease characterized by genetic, biological, and behavioral susceptibilities. Access, affordability, tolerability, and the chronicity of use remain major challenges for all available obesity management strategies, including new glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapies. Potential solutions require a coordinated, multisector response and include efforts to prevent obesity at the societal level, improve care of individuals with obesity, and strengthen research and innovation. Priority areas include improving the food and physical activity environment; strengthening communication and education; strengthening childhood obesity prevention; addressing health inequities; reducing stigma and bias; modernizing obesity care delivery; expanding access to lifestyle, healthy food, medication, and surgical interventions; and supporting long-term treatment adherence and maintenance. Proposed actions include new government policies on food production, labeling, marketing, and school nutrition; modernization of drug evaluation; payment reform to support comprehensive obesity treatment; development of multidisciplinary care models; incentives to promote cross-sector partnerships; and research to advance personalized prevention and treatment strategies. Conclusions and relevance The emergence of effective obesity management medications offers a significant opportunity to curb the prevalence of obesity. However, no single intervention will be enough. Sustained improvement will require addressing the underlying structural and environmental drivers of obesity, along with person-centered, multilevel strategies that simultaneously improve prevention, reduce stigma, and expand equitable access to evidence-based treatment. Coordinated action across government, health care systems, clinicians, payers, industry, schools, communities, and researchers will be essential to achieving long-term improvement.

items.title: Impact of 22 Comorbidities on Number of Hospitalizations and Emergency Department Visits in U.S. Community-Dwelling Older Adults With Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (AD/ADRD).
items.abstract: ObjectivesExamine the impact of 22 comorbidities on number of hospitalizations and Emergency Department (ED) visits among community-dwelling persons with Alzheimer's Disease and Alzheimer's Disease Related Dementias (AD/ADRD).MethodsAnalyzed 2018-2019 Medicare Claims data for 7.1 million beneficiaries aged ≥65 with AD/ADRD. Each comorbidity's impact was assessed using net effect (NE), a measure of attributable risk for multiple interacting factors.ResultsPneumonia showed the highest contribution to all-cause hospitalizations (NE = 1.58), indicating that pneumonia contributed 1.58 all-cause hospitalizations per year. Acute myocardial infarction had an NE of 1.37; hip fracture, 1.20; anemia, 0.89; and stroke, 0.78. Stroke had the highest contribution to all-cause ED visits (NE = 0.477), followed by arthritis (0.421), pneumonia (0.400), depression (0.394), hypertension (0.325), and hip fracture (0.323).ConclusionOur results highlight a large discrepancy in how the various comorbidities of AD/ADRD impact healthcare utilizations. Certain conditions, particularly pneumonia and arthritis, may be key targets for reducing hospitalizations and ED visits.

items.title: Supporting public health outbreak investigations with improved Legionella pneumophila isolate recovery using a comprehensive culture algorithm including an off-label use of a Legionella detection kit.
items.abstract: Legionella pneumophila (Lpn) is a gram-negative, fastidious environmental pathogen that is the major cause of Legionnaires' disease (LD). In New York State (NYS), Lpn is responsible for multiple outbreaks each year. For source attribution during an outbreak, whole-genome sequencing of culture isolates is needed to assess relatedness. Isolation of Lpn from clinical and environmental samples may pose challenges due to overgrowth of competing organisms and the potential for the initiation of patient antimicrobial treatment prior to specimen collection. In this study, we evaluated the IDEXX Legiolert method to improve recovery of Lpn isolates in both PCR-positive clinical specimens and environmental water samples. Our initial prospective study of 43 respiratory (RES) and 16 environmental samples found that isolate recovery of Lpn was improved by 25.6% for RES specimens and 43.8% for non-potable (NP) water samples when IDEXX Legiolert method was compared to our existing culture method. When the validated IDEXX Legiolert method was employed during several major outbreaks in NYS over the course of 4 years (2019-2023), encompassing 22 RES and 68 environmental samples, Lpn recovery was also improved (35% RES, 42% NP), further confirming the significant impact the IDEXX Legiolert has on outbreak source attribution. Importance Legionnaires' disease (LD) is a serious and potentially lethal form of pneumonia, primarily resulting from the inhalation of aerosols contaminated with Legionella from artificial water supply or cooling systems. LD is frequently underdiagnosed due to its lack of distinguishing clinical presentation, rarity as a cause of pneumonia, and need for specialized testing. Furthermore, obtaining a lower respiratory specimen from LD cases is often challenging, and even when these specimens are available, culturing requires specific media that may not be available in all microbiology laboratories. In the present study, we assessed and implemented a modification to the culture procedure that improved Legionella pneumophila isolate recovery from PCR-positive samples. This innovative method, utilizing an off-label IDEXX Legiolert culture step, provides an improvement over current methods for determining source attribution of LD outbreaks, particularly in situations where isolating Legionella is challenging.

items.title: Association of treponemal chemiluminescent immunoassay signal intensity with TPPA reactivity in reverse sequence syphilis screening.
items.abstract: Reverse sequence screening for syphilis using treponemal chemiluminescent immunoassays (Tp-CIAs) is widely used in clinical laboratories; however, interpretation is typically based on binary cutoff values, and the clinical value of signal intensity remains underutilized. We conducted a retrospective diagnostic performance accuracy study including 1,827 individuals undergoing routine screening to evaluate the clinical utility of the Tp-CIA cutoff index (COI) as a continuous variable, using the TPPA as the reference standard. ROC analysis was performed to determine the optimal cutoff, and associations between COI values and TPPA reactivity were assessed. Tp-CIA demonstrated excellent discrimination of TPPA reactivity (area under the curve 0.992). COI values showed a strong monotonic association with TPPA reactivity (Spearman r s = 0.855), increasing from 2.5% at a COI r s = 0.637) and toluidine red unheated serum test ( r s = 0.705) titer levels. These findings demonstrate that, within the analytical conditions of this study, higher assay-specific COI values were associated with a greater likelihood of TPPA reactivity. COI-based interpretation should remain supplementary to established confirmatory testing and clinical assessment; exploratory threshold requires independent analytical and clinical validation. Importance Syphilis remains a growing global public health concern, and reverse sequence screening using Treponema pallidum chemiluminescent immunoassay (Tp-CIA) is widely adopted. Although these assays are interpreted qualitatively using manufacturer-defined cutoffs, the underlying signal intensity varies across specimens. In this study cohort, increasing Tp-CIA cutoff index (COI) values were associated with an increasing observed proportion of TPPA-reactive results. This association was assay- and cohort-specific and should be interpreted descriptively. COI should not replace established confirmatory testing, quantitative non-treponemal testing, or clinical assessment, and its potential supplementary value requires independent analytical and clinical validation.

items.title: Zebrafish float new hopes for fighting Vibrio cholerae with phage therapy.
items.abstract: The increasing number of bacterial pathogens showing resistance against commonly used antibiotics has rendered currently available treatments alarmingly ineffective and has become a major public health issue. Phage therapy, using viruses that infect bacteria in a bacteria-specific fashion, is an alternative approach that has shown promising efficacy at killing multidrug-resistant species. However, understanding the basic mechanisms of bacteriophage biology poses substantial challenges. We are notably missing model systems to better comprehend phage-bacteria-human host interactions and to bridge the gap between in vitro research and clinical applications. In an article published in Microbiology Spectrum , Sidi Mabrouk et al. establish Danio rerio as a model to investigate bacteriophage-bacterium dynamics in a naturalistic context for Vibrio cholerae , an important human pathogen (A. Sidi Mabrouk, J. S. Depelteau, C. Foini, A. Kempff, et al., Microbiol Spectr 14:e03565-25, https://doi.org/10.1128/spectrum.03565-25). Leveraging key features of the zebrafish model, Sidi Mabrouk and colleagues highlight the complex interplay between the ICP1 bacteriophage, V. cholerae , and zebrafish-associated gut microbiome in the phage efficacy to clear the pathogen.

items.title: Tuberculosis Notifications in Albania, 2015-2025: Geographical Inequalities, Seasonality and Pandemic-Associated Disruption.
items.abstract: Background Albania has experienced a sustained decline in tuberculosis (TB) notifications, but contemporary national epidemiology and sub-national heterogeneity remain incompletely characterised. We assessed spatial and temporal patterns in TB notifications, contact investigation, diagnostic ascertainment, drug resistance and COVID-19-associated disruption. Methods We analysed all 3759 national TB notifications from January 2015 to December 2025. Population-adjusted spatial risk was estimated using Bayesian BYM2 models, with contextual analyses incorporating internal migration, unemployment and gross domestic product. Seasonality, contact-investigation performance, culture and drug-susceptibility testing (DST) and resistance patterns were evaluated longitudinally. A Bayesian negative-binomial counterfactual model estimated notifications expected after March 2020 had pre-pandemic seasonal patterns continued. Results Marked North-South geographical heterogeneity persisted throughout the study period, with highest adjusted notification risks in Kukes, Lezhe and Diber prefectures. Contextual indicators did not explain this northern regional excess. Notifications peaked in spring-summer and were lowest in late autumn-winter. Contact-screening deficits narrowed substantially after 2019, although incomplete screening persisted. Culture ascertainment increased from an adjusted 47.5% pre-pandemic to 81.1% post-pandemic, while DST increased from 8.2% to 32.6%. Rifampicin resistance was identified in 7.0% of interpretable results and multidrug-resistant TB in 2.9%. During the COVID-19 pandemic (March 2020 to December 2021), 469 notifications were observed versus 755 expected, corresponding to a 37.6% deficit (95% posterior predictive interval: 30.1%-44.2%), with recovery remaining incomplete through 2025. Conclusions TB epidemiology in Albania remains geographically heterogeneous and vulnerable to programme disruption. Risk-adapted case finding, strengthened contact follow-up and resilient diagnostic capacity may improve future TB control.

items.title: Prophylactic granulopoiesis-stimulating factors for people with solid tumors undergoing cancer treatment.
items.abstract: Rationale Many chemotherapy agents used in the treatment of solid tumors can induce myelosuppression, resulting in hematologic toxicities such as neutropenia and febrile neutropenia (FN), which are major causes of treatment-related morbidity and mortality. Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) and granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) are well-established stimulators of myelopoiesis and hematopoietic stem cell mobilization. Although previous reviews have suggested improved overall survival among individuals receiving intensified chemotherapy supported by primary G-CSF, it remains unclear whether prophylactic administration of G-CSF or GM-CSF itself improves overall survival, freedom from treatment failure (FFTF), or FN-associated complications when compared with placebo or no prophylaxis under the condition of identical treatment regimens. Objectives To assess the efficacy of prophylactic granulopoiesis-stimulating factors compared with placebo or no prophylaxis on survival outcomes and preventing adverse effects of cancer treatment in people with solid tumors. Search methods We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, and Embase and ongoing trials registers, together with reference checking, in June 2025. There were no restrictions on language or publication status. Eligibility criteria We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing primary granulopoiesis-stimulating factors with placebo or no prophylaxis in participants aged 18 years and older with solid tumors. Outcomes Our outcomes were overall survival, FFTF, risk of infection, quality of life, all-cause mortality during chemotherapy, risk of bone pain, and duration of hospitalization. Risk of bias We used Cochrane's RoB 1 tool to assess risk of bias in the included studies. Synthesis methods We synthesized results for each outcome using meta-analysis where possible. We assessed statistical heterogeneity between studies using a Chi 2 test and I 2 values. We used hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for time-to-event data and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs for dichotomous outcomes. We used GRADE to assess the certainty of evidence for each outcome. Included studies We included 26 RCTs with a total of 5320 participants. Synthesis of results We assessed two trials as having a high risk of bias, and the remaining studies as having a low or unclear risk of bias. Primary prophylaxis G-CSF or GM-CSF compared with control likely results in a reduction in risk of infection (RR 0.64, 95% CI 0.49 to 0.83; P = 0.001; 7 studies, 915 participants; moderate-certainty evidence), but may result in little to no difference in overall survival (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.28 to 2.54; P = 0.59; 3 studies, 537 participants; low-certainty evidence) and FFTF (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.63 to 1.25; P = 0.50; 1 study, 259 participants; low-certainty evidence). Primary prophylaxis G-CSF or GM-CSF compared with control likely results in little to no difference in all-cause mortality during chemotherapy (RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.53 to 1.60; P = 0.75; 11 studies, 3001 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). Regarding adverse events, primary prophylaxis G-CSF compared with control probably results in a large increase in risk of bone pain (RR 3.55, 95% CI 1.09 to 11.56; P = 0.04; 10 studies, 3152 participants; moderate-certainty evidence), a clinically important adverse outcome. One study reported that participants in the GM-CSF group had a significantly longer mean hospitalization duration (9.7 days versus 5.2 days, P Authors' conclusions There is moderate-certainty evidence that primary prophylaxis G-CSF or GM-CSF likely reduces risk of infection versus control. In contrast, low- to moderate-certainty evidence suggests little to no improvement in overall survival and FFTF, and likely little to no difference between groups in all-cause mortality during chemotherapy. Regarding adverse events, moderate-certainty evidence shows a likely large increase in risk of bone pain. Data on the effects of prophylaxis G-CSF or GM-CSF compared to control on duration of hospitalization were inadequate to draw any conclusions, and no studies evaluated quality of life. We identified no new ongoing studies, and the number of recent publications is limited. Further research in this field is warranted. Funding This Cochrane review was funded by the "Innovation Star" project of outstanding graduate students in Gansu Province (2023CXZX-142), China. Registration Protocol was available via 10.1002/14651858.CD015656.

items.title: The Muheza Approach: A 7-Year Experience of Sustainable and Affordable Mesh Hernia Surgery in a Lower-Middle Income Country.
items.abstract: Introduction Hernias are a public health priority in Africa, with a focus on hernia surgery providing the potential to reduce the significant burden of hernia-related morbidity. Only a minority of patients in Africa are currently receiving a gold-standard mesh repair, owing to the cost of commercial mesh. In this study, we describe the long-term outcomes for patients undergoing hernia repairs utilising an affordable polyethylene 'mosquito-net' mesh (MNM) in Muheza, Tanzania. Methods Data from consecutive patients undergoing MNM hernia repair in a single centre in Muheza between November 2018 and February 2026 were recorded in a prospectively maintained database. Operative technique using a tension-free sublay technique and postoperative care, where feasible, was standardised. Follow-up was performed through a mix of face-to-face and telephone consultation. Results A total of 268 hernia repairs were included in the final analysis with a 596-day median follow-up. Most cases were inguinal hernias (89.9%) and primary repairs (85.1%). Thirty-day morbidity rate was 3.5%, including one (0.4%) mesh infection and two patients (0.7%) who required a return to theatre. Chronic pain was reported in 17 (6.3%) patients. There was one hernia recurrence during the study period. Conclusion Following our reporting of the early results in 2020, we now offer the longer-term data to demonstrate that the Muheza Approach to hernias utilising MNM is a safe, effective, affordable and sustainable strategy that could provide a platform for wider implementation across LMICs to address the shortfall in high-quality hernia surgery.

items.title: Coverage, equity and barriers of preconception care in the Chilean public health system: A national mixed-methods study (2019-2022).
items.abstract: Objective To analyze the use of preconception care (PCC) in the Chilean public health system between 2019 and 2022, and to explore the perceptions of regional and ministerial program leads regarding the barriers and facilitators that constrain its prioritization and uptake. Methods Sequential explanatory mixed-methods study. We analyzed all 145 024 PCC visits in the Monthly Statistical Record (REM A-01, DEIS) for 2019-2022, by year, region, age group, and cadre. Visit rates and a coverage proxy used the National Health Fund (FONASA) female beneficiaries aged 15-44 as denominator (assumption: one visit/woman/year). Five semi-structured interviews with regional Programa Salud de la Mujer leads and the Ministry of Health (MINSAL) national lead were analyzed by inductive content analysis. The study was approved by CEC-Salud UC (December 2023; protocol 230 725 004). Results PCC visits were 51 466 (2019), 21 799 (2020; -58% during COVID-19), 32 996 (2021) and 38 763 (2022); pre-pandemic levels were not recovered in any region except Magallanes. Coverage proxy percentages were 1.53%, 0.64%, 0.96%, and 1.10%. Visits concentrated in women aged 25-34; 40 years had markedly lower rates. Midwives delivered 99.06%-99.39%. Ñuble had the highest regional rate and Arica y Parinacota the lowest. Qualitative analysis yielded five categories (professional perceptions, facilitators, needs, challenges, recommendations) mapped. Conclusion PCC remains a covered but invisible service in Chile, severely underutilized and inequitably distributed. Embedding PCC into a renewed national policy, with clear technical guidance, monitoring indicators, and protected resources, is required.

items.title: Environmental contamination, human rights and medico-legal responsibility after Cannavacciuolo and Others v Italy (ECtHR).
items.abstract: Environmental contamination is increasingly recognised as a human rights issue engaging State obligations under the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR). In Cannavacciuolo and Others v Italy , the European Court of Human Rights held that prolonged environmental exposure may trigger positive obligations under Article 2 ECHR, requiring public authorities to identify, monitor and mitigate foreseeable risks to life. Implementing these obligations depends on the integration of environmental, clinical and epidemiological evidence. This paper argues that legal medicine can provide the methodological bridge between legal principles and scientific assessment. We propose an Integrated Environmental Medico-Legal Assessment Framework (I-EMAF), a conceptual model supporting transparent, multidisciplinary and evidence-based evaluation of environmental contamination. Rather than introducing new investigative methods, I-EMAF organises established scientific approaches within a coherent medico-legal structure to assist courts, public authorities and healthcare systems to implement their Article 2 obligations.

items.title: Resilience and Its Foreclosure: International Students' Communicative Struggles and Negotiations Within the U.S. Healthcare System.
items.abstract: International students enter a US healthcare system that is opaque, culturally unfamiliar, and costly, and they do so without the familial, financial, and cultural support that surrounds care. Drawing on the communication theory of resilience (CTR), this study examines how international students communicatively navigate that system and how cultural, institutional, and material conditions enable or hinder their resilience. Twenty-eight international students, predominantly graduate students, at a large public Hispanic-Serving institution took part in semi-structured interviews, analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis with CTR as a sensitizing framework. Five themes emerged from the analysis: financial precarity and systemic opacity; a different logic of care; from collective to individual care; institutional failure, formal and informal lifelines; and the limits of belonging. Participants enacted resilience by crafting normalcy, affirming identity anchors, drawing on communication networks, constructing alternative logics, and foregrounding productive action, yet the same conditions of precarities consistently foreclosed these very processes. The study examines how resilience is communicatively enacted and, under conditions of precarity, foreclosed, and it offers guidance for institutions seeking to support international students.

items.title: Counterfeit and grey market dental products: A public health perspective on risks, detection and mitigation strategies.
items.abstract: Counterfeit and grey market dental products endanger health and patient safety, effective treatment and integrity of the healthcare system. This review summarises evidence gathered on the increasing use of counterfeit dental products, such as composites, adhesives, implants and diagnostic equipment, which frequently possess low-quality or even toxic materials. Based on international case studies and methods of analysis, we discuss the clinical outcomes, including allergic reactions, treatment failures, infections, and the health-related problems, and their impact on public health, including economic costs and lost trust in oral health care. The methods of identification (including chemical spectroscopy and supply chain tracing) and addressed with the preventive measures in dental professionals. We describe the functions of major regulatory organisations, such as FDI, FDA, ADA and ISO with emphasis on standards, regulation and cooperation. We offer an analysis of legal and ethical frameworks with a focus on the issues of enforcement and measure differences between the developed and developing regions. A dedicated analysis of the ADA Seal of Acceptance highlights a key aspect of quality assurance. We recommend more collaboration among regulators, manufacturers and practitioners to reduce the risks and promote better surveillance, education and technological implementation. Action is needed to fight this illegal trade and safeguard vulnerable people and provide equitable access to safe dental care.

items.title: Translation, Localization and Validation of a School-Based Mental Health Literacy Curriculum, "The Persian Guide".
items.abstract: Mental health literacy training programs can be effective across diverse settings, yet their customization is crucial for success in each new setting. The main objectives of this study were to develop, through translation and localization, as well as to validate the effectiveness of a school-based mental health literacy curriculum guide called "the Persian Guide" in Iran. These objectives were pursued in two distinct phases. First, the guidelines set forth by Beaton et al. were strictly followed during the translation process. In the second phase, the mental health curriculum was examined by a group of experts to assess its cross-cultural and localization aspects in a discussion group. This study employed Leitz's textbook evaluation checklist to examine the feasibility, acceptability, and educational impact of the Persian Guide. Persian-language users were provided with translations and localizations of comprehensible and appropriate items. In validation the content validity ratio of school-based mental health curriculum modules was acceptable. In the evaluation of the mental health curriculum, the content validity index was 0.92 and the Cronbach's alpha coefficient was 0.82. The study concluded that this adapted guide is a reliable and applicable tool that can greatly benefit schools in their efforts to increase students' mental health literacy in Iran.

items.title: Reproducibility and class-level audit of wellbeing classification in the DigitalExposome dataset.
items.abstract: BackgroundRepeated observations and missing participant and time metadata can complicate interpretation of wellbeing classification results from public sensor datasets.ObjectiveTo assess reproducibility and split sensitivity of wellbeing classification on the released DigitalExposome CSV.MethodsWe reconstructed an initially submitted 30-sample, 15-sample-stride windowed Random Forest (RF) analysis and compared matched 70/30 file-order and unstratified random row splits. Ten random seeds quantified partition variability. We recalculated class-level metrics and ran a deduplicated, 30-row positional-embargo sensitivity analysis. The CSV contains no participant identifiers or timestamps.ResultsThe file-order RF holdout gave Macro F1 = 0.8515; random splits yielded mean Macro F1 = 0.9772 (SD = 0.0014). Reconstructed windows yielded accuracy = 0.7887, Macro F1 = 0.7632, and weighted F1 = 0.7549. Recalculated recall was 0.205 for wellbeing level 2. The deduplicated sensitivity analysis produced Macro F1 values of 0.128-0.162 across examined split fractions and leaf settings.ConclusionScores were sensitive to split procedure and repeated feature vectors. Because row chronology and participant membership cannot be recovered, these results do not estimate future-time or participant-independent performance and do not establish clinical utility.

items.title: Midlife Cardiorespiratory Fitness and Site-Specific Cancer Outcomes in Men.
items.abstract: Purpose Higher cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) is associated with a lower risk of cancer and mortality after diagnosis. However, mortality data are generally not specific to cancer sites or causes of death, limiting insights into the underlying mechanisms and opportunities for targeted prevention and survivorship strategies. This study aimed to examine the association between CRF and site-specific cancer incidence and mortality after diagnosis in men. Methods This cohort study used data from the Cooper Center Longitudinal Study (1971-2018) linked to Medicare claims (1999-2019). CRF was estimated using a maximal treadmill test. The associations between CRF and site-specific cancer incidence and death after cancer for the leading cancer sites in men (colorectal, lung, and prostate) were estimated using multivariable illness-death models and proportional hazards regression with Gompertz baseline hazards. Results Among 28,612 men with a mean Medicare follow-up of 7.9 years to cancer incidence, 4,998 colorectal, lung, and prostate cancers were identified. Higher CRF was associated with a lower risk of colorectal (HR: 0.91 per metabolic equivalent of task [MET]; 95% CI: 0.87, 0.96) and lung cancer (HR: 0.81 per MET; 95% CI: 0.77, 0.85), but not prostate cancer. During a mean follow-up of 7.1 years to death after diagnosis of colorectal, lung, or prostate cancer, 1,549 deaths were identified. High- (vs. low-) fit men with colorectal, lung, or prostate cancer had a 33-41% lower likelihood of all-cause mortality, including a generally lower risk of death from cardiovascular disease and other non-cancer causes. Conclusions Achieving higher CRF levels may contribute to cancer prevention and longer survival after diagnosis. Interventions that increase CRF through physical activity may improve health across the cancer control continuum.

items.title: Association of omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acid intake and their ratio with severe dysmenorrhea among female adolescents: A case-control study.
items.abstract: BackgroundDysmenorrhea is a reproductive health disorder related to menstruation that is prevalent among adolescents and may lead to reduced productivity and quality of life. Severe dysmenorrhea is thought to be influenced by inflammatory mechanisms mediated by an imbalance in the dietary intake ratio of omega-3 to omega-6 fatty acids.AimTo examine the association between omega-3 intake, omega-6 intake, and the omega-3:omega-6 fatty acid intake ratio and severe dysmenorrhea compared with no dysmenorrhea among female adolescence.MethodsThis study used an analytical observational case-control design. The research was conducted from January to February 2025 at SMA Negeri 9 Surabaya, Indonesia, involving 90 female adolescents. The severity of menstrual pain was assessed using the Verbal Multidimensional Scoring System (VMSS). Dietary intake of omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids was measured using a semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire (SQ-FFQ). Statistical analysis was performed using the Chi-squared test with a 95% confidence interval (CI).SummaryThe results of the study indicated a significant association between omega-3 fatty acid intake [ P = 0.036, OR (95% CI) = 3.083 (1.170-8.129)] and the omega-3 to omega-6 intake ratio [ P = 0.005, OR (95% CI) = 3.864 (1.573-9.492)] with severe dysmenorrhea. However, no significant association was found between omega-6 fatty acid intake and severe dysmenorrhea [ P = 0.168, OR (95% CI) = 2.588 (0.818-8.188)]. Female adolescents are encouraged to pay attention to their dietary intake, particularly the consumption of omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids, which may be associated with the presence of severe dysmenorrhea.

items.title: Development and preliminary assessment of a multimedia-based nutrition education module for mothers of stunted children in Malaysia.
items.abstract: BackgroundChildhood stunting remains an important public health concern in Malaysia. Mothers of stunted children require accessible and relevant nutrition guidance. Multimedia education delivered through mobile platforms such as WhatsApp may provide a practical approach.AimTo develop a multimedia-based nutrition education module (MNEM) and conduct a preliminary assessment of its content and presentation for mothers of stunted children in Malaysia.MethodsMNEM was developed through the analysis, design and development phases of the ADDIE model. In the analysis phase, three focus group discussions involving 13 healthcare providers and 12 mothers informed the module's content, presentation and delivery. During the design phase, seven experts rated the draft content using a 10-point scale. During the development phase, six healthcare providers and two mothers assessed the completed videos using 5-point scales. Ratings were summarised as percentage scores relative to the maximum possible scores.SummaryThe needs analysis generated seven themes relating to the module objectives, intended users, design and implementation, technology, delivery method, session duration and assessment, which guided the development of eight videos. The overall content-assessment percentage score was 86.2% during the design phase. During the development phase, the overall percentage scores for content and preliminary face assessments were 94.6% and 93.3%, respectively. Assessor feedback informed revisions to the content, sequence, language, visuals, duration and audio. In conclusion, MNEM received favourable ratings for its content, perceived usefulness and presentation, supporting its progression to further end-user evaluation to assess usability, acceptability and feasibility before its effectiveness is investigated.

items.title: Programmable nucleases for nucleic acid detection: bridging the gap between analytical sensitivity and clinical adoption.
items.abstract: Nucleic acid testing faces a persistent tension between analytical sensitivity and field deployability. Centralized qPCR relies on thermal cyclers and trained personnel, whereas isothermal amplification eliminates thermal cycling but often compromises sensitivity and stability. The COVID-19 pandemic intensified these constraints in primary care and point-of-care settings. Programmable nucleases offer a different detection logic: after guide-mediated target recognition, effector activity converts the recognition event into a detectable signal. Effector families such as CRISPR (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats), pAgo (prokaryotic Argonaute), and TnpB/Fanzor have yielded diverse assays, although TnpB has only recently been demonstrated, and Fanzor remains at the proof-of-principle stage. This review integrates effector mechanisms, engineering strategies, clinical evidence, and commercialization. It highlights three shifts: (i) an expanding effector toolbox with greater diversity in size, targeting requirements, and signal encoding; (ii) a transition from optimizing detection limits toward system-level capabilities, such as single-tube operation, multiplexing, absolute quantification, and robustness with unextracted or minimally processed samples; and (iii) a growing mismatch between analytical performance and regulatory maturity. Most CRISPR-based COVID-19 diagnostic products have been withdrawn, expired, or discontinued, likely reflecting commercial and regulatory factors rather than inherent technical limitations. In 2026, a CRISPR-based tuberculosis blood test received regulatory authorization in Colombia, extending the technology beyond respiratory virus detection. Bridging the laboratory-to-clinic gap now depends less on further sensitivity gains than on clear clinical indications, rigorous validation, and cost-controlled engineering. This review aims to guide assay selection and the development of next-generation diagnostics.
