Significantly more erosive lesions were found on first molars (47%), compared to both central (26%) and lateral (14%) incisors (p Conclusion The findings demonstrate that ETW is a highly prevalent condition that progresses from adolescence through early adulthood. The results underscore the need for early diagnosis, preventive strategies, and public health interventions to address modifiable risk factors.

items.title: Trends in the intervals between and distribution of diagnostic dental visits among adults in Denmark.
items.abstract: Before 1999, the recommended dental recall interval for adults in Denmark was 6-7 months. In 1999 and in 2013-2015, two major regulations were made aiming to increase this interval. This study analyzes the use of dental examination services for adults in Denmark over the 32-yr period from 1990 to 2021 using national registry data comprising information on 6,894,773 persons (133,811,495 person-years). Overall, 24% of the adult population did not receive a subsidized dental examination during the entire follow-up period, whereas 69% (n = 4,774,716) had at least two registered dental examinations. Median examination intervals increased slightly before 2013, increasing by about 3 months in the period 2013-2015 to 11 months, whereafter they remained stable. Examination intervals increased among 20-59-yr-olds but remained stable for older ages. Lower income, lower education, and immigrant or descendant status were associated with no dental examinations or longer examination intervals. Our analyses show that dental practices compensated for the 1999 restriction on standard examination intervals by use of control examination services, and the 2013-2015 risk-based interval reform was counteracted by increasing use of preventive and supragingival scaling services. Our findings support the notion that dentists working in a fee-for-service system have and exercise market power.

items.title: Climate-induced vulnerability of cutaneous leishmaniasis in Sri Lanka: an assessment using the Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit framework.
items.abstract: Objectives Cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL), caused by Leishmania donovani and transmitted by Phlebotomus argentipes, has emerged as a growing public health concern in Sri Lanka since the disease was declared notifiable in 2008. Despite the rising burden, no district-level, climate-induced vulnerability assessment has been undertaken. This study quantified and mapped CL vulnerability across all 25 administrative districts of Sri Lanka using epidemiological, climatic, land-use, and socioeconomic data. Methods Forty-one candidate variables, spanning epidemiological data for 2009-23 and contemporary climatic, land-use, and socioeconomic data, were compiled and reduced through principal component analysis (PCA) with Varimax rotation to derive statistically representative, non-collinear indicators and objective weights for three subindices: exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity, following the Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) framework. Thirty-six variables were retained to form a composite vulnerability index. Results Hambantota district recorded the highest exposure (0.90), Polonnaruwa the highest sensitivity (0.63), and Colombo the highest adaptive capacity (0.91). Overall, Polonnaruwa exhibited the greatest vulnerability (0.75), while Colombo demonstrated the lowest (0.25). Conclusion Polonnaruwa, Hambantota, and Anuradhapura districts warrant prioritized investment in vector surveillance, active case detection, healthcare infrastructure, and community awareness. The GIZ-PCA framework developed here provides a transferable, evidence-based tool for subnational CL risk prioritization in Sri Lanka and comparable endemic settings.

items.title: An Embedded Case Study on Co-production in Dental and Municipal Old Age Care.
items.abstract: Objectives The aim of this study was to identify and discuss different implementation strategies developed using a co-produced approach within a collaborative project between dental care and municipal care organisations. Methods This embedded, descriptive case study was based on 1 overall collaborative project between the Public Dental Care Service and four municipalities in the west of Sweden. Three cases from the overall project are analysed using intervention strategy components, all grounded in the Behaviour Change Taxonomy (version 1). Results Across the three cases, the collaborative project generated implementation strategies co-produced by dental and municipal care professionals. The strategies targeted specific behavioural determinants, such as knowledge, role clarity, environmental conditions and social support, using defined behaviour change techniques. Each case produced context-specific strategy components that were feasible to integrate into existing workflows within both dental and municipal care services. Conclusion This article stresses the potential of co-production when addressing complex health care challenges. By involving various endusers, conducting thorough needs assessments and implementing tailored strategies, the project reported successfully developed oral health care processes for older adults in municipal settings. The findings suggest that co-production can assist when developing and implementing health interventions that are context specific and responsive to the needs of diverse populations.Knowledge Transfer Statement:This study shows that co-production between dental and municipal care professionals and organisations can strengthen oral health practices for and with older adults. By working together across organisational boundaries, stakeholders co-designed strategies that bridged knowledge gaps and improved care processes, demonstrating the value of collaborative approaches.

items.title: Environmental noise and cognitive function in middle-aged and older adults: evidence of the inverted U-Shaped associations from a longitudinal study.
items.abstract: Cognitive impairment poses a growing public health challenge in ageing populations. Although environmental noise has been linked to cognitive health, less is known about the association between public attention to noise and cognitive function. Using three waves of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study from 2013, 2015 and 2018, this study linked individual cognitive scores to city-level noise-related search intensity from the Baidu Index, green coverage and healthcare resources. Pooled linear regression models adjusted for individual covariates and survey-year fixed effects, with standard errors clustered at the participant level. Quadratic terms were used to examine nonlinear associations between city-level noise-related search intensity and cognitive function. The models suggested an inverted U-shaped association, with higher predicted cognitive scores at intermediate index values. Interaction analyses suggested that this association varied with green coverage and hospital bed resources. Because the Baidu Index reflects public attention rather than acoustic exposure, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence that moderate noise benefits cognition. The study contributes longitudinal evidence from repeated observations in a national cohort using a digital indicator of noise-related attention. Further research integrating objective acoustic measurements is needed to clarify these associations and their implications for cognitive health in ageing populations.

items.title: Anti-ZIKV IgG Subclass Profiles and Anti-DENV IgG Are Associated With Neonatal Outcomes Following ZIKV Infection During Pregnancy.
items.abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes. Most infected individuals present mild symptoms; however, vertical transmission of ZIKV can lead to Congenital Zika Syndrome (CZS), which includes microcephaly, neurological, hearing, ophthalmological, and morphological abnormalities. Given the high prevalence of dengue virus (DENV) exposure and antibody cross-reactivity among flaviviruses, understanding how maternal humoral antibody profiles relate to neonatal outcomes after ZIKV infection is important. In this exploratory study, we evaluated maternal and neonatal anti-ZIKV total IgG, anti-ZIKV IgG1 and anti-ZIKV IgG3, and anti-DENV IgG reactivity in relation to maternal-neonatal antibody patterns and neonatal outcomes. Samples from pregnant women and their newborns were collected in Brazil, including pregnancies with microcephaly and other clinical or imaging abnormalities. Anti-ZIKV and anti-DENV IgG reactivity was measured by ELISA. Lower neonatal anti-ZIKV IgG3 reactivity was observed in pregnancies with ophthalmological abnormalities in the individual comparison, although this association did not remain significant after false discovery rate adjustment. Lower neonatal anti-DENV IgG reactivity was observed in pregnancies with ophthalmological abnormalities and with any clinical or imaging abnormality, and both associations remained significant after false discovery rate adjustment. These exploratory associations are hypothesis-generating and do not establish functional protection or a causal role for the measured antibody profiles.

items.title: Oral Health in Long Term Residential Care in Ireland-A Qualitative Study With Healthcare Staff.
items.abstract: Objective This study aimed to explore staff perceptions and experiences of oral care provision in a publicly funded long-stay ward of a community hospital in Ireland. Background Oral health is a critical component of overall health and quality of life in older adults, particularly those in long-term residential care who are at higher risk of oral disease due to age-related changes, multimorbidity, and reliance on caregivers. Cognitive impairment further complicates care provision, making the knowledge and practices of nursing staff and healthcare assistants essential. Materials and methods A qualitative study design was employed using semi-structured interviews, underpinned by reflexive thematic analysis. Participants included nursing staff and healthcare assistants recruited through convenience sampling from long-stay wards in a community hospital. Twelve semi-structured interviews were conducted on the long-stay wards of the community hospital during August 2025. Participants included nurse managers, senior nurses, staff nurses, and healthcare assistants. Results Following reflexive thematic analysis, four major themes, each with associated subthemes, emerged from the data: (1) Perceived Importance of Oral Care as Part of Overall Personal Care for Residents; (2) Nurses and Healthcare Professionals as Providers, Supporters, and Promoters of Independence in Oral Care; (3) Reliance on Informal Learning Methods for Oral Care Skill Acquisition; and (4) The Importance of Collaboration with Other Healthcare Professionals and Services for Oral Health Support. Conclusion Despite positive attitudes towards oral care, systemic and organisational challenges hinder its consistent delivery. Addressing these barriers through formal training, interdisciplinary collaboration, and organisational support may improve oral health outcomes. Further research should examine the impact of targeted interventions and national guidelines on oral care practices in long-term care settings.

items.title: EXPRESS: Dysbiosis correlates with more severe changes in intestinal function in cats with chronic enteropathy.
items.abstract: BackgroundMultiple pathophysiological mechanisms have been reported in animals with chronic enteropathy, as reflected by altered serum and fecal metabolites indicative of mucosal damage (e.g., fecal cholesterol, nervonic acid, arachidonic acid), malabsorption (e.g., serum cobalamin, fecal glucose), and loss of microbial function (e.g., fecal bile acid conversion). Furthermore, in dogs, marked intestinal dysbiosis has been linked to more severe underlying intestinal dysfunction, but this relationship is less characterized in cats.ObjectivesCharacterizing fecal microbiome and metabolome in healthy cats (HC), and cats with chronic enteropathy (FCE), either with increased dysbiosis index (DI > 0) or normal DI ( 2 [95% CI]: 0.19 [0.15-0.24]), microbial (0.17 [0.11-0.24]), and functional gene (0.16 [0.10-0.25]) profiles in cats with FCE (adjusted-P < 0.01), with more pronounced shifts in those with increased DI. Fecal cholesterol, nervonic acid, and arachidonic acid were higher in FCE (adjusted-P < 0.01) and correlated positively with DI (r = 0.33, 0.41, and 0.44, respectively; adjusted-P < 0.01). Increased fecal glucose and primary bile acid percentage were observed only in FCE-increased DI. A significantly lower cobalamin concentration was observed in cats with increased DI compared to those with a normal DI.Conclusions and relevanceFCE is associated with multiple functional marker alterations, including intestinal cell structural damage, malabsorption, and disrupted microbial function. These changes are not present in all cats, confirming that FCE is heterogeneous with varying degrees of underlying pathology. Cats with FCE with increased dysbiosis index exhibited more severe functional changes compared to those with normal dysbiosis index.

items.title: Delivery mode and breastfeeding duration after first birth among Brazilian women: The Pró-Saúde Study.
items.abstract: High cesarean rates in Brazil, particularly for low-risk pregnancies, have raised concerns about their impact on maternal and child health outcomes, including breastfeeding duration. This study aims to investigate the influence of delivery mode on breastfeeding duration among primiparous women. Additionally, it examines how education level and social support may modify this relationship. Data from the Pró-Saúde Study (1999-2012) were used to analy1ze breastfeeding duration. Kaplan-Meier survival curves were employed to estimate the time until breastfeeding cessation, while Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the effects of delivery mode, education level, and social support on breastfeeding duration, adjusting for potential confounders. Hazard ratios with 95 percent confidence intervals were calculated to assess the strength and direction of these associations. No significant association was observed between mode of delivery and breastfeeding duration. Compared with vaginal delivery, the adjusted hazard ratios for breastfeeding cessation were 0.96 (95 percent CI: 0.78-1.19) for elective cesarean delivery and 0.98 (95 percent CI: 0.83-1.17) for emergency cesarean delivery. Breastfeeding duration increased across successive birth decades, whereas the interactions between delivery mode and maternal education or social support showed no consistent evidence of effect modification. Maternal age was associated with lower risks of breastfeeding cessation among older women. Education level did not significantly affect breastfeeding duration in this study. The Schoenfeld residuals test confirmed the proportional hazards assumption for the model. Furthermore, an upward trend in breastfeeding rates over time suggests the influence of evolving public policies in Brazil. These findings highlight the complex interplay between delivery mode, maternal characteristics, and social support, emphasizing the need for tailored support strategies.

items.title: Exploring Barriers Experienced by Older People Living with HIV Related to Their Engagement in Activities of Daily Living
items.abstract: Background: HIV places enormous stress on the well-being of older people when performing activities of daily living. Surviving with HIV can be extremely challenging across the lifespan at any age; however, older people living with HIV experience physical, mental and psychological barriers that may affect their overall well-being and quality of life. Unmet needs related to activities of daily living may lead to adverse consequences resulting in deteriorating health outcomes. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to explore barriers experienced by older people living with HIV related to activities of daily living. Methods: An explorative qualitative study was conducted, using a purposive sampling method to recruit participants. A total of 58 participants were part of ten focus group discussions. These were older people living with HIV aged 60 and more. The data was analysed thematically. Results: The themes produced were psychological, physical, and cognitive barriers, functional mobility, change in sexual engagement, personal hygiene and eating barrier. Conclusions: Understanding the barriers of older people living with HIV will inform the development of appropriate interventions to improve their well-being, health and quality of life.

items.title: Association between family socioeconomic status and toddlers’ social-emotional development: the mediating role of the home nurturing environment
items.abstract: Inroduction Social-emotional development in early childhood lays the foundation for later adjustment and well-being. Although low family SES is consistently linked to poorer developmental outcomes, the mechanisms driving this association remain unclear. Guided by ecological systems theory and the family investment model, this study examined whether the home nurturing environment mediates the association between family SES and toddlers’ social-emotional development aged 12-36 months. Methods A cross-sectional survey of 370 healthy toddlers was conducted at a maternal and child health hospital in Wuhan, China. Family SES was constructed as a composite index of parental education and household income via PCA. The home nurturing environment was measured with the home rearing environment scale ( α = 0.930), and toddler social-emotional development with the ITSEA. Mediation analysis used the PROCESS macro (model 4) with 5,000 bootstrap resamples, controlling for child sex, age, residence, and family structure. Results Mean age was 27.71 +/- 7.76 months. Family SES was weakly but significantly correlated with social-emotional competence ( r = 0.146, p <0.01) and the home nurturing environment ( r = 0.213, p <0.01). The home environment was strongly correlated with competence ( r = 0.545, p <0.01). After entering the home environment, the direct SES path became non-significant ( c’ = 0.042, p = 0.955), while the indirect effect was significant (completely standardized indirect effect = 0.099, 95% CI 0.036-0.162), indicating full mediation. Discussion Family SES was associated with toddlers’ social-emotional development only through its shaping effect on the home nurturing environment. The home nurturing environment is a modifiable intervention target; enhancing parenting support and warm, cognitively stimulating home environments, particularly in low-SES families, may mitigate socioeconomic disparities in early social-emotional development.

items.title: Posterior alpha/beta oscillations reflect oculomotor dynamics underlying subsequent memory effects
items.abstract: Abstract Neural activity and eye movements are well-established predictors of human memory performance. Successful memory formation is associated with reduced alpha/beta power and increased eye movements. However, their coupling and combined contribution to memory formation remain largely unknown. Across four experiments combining eye tracking with scalp or intracranial electroencephalography during free or constrained viewing, we identify the degree of visual exploration, rather than subsequent memory performance, as consistent modulator of posterior alpha/beta power. Going beyond correlations, manipulating eye movements dissociated alpha/beta power reductions from memory. Together with the finding that saccade parameters predicted alpha/beta dynamics, our results directly link posterior alpha/beta activity to the oculomotor system. Moreover, the accumulation of saccades over time accounted for reduced alpha/beta power, resembling the canonical post-stimulus alpha/beta pattern. Our work demonstrates that posterior alpha/beta activity strongly reflects eye movements, supporting alternative perspectives on alpha/beta subsequent memory effects and the general function of posterior alpha/beta activity.

items.title: The NeuroDesign/NeuroArchitecture Index (NDIX): development of a method to evaluate the impact of the built environment on health, cognitive performance, and wellbeing
items.abstract: The built environment shapes physical and mental health. Evidence across neuroscience, psychology, physiology, and public health shows that spatial properties of our environment can modulate stress physiology, affect, attention, memory, and social cognition. Yet, no standardised instrument translates these multisensory dynamics into measures that quantify environmental qualities, enabling linking them to context-specific outcomes. Certification schemes (e.g. WELL, LEED, BREEAM) have advanced practice, but do not directly measure how specific spatial or contextual features impact psychology or physiology. Here, we introduce the NeuroDesign/NeuroArchitecture Index (NDIX), a theoretically grounded framework for evaluating dimensions of human experience of the built environment that may be relevant to mental health, cognitive performance, and wellbeing. The NDIX operationalises six domains; safety and accessibility, sensory, cognitive, emotional, social, and naturalness. The self-report component generates domain-specific and overall percentage scores describing environmental experience, while a complementary framework for profiling environmental features remains under development. Domain-level interpretation and practical application require further validation. The first pilot in a controlled indoor environment showed feasibility and meaningful detection of environmental variation, providing an initial proof-of-concept for the NDIX framework. Future research should extend validation across office, care, educational, residential, public and urban contexts and incorporate biomarkers (e.g. from wearables, neuroimaging).

items.title: Geschlechtsübergreifende Maskulina im Sprachgebrauch: Eine korpusbasierte Untersuchung zu lexemspezifischen Unterschieden
items.abstract: Abstract This study examines the distribution and linguistic characteristics of generic masculines (GM) in contemporary German press texts. The use of masculine personal nouns to refer to mixed-gender groups or unspecified individuals has been widely debated in academia and the public, with conflicting perspectives on its gender-neutrality. While psycholinguistic studies suggest that GM is more readily associated with male referents, corpus-based analyses of its actual use remain scarce. We investigate GM in a large corpus of press texts, focusing on lexeme-specific differences across different types of personal nouns. We conducted manual annotations of the whole inflectional paradigm of 21 personal nouns, resulting in 6,195 annotated tokens. Our findings reveal considerable differences between lexical items, especially between passive role nouns and prestige-related personal nouns. On a grammatical level, we find that GM occurs predominantly in the plural and in indefinite noun phrases. Furthermore, our data shows that GM is not primarily used to denote entire classes of people, as has been previously claimed. By providing an empirical insight into the use of GM in authentic written language, we contribute to a more nuanced understanding of its forms and manifestations.

items.title: From the fluency fallacy to the micro-to-macro validity gap: opportunities and pitfalls of LLMs in social simulation
items.abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into social simulation has generated considerable enthusiasm, but also raises substantial methodological and epistemological challenges. This critical review examines the use of LLMs as cognitive or decision-making components of simulated agents from a computational social science perspective. Rather than treating the psychological evaluation of LLMs as separate from simulation mechanics, we argue that their behavioral and epistemic limitations can become systemic vulnerabilities when scaled to multi-agent societies. We first map the rapidly evolving landscape of LLM-driven platforms, ranging from small narrative sandboxes to population-scale and spatially structured simulations. We then develop a unified critical framework for analyzing the Micro-to-Macro Validity Gap: the propagation, nonlinear amplification, or convergent contraction of micro-level limitations—including hallucinations, stochastic inconsistency, representational biases, and alignment effects—into agent-level distortions (such as average persona convergence) and macro-level risks (such as artificial consensus and behavioral homogenization), while exposing evaluators to epistemic vulnerabilities such as the Fluency Fallacy and automation bias. We identify contexts in which LLM-based agents offer genuine operational value, including serious games, participatory environments, and exploratory modeling, while distinguishing these uses from confirmatory research with unconstrained models and precise social forecasting. Finally, we examine theory-driven hybrid architectures that embed LLMs within explicit, mechanistic, and reproducible Agent-Based modeling (ABM) frameworks. We argue that such architectures offer a promising but not sufficient path toward improving epistemic control: their validity depends on multi-level evaluation of environmental dynamics, individual behavior, cross-level interactions, and aggregate outcomes, and they remain vulnerable to the risk of physics washing.

items.title: Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation at Yintang attenuates nap-deprivation-induced working memory decline: parallel associations with prefrontal activation and cardiac vagal tone
items.abstract: Abstract Background ​ Working memory (WM) decrement due to circadian dips and sleep restriction is a prevalent issue among interns, potentially impacting clinical decision-making. Non-invasive neuromodulation techniques, such as transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS), offer a promising approach to mitigate cognitive fatigue. This study investigates the efficacy and underlying neurophysiological mechanism of TEAS at the Yintang (EX-HN3) acupoint in counteracting WM impairment induced by nap deprivation. Methods We enrolled 90 interns with habitual napping behavior, who were randomly assigned to one of three groups: normal control group (NC), nap deprivation group (ND), and nap deprivation group receiving TEAS intervention (ND+TEAS). Cognitive performance was assessed using a 3-back WM task at baseline (12:00) and post-intervention (15:00). Concurrently, prefrontal cerebral hemodynamics and autonomic nervous system activity were monitored via functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and heart rate variability (HRV), respectively. Subjective cognitive load was evaluated using the NASA-Task Load Index (NASA-TLX). Results Compared to the NC group, the ND group exhibited significant deterioration in WM accuracy and speed, accompanied by reduced prefrontal cortex (PFC) activation and attenuated parasympathetic activity (reflected by decreased HRV high-frequency power). The ND+TEAS group demonstrated a reversal of these effects, showing superior WM performance, enhanced PFC oxygenation, and increased vagally-mediated HRV indices relative to the ND group. Crucially, mediation analysis revealed that the improvement in WM performance following TEAS was mediated by its effect on augmenting PFC activation, which in turn was associated with increased parasympathetic tone. Conclusions TEAS at the Yintang acupoint effectively alleviates nap deprivation-induced WM impairment. The mechanism appears to involve the enhancement of parasympathetic nervous activity and the subsequent facilitation of prefrontal cortical function. These findings provide novel experimental evidence for the brain-heart interaction as a pathway for cognitive enhancement and position TEAS as a viable, non-invasive strategy to bolster cognitive resilience in populations susceptible to circadian fatigue, such as clinical staff.

items.title: A dataset of structural, functional, and diffusion MRI with detailed reading behavior in older adults
items.abstract: Reading is a critical skill in modern society. Most research on reading is conducted in school age children or young adults. However, acquired brain disorders often affect reading ability, and these disorders tend to occur in older adults. It is therefore critical to examine the normative distribution of reading behavior and the brain basis of reading in older adults. Here, we provide trial-wise single word and pseudoword oral reading and lexical decision data, as well as structural, functional, and diffusion-weighted MRI data from 115 neurotypical adults (109 with scanning data) aged 22 to 84 years (mean = 59). Accuracy, reaction times, and errors are provided for corpora that are parametrically modulated in frequency, imageability, and regularity for real words and consistency of spelling-sound mappings for pseudowords. This dataset includes raw behavioral data and participant- and item-wise behavioral summary scores, and minimally processed and fully processed MRI data. These data serve as a normative sample for reading behavior and as a valuable resource for identifying brain-behavior relationships in older adults.

items.title: Effects of interruptions on doctors’ diagnostic reasoning and diagnostic accuracy: an experimental study with internal medicine residents
items.abstract: Attention to medical errors, adverse events, and the resultant literature has grown exponentially over the last few years. Diagnostic errors can occur across various care settings and are multifactorial, encompassing system-related, cognitive, and patient-related errors. Among these factors, interruptions inevitably influence people’s decision-making and behavior. Interruption during a cognitive task can affect the quality of decision-making in knowledge-intensive work environments. This study investigated whether interruptions during case diagnosis affect doctors’ diagnostic accuracy. This is an experimental computer-based study in which doctors diagnose complex and simple cases with or without interruption during the diagnostic process. The interruption time was 20 to 40 seconds. Participants were interrupted after 20 seconds and 40 seconds. The participants were third-year internal medicine residents from 3 teaching hospitals in Khartoum, Sudan. The participants diagnosed eight clinical cases (4 simple cases and 4 complex cases) presented to them on a laptop computer. In half of the cases (2 simple and 2 complex), participants were interrupted by another task while diagnosing the case. The primary outcome was diagnostic accuracy for simple and complex cases, with and without interruption. We also measured time spent diagnosing the cases. For inter-rater agreement, raters agreed on their judgments; diagnostic accuracy was scored as 1 for completely correct, 0.5 for partially correct, and 0 for incorrect, and differences were resolved through discussion to reach final agreement. Mean diagnostic accuracy (range: 0 – 1) was lower when participants were interrupted during diagnosis, both for simple (0.96, 95% confidence interval 0.92 to 1.00, without interruption; 0.74, 95% confidence interval 0.65 to 0.84, with interruption; p < .01) and for complex cases (0.78, 95% confidence interval 0.67 to 0.89, without interruption vs 0.58, 95% confidence interval 0.51 to 0.65 with interruption; p = .01). Interruptions caused the doctors to spend less time diagnosing both simple and complex cases. The ANOVA showed a significant main effect of case complexity: for simple cases, participants spent 47.9 seconds with interruption compared with 62.2 seconds without interruption, with p-value < .01. For complex cases, the time spent was 53.6 seconds with interruption and 89.0 seconds without interruption, with a p-value < .01. The study provided experimental evidence that interruptions during the diagnostic process may cause reduced diagnostic accuracy and altered diagnostic processing time. Interruptions affect the diagnosis of both simple and complex clinical cases and may therefore threaten patient safety. Interruptions in real settings are even more pervasive and potentially more distracting than the ones used in this experiment. Future studies may need clinically relevant distractions such as a pager going off that needs to be answered, nursing discussion, or interference from co-patients.

items.title: Affect-aware human-agent conversations: towards empathic LLM interaction
items.abstract: Abstract Large Language Models can produce supportive responses, but their apparent empathic behavior is usually grounded only in explicit textual input. This paper presents Empathic Extended Prompting a real-time affect-aware framework that enriches human--LLM conversation with facial affective descriptors to support perceived empathic attunement. The system integrates FaceReader-based affective descriptors into the LLM context, including emotional intensity, valence, and arousal. We evaluated the approach in a within-subjects study with N=20 participants, comparing an affect-aware experimental condition with an empathic text-only baseline. Results favored the affect-aware condition on key perceived qualities of the interaction, particularly emotional intelligence and mood responsiveness. These findings suggest that real-time affective context may add relational grounding to LLM conversations without reducing usability or eliciting uncanny-like perceptions.

items.title: Lake hydrochemistry and aquatic plant diversity across permafrost landscapes of Yakutia, Eastern Siberia
items.abstract: Central Yakutia in eastern Siberia is characterized by abundant lakes in permafrost-thaw depressions, named alaas. They constitute the traditional cultural landscape that is home to the indigenous Sakha people, providing critical ecosystem services. This study aims at assessing present-day lake characteristics and exploring their drivers based on lake hydrochemistry and aquatic and terrestrial plant diversity derived from sedimentary DNA in surface sediments. Macrophyte diversity reflects different lake types distinguished using both lake morphology and hydrochemistry. It also reveals a dominance of brackish water-tolerant cosmopolitan submerged macrophytes across all lakes, particularly Stuckenia and Potamogeton . In contrast, Myriophyllum and M. verticillatum are exclusively found in mountain lakes and freshwater lakes in the lowlands. The hydrochemical analysis reveals a clear distinction between low-mineralised mountain lakes and the highly variable hydrochemistry of the lowland lakes with much higher mineral content. Mountain lake hydrochemistry seems to be mainly determined by climate, whereas environmental drivers of hydrochemistry in lowland thermokarst lakes are more diverse. New thermokarst lakes are characterised by high dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and mainly located in forests. In contrast, connected alaas lakes, typically located in large alaas systems with settlements and active land use, display lower DOC and mineralisation, despite their location close to anthropogenic influence. We assume that temporary high discharge, such as during snowmelts, enables dilution, thus lowering organic and mineral contents. Future warming may lead to prolonged exposure to evaporation, but also to increased hydrological connectivity and increase in the number of connected alaas lakes, thereby potentially providing more freshwater to the region.

items.title: Ecological change in the native Scottish pinewoods since 1971 – data from the Bunce 2018–2022 re-survey
items.abstract: The native pinewoods of Scotland are acknowledged to be an important ecological resource, both for their biodiversity value and as a cultural and amenity resource. Due to the unique nature of the habitat and its limited range, it plays a critical role as an early warning system for broader environmental issues. In the late 1960s and 70s, increased concern was expressed regarding a decline in the status and management of the pinewoods. In response to the concerns, an ecological monitoring survey was initiated by R. G. H. Bunce of the Nature Conservancy in 1971, recording ground flora, tree information, soils and other descriptive attributes. Since that time, interest in the pinewoods has increased further, and there is a general consensus that the habitat is more vulnerable than ever. Thanks to a recent repeat survey between 2018 and 2022, questions addressing the threats and changes occurring in the pinewoods can now be explored in a statistically robust way. These questions include issues surrounding the impacts of deer grazing, regeneration, the balance between native and exotic species, local disturbances, trends in ground flora species occurrences, climate change and recovery from acidification. The new data from the 2018–2022 survey are now publicly available via the following DOI: https://doi.org/10.5285/5e268e86-4a4f-4112-bf2d-c3b0179c915c (Smart et al., 2023). Change data are available at: https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.34574874 (Wood et al., 2026).

items.title: Social Distance and Fungal Disease in an Australian Wild Lizard Population
items.abstract: Abstract Social living often confers substantial fitness benefits; however, close spatial association among individuals can also elevate opportunities for pathogen transmission, especially where populations are dense. Despite this, the extent to which avoidance behaviours are expressed by wild reptiles facing fungal disease remains unclear. We examined Eastern Water Dragons (Intellagama lesueurii) in Roma Street Parklands, Brisbane, Australia, where a population is affected by the emerging fungal pathogen Nannizziopsis barbatae (Nb). Using a five-year dataset (2018–2023) spanning 146 individuals, we quantified social distance as the minimum distance to the nearest neighbour, in relation to the number of diseased conspecifics that overlapped each individual’s seasonal core home area. Shorter social distances were observed in core home ranges with more diseased conspecifics. However, this pattern was weaker when the focal individual was diseased. Diseased focal dragons were often observed at larger distances than healthy individuals, even when the number of diseased conspecifics was high. Together, these patterns indicate a context-dependent spacing response associated with disease status and local disease context, suggesting that infection risk constrains density-driven proximity. Our findings provide new insights into how disease pressure shapes social spacing in reptiles and contribute to a broader understanding of behavioural responses to emerging infectious fungal diseases.

items.title: Evaluating MaxEnt Modeling Strategies for Mapping the Climatic Suitability of Five Pest Insects in the Contiguous United States Under Climate Change Scenarios
items.abstract: Species distribution models depend on modeling choices. We used MaxEnt for five pest insects in the contiguous United States, four introduced and one native: the brown marmorated stink bug (Halyomorpha halys), corn earworm (Helicoverpa zea, native), spongy moth (Lymantria dispar dispar), Diaprepes root weevil (Diaprepes abbreviatus) and spotted lanternfly (Lycorma delicatula). Models trained on US records and the 1970–2000 climate were projected to 2021–2040 and 2041–2060 under four emission pathways with five climate models, mainly ACCESS-CM2. We varied m, the share of background points drawn near the records over the whole country and inside species-specific accessible areas. No single m was best in either extent. The Boyce index separated the settings, while the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) changed little for m≤0.75. Removing out-of-range records made a uniform background clearly best for the spongy moth. Averaged over climate models, the suitable area decreased by 2041–2060 for four species and increased for the root weevil. Its size, and for two species its sign, depended on the climate model; the corn earworm loss and root weevil gain also depended on the calibration area. Permutation-importance rankings changed between background draws. The maps show climatic suitability, not forecasts of occupation.

items.title: Field testing of floating mat systems for grass cultivation and biochar generation under variable weather conditions
items.abstract: Variable weather conditions can substantially affect the stability and performance of a floating treatment wetland used to cultivate aquatic plants. This study evaluates the field performance and ecological potential of a floating foam mat designed to support aquatic plant growth and provide multiple benefits, including accumulation of nitrogen and phosphorus in plant biomass, atmospheric carbon sequestration, heavy metal removal, and biochar production. Plant growth trials were conducted in a watershed using 10 modular floating mats containing two aquatic macrophytes, common rush ( Juncus effusus ) and Switchgrass ( Panicum virgatum ), from mid-June to December 2025 (6 months) to assess vegetation growth, biomass composition, and pyrolysis product yields. Biomass monitoring showed that J. effusus had a root length of 64 cm (2′1″) and a stem length of 67 cm (2′2″), while P. virgatum had the highest root length of 97.5 cm (3′2″) and a stem length of 128 cm (4′2″) over a five-month period. The plant survival rate for each mat ranged from 90 to 92% by the end of harvesting. The Carbon, Hydrogen, Nitrogen, and Sulfur (CHNS) analysis revealed that P. virgatum roots had the highest concentrations of nitrogen (2.2%) and sulfur (0.3%). The J. effusus stem had higher concentrations of carbon (~ 45%) and hydrogen (~ 6%), like P. virgatum . Elemental concentrations showed high potassium (K) levels (> 10,000 ppm) in both biomasses. Furthermore, the highest biochar yields were obtained from pyrolyzed J. effusus root collected from the pool (JE-PR; 0.48 g/g) and P. virgatum root collected from the watershed (PV-WR; 0.42 g/g). The lowest yields were observed for J. effusus combined samples from the watershed (JE-WC; 0.35 g/g) and P. virgatum stems from the watershed (PV-WS; 0.39 g/g). These variations in the amounts of pyrolysis products and elemental compositions highlight differences in biomass chemical composition among plant parts. This study provides practical insights into the performance of a floating mat under variable weather conditions and explores the potential to combine aquatic plant cultivation with biomass valorization through pyrolysis.

items.title: Spatiotemporal Modeling of Aedes aegypti in La Guajira: An Approach Based on Environmental Suitability (MaxEnt) and Temporal Dependence (ARIMA)
items.abstract: Environmental, climatic, and socioeconomic conditions coexist in La Guajira, northwestern Colombia, which may be conducive to dengue (DENV) transmission. However, knowledge gaps remain regarding the distribution and temporal dynamics of its primary vector, Aedes aegypti. In this study, the potential distribution and autoregressive temporal persistence of Aedes aegypti in the municipality of Manaure were assessed by incorporating climatic variables into maximum entropy (MaxEnt) and autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models with the goals of identifying areas of entomological risk and supporting vector surveillance. First, occurrence records were obtained from published literature, the National Institute of Health’s collection of medically important insects, the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF), and field surveys to model environmental suitability. Nineteen WorldClim v2.1 bioclimatic variables were initially considered to model the potential distribution using MaxEnt, and model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Second, the temporal dynamics of Ae. aegypti were assessed over one year in two neighborhoods that exhibited high and low DENV incidence using Prokopack aspirators for indoor sampling. The MaxEnt models exhibited good predictive performance (AUC > 0.8), and the annual temperature range (BIO7) was identified as the most influential predictor. To address the temporal dynamics, a total of 2313 mosquitoes (53% females) were collected. The La Cruzada (LC) neighborhood exhibited greater temporal dependence (φ1 = 0.679; p < 0.001) than the Altos de Salinas (AS) neighborhood did (φ1 = 0.309; p = 0.02), whereas rainfall that occurred one to two weeks earlier was positively associated with an increase in female abundance in both neighborhoods. The integration of spatial and temporal models facilitated the identification and prioritization of risk areas. At the spatial level, MaxEnt identified patterns that were consistent with the ecology of the vector at the state level; in municipalities in which entomological risk is highest, time series analyses could be conducted to improve forecasts and planning for the integrated management of arboviruses transmitted by the Ae. aegypti mosquito.

items.title: A DPSIR-Based Evidence-to-Design Framework for Restoration Readiness at Pallikaranai Marshland, Chennai
items.abstract: Abstract Purpose Urban coastal wetlands face encroachment, pollution, fragmented governance and disputed boundaries. Pallikaranai Marshland in Chennai, India, a Ramsar site partly under Reserve Forest, is well documented ecologically, yet few studies link this evidence to planning that accounts for legal and spatial uncertainty. This study develops a framework to make that link. Methods An evidence-to-design framework was structured around three intervention families: Revive, Restore and Reconnect. Evidence was graded by source type and coded using the Drivers–Pressures–States–Impacts–Responses (DPSIR) framework. An intervention was included only when supported by graded evidence and at least one stated precondition (empirical, legal or safeguard-related). Each intervention was assigned a readiness class and tested under three boundary scenarios: the Reserve Forest limit, an interim Zone of Influence of 128.19 ha proposed in October 2026, and the full Ramsar boundary. Results The framework identified six interventions. Hydrological connectivity beyond the Reserve Forest and cross-agency governance depend on the boundary outcome. Most other interventions mainly await baseline surveys. Edge treatments and a pilot removal of Prosopis juliflora can proceed within the Reserve Forest, and several interventions keep the same readiness class across all scenarios. Conclusion The framework provides a transparent, transferable planning method that distinguishes evidentiary uncertainty from statutory dispute. This allows boundary-independent restoration to begin while legal questions remain unresolved.

items.title: First report of myiasis in the glass frog Cochranella granulosa (Anura: Centrolenidae) from Costa Rica
items.abstract: Abstract Myiasis, defined as the infestation of living vertebrates by dipteran larvae, is a widespread host-parasite interaction, still poorly documented among Neotropical amphibians. Here, we report the first documented case of myiasis in the glass frog Cochranella granulosa from Costa Rica. The observed individual was found harbouring numerous dipteran larvae and exhibited pale colouration and lethargic be​haviour, suggesting that the infestation likely compromised its survival. Only three published reports of anuran myiasis have previously been documented in Costa Rica, involving members of the families Bufonidae and Ranidae, whereas myiasis in Centrolenidae has been documented in the Neotropics only once, from Panama. This scarcity of records is unlikely to reflect the rarity of these interactions alone, and may instead be at least partly attributable to the limited attention given to this host-parasite interaction and to the difficulty of systematically detecting and documenting myiasis in wild amphibians. Our observation highlights the need for further research on this phenomenon in the Neotropics, particularly given the ongoing declines affecting both dipterans and amphibians worldwide.

items.title: divent: An R Package for Diversity Measures Based on Entropy
items.abstract: divent is an R package dedicated to the measurement of diversity in general, and biodiversity in particular.It provides functions to estimate 𝛼, 𝛽 and 𝛾 diversity of communities, including phylogenetic and functional diversity.It is a reboot of the entropart R package to make it easier to use and computationally more efficient.It also extends its functionality.Data may be abundance vectors or matrices (the number of individuals per species, possibly per site), lists of individuals, or point patterns to address spatially-explicit diversity.Random communities can be simulated (function rcommunity()) and spatialized (function rspcommunity()).The main functions allow computing:• Taxonomic entropy: HCDT entropy (ent_tsallis()) including Shannon and Simpson's entropies.• Phylogenetic (ent_phylo()) or functional (ent_similarity()) entropy when dissimilarities between species are taken into account in a dendrogram or a similarity matrix.• Effective numbers of species, aka Hill numbers, for all entropies (div_hill(), div_phylo(), div_similarity()).• Diversity partitioning (div_part()), i.e. 𝛼, 𝛽 and 𝛾 diversity of a set of communities.• Diversity profiles (profile_hill(), profile_phylo(), profile_similarity()), with respect to the order of diversity.• Diversity accumulation curves (accum_hill()) with respect to the sample size or coverage.• Spatial accumulation of diversity (accum_sp_hill()) with respect to the distance from individuals, with maps (plot_map()).Many estimators are proposed, with sensible automatic choice, to deal with incomplete sampling. items.title: Pathways to carbon neutrality by 2040: Modeling a coastal-urban city nexus with blue carbon integration
items.abstract: Abstract Acknowledging climate change is easy; designing and implementing effective, sustainable management strategies to mitigate it is far more challenging. To reduce carbon emissions, identifying actionable levers—particularly in complex socio-ecological systems (SESs) or city nexus—is critical for policymakers. The SES approach provides a robust lens for connecting anthropogenic and natural drivers of greenhouse gas increases. Using qualitative and possibilistic tools, like the Ecological Discrete-Event Network (EDEN) framework, we integrated various variables (e.g., transportation, maritime activities, land artificialization, and blue carbon ecosystem development) into a decision-support model. We developed the Socio-Economic Net (SEN) model to evaluate whether the costal-urban La Rochelle Metropolitan Area (France) could achieve carbon neutrality by 2040 through adaptive management, while addressing 16 of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Given prevailing social resistance to behavioral change, we hypothesized that this transition would be unattainable within the timeframe. However, our results demonstrated the opposite: carbon neutrality, alongside SDGs 13–17, was achievable under specific policy-driven scenarios. These included the implementation of green policies at national/EU levels, a shift from conventional to organic agriculture, and demographic stabilization. Critically, the SEN model revealed that top-down actions are essential to enable bottom-up changes, offering multiple, actionable pathways for local governments. For environmental managers and policymakers, this study demonstrates that systemic, multi-scale interventions can overcome apparent barriers to sustainability while also highlighting the trade-offs—economic, social, and ecological—that must be navigated. Finally, the EDEN framework offers a replicable approach for other coastal cities seeking to balance development and climate goals.

items.title: Global Bibliometric Analysis of Citizen Science for Biodiversity Exploration: Trends, Methodological Advances, and Future Directions
items.abstract: The rapid growth of citizen science since 2010 has positioned this domain as a primary source of global biodiversity data, fundamentally transforming biological inventory. This study aims to map global publication trends, taxonomic and ecosystem biases, international collaboration patterns, and adoption of advanced analytical methods in citizen science biodiversity research. Using a structured bibliometric approach, we analyzed publications from 2000 to 2025 retrieved from the LeapSpace database, applying co-authorship network analysis, keyword co-occurrence mapping, and citation analysis. Our findings reveal exponential publication growth post-2010, anchored by highly cited foundational papers from 2009–2012 (Bonney et al., Silvertown, Sullivan). The field is thematically concentrated around biodiversity monitoring, conservation, and data quality, with keyword clusters emphasizing ecology (BIO), public participation (PUBLIC), methodological rigor (DATA), and spatial analysis (GEO). Publication output remains heavily concentrated in the Global North (USA, UK, Germany), with limited Global South representation. Taxonomic bias strongly favours birds (54% of papers), while ecosystems such as tropical rainforests, deep-sea environments, and soil systems are severely underrepresented. Advanced methods including machine learning and spatial bias correction have seen increased adoption in recent years yet remain underrepresented in titles and abstracts compared to general terms like "crowdsourcing." These results underscore the need to strengthen data validation, mitigate spatial and taxonomic biases, reduce North-South disparities, and adopt cross-method integration models to support global conservation targets and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Keywords: citizen science, ecosystem, biodiversity, crowdsourcing, taxa

items.title: GREEN EDUCATION AND THE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS IN THE SCHOOL CURRICULUM
items.abstract: Sustainable development requires a generation of learners who understand environmental challenges and are equipped to transform societies. Green education embeds environmental awareness, climate change literacy, and sustainable practices across school curricula, aligning classroom learning with the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This chapter examines the theoretical foundations of Education for Sustainable Development (ESD), surveys global and Indian initiatives, and proposes strategies for integrating sustainability into various subjects. Drawing on cases from Finland’s cross-curricular theme, Ontario’s Eco Schools, Australia’s Resource Smart program, New Jersey’s climate-change standards, and India’s National Curriculum Framework and eco-club movement, it illustrates how schools can move beyond isolated environmental lessons to achieve systemic change. The chapter discusses pedagogical approaches, such as project-based learning, fieldwork, and community partnerships, highlights teacher training needs, and analyses challenges related to time, resources, and assessment. It concludes by offering policy recommendations and a framework for evaluating impact.

items.title: New knowledge for feral cat (Felis catus) management: Space-use patterns and responses to food provisioning in New Zealand
items.abstract: Global biodiversity is declining, with invasive mammalian predators recognised as a primary cause. In Aotearoa New Zealand, feral cats have caused declines and extinctions of native species that evolved without mammalian predators and lack effective defences against them. Globally, feral cats (Felis catus) are among the most damaging invasive predators but are difficult to manage because they are cryptic, behaviourally flexible, and neophobic. Addressing knowledge gaps in how cats move within landscapes and how their activity can be concentrated at predictable locations would improve our ability to detect and control their populations. Knowledge of feral cat space use in New Zealand is largely based on radio-telemetry studies with sparse location data and GPS-tracking studies concentrated in unforested dryland environments of eastern Te Waipounamu/the South Island. The findings from these studies have helped establish the foundation of our understanding of feral cat spatial ecology in New Zealand but have not been combined to identify consistent patterns across landscapes. I investigated feral cat space use across eastern Te Waipounamu using GPS data from 83 cats across eight sites spanning pastoral farmland, open dryland, high-country valleys, and scrub– tussock ecosystems. I examined habitat selection and selection for potential movement corridors using a used–available resource selection function and tested whether these patterns varied across diel periods, seasons, and estimated nocturnal ambience derived from cloud cover and lunar illumination. I also investigated food provisioning as a means of attracting feral cats and concentrating their activity. Food provisioning involves establishing a substantial, predictable food resource to encourage repeated visitation by scavenging cats. Although used during feral cat removal operations in New Zealand, its effectiveness at localising activity and increasing encounters has not been formally evaluated. I used GPS and camera-trap data from Sheffield and Kōwai Bush in inland Canterbury and Maukahuka/Auckland Island to assess whether provisioning could concentrate feral cat activity and improve detection. Across eastern Te Waipounamu, feral cats strongly selected closed habitats, including willows, dense scrub, and exotic conifers, and avoided open habitats. Feral cats also showed positive selection for locations near all three habitat-edge types and most linear-feature classes. Diel period and season modified the strength of several habitat and corridor associations, whereas estimated nocturnal ambience had weaker and less consistent effects. At Sheffield, most GPS-tracked cats shifted closer to provisioning sites after encountering them. Camera traps in inland Canterbury and Maukahuka recorded repeated visitation, although visit frequency and duration varied with food type, persistence, and site context. Most notably, monitoring at two Maukahuka provisioning sites detected up to 15 putative adult cats and two dependent-kitten groups within five days, compared with up to nine individuals across a 30-camera grid over one month. Feral cat surveillance and control may benefit from the findings of this study. Firstly, closed woody habitats, their associated edges, and strongly selected linear features such as tracks may provide effective locations for deploying monitoring and removal tools in eastern Te Waipounamu. Secondly, by repeatedly attracting cats to predictable locations, food provisioning may provide conservation managers with an additional means of supporting targeted surveillance and removal efforts in New Zealand.

items.title: Environmental Management System and Lifecycle Carbon Accounting for Road Pavement Works Programme
items.abstract: Abstract Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII) has embedded an Environmental Management System (EMS) into its pavement management programme to enable lifecycle carbon accounting and support national climate goals. Through the EMS, TII quantifies Global Warming Potential (GWP) for individual pavement segments across the national road network, capturing emissions from vehicle operations, construction activities, material use, and maintenance-related delays. By comparing “do-nothing” and programmed treatment scenarios, TII identifies opportunities to reduce carbon emissions while maintaining performance and cost efficiency. This data-driven approach enables TII to optimise maintenance strategies for both lifecycle cost and lifecycle carbon. The integration of EMS into pavement planning directly supports Ireland’s climate action targets by reducing the carbon footprint of essential infrastructure works. It also allows for more informed trade-offs between sustainability, service levels, and budget. This methodology enables TII to apply carbon reduction as a core criterion in asset management.

items.title: Common Ground: Aligning Forest Protection and the Transition Away from Fossil Fuels
items.abstract: The transition away from fossil fuels and the protection of forests are both essential to achieving global climate goals. This UNEP policy brief examines how the two COP30 Roadmaps can be implemented together, focusing on the land-use implications of bioenergy, including biofuels, woody biomass and bioenergy with carbon capture and storage, as well as pressures from transition minerals. It explores how policy choices can prevent the energy transition from driving deforestation, forest degradation and competition for land, while recognizing the role of sustainable bioenergy in climate mitigation. The brief provides recommendations for aligning energy and land-use planning, strengthening carbon accounting and safeguards, and protecting forests, biodiversity and local livelihoods.

items.title: Patterns of soil organic carbon, nutrients, and vegetation traits along a tidal elevation gradient in subtropical artificial mangroves
items.abstract: Tidal elevation is a key environmental factor influencing planted mangrove growth and soil processes. However, many previous studies have focused on surface soil organic carbon (SOC) or single nutrient indicators, and it remains unclear whether tidal elevation is consistently associated with soil carbon (C), nitrogen (N), and phosphorus (P) concentrations and stocks throughout the 0–100 cm profile in young Kandelia obovata plantations, especially across multiple coastal bays. This study examined vegetation attributes and soil C, N, and P concentrations and stocks along a tidal elevation gradient in approximately 8-year-old K. obovata plantations across three coastal bays in Wenzhou, Zhejiang, China. Vegetation attributes, soil physicochemical properties, and SOC, total nitrogen (TN), and total phosphorus (TP) concentrations and stocks were quantified within the 0–100 cm soil profile. In models accounting for non-independence at the plot scale and variability at the sampling point scale, elevation and soil depth were significantly correlated with soil organic carbon (SOC), total nitrogen (TN), and total phosphorus (TP) concentrations ( P < 0.05). Across the 0–100 cm profile, SOC stocks were significantly higher at high elevation (HE) than at low elevation (LE) ( P < 0.05), whereas middle elevation (ME) showed intermediate values and did not differ significantly from HE or LE. TN and TP stocks did not differ significantly among elevation groups, indicating contrasting patterns between soil carbon and nutrient pools along the elevation gradient. Higher elevation plots were also associated with greater vegetation biomass and larger root C and N pools. Overall, tidal elevation was more strongly associated with vegetation and carbon-related soil variables than with TN and TP stocks in these 8-year-old plantations. These findings suggest that soil carbon indicators may be useful for monitoring planted mangrove dynamics and for informing site selection in high-latitude coastal ecosystems.

items.title: From single‑target conservation to comprehensive resource utilization: A case of VEP accounting for the eco-cultural heritage in Beijing
items.abstract: Eco-cultural heritage faces the dilemma of transitioning from single-target conservation to comprehensive resource utilization. This study introduces the Value of Ecosystem Product in specific geographical units (VEP) theory to address this challenge, using Beijing’s Three Hills and Five Gardens as a case study. The research develops a three-dimensional analytical framework encompassing value identification, composite accounting, and layered transformation. Theoretically, it extends VEP from natural ecosystems to eco‑cultural composite systems by proposing a “three‑tier progressive” evaluation paradigm that distinguishes monetizable, quantifiable cultural services with partial monetization, and non‑quantifiable values, together with a “layered matching” transformation principle. This framework clarifies the identification criteria and transformation pathways for each value type while defining a normative “monetization boundary” that protects non‑tradable values from market forces. A simplified accounting of the Western Beijing rice fields is provided to illustrate the framework’s application in principle; this is a methodological demonstration rather than an empirical valuation, as it relies on secondary data and hypothetical assumptions rather than primary field surveys. The study also outlines a three-stage transformation model covering activation, appreciation, and realization, and identifies governance bottlenecks including fragmented property rights. The central argument is that value transformation should distinguish between tradable and non‑tradable values, and achieve a virtuous cycle of conservation and development through the synergy of market mechanisms and public safeguards. Policy implications are offered for the valuation and transformation of eco‑cultural heritage, though the proposed framework requires further empirical testing across diverse heritage contexts.

items.title: Totemism as Indigenous ecological governance: crocodile conservation, cultural ecology, and environmental stewardship among the Paga and Nyibivian clans in Ghana
items.abstract: Introduction This study examines clan totemism as a socio-ecological governance system among the Paga and Nyibivian crocodile clans in Ghana and its implications for conservation and sustainable development. Methods A qualitative multi-site case study involved 37 participants, including clan leaders, traditional priests and cultural enthusiasts, recruited through purposive and snowball sampling. Data from semi-structured interviews, focus group discussions and participant observation were analysed using inductive and deductive reflexive thematic analysis with MAXQDA (v24.4.1). Results Participants described totemic beliefs, customary rules and rituals as shaping responsibilities towards crocodiles and water bodies. Paga accounts emphasised pond protection and community education, whereas Nyibivian accounts highlighted customary sanctions, pollution prevention, water scarcity and habitat support needs. Ecological outcomes were not independently measured. Discussion Indigenous ecological knowledge and customary authority may support culturally legitimate environmental responsibility and complement formal conservation governance through community partnerships, although their ecological effectiveness requires independent assessment.

items.title: Influencing mechanisms of settlement layout evolution in counties adjacent to protected areas from a production–living–ecology perspective: Evidence from Wuyishan, China
items.abstract: Land-cover change in the peripheries of protected areas (PAs)—particularly settlement expansion—threatens biodiversity conservation and landscape connectivity. However, the spatiotemporal layouts of settlements around PAs, the spatial extent of their influence, and the influencing mechanisms remain unclear. Using hot spot detection, landscape pattern analysis and Boolean overlay, the evolution of settlement layouts around Wuyishan National Park from 1990 to 2020 was analyzed. Furthermore, an Optimized Parameters-based Geographical Detector was integrated with the Driver–Pressure–State–Impact–Response framework to quantitatively and qualitatively interpret plausible association pathways from a Production–Living–Ecology Perspective. Based on these analyses, tiered buffer-zone management strategies were proposed. The results show that: (1) The settlement area expanded from 6232.68 to 7510.68 hm 2 , with the 20–30 km buffer zone forming a hotspot and the 0–10 km buffer zone a coldspot. (2) The overall settlement landscape pattern exhibited progressive expansion and agglomeration, characterized by increasing patch size, enhanced connectivity, and reduced spatial dispersion. (3) Four spatial evolution patterns were identified, with edge expansion dominating (63.7% of total change), primarily within the 20–30 km buffer zone. (4) Interactions between ecological and living factors had greater explanatory power than production factors, with NDVI ∩ population density showing the highest explanatory power (q = 0.683). Our findings offer a fresh perspective on understanding the complexities of human-land relationships in PA peripheries and provide a reference framework for buffer-zone management that may be adapted to other PAs facing similar socio-ecological pressures.

items.title: A Matter of Timing and Traits: The Role of Vegetation Type in the Conservation of Arthropod Natural Enemies
items.abstract: Agricultural intensification has reduced and simplified many non-crop habitats that support arthropod biodiversity and ecological interactions. In Alberta’s Aspen Parkland, canola fields occur alongside herbaceous margins, treed borders, and remnant native plant communities, creating opportunities to examine how arthropods use crop and non-crop habitats in a region where agriculture is embedded within structurally diverse vegetation. In this thesis, I examined arthropod activity and interactions in two study contexts. First, I used canola field margins to evaluate how arthropods with different ecological roles respond to crop–margin habitats, margin vegetation type, and seasonal changes in crop development. Second, I used plant–natural enemy interaction networks from native grasslands to examine how temporal resolution, floral traits, and flower abundance shape the importance of plant species for flower-visiting natural enemies. Together, these chapters evaluate how local vegetation context, seasonal dynamics, and species ecology influence arthropod activity, movement, and interactions in managed and less-managed habitats. In canola field margins, social wasp activity differed between herbaceous and treed margins, but these differences changed through the growing season and among species. Treed margins supported higher activity for some species and generated higher cumulative estimates of potential worker activity at field-relevant scales, suggesting that woody borders may provide important nesting habitat for social wasps. Herbaceous margins also contributed to wasp activity, but with different species assemblages and seasonal patterns. Specific vegetation variables measured within treed margins did not explain variation in wasp activity, suggesting broad vegetation structural class was more important than any specific vegetation component. I also examined directional activity of the introduced ground beetle Pterostichus melanarius between canola fields and adjacent margins. A total of 66,619 individuals were collected from 1,837 trap samples. Movement at the crop–margin interface changed with crop development and harvest. During partial bloom, captures were higher on trap faces oriented toward the crop, indicating movement from margins into canola, while activity-density inside the crop increased. During harvest and post-harvest, movement shifted toward field margins. These results suggest that field margins were associated with movement into canola during crop development and movement away from the crop during harvest-associated disturbance. In investigating use of vegetation to better conserve natural enemies, it is important to also consider the effects of non-crop vegetation on potential pests. I found that activity of adult Pieris rapae (Lepidoptera, Pieridae, an herbivore of brassicaceous plants), peaked during canola flowering and was higher in herbaceous than treed margins during the main activity period. Movement direction to and from the margins was equal, such that its use of margins was not detectably different from its use of crops. This pattern contrasts with that of natural enemies observed in the same study system, which showed vegetation-type- and time-specific associations with field margins, potentially reflecting differences in nesting or resource use. In contrast, the broadly distributed and largely non-directional movements of P. rapae provided little evidence that adults selected field margin vegetation over crop vegetation. Field margins therefore did not appear to uniquely support or retain P. rapae within the landscape, perhaps because adults could meet their requirements in either habitat. Finally, I examined plant–natural enemy visitation networks in native grasslands. Floral traits and flower abundance both influenced plant importance, but their effects depended on temporal resolution. In season-aggregated networks, abundance effects were more apparent, whereas temporally resolved networks revealed stronger trait effects after accounting for abundance. These results show that temporal aggregation can obscure trait-based patterns and can change how plant roles are interpreted in ecological networks. Overall, this thesis shows that the ecological function of field margins and plant communities depends on the organisms being considered, the local vegetation context, and the temporal scale of analysis. Herbaceous and treed margins did not have a single, consistent effect across taxa. Instead, social wasps, ground beetles, and butterflies responded differently according to their life history, movement behavior, and resource use. Similarly, plant importance in native grasslands depended on whether interactions were evaluated across the full season or within shorter phenological windows. By documenting how several functionally important insect groups respond to margin type, crop phenology, seasonal timing, and floral resources, this thesis provides taxon-specific information needed to guide more targeted habitat management in canola agroecosystems.

items.title: Detecting regular precession using a new gravitational waveform model directly parameterized by both precession amplitude and frequency
items.abstract: Nearly 210 binary black hole (BBH) mergers have been observed by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA network during its four observing runs. Generic BBHs are spinning, and their spins are misaligned with the orbital angular momentum $\vec{L}$. These misaligned spins cause $\vec{L}$ to precess in a cone with dimensionless precession amplitude $\tildeθ$ and frequency $\tildeΩ$ about the nearly constant direction of the total angular momentum. This precession modulates the observed GWs. We propose a model of regularly precessing (RP) waveforms that incorporates $\tildeθ$ and $\tildeΩ$ directly as parameters. We investigate how these waveforms vary as functions of these precessional parameters, as well as binary orientation and sky location. We use the Lindblom criterion to estimate that precession can be detected in a RP source with signal-to-noise ratio $ρ$ when the mismatch $ε$ with a non-precessing (NP) source with otherwise identical parameters exceeds $1/2ρ^2$. Precession is most detectable when $\vec{L}$ precesses through configurations we call +~nulls during the inspiral. At +~nulls, a NP source only emits +-polarization to which the GW detector is insensitive. The large mismatch between a RP source and this vanishing NP signal enhances the detectability of precession. We also explore the detectability of precession as a function of redshift $z$ for different BBH populations. We find that for BBHs with isotropically oriented maximal spins, precession is detectable in a majority of systems out to $z \approx 0.3$ for chirp masses $10 \lesssim M_c/M_\odot \lesssim 40$ and mass ratios $q \gtrsim 0.5$. Reduced spin magnitudes or greater alignment between the spins and $\vec{L}$ make it difficult to observe beyond $z \approx 0.1$. (abridged)

items.title: UNCOVER/MegaScience Finds Uniform and Highly Bursty Star Formation at 3 < z < 9, Consistent with the High-redshift UV Luminosity Function
items.abstract: Abstract Star formation timescales are key to understanding fundamental physics like feedback mechanisms, as well as the abundance of bright galaxies at z > 10. We investigate galaxy star formation histories (SFHs) and their evolution across z ∼ 3–9 by measuring the line-to-UV ratio ( R line ) and line equivalent width (EW) of H α +[N ii ] and [O iii ]+H β directly from UNCOVER/MegaScience spectro-photometry without relying on a specific SFH or nebular line modeling. Our photometric measurements recover R line and EW to 10. This suggests that no significant evolution in star formation burstiness is required to explain the abundance of UV-bright galaxies at high redshift.

items.title: Encoding Topological Magnetic Spin Textures with Topological Light
items.abstract: Abstract Structured light fields, featuring unique topological properties and high tunability, have opened new frontiers in light–matter interactions with magnetic systems, yet ultrafast, reconfigurable optical writing of diverse topological magnetic textures remains a significant challenge. Here, we systematically investigate the encoding mechanism of topological light in magnets via the higher-order Poincaré sphere. By relating the light’s winding number to the topological charge of magnetic textures, we establish a light–magnetism topological connection. This framework enables ultrafast, all-optical encoding of diverse topological spin textures─skyrmions, antiskyrmions, and skyrmion bags. Our work advances the understanding and all-optical control of topological magnetism and offers a promising route for skyrmion-based devices.

items.title: Coherence Protection of Mobile Spin Qubits in Silicon via Dressed-state Shuttling
items.abstract: Mobile spin qubit architectures promise flexible connectivity for efficient quantum error correction and relaxed device layout constraints, but their viability rests on preserving spin coherence during transport. While shuttling transforms spatial disorder into time-dependent noise, its net impact on spin coherence remains an open question. Here we demonstrate systematic noise mitigation during spin shuttling in a linear $^{28}$Si/SiGe quantum dot device. First, by passively reducing magnetic field gradients, we minimize charge-noise coupling to the spin and double the spatially averaged dephasing time $T_2^*(x_n)$ from $4.4$ to $8.5\,μ\text{s}$. Next, we exploit motional narrowing by periodically shuttling the qubit, achieving a further enhancement in coherence time up to $T_{2}^{*,sh} = 11.5\,μ\text{s}$. Finally, we incorporate dynamical decoupling techniques while periodically shuttling over distances exceeding $200\,\text{nm}$, reaching $T_\text{2}^{H,sh}= 32\,μ\text{s}$. For the same setup, we demonstrate that dressed-state shuttling provides robust protection against low-frequency noise with a decay time $T_R^{\text{sh}} = 21\,μ\text{s}$, without the overhead of pulsed control and allowing protection during one-way spin transport. By preserving coherence over timescales exceeding typical gate and readout operations, the demonstrated strategies establish mobile spin qubits as a viable solution for scalable silicon quantum processors.
