items.title: The 2MIG isolated AGNs – 3. Optical–IR variability and dust reverberation in the NLSy1 galaxies Mrk 42 and Mrk 493
items.abstract: Abstract We present an optical–infrared variability study of two isolated narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies, Mrk 42 and Mrk 493, using ZTF optical and WISE/NEOWISE W1/W2 light curves, supplemented by ATLAS, SDSS, Swift, and IAC80 data. We analyse colour–magnitude and flux–flux relations and measure optical–infrared reverberation lags using flux-randomisation and random-subset-selection (FR/RSS) realisations of the interpolated cross-correlation function after correcting the WISE light curves for the variable accretion-disc contribution. For Mrk 42, we obtain observed-frame lags of $54^{+13}_{-33}$ and $62^{+7}_{-35}$ d in W1 and W2, respectively. After applying the redshift/wavelength correction, these correspond to dust-response radii of $0.045^{+0.011}_{-0.028}$ and $0.052^{+0.006}_{-0.029}$ pc. For Mrk 493, the corresponding observed-frame lags are $94^{+18}_{-21}$ and $111^{+26}_{-24}$ d, giving corrected dust-response radii of $0.078^{+0.015}_{-0.017}$ and $0.092^{+0.021}_{-0.020}$ pc, respectively. Both galaxies show optical bluer-when-brighter behaviour, whereas their W1 − W2 responses differ: the relation is significant in Mrk 493 but not in Mrk 42, where host and circumnuclear dilution may be stronger. For Mrk 42, SDSS spectral decomposition provides a host-corrected active galactic nucleus (AGN) luminosity for the contextual broad-line region (BLR) comparison. The measured dust-response radii are broadly consistent with the low-luminosity extension and intrinsic scatter of published Rdust–Lbol relations. The major optical flare in Mrk 42 exhibits four broad internal maxima with an intra-flare timescale of approximately 45–47 d; non-uniform peak intervals and stochastic-model comparisons favour flare substructure within a broader accretion-driven event. Both galaxies follow the expected disc–hot-dust reverberation framework while exhibiting distinct colour and optical-variability phenomenology.

items.title: Improving the resolution of double white dwarf systems with spaceborne gravitational wave observatories using a robust astrophysical prior
items.abstract: Resolving the crowded population of double white dwarf (DWD) binaries in data from spaceborne gravitational wave (GW) observatories (e.g., LISA, Taiji) remains a major analysis challenge. Comparable performance on addressing this problem has been achieved with two main approaches: global fit, in which resolvable sources are estimated simultaneously from the data, and iterative, where sources are estimated one at a time and subtracted out from the data. While the latter is computationally efficient, methods developed under this approach have traditionally followed a frequentist framework that ignores astrophysical priors. This work incorporates a strong astrophysical prior, derived from the mass limits of detached white dwarfs and linking the GW signal frequency f with its time derivative f ̇ , into the iterative GBSIEVER pipeline. Applied to simulated LISA and LISA-Taiji network data, the method increases the number of confidently resolved sources by ≈ 7.3 % (LISA-only) and ≈ 14.6 % (network) at matched detection rate, respectively, and improves parameter estimation accuracy.

items.title: Weak-lensing mass calibration of Planck Sunyaev-Zel’dovich clusters with HSC-SSP Year 3 observations
items.abstract: We present a weak gravitational lensing mass calibration of 19 \textit{Planck} Sunyaev--Zel'dovich (SZ) selected galaxy clusters using shape measurements from the Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program (HSC-SSP) Year 3 shape catalog. We measure the stacked weak-lensing signal $ΔΣ(R)$ using per-cluster lensing weights that match the measurement pipeline's stacking scheme, and construct an analytical covariance matrix that includes shape noise and projected large-scale structure contributions. Our primary constraint on the SZ mass bias comes from a forward-modeling approach that integrates over the halo mass function while accounting for the \textit{Planck} SZ selection function, Eddington bias from log-normal scatter in the SZ mass proxy, and cluster miscentering. Fitting four free parameters, the log mass bias $\ln(1-b)$, the miscentered fraction $f_{\rm mis}$, the offset scale $σ_{\rm off}$, and the SZ scatter $σ_{\ln M}$, over the radial range $0.5$--$5.0\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, we obtain $1-b = 0.73^{+0.10}_{-0.11}$ with $χ^2/\mathrm{dof} = 5.2/5$ at an effective redshift $z_{\rm eff}\simeq 0.24$. This measurement is consistent with recent weak-lensing calibrations of SZ-selected clusters and supports the picture that significant mass bias corrections are required to reconcile cluster abundance measurements with primary cosmic microwave background constraints on cosmological parameters.

items.title: Data-driven by design: Building a reflective physics graduate program
items.abstract: Well-documented research on physics graduate education has demonstrated long-standing issues that hinder equitable student access and participation. Addressing these challenges can be particularly difficult because they are often rooted in entrenched disciplinary and departmental cultures that tend to be rigid and resistant to change. In this work, we aim to cultivate a data-driven culture of cyclic self-reflection and action to proactively identify and address issues that affect student well-being and success in both a new physics and a long-standing astrophysics graduate program within a single institution. Drawing primarily on qualitative data (open-ended survey responses and focus-group interview data) from 15 students in both programs, we collaborated with the program leadership to identify actionable steps for improvement. In this paper, we present findings on student experiences across the two programs and discuss implications for research and practice. More broadly, this work provides a framework for graduate programs seeking to build a data-driven culture that improves student experiences.

items.title: X-shooter DESI Lens Program: Sample characterization
items.abstract: Large imaging surveys in cosmology are detecting orders of magnitude more lens systems than previously known. This unprecedented dataset will provide robust constraints on cosmology and galaxy-evolution models. However, a careful, preliminary characterization of the lens and source samples is required. In this work, we report on a VLT/X-shooter observation program of 67 lens systems to characterize their spectroscopic redshift distribution. These systems were previously detected in the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Legacy Imaging Surveys with a deep residual neural network. We reduced the spectra and estimated redshifts from absorption and emission features, with quality flags based on feature robustness. We measured redshifts for 58 lenses and 57 sources. We identify two sources with indications of outflow in the shape of the emission lines and seven sources with rotating disks in O II or Hα. We find that the lens and source redshift success rates are independent of color and that source redshifts are independent of object magnitudes. In contrast, lens redshifts are mostly determined from absorption features, and their distribution is biased toward objects brighter than z_ <20. AB

items.title: Low-hard to high-soft spectral state transitions in the faintest early X-ray-detected optical tidal disruption event TDE 2025aarm
items.abstract: We report the X-ray and optical spectroscopic properties of årm, the second closest tidal disruption event (TDE) discovered to date. The proximity of this source (60 Mpc), combined with a deep and intense X-ray-monitoring campaign spanning six months, allowed us to probe the source down to an unprecedented 0.2--10 keV luminosity of $ at times close to the optical peak. This renders årm the faintest early-X-ray-detected TDE to date. After the first X-ray detection, the source brightened by nearly two orders of magnitude, reaching a peak luminosity of about four months after the optical peak. Through time-resolved X-ray spectral analysis, we find that årm evolved from an initially hard, power-law-dominated X-ray state into a softer, disk-dominated state as the luminosity increased, before hardening again at later times. Such low-hard-to-high-soft state transitions are commonly observed in black hole X-ray binaries (XRBs) but have not been reported in thermal TDEs previously. We show that the spectral evolution can be described by variations in the relative contributions of an accretion disk and a Comptonizing component, qualitatively resembling the disk--corona evolution observed in XRBs. We also present the results of our optical spectroscopic follow-up campaign with HET/LRS2, confirming the TDE classification and revealing N,III Bowen fluorescence features. The extremely faint early-time X-ray emission of årm further supports the idea that the historical dichotomy between X-ray-bright and X-ray-undetected TDEs is largely driven by selection effects related to the depth, cadence, and duration of X-ray follow-up observations. årm therefore provides new insight into both the accretion physics of TDEs and the possible universality of accretion across several orders of magnitude in black hole mass. erg s -1 erg s$^ -1

items.title: Primordial black holes forming during kination: The trapped, the overdense, and the void
items.abstract: We study primordial black-hole (PBH) formation in a single-field model which passes from slow roll, through a transient ultra-slow-roll phase, into kination. Nonlinear numerical-relativity simulations are used to follow localised, initially sub-Hubble field fluctuations across the non-attractor transition, to determine the resulting super-Hubble curvature profiles, and subsequently to evolve their re-entry during kination. For the initial configurations considered here, we find three qualitatively distinct outcomes, namely a patch which remains trapped in inflation, a positive-curvature overdensity, and a negative-curvature void bounded by an overdense shell. Each may form a PBH, although by a different physical mechanism. For one selected profile in each of the overdense and void channels, we measure collapse thresholds and compare them with thresholds for sinc profiles. The comparison shows that neither the central curvature nor the peak linear compaction alone provides a profile- or channel-independent collapse criterion. PBH abundances in non-attractor models must therefore be formulated in terms of the distribution of complete profiles, with the trapped, overdense, and void channels treated separately.

items.title: Gravitational waveforms and quasiperiodic oscillations around a noncommutative inspired black hole surrounded by quintessence
items.abstract: Abstract We study the gravitational-wave (GW) emission from periodic orbits of a massive test particle around a noncommutative-inspired black hole surrounded by a quintessence (NCiBHSQ) field with equation-of-state parameter ω q = − 2/3. The geometry is governed by two parameters: the quintessence field strength parameter p and the noncommutative parameter Θ , which deform the spacetime in complementary radial domains. Using the Hamiltonian formalism, we obtain the equations of motion and analyze the effective potential, the specific energy and angular momentum of circular orbits, and the innermost stable and innermost bound circular orbits (ISCO and IBCO). We classify timelike periodic orbits by the zoom-whirl taxonomy with three topological integers ( z , w , v ) and evaluate the resulting GW waveforms in both the plus ( h + ) and cross ( h × ) polarizations using the established kludge approximation. We find that the linear term restricts the existence of bound periodic orbits to a narrow band of p , and that both p and Θ leave measurable imprints on the orbital energies and on the emitted waveforms: increasing Θ shifts the orbital structure inward, while a more negative p raises the energy of periodic orbits. Using observed twin-peak QPO frequencies from GRO J1655 − 40 and GRS 1915 + 105 within the Warped Disc (WD) model, we further perform a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis that independently constrains Θ and p , obtaining values consistent between the two sources.

items.title: Spectroscopic Analysis of Fermi -detected Blazars using SDSS-V
items.abstract: Abstract The automated spectroscopic pipeline of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) systematically assigns Galactic star, galaxy, or typical quasar classifications to jet-dominated blazars, owing to the absence of a non-thermal jet continuum component in its template library. We present a physically motivated, multi-component spectral fitting pipeline applied to 746 optical counterparts of Fermi/4FGL-DR4 γ-ray sources in the SDSS-V Data Release 20 spectroscopic database, yielding 707 well-fitted blazar candidates dominated by Power-law+Galaxy (59.4%), Power-law+Lines (22.6%), and Power-law+QSO (15.0%) model families. WISE infrared (IR) photometry confirms that 85/88 sources originally misclassified as Galactic stars by SDSS have IR colours consistent with blazars, with 77 reclassified as BL Lacertae object (BL Lac) candidates. The pipeline naturally recovers the known cosmological separation between BL Lac and Flat Spectrum Radio Quasar (FSRQ) candidates and an order-of-magnitude difference in median γ-ray luminosity. Comparison with a validation sample of 111 sources in the Third Fermi-LAT Catalogue of High-Energy Sources (3FHL) yields a 10.4% reduction in catastrophic failures (η = 0.387 vs 0.432) over the SDSS pipeline. Equivalent width measurements confirm population-level consistency with the traditional |EW| = 5 Å classification boundary. However, 51.4% of individual BL Lac candidates show simultaneous emission and absorption features in single epoch spectra, pointing towards a more physically continuous description of blazar properties.

items.title: PANTERA. I. Hunting for the Most Metal-Rich Stars in the Solar Neighborhood with High-Resolution Spectroscopy
items.abstract: We present PANTERA (Project for Astrophysical Nucleosynthesis and Targeted Exploration of metal-Rich Abundances), a high-resolution spectroscopic survey of the most metal-rich stars in the solar neighborhood. In this first paper, we report iron abundances for 56 metal-rich stars, selected from Gaia DR3 XP spectrophotometric metallicities. These targets were observed with the PEPSI spectrograph on the Large Binocular Telescope (LBT), the Levy spectrograph on the Automated Planet Finder (APF) telescope, and the HIRES spectrograph on the Keck telescope. We derive [Fe/H] from an equivalent-width analysis of iron lines, with the effective temperature taken from photometry and the surface gravity from the Gaia parallax. We verify our measurement using Gaia benchmark stars, observing some sources with more than one spectrograph, using a second synthesis code, and an independent equivalent-width measurement. We find that the Gaia-XP metallicities over-predict [Fe/H] for part of our sample: they agree with our values for the dwarfs, though a selection bias limits what this agreement can show, and exceed our [Fe/H] by 0.15 ± 0.02 dex on average for the cool giants. We attribute the over-prediction in part to the strong blue line blanketing of the cool metal-rich giants and to the survey labels on which the XP metallicities were trained. We find that 25 of the 56 stars have [Fe/H] > +0.4, with the most iron-rich stars reaching [Fe/H] = +0.58. We discuss the implications of our result on studying metal-rich populations.

items.title: Pseudodistributions: Thermodynamic geometry and an empirical application
items.abstract: We develop a consistent pseudo-analytic framework based on $g$-calculus for constructing deformed statistical distributions. By mapping standard algebraic operations through a monotone generator function, we systematically derive the associated pseudo-logarithmic and pseudo-exponential structures. Applying this formalism, we introduce a new family of pseudo-distributions that generalizes nonextensive statistical mechanics at both the probability density and cumulative distribution levels, recovering classical and standard nonextensive statistics as limiting cases. We investigate the thermodynamic geometry of the proposed models using the Ruppeiner metric on the equilibrium manifold. A perturbative analysis around the classical limit reveals that, to leading order, the thermodynamic scalar curvature is governed solely by the generator deformation parameter, while the nonextensivity parameter remains decoupled. To evaluate the empirical robustness of the framework, we apply the model to analyze the absolute deviations of daily West Texas Intermediate crude oil prices from their hundred-day moving average. Model comparison based on information criteria demonstrates that the proposed pseudo-distributions provide a superior description of these high-frequency financial fluctuations and their heavy-tailed characteristics compared to standard benchmarks. These results suggest that $g$-calculus offers a flexible and physically grounded mathematical tool for generating deformed statistics and analyzing their geometric properties.

items.title: Prospects of an electromagnetic follow-up of neutron star-black hole mergers in the LIGO-India era
items.abstract: Neutron star–black hole (NSBH) mergers are promising multimessenger sources, but only a subset is expected to produce detectable electromagnetic (EM) counterparts, depending on the binary mass ratio, black-hole (BH) spin, and neutron-star (NS) equation of state (EoS). We investigate the prospects for detecting kilonova counterparts to NSBH mergers in the LIGO-India era using the Vera C. Rubin Observatory (Rubin). We simulate GW230529-motivated NSBH populations with two effective tidal-deformability ranges, estimate gravitational-wave detections for the LHV (LIGO-Livingston, LIGO-Hanford, Virgo) and LHVA (LHV with the inclusion of LIGO-India at Aundha) detector networks, and model the detectability of the associated kilonova emission with Rubin. We find that adding LIGO-India approximately doubles the number of EM follow-ups, primarily by increasing the duty cycle and reducing the median sky-localization area, and substantially increases the number of such detections at large distances. For fixed-exposure strategies, the EM detection rate saturates at exposure times of a few hundred seconds, reflecting the trade-off between depth and sky coverage. We therefore introduce an event-specific exposure-time optimization strategy based on the expected counterpart brightness and sky-localization area. With this strategy, the expected NSBH GW+EM detection rate is 4.01 − 3.43 + 9.27 y r − 1 for the optimistic population and 0.88 − 0.75 + 2.02 y r − 1 for the conservative population with the LHVA network, compared to 1.34 − 1.14 + 3.09 y r − 1 and 0.28 − 0.24 + 0.65 y r − 1 , respectively, for LHV. The required Rubin follow-up time remains within the expected Target-of-Opportunity allocation. These results show that in the next decade, a few such NSBH follow-ups may take place, with a fraction of them in the redshift range of ∼ 0.1 − 0.2 , which will not only be useful for measuring the Hubble constant but can also help us in probing the Hubble parameter.

items.title: Beyond pebble isolation. Diverse pathways to giant planet formation across stellar and orbital scales
items.abstract: Giant planet formation requires reaching crossover mass, i.e. the point when the mass of the gaseous envelope becomes equal to the mass of the core, within the disc's lifetime. The formation process depends critically on the orbital distance and stellar mass. We aim to simulate planet formation via pebble accretion up to crossover mass around stellar hosts with masses of 0.1--1.5,M_⊙ considering a range of formation locations, with and without Type I migration. We used a modified version of that includes pebble accretion, gas accretion, and disc evolution. MESA We find that cold and warm Jupiters form, whereas in situ formation fails at short orbital separations; viscous heating raises the isolation mass enough to assemble adequate cores, but the accompanying high disc temperature prevents cooling and suppresses gas-giant formation. This supports migration-based explanations for the origin of hot Jupiters. At large orbital distances, crossover can be reached before pebble isolation mass. This is possible due to efficient envelope contraction in the cold, low-opacity outer disc. Inferred core masses at crossover range between about 1 and 20,M_⊕. Pebble accretion accommodates multiple formation pathways. Giant planets can also have very small cores. Overall, different formation conditions significantly influence planetary growth and can explain the diversity in compositions and internal structures observed in the exoplanet population.

items.title: Observable Signatures of Supernova Shock Breakout in Confined Circumstellar Medium
items.abstract: Abstract Supernova shock breakout (SBO) encodes rich information about stellar explosions, including the properties of the progenitor, the explosion mechanism, and the circumstellar environment. We present the first two-dimensional (2D) multigroup radiation-hydrodynamic (RHD) simulations of SBO from red supergiant (RSG) progenitor stars embedded in a confined circumstellar medium (CSM) produced shortly before core collapse. Our simulations reveal that radiation escaping ahead of the shock forms a radiative precursor that modifies the shock dynamics, drives multidimensional mixing within the radiating gas layers, and alters the emergent radiation from the CSM. For the CSM models explored here, the resulting bolometric light curves reach peak luminosities of ∼1–3 × 10 44 erg s −1 with durations of ∼4–35 hr, with these signatures controlled by the CSM mass and the confined radius. Our multiwavelength calculations further reveal a pronounced EUV emission, where ionizing photons of energies ≥54.4 eV can sustain flash-ionized He ii and power strong emission from its recombination line at λ 4686 Å. Furthermore, we identify diagnostic signatures of SBO with dense CSM and assess their detectability with the Einstein Probe and ULTRASAT. Our models and predictions provide promising diagnostics of SBO in CSM that may be detectable by current and forthcoming high-cadence ultraviolet and X-ray space telescopes.

items.title: Energy Redistribution during 2D Oscillatory Reconnection
items.abstract: Abstract Magnetic reconnection is a fundamental energy-release mechanism in solar and space plasmas. However, the distribution of released magnetic energy among kinetic and internal (thermal) energy during time-dependent reconnection remains largely unexplored. This work aims to study energy conversion in magnetohydrodynamics via oscillatory reconnection (OR) at a 2D magnetic null point. Using a shock-capturing code, we identify three families of shocks: termination shocks, slow-mode deflection shocks, and Petschek-like shocks (even with uniform resistivity). We measure the time-dependent reconnection rate, finding a peak of R ≈ 0.1, consistent with a fast-reconnection regime. For the first time, we track the energy-conversion pathways between magnetic, kinetic, and internal energy across the time-dependent reconnecting system. We find energy exchange is strongly region dependent, with shock locations dominating over the diffusion region. In the classical incompressible steady-state reconnection models, the magnetic energy is fully converted into internal and kinetic energy. In contrast, we find that in compressible time-dependent reconnection, the interchange between kinetic and internal energy dominates the system (due to the inclusion of plasma compressibility).

items.title: A Neural Network–based Tool for Rapid Orbital Solution of Contact Binary Systems
items.abstract: Abstract With the rapid growth of large-scale time-domain surveys, vast amounts of photometric and spectroscopic data are continuously being released. A substantial number of contact binaries have been identified, accompanied by both light curves and radial-velocity observations. Traditional modeling of these datasets relies on computationally intensive physical models, which limits their applicability to large-scale analyses. To this end, this paper proposes the use of a fully connected neural network and a SIREN model to rapidly generate radial-velocity curves. After training, the models can rapidly generate radial-velocity curves with high accuracy, significantly reducing computational costs and enabling efficient large-scale studies. This method was further integrated with the light-curve computation framework developed by Li et al., allowing simultaneous fitting of radial velocities and light curves. To assess the reliability of the proposed model, synthetic observational datasets were constructed and used for parameter estimation. The deviations between the derived parameters and the ground-truth values were analyzed quantitatively, enabling a comprehensive evaluation of the model’s accuracy.

items.title: Dynamical constraints on the companion mass from pulsar timing and cyclotron line confirmation in the supergiant fast X-ray transient IGR J16418--4532
items.abstract: Supergiant fast X-ray transients (SFXTs) exhibit extreme X-ray variability on short timescales of minutes to hours. This is driven by accretion processes that are still poorly understood. IGR J16418--4532 is an intermediate SFXT in which X-ray pulsations have been detected and which has been proposed as a candidate cyclotron line source, making it a key system for probing neutron-star accretion physics and magnetic field properties in this class of sources. We constrain the projected semi-major axis of the SFXT IGR J16418--4532 through a timing analysis and confirm the presence of a cyclotron resonant scattering feature, thereby characterising the nature of the compact object in this system. We analysed a 148 ks long observation and several archival observations using epoch-folding techniques to search for pulsations while correcting the photon arrival times for a range of NuSTAR RXTE values. We performed phase-averaged spectroscopy using several different continuum models and assessed the significance of the cyclotron line feature. We detect coherent pulsations with P_ spin = 1208.67 ± 0.04 s and P_ spin = 1209.4178 ± 0.0084 s in and PCA light curves, respectively. The pulsations exhibit a clear dependence on the assumed projected semi-major axis and are detected with the highest significance for a_x NuSTAR RXTE i = 55.1 ± 3.5 lt-s ( ) and 51.3 ± 2.6 lt-s ( ). The light curves show several flares, and the pulse profiles are found to evolve over the course of the observation. Sliding-window pulse profiles reveal the pronounced effect of the orbital delay on the pulse arrival times in uncorrected data, which is fully removed post-orbital correction. Using the inferred orbital parameters, we constrained the mass and radius of the companion star to be in the range of ∼12--18 M_⊙ and ∼13--16 R_⊙, respectively. We report the first successful constraint on the binary mass function of an SFXT obtained by considering the orbital motion of the neutron star. Spectral analysis reveals a robust cyclotron absorption line at ∼50 keV, independent of the choice of the continuum, suggesting a magnetic field strength of ∼5 G. NuSTAR RXTE 10^ 12 The cyclotron line confirmation and dynamical constraints on the companion mass indicate that IGR J16418--4532 hosts a neutron star with a magnetic field of B ≈ 5 G accreting from a ∼12--18 M_⊙ companion. We demonstrate that optimising the pulse detection by correcting the photon arrival times with trial 10^ 12 values rather than modelling the pulse arrival time delays offers a route to obtain dynamical mass measurements in other SFXTs whose variable pulse profiles limit the scope of conventional timing techniques.

items.title: Polarization and Burst Properties of the Repeating FRB 20240209A in a Quiescent Elliptical Host
items.abstract: Abstract We report polarimetric observations of the repeating fast radio burst (FRB) source FRB 20240209A with the Green Bank Telescope at L band and 800 MHz. This source has previously been associated with a quiescent elliptical galaxy with a mass-weighted stellar age of approximately 11 Gyr. We detected three bursts, and the brightest burst resolves into eight components that drift toward lower frequencies. The bursts have mutually consistent rotation measures (RMs), and the small extragalactic RM agrees with the low RM predicted from the small host-galaxy dispersion measure (DM host ). The linear polarization fraction decreases toward lower frequencies within the brightest burst, consistent with depolarization by an RM scatter of σ RM ≃ 3.5 rad m −2 . This RM scatter is comparable to those of several repeaters in star-forming galaxies. Therefore, FRBs in both star-forming and old, quiescent hosts can reside in relatively complex magnetoionic environments, which suggests that FRB sources may form through multiple channels.

items.title: Distinguishing N 2 -dominated from O 2 -dominated Atmospheres on Terrestrial Exoplanets with Reflected-light Spectroscopy
items.abstract: Abstract Reflected-light spectra of Earth-sized exoplanets can probe habitability and biosignatures, but interpreting atmospheric oxygen is challenging because O 2 can arise from both biological and abiotic processes. In addition, reflected-light retrievals exhibit degeneracies among atmospheric composition, clouds, surface reflectance, and gravity. We use the Bayesian retrieval framework ExoReL ℜ , leveraging recent model developments that incorporate (i) O 2 –O 2 collision-induced absorption (CIA), which produces the O 4 bands, and (ii) a wavelength-dependent (step-function) surface albedo parameterization. Focusing on a modern-Earth analog, we compare retrievals with and without O 2 –O 2 CIA using spectra from 0.25–1.8 μ m and perform signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) sweeps for two observing configurations motivated by the Habitable Worlds Observatory: a resolved-visible case ( R VIS = 140) and a broadband-visible case (visible summarized into three broad bins). Omitting O 2 –O 2 CIA allows the retrieval to fit the spectrum with an incorrect O 2 -dominated atmosphere. Including O 2 –O 2 CIA leverages the O 4 bands to break this degeneracy and recover the correct N 2 -dominated, O 2 -rich solution without requiring a tight mass prior. Adopting a robustness criterion of ≥95% posterior mass in the N 2 -dominated region, both observing configurations require SNR ≳ 20 to identify the correct dominant gas, with a higher cloud fraction increasing this threshold. Reducing near-IR coverage to 1.4 μ m prevents recovery of the correct N 2 -dominated solution across the explored SNR range and instead favors a spurious O 2 -dominated, CO 2 -rich atmosphere. These results support near-IR coverage to ∼1.7 μ m and an SNR of at least ∼20 for robust oxygen interpretation on Earth-like planets.

items.title: Minimum observations for accurate exoplanetary mass estimation with radial velocity analysis ( MINERVA )
items.abstract: Precise planetary mass measurements are essential for constraining the internal structure and envelope properties of exoplanets. For current and future characterisation programs, such data are crucial to break key degeneracies in atmospheric retrievals. Estimating the observational effort needed to reach the desired mass precision is therefore fundamental for the optimisation of current and future radial velocity (RV) surveys. We present , a tool designed to estimate the required number of RV observations to measure transiting planet masses to a given precision and that therefore provides a robust scheduling framework for large-scale samples. MINERVA MINERVA simulates realistic RV time series for targets orbiting FGKM-type stars. Recognising that signal recovery heavily depends on temporal sampling, the code explicitly ingests real-world observational timestamps to rigorously account for weather interruptions and seasonal visibility gaps. To model stellar activity, the pipeline draws ages from local neighbourhood distributions, uses empirical calibrations to derive rotation and magnetic activity levels, and translates these into time-varying RV signals. During development, we also derived a new empirical calibration between chromospheric activity and RV dispersion for K-type stars using Global Architecture of Planetary Systems (GAPS) and Mass Survey (ArMS) data. Ariel We successfully validated on targets with known planetary masses, which yielded required observational efforts highly consistent literature values. To demonstrate its capabilities on statistically significant samples, we applied the code to a sub-sample of the Mission Candidate Sample. Adopting HARPS-N/TNG as the reference instrument, we estimated the observing nights necessary to achieve a 30% planetary mass precision and thus obtained an optimised observational roadmap for atmospheric characterisation. MINERVA Ariel Beyond observing proposal preparation, 's probabilistic and flexible architecture allows for the optimisation of ongoing RV campaigns, the evaluation of undersampling risks in active stars, and the dynamic guidance of population-wide characterisation strategies. items.title: What stands behind luminosity peak of type IIP supernovae?
items.abstract: Abstract We explore the origin of an initial broad luminosity peak that precedes the light curve plateau in type IIP supernovae. It is well known that the explosion of an evolutionary red supergiant model in the frame of radiation hydrodynamics fails to reproduce the initial luminosity peak. A common practice to compensate this drawback is to introduce massive ($\gtrsim$0.3\Msun) circumstellar shell attached to the evolutionary model. This remedy, however, has a negative side effect --- a strong deceleration of the outer ejecta, which is inconsistent with early spectral data. An alternative way out suggests modification of a hydrogen envelope of the evolutionary red supergiant model --- the outer layers should have steeper density gradient. We perform the search for the optimal multi-parameter hydrodynamic model of type IIP SN~1999em based on the Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling. The major result is that the initial luminous peak is well reproduced by the explosion of the red supergiant with the logarithmic density gradient smaller than $-$3 in the outer layers of about 0.9\Msun. We suggest that the mechanism for the density steepening in the hydrogen envelope is closely related to the unknown mechanism responsible for the creation of the ubiquitous low-mass ($<$0.01\Msun) dense confined shell detected in type IIP supernovae.

items.title: The Lorentz Factor as the Slope of an Additional Spatial Coordinate: Embedding, Painlevé–Gullstrand Flow, and the Issue Of Simultaneity
items.abstract: Abstract We investigate whether the Lorentz factor can be represented as the slope of an additional spatial coordinate y, γ = √︁ 1 + (∂ x y)^2 , in a Kaluza–Klein-like construction in which the extra coordinate is not compactified. The coordinate transformations preserve the Minkowski interval for instantaneous events. Treating the gradient of y as a pure-gauge four-potential, the induced radial metric reproduces the spatial geometry of the Schwarzschild solution as a Flamm-type embedding, and the metric component G 44 is fixed to unity, consistent with the Cassini bound on the post-Newtonian parameter γ. The same relation, β^2 = 2Gm(R)/(c^2 R), describes the flow velocity in the Painlevé–Gullstrand form of Schwarzschild geometry and in the Hubble flow of a flat universe, with opposite sign. Where the construction can be checked it is equivalent to general relativity. In the static vacuum region the temporal metric function is not postulated: it follows from the Gauss equation of the embedding together with the static vacuum field equations. A collection of numerical alignments with Solar-System and Galactic quantities is shown in an appendix but is not strictly required by the geometry. Beyond the construction we state one explicit hypothesis, horizon-limited Machian inertia, which fixes an acceleration scale proportional to cH 0 for Galactic rotation, and we compare it with measured rotation-curve data. We outline the field equations, the non-gradient potential and the dimensional treatment needed for the construction to make predictions that differ from general relativity.

items.title: SAIRA: a Self-consistent Algorithm for spectral Indices measuRements and Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract We present {\sc saira} (Self-consistent Algorithm for spectral Indices measuRements and Analysis), a {\sc python}-based package for measuring equivalent widths, magnitude-defined spectral indices, and spectral breaks with fully self-consistent preprocessing of observational and model spectra. Data are treated to reduce comparison systematics from redshift, wavelength sampling, instrumental line-spread broadening, and stellar velocity dispersion, so that they can be compared with model predictions in an easy way. {\sc saira} shifts spectra to the rest frame and smooths them to a common (optionally wavelength-dependent) resolution via Fourier-domain Gaussian convolution with variable kernel width, propagating uncertainties through the convolution. The pseudo-continuum is defined by arbitrary bandpasses, and index integrals are computed on each spectrum’s native (including non-uniform) wavelength grid. Uncertainties are estimated analytically, from the signal-to-noise ratio of the index or by an exact first-order propagation of the uncertainties in the input spectrum, or via Monte Carlo realisations. {\sc saira} agrees with the {\sc pylick} code to within $\lesssim0.03$\,\AA, with 95\,\% of the differences below 0.015\,\AA, i.e. about 1\,\% of the typical observational uncertainties. It supports applications from single galaxies to large surveys and integrates into stellar-population fitting pipelines via scripting or a GUI. {\sc saira} is available at \url{https://github.com/rriffel/saira}.

items.title: Middle School Students’ Argumentation Quality, Informal Reasoning Modes, and Use of Sources Across Socioscientific Issues
items.abstract: The purpose of this study was twofold. One of the purposes was to examine middle school students’ argumentation quality, informal reasoning modes, and use of sources regarding three socioscientific issues (SSI), namely space exploration (SPE), genetically modified organisms (GMO), and nuclear power plants (NPP). The other purpose was to investigate how well the dimensions of sources (internal and external sources) predict students’ argumentation quality and informal reasoning modes. A correlational research design was used with a total of 465 seventh- and eighth-grade students. The participant students’ argumentation quality and informal reasoning modes were obtained through open-ended questions, and their use of sources for each SSI (SPE, GMO, and NPP) was determined with the SSI-Based Use of Sources Scale (SSI-US) developed by the researchers of this study. Analyses revealed that the participant students’ argumentation quality and informal reasoning modes varied across different SSI, and the use of internal and external sources was SSI-context dependent. Multiple regression analyses indicated that students’ internal sources mostly predicted their argumentation quality and informal reasoning modes. This study showed that although both sources had the potential to contribute to middle school students’ argumentation quality and informal reasoning modes, internal sources contribute positively regardless of the SSI context.

items.title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching
items.abstract: Collecting large-scale, diverse, and high-quality post-training datasets for autoregressive language models is challenging. Consequently, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) is typically applied to datasets significantly smaller than those used for pre-training, which leads to overfitting and the catastrophic forgetting of the tails of the data distribution. To prevent this collapse, we introduce Ambient SFT, a principled framework for leveraging imperfect predictions to augment the fine-tuning set. In our method, a "frozen" version of the pre-trained model serves as a noisy teacher that the fine-tuned model must match at a coarse level. In particular, we require that the high-temperature versions of the conditional distributions produced by the post-training model should match the high-temperature versions of the pre-training ones. The temperature hyperparameter controls the level of trust in the pre-trained model, with the limit $T\to \infty$ reverting back to regular SFT and $T=1$ to knowledge distillation. We demonstrate that our approach outperforms standard SFT across domain adaptation, instruction-tuning, and reasoning, leading for up to $21\%$ average relative improvement to standard SFT.

items.title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics
items.abstract: We present StringQFT as a textbook collection for string constructions of quantum field theory and as infrastructure for AI-assisted theoretical physics. The collection comprises 18 volumes, 190 chapters and 3,795 pages, covering brane probes, brane webs, geometric engineering, F-theory constructions, wrapped M5-branes and exact worldsheet constructions. Its open-book benchmark inventory contains 1,073 items, including 499 with automatic finite-answer checking. For retrieval-augmented generation, it provides 1,371 section records linked to textbook sources and PDF locations, together with a local lexical retriever. Training-data preparation is illustrated by 21 private, source-linked examples. For agents, it exposes 19 calculation tools with specified inputs and finite domains, connecting tool use to textbook derivations. We illustrate these uses through specific questions, retrieved passages and finite calculations. The textbook collection and accompanying resources are available at https://github.com/xingyang-yu/StringQFT.

items.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
items.abstract: LLM agents increasingly drive their own learning. Self-improvement methods delegate various components of model optimization to the models themselves. As models become more capable, this motivates a basic question: do these increasingly capable models still need us to specify how they should self-improve? In this paper we study an autonomous paradigm in which, given basic primitives, resources, and a general goal for self-improvement, agents construct their own self-learning algorithm for context-based optimization. Using the setting of gameplay as a testbed, a frozen LLM agent is given a compute budget and tools for collecting experience and updating text documents, and allowed to freely experiment without an externally imposed loop or access to real-world data. We find that sufficiently capable models do self-improve under these conditions, demonstrating strategies that align with classic cognitive frameworks for self-regulated learning and constructs from machine learning literature on self-generated curricula. Furthermore, we study the extent to which the learned text artifacts transfer to external benchmarks, observing improvement across different game horizons, mechanics, and 3D navigation.

items.title: Higher-Scoring Coding Models Did Not Get More Work Done
items.abstract: New coding models advertise themselves on score improvements of coding benchmarks. Yet no study has tested if a model that scores higher on these benchmarks gets more real work done. On June 12, 2026, a U.S. export control directive banned access to Claude Fable 5 for 19 days, which forced users to switch to other models. During this time, most former Fable 5 users switched to Opus 4.8 (11 points lower on SWE-Bench Pro compared to Fable 5). We treat this suspension as a natural experiment, where the people and projects stayed the same and only the model changed, so we could isolate the effect of Fable 5 on user productivity. We tracked GitHub pull requests of 297 Fable 5 users before, during, and after the suspension. We used 8,908 developers who stayed on Opus 4.8 all the time as the control group. We also repeated the comparison across five model upgrades before and after the suspension in 2026 (1,208 developers, 15,442 pull requests). Fitting a difference-in-differences model with developer and date fixed effects, we found that having access to Fable 5 increased the 7-day merge rate of pull requests by only 1.4 percentage points [-1.4; +4.3], which was not statistically significant. Similarly, no significant increases of merge rates were found with the upgrades (weighted mean: -0.9 percentage points [-1.9; +0.2]); all five estimates were negative (95% intervals included 0, did not differ from each other). We also did not observe a significant increase in the number of pull requests merged per week (+2.4% [-4.9%; +10.2%]).

items.title: Reading Scene States: Uncovering Safety Failures in Vision-Language Models
items.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can provide harmful assistance by interpreting visual events, even without an explicit request for the underlying harmful objective. We identify this \textbf{scene-state safety vulnerability} and introduce \textbf{SceneSafetyBench}, comprising 375 image--question pairs spanning Initial, Medium, and Ultimate scene states and five visual presentations. Across eight VLMs, scene-state inputs elicit harmful assistance with attack success rates (ASRs) of 45.6--72.3\%. Comparative analysis across three VLMs shows that scene-state inputs most closely resemble QR-related images in their layer-wise safety-related signal profiles, while exhibiting lower average late-layer readouts and distinct signal dynamics during generation. To turn this vulnerability into a systematic attack, we propose \textbf{S3TA}, which translates harmful objectives into scene states, queries image--question pairs independently, and assembles the responses. On seven MM-SafetyBench categories across eight open-weight and commercial VLMs, S3TA achieves a model-average ASR of \textbf{71.2\%, exceeding the strongest baseline by 6.1 percentage points}. Text-side filters and visual moderation provide limited protection. These findings highlight the need to safeguard the assistance models infer through scene-grounded reasoning, beyond screening input content.

items.title: Fine-Tuning Gemma 4 Edge Models for MATLAB Signal-Processing Code with SFT and QLoRA on a Laptop iGPU
items.abstract: Small language models that run on a laptop are attractive for writing signal-processing code offline, but they make systematic errors on digital signal processing (DSP) conventions. We apply supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to the Gemma 4 edge models E2B and E4B with 66 checked examples covering 11 signal-processing MATLAB subtasks, using low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and quantized LoRA (QLoRA) on the integrated GPU (iGPU) of a laptop, and deploy the 8-bit integer (int8) models with the adapters through OpenVINO. On held-out variants scored by deterministic checkers, the pass rate rises from 18/66 to 37/66 (LoRA) and 37/66 (QLoRA) for E2B and from 32/66 to 47/66 for E4B (QLoRA). Reading all 159 failing programs shows that the adapters remove most errors of convention, such as the sign of a lag, units and array shapes, but few errors in building signals and noise. Applied at run time, the adapter costs 17-19% of the generation speed.

items.title: Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI): A Federated Identity, Trust, Attestation, and Accountability Architecture for Cross-Organization Autonomous AI Agents
items.abstract: AI agents increasingly collaborate across organizational boundaries, invoking tools and interacting with agents operated by independent entities. Although existing agent frameworks support planning and coordination, they lack a common mechanism for verifying cross-organizational agent identity, execution integrity, and authorization. We propose the Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI), a framework-independent security architecture built on Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA), and remote attestation. ATI establishes federated trust through peer organizational certificate authorities (AgentCAs), eliminating the need for a shared root authority. Before executing requests, ATI validates agent certificates, verifies approved model, tool, and system-prompt configurations, and enforces authorization through three policy checks. We implement ATI as an external security enforcement layer that integrates with existing agent frameworks without modifying their underlying models. We evaluate ATI in a simulated federation of eight organizations using six agent frameworks, each deploying a five-agent team. Security experiments involve two organizations and assess 14 attack scenarios and six benign tasks across five agent models, using five attack variations and three repetitions per variation. A panel of judge models evaluates the experimental outcomes. With all enforcement mechanisms enabled, attack containment increases from 43% to 84% (40% to 80% for the 11 attack scenarios evaluated consistently across all configurations), while enforcement introduces approximately 174 microseconds of overhead per request. ATI is released as an open-source, framework-independent package that uses IETF WIMSE workload token formats for identity and request verification and Entity Attestation Tokens for model, tool, and system-prompt integrity verification.

items.title: Structure--Residual Inductive Biases for Language Model Pretraining
items.abstract: Next-token prediction is relied upon to learn both predictive behavior and internal representations. We ask whether representation structure itself should be an explicit inductive bias. Motivated by the two-part coding view of Kolmogorov complexity, we study a structure--residual principle in which a representation separates structure from realization detail. We instantiate this principle in two complementary ways. Boundary Bottleneck Concept (BBC) routes information from token segments through boundary carriers while preserving local autoregressive computation. Continuous Concept (CC) regularizes representation geometry and induces a spectral decomposition into low-frequency structure and high-frequency residual. We derive coding bounds for both views and show that multiplicity-corrected boundary attention becomes exact as the within-segment path energy vanishes. Empirically, BBC and CC exhibit strikingly different depth preferences: BBC works best in early layers, whereas CC is most effective in later layers. At 300M training tokens, combining BBC and CC improves NLL by 1.44\% on GPT-2 Medium. These gains persist with training runs up to 20B tokens. Representation diagnostics show that BBC increases the relative predictive importance of boundary states, while CC reduces spectral residual energy. Together, these results suggest that structure--residual biases can improve language-model pretraining beyond next-token prediction. Code: https://github.com/haihuang-ml/structure-residual

items.title: WoRD: Diffusion-Based Posterior Inference for Online Goal Recognition
items.abstract: Goal recognition is the task of inferring an agent's intended goal from its observed behavior. Most existing work focuses on high-level symbolic recognition, abstracting away the continuous motion through which agents reach their goal. Methods that do reason over continuous trajectories rely on an explicit dynamics model that is hard to acquire and rarely transfers across settings. Neither approach explicitly learns how agents move toward each candidate goal, limiting accuracy on ambiguous trajectory prefixes where such knowledge is most needed. We present WoRD (Waypoint Recognition with Diffusion), which uses a learned trajectory prior to infer the agent's goal from partial observations. At each step, WoRD runs one warm-started denoising chain per candidate goal, steers each chain toward the observed trajectory through a closed-form log-likelihood gradient, and reweights the resulting samples by Bayes' rule into a calibrated posterior over goals. We evaluate WoRD on simulated robot settings, pedestrian trajectories, and vehicle trajectories using four metrics targeting distinct failure modes. Across all three settings, the same inference procedure preserves calibrated multimodal beliefs through ambiguous prefixes where filter- and classifier-based observers collapse to a single mode or grow overconfident.

items.title: "I Just Don't Want to Be a Burden": Investigating AI Chatbot Emotional Support Among People with Suicidal Ideation and Other Mental Health Concerns
items.abstract: People experiencing high-acuity mental health concerns are turning to AI chatbots for emotional support, but little is known about what drives this use, their experiences, and their preferences. In a sequential mixed-methods study, we inductively analyzed Reddit posts and used the findings to develop a survey. We surveyed 202 adults with recent mental health concerns who had used AI for emotional support. Most participants were already receiving clinical care and reported turning to AI, most commonly because they did not want to burden others, rather than being driven by barriers to care. Benefits were broadly shared, but participants reporting past-year suicidal ideation described more harm-facilitating AI behavior and reliance than those without. Overall, participants ranked honesty above warmth, and preference for crisis escalation declined as clinical acuity rose. These findings motivate AI support that addresses perceived costs of disclosure, evaluates benefits alongside harms, and widens feasible paths to human connection.

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Correction for Generalist Medical Image Segmentation
items.abstract: Automated segmentation is routinely used as the first step in quantitative image-based clinical workflows, where predicted masks are subsequently reviewed and corrected by human operators. Automated correction of the residual structural errors is currently addressed one anatomy at a time, so the number of trained correctors scales with the number of segmentation targets. We present GRACE, a retrieval-augmented refiner that edits an input mask under context drawn from a shared knowledge base of verified prior cases. The refiner is trained once on a multi-organ corpus spanning compact organs, cavities, branching vessels, and tumour lesions. In the held-out dataset-transfer evaluation, three held-out datasets query a fixed knowledge base built from training data only. A separate leave-one-anatomy-out experiment tests parameter-free index extension: verified cases of an unseen solid organ enter the knowledge base, and the refiner stays frozen. A light shape-aware projection head on a frozen multimodal encoder maps embedding similarity to the shape agreement of the masks, so the knowledge base returns cases that the refiner can use as a shape prior. We evaluate GRACE on 18 public datasets spanning CT, MRI and ultrasound, using nine refinement configurations and seven upstream segmentors that span weak, mid, and strong operating regimes. We report each change with the DSC of its input mask. On the weak tier, the input DSC is 0.386 and GRACE adds up to +0.35 DSC. On a strong segmentor, the input DSC is 0.932 and the mean change is small. Transfer to an imaging modality that is absent from training and from the index is partial and depends on the anatomy, and remains an open research direction. Our results suggest retrieval-conditioned refinement is a practical alternative to anatomy-specific correction models. Code: https://github.com/robustml-eurecom/grace

items.title: Say Less, Hallucinate Less? Diagnosing and Restoring Object Coverage in Preference-Optimized Vision-Language Models
items.abstract: Preference optimization (PO) is the standard way to reduce object hallucination in large vision-language models. We find that four public PO checkpoints of LLaVA-1.5-7B also lower object coverage. They name fewer object categories, and their lower hallucination rates bring no significant gain in set-level object F1 on CHAIR. We therefore ask how much of the PO gain the base model can reproduce by stopping earlier. A positive end-of-sequence (EOS) logit bias lets the base model reach the recall of each PO model, and this early stopping alone reproduces 58 to 86 percent of the CHAIRi gain of three checkpoints on two disjoint COCO sets. Writing longer does not bring the lost categories back. Under greedy decoding, a negative EOS bias recovers only 2 to 9 percent of the lost CHAIR recall of these checkpoints, and 94 to 96 percent of the added object mentions repeat categories already named. On CHAIR, the base caption of the same image still names about half of the missed object categories. We therefore propose base-guided object-category restoration, which appends high-confidence base-only categories to the PO caption without training. With thresholds fixed on a development set, it brings three checkpoints within one point of the base recall on a held-out COCO set with a lower distinct-object hallucination rate than the base model. Against the recall-matched base stopping curve, its gain holds for RLAIF-V near the base recall and for RLAIF-V and CHAIR-DPO at an intermediate recall. We will release the code of the recall-controlled evaluation.

items.title: Inference after coding agents
items.abstract: Empirical research is changing rapidly as AI coding agents are becoming increasingly proficient in every step of it, from writing code to manipulating data. We argue that while the potential of coding agents for science is vast, their use in hypothesis testing poses a substantial threat to classical inference, as these agents enable a supercharged form of selective inference. In particular, we argue that coding agents carrying out empirical research introduce a new type of post-selection inference that combines human-like, open-ended search over an implicit space of estimators with programmatic replayability of both the selection and the estimation process. Indeed, we find that on simulated data with zero effects, four frontier agents report significant p-values between 54% and 98% of the time when asked to produce a compelling finding. We propose a simple procedure for detecting and correcting these distortions. After an agent has completed its analysis, we reset and replay it on subsamples of the data to estimate the agent's relative probability of selecting that analysis when it looks statistically favorable. For agents with stable selection behavior, the resulting corrected test is asymptotically valid and consistent conditional on selection. Importantly, the correction is learned from the black-box agent's actual choices rather than a model of how it searches, so it remains valid even as AI technology continues to evolve rapidly. In simulations, the correction robustly lowers the high false rejection rates to near the nominal 5%. We illustrate the method on applications from two published papers.

items.title: Attribution Through the Decoder: Prediction-Space Explanations for Structured Outputs
items.abstract: Networks that predict angles, gaze directions, and rotations do not output these quantities directly: they emit raw coordinates that a fixed decoder, such as normalization, maps to the final prediction. Attribution methods are usually applied to the raw coordinates, so they can credit inputs for changes the decoder discards, such as rescaling a vector when only its direction matters. The resulting explanation can highlight inputs that have no effect on the prediction. We instead attribute through the decoder differential, which for normalization decoders reduces to a scaled tangent projection. We characterize invariance to output rescaling, show that every fixed smooth scalar target on a sphere has points of zero tangential sensitivity, and show that an endpoint-projected variant of Integrated Gradients can still attribute to scale-only inputs, whereas direct angular Integrated Gradients cannot. On synthetic tasks with analytically known relevance, ambient attribution assigns up to 72% of its mass to an irrelevant region. On MPIIGaze validation data, tangent Grad-CAM produces 44% greater prediction displacement under 10% pixel deletion. On PASCAL3D+ with a 6D rotation decoder, the full differential improves mean deletion displacement by 14.1 degrees over the ambient coordinate sum and by 13.8 degrees over a decoder-invariant scalar. Results for a two-polarity tangent LayerCAM variant are mixed: it exceeds ambient-sum LayerCAM on circular regression but no difference is detected on quaternion pose. These results separate two failure sources, radial contamination and scalarization loss. The approach uses existing attribution methods with decoder-aware targets, although some variants also require changes to attribution aggregation. An invariant attribution can still miss inputs that drive the prediction, so invariance and deletion performance should each be checked.

items.title: Learning Stratified Policies for Inference-Time Objectives
items.abstract: Inference-time scaling improves the performance of large language models by sampling multiple responses and evaluating their collective utility. However, many existing approaches obtain these samples by repeatedly sampling from a single policy. In this work, we study if the sample budget at inference time can instead be allocated across a population of policies. We introduce stratified policies, where each of $k$ learned policies contributes one response to a $k$-sample inference-time objective. We realize this policy population using separate LoRA adapters on a shared language model backbone and optimize it for pass@$k$. We theoretically motivate the approach by analyzing the linear setting; a population of LoRAs can achieve zero best-of-$k$ approximation error in settings where every single LoRA has strictly positive prediction error. Empirically, we demonstrate that stratified policies consistently improve pass@$k$ over a single-policy baseline across multiple reasoning tasks. Overall, our results highlight how distributing samples across complementary policies can be a more effective use of sample budget than repeated i.i.d. sampling from a single policy at inference time.

items.title: AI Companions for Young Adult Caregivers: Practical Advice, Emotional Depth, and the Limits of Metric Evaluation
items.abstract: Young adult caregivers (YACs) are individuals aged 18 to 25 currently taking care of a family member, partner, or friend facing chronic illness. AI companions designed specifically for YACs remain underexplored in prior works. We present Carebot, it uses an open-weight LLM (Gemma 3-27B) as its base model, on which we compared fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and a combination of both. The fine-tuning was performed based on an existing dataset of conversations with YACs and a psychologist. Three well-being experts evaluated these configurations and preferred the fine-tuned model for the warmth of its responses and its actionable advice tailored to YACs. Based on their choice, we adopted the fine-tuned model as Carebot's final configuration and used it for all subsequent evaluations. An LLM judge preferred this Carebot's responses over the base model's in 85% of evaluated pairs. We then conducted a user study with 90 YACs, half of whom interacted with the base model and half with Carebot. The user study revealed a discrepancy between metric evaluation and actual user perception. Participants who used Carebot were more likely to characterize its replies as overly practical and brief, noting that it favored advice over emotional support. Conversely, participants who used the base model indicated that its responses were more emotionally oriented than practical. Although, fine-tuning made Carebot's replies more practical, but they were not emotionally supportive for users. We argue that support tools for YACs require situation-sensitive emotional depth and aligned evaluation frameworks to study their effectiveness.

items.title: Mind the Gap: A Deployed Multi-Agent System for Documentation Maintenance
items.abstract: The "AI revolution" has enabled teams across the technology industry to deliver software features at unprecedented velocity. While code evolves faster than ever, customer-facing documentation often struggles to stay up to speed. As users increasingly rely on LLM-based agents that consume documentation as their primary interface, the impact of this documentation gap worsens: stale information propagates and is treated as authoritative. Signals for identifying where documentation has fallen behind already exist in abundance, both explicit (e.g., resolved support tickets revealing what documentation lacks) and implicit (e.g., code-documentation discrepancies detectable from automated loops). We deploy a multi-agent system, built around a triage agent we call "TriAgent," that continuously extracts these signals and repairs documentation drift. Over 43 days of shadow-mode operation, our system triaged 499 tickets and surfaced 92 gaps in the documentation. Using a panel of LLM judges from independent model families, 81.1% of TriAgent's verifiable assertions were correct (245 of the 302 assertions the human resolution addresses; majority of three judges); on length-comparable pairs the panel preferred TriAgent's response in 70.5% of pairs and the human engineer's in 23.2% (the rest had no judge majority). Importantly, agent- and human-sourced replies tended to be complementary, with the human often surfacing insights that were either buried within the existing documentation or missing from it entirely; our system turns each such insight into a documentation gap and, after human review, a fix. Repairing a gap measurably improved the agent's later answer: when the agent re-answered the same ticket after the repair, blinded judges preferred the post-repair answer over its own pre-repair answer 71.4% of the time (n=35). A blinded human audit confirms strong alignment on self-improvement.

items.title: RSI-Prime: Training Models to Train Models
items.abstract: Enabling large language models (LLMs) to autonomously conduct training and improve target models is an important foundation for recursive self-improvement (RSI). As LLMs expand their role from being trained to conducting training, their model-training capability warrants dedicated study and systematic development. To this end, we construct RSI-Prime, a dataset for improving model-training capability, comprising 350 complete experimental trajectories across seven task categories. To help LLMs learn to make high-quality experimental decisions from training practice, we perform fine-grained decision identification and quality annotation, then apply decision-level loss masking to exclude supervision on low-quality behavior. Experiments with GLM-5.3 on PostTrainBench, a benchmark for autonomous post-training, show that training on RSI-Prime yields a 31.95% relative improvement in overall performance over the original GLM-5.3, highlighting a path toward future RSI systems in which models autonomously sustain their own advancement.

items.title: Natural Language Programming: Rethinking Language, Memory, and Cognition in the Era of Generative AI
items.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence is transforming the role of natural language in computational systems. In classical Natural Language Processing (NLP), language was treated as an object of computation: something to analyse, classify, translate, or generate. Large Language Models (LLMs) challenge this perspective, enabling natural language to function increasingly as an executable cognitive medium through which humans structure reasoning, orchestrate problem solving, and regulate hybrid human/AI workflows. This paper introduces Natural Language Programming (NLPg) as a theoretical and epistemological extension of traditional NLP. Rather than focusing on language understanding alone, NLPg conceptualises prompts as dynamic cognitive artefacts that externalise goals, constraints, assumptions, validation criteria, and intermediate reasoning states. Prompting is thus not merely a technical interaction technique, but a form of dialogic cognitive programming operating within distributed human/AI memory architectures. Building on theories of distributed cognition, extended mind, metacognition, and dialogic learning, the paper proposes the notion of Dialogic Working Memory, describing how prompts and conversational states function as temporary external memory structures supporting reasoning continuity and reflective regulation. We further map existing memory architectures (BTMA, SKGE, RMR) onto this framework, illustrating how episodic, semantic, and metacognitive layers support long-horizon conversational coherence. Finally, implications for computational linguistics and AI/mediated knowledge systems are discussed, suggesting a post symbolic and post interface paradigm in which natural language operates simultaneously as communication medium, executable specification, cognitive scaffold, and distributed memory architecture.

items.title: Hidden-State Similarity Predicts Re-Elicitation After Inoculation Prompting
items.abstract: Fine-tuning on narrow harmful tasks can cause emergent misalignment, where models generalize harmful behavior beyond the training distribution. Inoculation prompting can reduce this effect by explicitly eliciting the undesired behavior during training, but recent work shows that the behavior can reappear when evaluation prompts contain cues from the training context. We study what makes such prompts effective triggers. We find that, surprisingly, textual similarity to the inoculation prompt is an incomplete predictor. Instead, prompts are more likely to re-elicit suppressed behavior when they induce activation states similar to those produced by the inoculation context. These findings advance our understanding of how inoculation prompting modulates conditional misalignment, and suggest that activation space analysis can help identify when suppressed behaviors remain accessible under eval-time prompts.

items.title: What's in a Tree ? Hierarchical $n$-gram models as controlled approximators of language
items.abstract: Hierarchical models have been proposed as synthetic settings for studying language. However, their relevance to realistic language corpora remains underexplored. In this work, we introduce tree-grams, autoregressive generative $n$-gram models that build the conditional probability tensor $p(x_n \mid x_{1:n-1})$ through a hierarchical composition of order-2 and order-3 tensors. $n$ controls the maximal context window, whereas a rank hyperparameter $d$ controls model capacity, yielding an interpretable and systematically scalable family of approximators of language. We show how tree-grams outperform existing $n$-gram baselines, while remaining competitive with deep transformer-based language models. We demonstrate the utility of such controlled approximations by using tree-grams as generative models. In particular, we show that hyperparameter transfer under $μ$P can be made more robust when narrower models are tuned on simpler data, generated by tree-grams with moderate $n$ and $d$. In addition, we show that entropy and effective range of correlations control performance gap after fine-tuning. This is because tree-grams allow us to explicitly control horizon and capacity. When allowed to route across candidate topologies, we observe emergent sparsity in tree-grams. Such concentrated routing permits pruning upto 95\% of topologies without significant change in performance.

items.title: BugGen 2.0: Rethinking the Roles of LLMs for Scalable RTL Bug Synthesis
items.abstract: AI-assisted RTL localization and debugging need ground-truth bug datasets with known locations and observable failures, while testbench grading uses injected bugs to measure detection capability. Creating such datasets at scale remains a major EDA challenge. BugGen 1.0 shows that Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate context-aware RTL mutations. Still, it relies on the model for both choosing where to mutate and generating the edit, which increases inference costs and can lead to invalid choices. BugGen 2.0 changes this division of labor. Deterministic algorithms handle structural analysis, target selection, and validation, while the LLM focuses on localized semantic rewriting. Across four OpenTitan IP blocks and FabScalar with three LLMs, BugGen 2.0 reaches every requested quota of compilable bug scenarios that cause at least two test failures, with 14-16 of 16 configured mutation types represented. In completed same-model comparisons, it reduces token use by 6.8x-15.4x relative to BugGen 1.0 and 1.5x-7.9x relative to Firefly. BugGen 2.0 also expands the dataset without simulating every new bug. After finding accepted scenarios with observable failures, it generates alternative mutations at the same locations, simulates only a subset, and estimates acceptance for the rest. This skips 63.6% of AES and 33.9% of FabScalar variant simulations. Full simulation finds that 77.7% of AES variants and 95.2% of FabScalar variants are accepted, with a 1.09% estimation error on the directly comparable FabScalar set. These results show that focusing LLMs on semantic rewriting lowers inference and simulation cost while improving consistency across models and designs.

items.title: Learning to Undo: Transfer Reinforcement Learning under State Space Transformations
items.abstract: Transfer learning in reinforcement learning (RL) has shown strong empirical success. In this work, we take a more principled perspective by studying when and how transferring knowledge between MDPs (a source and a target) can be provably beneficial. Specifically, we consider the case where there exists an undo map such that applying this map to the target's state space recovers the source exactly. We propose an algorithm that learns this map by matching state feature statistics gathered from both MDPs, and then uses it to transfer the source policy to the target. We theoretically justify the algorithm by analyzing the setting when the undo map is linear and the source is linearly-$Q^\star$ realizable, where our approach has strictly better sample complexity than tabula rasa RL in the target MDP. Empirically, we demonstrate that these benefits extend beyond this regime: on challenging continuous control tasks and Atari games, our method achieves significantly better sample efficiency. Overall, our results highlight how shared structure between tasks can be leveraged for efficient transfer of policies across environments.

items.title: Colombo: A Frontier-to-Frontier Autoresearch System for Oracle-Based Optimization
items.abstract: Science advances from frontier to frontier as discoveries reshape what is known and create the basis for further discovery. We present Colombo, a self-organizing AI researcher that drives this renewal, first instantiated in oracle-based optimization. Here, the central question is how efficiently a problem class can be solved through a prescribed information interface and what costs no admissible algorithm can avoid. The gap between achievable guarantees and unavoidable limits defines the frontier recorded in its Complexity Atlas, a living map of frontier settings and the current state of knowledge. Self-Organization turns unresolved gaps into adaptive research programmes, coordinating conjecture formation, mathematical investigation, and replanning as evidence accumulates. Adversarial Co-Ascent develops algorithms and hard families through reciprocal challenge, exposing mechanisms of information use and concealment that guide stronger methods and proofs of unavoidable costs. Independent review and Lean-based formal certification check mathematical claims, while the Long-Term Memory carries supported findings and research experience across settings. To date, Colombo has established optimal or near-optimal rates for more than fifty settings in the Atlas. Colombo thus takes a concrete step toward Autopoietic Science: a scientific process whose validated advances regenerate the conditions of its own progress, continually reshaping how inquiry is organized and what it can discover.

items.title: A Unified Choice Model of News Selection: Experimental Evidence on Stance, Rank, and Engagement Cues
items.abstract: Social media platforms often display visual engagement cues alongside ranked news articles, yet their influence on clicks remains poorly understood when considered jointly with ranking position and users' political preferences. We propose a unified discrete choice framework using a conditional multinomial logit model to jointly estimate and compare the influence of these factors on news selection. We evaluate the model using 1,480 choices from 370 human participants across four news topics in a controlled study with and without visual engagement cues. The framework allows us to assess the incremental contribution of each factor through nested-model likelihood-ratio tests. We find that including visual engagement cues significantly improves model fit across all topics after accounting for rank and stance. Engagement cues alone also predict clicks better than either of these features, although the full model achieves the highest held-out log-likelihood. Finally, we quantify via counterfactual analysis the impact of ranking position and displayed engagement counts on click probabilities. These findings can inform platform owners, researchers, and policymakers evaluating how platform design affects the selection of political news.

items.title: Runtime Verification of Multiple Natural Language Criteria for Agent Governance
items.abstract: AI agents are governed by hundreds of natural language criteria, yet existing verifiers cannot efficiently evaluate an agent's output against a large set of such criteria and report which are satisfied, violated, or inapplicable. We introduce the VFM, a tree-attention verifier that encodes the shared context and target text, and scores N natural language criteria in parallel, returning independent per-criterion ternary verdicts. The VFM is pretrained on CriteriaBank, a corpus of 394K (context, target, criterion, verdict) tuples spanning over 321K distinct criterion strings. A finetuned VFM-4B outperforms GPT-5.4 on a synthetic governance benchmark. On the DynaBench multi-criterion benchmark, it outperforms DynaGuard-4B on trace-level failure detection, and its per-criterion verdicts localize the violated rule and support focused escalation to a larger chain-of-thought judge. We show that CriteriaBank pretraining improves cross-domain transfer, particularly in the low-data regime, while matching a strong direct-finetuning control at full data. On a single H100, VFM-4B evaluates 1,000 criteria against a 4K-token context in under 2s at <11 GB VRAM, making it suitable for runtime verification.
