items.title: Cardiovascular Reactivity to Peer Rejection Moderates the Impact of Early Life Stress on Body Mass Index in Adolescent Girls: A Cluster Analysis Approach.
items.abstract: Early life stress is linked to poor cardiometabolic outcomes including obesity. Blunted physiological stress reactivity, which may be adaptive in adverse contexts, has also been associated with obesity. The present study examines whether cardiovascular reactivity (CVR) serves as a biological susceptibility factor that moderates the longitudinal association between early life stress and body mass index (BMI) in female adolescents. Participants were 80 female adolescents (Mage= 13.3 years). Participants completed the Psychosocial Schedule to assess cumulative early life stress. The Yale Interpersonal Stressor-Child paradigm was executed to assess systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), and heart rate (HR) during acute stress exposure. K-means clustering identified CVR patterns based on reactivity from baseline to the stressor. Height and weight were measured at baseline and twelve months later to derive BMI-for-age. Two CVR clusters were identified: high CVR (n=31; MΔSBP=15.0mmHg, MΔDBP=8.21mmHg, MΔHR=7.05 bpm) and low CVR (n= 49; MΔSBP=4.70mmHg, MΔDBP=3.58mmHg, MΔHR=0.94 bpm). CVR moderated the association between early life stress and BMI-for-age at 12-month follow-up, controlling for pubertal status, socioeconomic status, depression, and race/ethnicity (B(SE) =-4.61 (1.71), p =.009). Higher early life stress predicted higher BMI-for-age among adolescents with low CVR (B(SE)=3.53 (1.39), p=.01) but not among those with high CVR. Early life stress was associated with higher BMI-for-age only among adolescents with blunted CVR, suggesting reduced stress reactivity as a potential physiological risk pathway for obesity among adolescent females.

items.title: Cognitive capacity in subjective cognitive decline: Insights from electrophysiological markers and dual-task performance.
items.abstract: Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) refers to self-reported cognitive deficits in the absence of objective cognitive impairment. Evidence suggests that neural changes may precede performance declines, highlighting the potential of electroencephalography (EEG) to detect early cognitive declines. Electrophysiological markers and changes in cognitive and motor performance were examined during dual-task performance to better understand the neural mechanisms underlying SCD. Older adults with (n=20) and without (n=20) SCD performed a working memory and finger tapping task simultaneously (i.e., dual task) and alone (i.e., single cognitive or motor). Linear mixed models were used to assess task and group effects for behavioural performance and EEG measures, including mean amplitude and power spectral density, in frontal, central, and parietal regions of interest (ROI). P2 and P3b mean amplitude were smaller during the dual task compared to single cognitive task. Additionally, the SCD group exhibited higher theta power overall and higher alpha power in each task and ROI compared to the non-SCD group. Higher power was observed during the dual task compared to single tasks except in the alpha band where the opposite was observed. Cognitive and motor performance decreased between single and dual tasks, and slower finger tapping speed was observed in the SCD compared to the non-SCD group. Neural and performance findings support the capacity sharing model of attention and may reflect the use of compensatory mechanisms in the SCD group. Electrophysiological changes may precede objective cognitive deficits and have the potential to complement existing approaches to characterizing SCD but must be examined longitudinally.

items.title: Cardiac vagal and cardiac sympathetic activity in healthy humans during and after face immersion are moderated by water temperature and apnea.
items.abstract: The interaction between cardiac vagal and cardiac sympathetic activity during face immersion remains poorly understood, yet it is critical for identifying potential autonomic conflict. This study sought to disentangle the individual and synergistic contributions of breathing mode (apnea vs. snorkel breathing) and water temperature (10°C vs. 30°C) on heart rate, cardiac vagal (RMSSD), and cardiac sympathetic (PEP) indices before, during, and after exposure. In a randomized within-subjects design, 52 healthy adults completed five 30-second conditions: 1) apnea in an empty bowl, 2) apnea in cold water, 3) apnea in warm water, 4) snorkel breathing in cold water, and 5) snorkel breathing in warm water. Heart rate, RMSSD, and PEP were measured for 30 seconds before, during and after each condition. Significant bradycardia occurred in all five conditions. Apnea in an empty bowl resulted in the smallest bradycardia and a decrease in RMSSD. While cold-water apnea caused the strongest bradycardia, snorkel breathing in cold water elicited the largest RMSSD increase. PEP remained stable throughout all conditions and time points. These results demonstrate that face immersion triggers stimulus-dependent autonomic pathways. The observed decoupling of heart rate and RMSSD during apnea questions the validity of RMSSD as an index of cardiac vagal activity during breath-holding. The stability of PEP is consistent with predominantly cardiac parasympathetic involvement in diving bradycardia. These findings highlight limitations of RMSSD interpretation during apnea and emphasize the necessity of accounting for breathing modality in autonomic assessments. Applied interventions using cold-water face immersion under safe conditions are encouraged.

items.title: Dynamics of Daily Stress and Negative Affect Intensity in Early Adolescence: A DSEM Analysis of Cognitive Reappraisal, Physical Activity, and Trait Resilience.
items.abstract: Early adolescents exhibit heightened emotional reactivity to daily stress (defined here as the subjective intensity of the most bothersome daily hassle). However, the daily factors associated with variation in this reactivity in naturalistic settings remain inadequately understood. Specifically, cognitive reappraisal and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) were examined as daily state-level moderators, alongside trait resilience as a stable dispositional moderator. To explicitly test both within-person and cross-level moderating effects, this study utilized a 21-day daily diary design to track 120 junior high school students (yielding 1,965 valid daily observations). Variables were assessed using brief self-reports, including a Visual Analogue Scale for negative affect intensity and categorical assessments for moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA). Bayesian dynamic structural equation modeling (DSEM) was employed to disentangle within-person fluctuations from between-person traits while accounting for the carry-over effects of previous-day negative affect. Daily stress significantly and positively predicted same-day negative affect intensity (b = 2.95, 95% CI [2.63, 3.27]). Crucially, DSEM revealed that engaging in same-day cognitive reappraisal (b = -1.62, 95% CI [-1.97, -1.27]) or MVPA (b = -2.38, 95% CI [-2.69, -2.08]) was associated with a significantly weaker daily stress-affect intensity link at the within-person level. Furthermore, trait resilience significantly moderated this association at the cross-level (b = -1.20, 95% CI [-1.76, -0.63]), with a weaker stress-negative affect association at higher resilience. These findings identify cognitive reappraisal, MVPA, and trait resilience as moderators of the daily stress-negative affect association in early adolescence.

items.title: Mapping the shared genetic architecture between anorexia nervosa and metabolomic biomarkers.
items.abstract: Anorexia Nervosa (AN) has the highest mortality rate of any psychiatric disorder yet lacks effective treatments. While recent genomic efforts have reframed AN as a metabo-psychiatric condition that overlaps with cardiometabolic traits, AN's relationship to circulating metabolomic markers remains unknown. We examined shared genetic architecture between AN and 249 metabolomic biomarkers, and compared profiles with related mental health, anthropometric and cardiometabolic traits. Genetic and biological overlap was assessed with global genetic correlations, conjunctional false discovery rate, bivariate Gaussian mixture modeling, and gene set enrichment analysis across body tissues. We also explored putative causal relationships between AN, body mass index (BMI), and metabolomic biomarkers. Significant genetic correlations emerged between AN and 142 metabolomic biomarkers, which were opposite in direction to cardiometabolic traits such as BMI and type 2 diabetes (rs<-0.94), and stronger than correlations with anxiety. Shared variants between AN and metabolomic biomarkers, particularly lipid-based metabolites, exhibited a mixture of positive and negative effects. These were mapped to genes involved in lipid-related cell signals, developmental growth, and inflammation, and were widely expressed in the brain, most internal organs and female reproductive organs. Bidirectional associations between AN and metabolomic biomarkers were found to act through their respective influence on BMI. These findings reveal a complex, bidirectional mixture of positive and negative genetic relationships between AN and systemic metabolism, which would be obscured by examination of broader cardiometabolic traits. Uncovering specific shared lipid and developmental pathways provides a genetically-anchored mechanistic understanding of the illness, while highlighting promising metabolomic targets for weight restoration approaches.

items.title: Mental health and behavioral difficulties in children with rare neonatal gastrointestinal surgical conditions: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Introduction This systematic review aimed to assess prevalence and characteristics of mental health and behavioral difficulties in children with seven neonatal gastrointestinal surgical conditions, to compare these to normative populations, and identify associated factors. Material and Methods Using a PRISMA compliant protocol (PROSPERO CRD42023443731), studies on congenital diaphragmatic hernia(CDH), esophageal atresia(EA), abdominal wall defects (AWD: gastroschisis/omphalocele), anorectal malformations (ARM), Hirschsprung's disease (HSCR) and surgical necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) were identified through searches in MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, CINAHL, and Cochrane Library (inception-November 2025) A random-effects meta-analysis of prevalence was conducted, with heterogeneity assessed using I². Significance level was p<0.05. Results Forty-seven studies (published 1991-2025) with 1786 children (median sample size 28, range 10-157) were included: CDH (n=10), EA (n=11), AWD (n=9), NEC (n=2), ARM (n=17), and HSCR (n=5). Most studies originated from Europe (n=31). Mental health and behavioral difficulties were more frequently reported than in norms, in CDH (7/8 studies), EA (6/7 studies), and ARM (4/6 studies). Meta-analysis showed elevated difficulties in 25,7% (Child Behavior Check List; I²=59.6) and 17.8% (Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire; I²=65.3). The prevalence of autism ranged from 10-23% (CDH, AWD) and ADHD from 0-20% (CDH, AWD, NEC, ARM, HSCR). Across studies, methodological quality was generally 'fair' to 'poor'. Clinical and family-related factors were significantly associated with outcomes (p<0.05). Conclusions Children with rare neonatal gastrointestinal surgical conditions risk mental health and behavioral difficulties. Current research leaves room for improvement of study quality. Multidisciplinary follow-up care is warranted, and its effects should be evaluated.

items.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials investigating cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia in stroke and traumatic brain injury populations.
items.abstract: Insomnia is highly prevalent following stroke and traumatic brain injury (TBI), and can contribute to challenges with mood, psychological functioning and quality of life. Emerging evidence supports the efficacy of cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) for those who have experienced stroke or TBI, however a broader review incorporating sleep and mood-related outcomes has not yet been conducted. A systematic literature search was performed on Scopus, PubMed, Embase, and PsycINFO databases. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2.0 tool. Random-effects meta-analyses calculating pooled effect sizes were performed, alongside assessment of heterogeneity and sensitivity analyses. Nine randomised controlled trials were included, with seven contributing to the primary meta-analysis. CBT-I was associated with lower insomnia disorder severity on the ISI (MD = -3.07, 95% CI [-4.46; -1.67], p = 0.0037) and lower sleep disturbance on the PSQI (MD = -1.81, 95% CI [-2.82; -0.80], p = 0.0058). Secondary analyses demonstrated a small, significant effect on anxiety symptoms (Hedges' g = -0.30, 95% CI [-0.49; -0.12], p = 0.0106), and a small-moderate non-significant effect on depressive symptoms (Hedges' g = -0.36, 95% CI [-0.84; 0.12], p = 0.1146). CBT-I appears a promising intervention for improving insomnia after stroke or TBI, with additional modest benefits for depression and anxiety.

items.title: Dramatised Reading Workshops for Older Adults With Neurocognitive Disorders: A Pilot Study.
items.abstract: Theatre workshops for older adults have proliferated over the last ten years and have become a field of study in psychology. These workshops include dramatised reading, which has positive effects on mood, behaviour and social relationships in older adults who do not live from neurocognitive disorders. However, no study has explored the effects of these workshops on older adults with neurocognitive disorders. The aim of this pilot study was to investigate the effects of participation in dramatised reading workshops on older adults with neurocognitive disorders. Ten women aged 70 to 95 with moderate neurocognitive disorder (MMSE score: M = 18.2, SD = 3.49) took part in dramatised reading workshops over 6 months. Participants self-assessed their feelings of loneliness, self-efficacy, quality of life, well-being and life satisfaction. Assessments were made before and after participation in the workshops. The results show positive effects on well-being (W = 0.00; p = 0.006), quality of life (W = 3.5; p = 0.017), anxiety-depressive symptoms (W = 34.5; p = 0.025) and feelings of loneliness (W = 53; p = 0.011). These results suggest that participation in dramatised reading workshops may have beneficial effects on general mood, quality of life, well-being and feelings of loneliness in older adults with neurocognitive disorders.

items.title: A theory of generalized vector coding and subicular function.
items.abstract: Neural information processing is inextricably linked to the selectivity of individual neurons, as described by their receptive fields. Far from the sensory periphery, neural representations are the result of substantial upstream processing, mixed with internally generated information. Low-dimensional spatial codes in the hippocampal formation offer a handle on understanding these representations. The subiculum, a key but comparatively understudied hippocampal area, exhibits numerous, seemingly unrelated neural codes. Neurons like boundary vector cells, corner cells, or axis-tuned cells are named after the environmental features that appear to drive them, but a common account for their neuronal selectivity is lacking. Here, we propose Disco, a theory explaining subicular functions and related neural codes in other areas. Given the continuous flow of experience, subicular activity can be understood as signaling discontinuities in that flow, coded in a vector base. Geometric discontinuities drive responses to walls, drops, objects, holes, corners, and curved surfaces. The generality of Disco enables predictions for 3D environments, natural scenes, and mixed-modality coding. Discontinuities are not identical to the concept of boundaries (abstract or spatial), as illustrated by non-spatial discontinuities in behavioral state. These yield axis coding in the model (activity along parallel maze arms). Finally, tracking population activity signals event boundaries as discontinuities in neural space. The emergence of diverse neural activity suggests that discontinuity coding may serve as a key principle in the subiculum and related brain areas supporting (spatial) memory and navigation.

items.title: Physical Activity in Daily Life and Mental Health: Investigating Aerobic Intensity and Strength Training.
items.abstract: The current study examined the relationships between different types of physical activity and mental health in daily life. Participants (24 adults, 71% females) completed physical activity and mental health surveys across seven months, contributing a total of 129 observations. Total physical activity as well as light, moderate, and vigorous aerobic activity and muscle-strengthening activity were assessed. Mental health was evaluated as depressive symptoms, anxiety, stress, positive affect, and negative affect. Mixed-effects regression models using total physical activity and types of physical activity to estimate associations with mental health were completed. Higher overall physical activity scores were associated with lower depressive symptoms and higher positive affect. Moderate aerobic activity scores were associated with lower depressive symptoms and stress as well as higher positive affect but were not associated with improvements in anxiety or negative affect. These results indicate a possible correlation between increased physical activity and improved mental health as indicated by depressive symptoms, stress, and positive affect. Given the prevalence of inactive lifestyles in many societies, physical activity is a modifiable lifestyle change that may help promote mental health.

items.title: Attention to faces and voices predicts internalizing problems in a community sample of toddlers: A new measure & novel predictors.
items.abstract: Heightened internalizing problems predict negative outcomes, including anxiety and depression. However, few studies have characterized whether foundational child behaviors, such as attention, predict internalizing outcomes. We recently demonstrated that three foundational "multisensory attention skills" (e.g., maintaining and shifting/disengaging attention, matching synchronous sights and sounds) predict a variety of socioemotional, language, and cognitive outcomes. Here, we investigated whether these multisensory attention skills predict emerging internalizing problems. A community sample of 36-month-olds (N = 84) participating in a longitudinal study received the novel Multisensory Attention Assessment Protocol to assess the three multisensory attention skills to faces and voices. Parents completed the Infant-Toddler Social and Emotional Assessment to assess internalizing problems. Results from structural equation modeling indicated that better multisensory attention skills, particularly better synchrony detection and matching of faces and voices, predicted lower levels of internalizing problems. Findings also demonstrated a pathway from basic to higher-order attention skills: faster shifting to look to faces predicted longer attention maintenance to faces, which predicted greater face-voice matching, which in turn, predicted lower levels of internalizing problems. Findings identify basic, early developing attention skills to non-threatening audiovisual social stimulation as novel predictors of internalizing problems in early childhood.

items.title: Child protection case management and adolescent mental health in humanitarian contexts: A mixed-methods study in Colombia and Nigeria.
items.abstract: Adolescents in humanitarian contexts are vulnerable to emotional distress, violence and trauma. Child protection case management (CM) is a primary response service for children in these contexts. To evaluate the association between CM and adolescents' wellbeing and mental health, and to explore the pathways through which CM supports these outcomes, including the role of the caseworker-adolescent relationship. Adolescents aged 13 to 17 in Norte de Santander, Colombia (N = 90) and Maiduguri Metropolitan Council, Nigeria (N = 99). Both contexts are socially and politically unstable, hosting large numbers of refugees and internally displaced populations. Using a pre-post, single-arm mixed-methods design, the assessed wellbeing (WHO-5) and emotional distress (PHQ-A) as primary outcomes, and safety, basic needs, agency, relationships, and empathy as intermediary outcomes. Fixed-effects regression models were estimated using baseline and endline data to assess change in primary outcomes. A parallel mediation analysis was implemented with intermediary outcomes as mediator variables between caseworkers' empathy and adolescent wellbeing using PROCESS framework, combined with qualitative interviews with adolescents analyzed using axial analysis. Participation in CM was associated with a significant increase in adolescents' wellbeing (WHO-5: β = 2.71, p < 0.001) and reduced emotional distress (PHQ-A: β = -3.45, p < 0.001) at endline, alongside self-reported improvements in family and peer relationships, safety, and agency. Higher perceived caseworker empathy was associated with increased wellbeing directly, and indirectly through enhanced feelings of safety (p < 0.01) and peer relationships (p < 0.05). CM contributes to adolescent mental health in humanitarian contexts. An empathetic relationship between caseworkers and adolescents is a key CM pathway.

items.title: Review of Stephen E. Finn's Therapeutic Assessment and Interpersonal Neurobiology.
items.abstract: Stephen Finn's Therapeutic Assessment and Interpersonal Neurobiology: Empathy, Intersubjectivity, and the Longing to Be Known extends his influential work on Therapeutic Assessment by framing psychological assessment as an intersubjective process through which clients can feel known, reduce shame, and develop new understandings of themselves. In this review I highlight the book's compelling clinical cases and practical insights regarding empathy, collaboration, pacing, epistemic trust, and the therapeutic use of psychological tests. I also discusses hypotheses about neuroscientific mechanisms that could underlie clinical processes active in the technique. Overall, the book offers a powerful account of assessment as an interpersonal intervention and provides valuable lessons for clinicians and clinical scientists well beyond Therapeutic Assessment.

items.title: Case Report: Manic Decompensation During the Second Trimester of Pregnancy Requiring Electroconvulsive Therapy.
items.abstract: Manic episodes during pregnancy represent a significant clinical challenge due to risks for both the mother and fetus, as well as the limitations inherent to pharmacological treatment during gestation. Severe affective episodes-particularly those with manic symptoms-may lead to heightened maternal stress, impulsive behaviors, impaired self-care, and potential obstetric complications. Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) constitutes a therapeutic alternative when pharmacotherapy is ineffective or contraindicated. We present the case of a 31-year-old pregnant woman with a history of an unspecified affective disorder within the bipolar spectrum, who developed an acute manic episode during the second trimester following withdrawal of lithium for conception planning. The patient required psychiatric hospitalization due to progressive psychomotor agitation, disinhibition, and insomnia. After multidisciplinary evaluation, nine ECT sessions were administered between 18 and 21 weeks of gestation, with standardized anesthetic management and close obstetric monitoring. No maternal or fetal complications were observed. The patient exhibited progressive clinical improvement, allowing stabilization and safe continuation of pregnancy. This case highlights the potential efficacy and relative safety of ECT in managing severe manic episodes during pregnancy when prompt maternal stabilization is required. It also underscores the importance of coordinated multidisciplinary care and individualized risk-benefit assessment.

items.title: Subjective Experience of a Severe Mental Disorder: A Qualitative Study of Siblings' Perspectives.
items.abstract: The subjective experience of siblings of individuals with severe mental disorders (SMDs) remains largely unexamined, despite their critical role within the family system and their growing involvement in informal caregiving. To explore in depth the subjective experience of SMD, analyzing the emotional impacts, informal caregiving demands, quality of life and family dynamics. An exploratory qualitative study involving 60 adult siblings of patients with SMD. Data were collected via semi-structured interviews and analyzed in accordance with the principles of Grounded Theory. Qualitative analysis identified four core empirical categories: Subjective Appraisal, Coping, Quality of life, and Family Relationships. Participants described persistent negative emotions (fear, anger, sadness, guilt) that compromised their well-being and relational dynamics. Ongoing involvement in informal caregiving was characterized as "emotionally draining," restricting personal trajectories and altering family structures. Grounded in these findings, the emerging theoretical model conceptualizes siblings' resistance as an active, dynamic, and processual phenomenon balancing adaptive and defensive mechanisms. The sibling experience in SMD is characterized by a substantial emotional and relational strain that remains largely unrecognized in mental health services. Emerging theory suggests that sibling resistance is neither a homogeneous nor a generalizable phenomenon, but rather a dynamic, evolving, and idiosyncratic process. Specific, sustained, and family-centered interventions are required to address siblings' unique needs as essential stakeholders in care.

items.title: Mentalization in Older People as a Function of Trauma and Somatic Stress.
items.abstract: Mentalization facilitates social interactions and helps to process traumatic experiences, but only a few studies have examined in detail the ability to mentalize in old age, with most of them suggesting that mentalization abilities are lower in later life. The aim of this study was to conduct a differentiated assessment of mentalization in older people and to identify possible influencing factors, such as sociodemographic, age-, and health-related variables, along with trauma and social support. Mentalization was assessed using the Adult Attachment Interview with the Reflective Functioning Scale (RFS), and the Reflective Functioning Questionnaire (RFQ-8). Additionally, trauma was assessed using the following self-report measures: the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire (CTQ) to determine early life stress (ELS); the Posttraumatic Diagnostic Scale (PDS); a questionnaire on war stress (Kriegsbelastungsfragebogen (KBF)); the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS); and a social support questionnaire (Fragebogen zur Sozialen Unterstützung (F-SozU)). The study included 72 participants, aged between 60 and 90 (mean age 78.9), who were patients at a geriatric day care clinic. The ability to mentalize as indicated on the RFS was poor (5.6% with RFS ≥ 4). No correlation was found between self- and other-related mentalization abilities. Trauma events in childhood were reported by 75% of the participants. High current trauma-related symptoms as indicated on the PDS were related to a greater mentalization ability (b = 0.031, p = 0.01). Age, the number of somatic and mental disorders, and the degree of anxiety/depressiveness and social support had no influence on the ability to mentalize. Poor mentalization skills may be due to age, but also cohort-specific trauma is a plausible contributing factor that warrants further investigation. The seemingly paradoxical connection between a high level of trauma-associated symptoms and a greater mentalization ability also needs to be examined more closely. Further research is necessary to enhance the assessment of mentalization, especially in old age.

items.title: Targeting and Tracking Personality Functioning in Psychotherapy: A Clinical Case Using the Diagnostic Interview for Personality Pathology Based on ICD-11 (DIPP-11).
items.abstract: Aspects of personality functioning are central to the World Health Organization's ICD-11 dimensional classification of personality disorder and are operationalized in the Diagnostic Interview for Personality Pathology based on ICD-11 (DIPP-11). The present case report illustrates how the DIPP-11 framework may be used to conceptualize, guide, and track psychotherapy with a young man, "Alex," whose stylistic trait presentation was characterized primarily by Negative Affectivity and Detachment in terms of anxiousness, shame, social withdrawal, and emotional inhibition. The report follows Alex before, during, and after a course of eclectic outpatient psychotherapy in a public mental health setting and demonstrates how the 16 DIPP-11 aspects of personality functioning can serve both as treatment targets and as indicators of therapeutic change. The case particularly shows how impairments in self-esteem regulation, self-direction, perspective-taking, emotional regulation, decision-making, and situational-interpersonal appraisal may gradually improve through a combination of supportive psychotherapy, corrective emotional experiences, and the mobilization of fundamental trust. Treatment progress is illustrated through repeated DIPP-11 ratings, showing change as movement from higher to lower dysfunction scores. The case is discussed as an example of how a focus on personality functioning may offer a more dimensional, individualized, recovery-oriented and less stigmatizing approach to psychotherapy with people presenting with personality problems. Clinical implications are considered for treatment planning, outcome monitoring, and service implementation across WHO member states.

items.title: Individual differences in infants' early home music environment are associated with later expressive vocabulary development outcomes.
items.abstract: Informal music experiences and engagement (e.g., parent-child singing activities) are common in infancy and early childhood. However, the specific role of the early home music environment in fostering infants' development remains understudied. Recent theories and empirical evidence demonstrate shared biology between music and language processing, as well as overlapping acoustic characteristics of speech and song. Emerging yet limited work has established positive links between infants' early home music environments and their later receptive vocabulary development. Here, we assessed whether infants' home music environment is a significant unique predictor of infants' expressive vocabulary development, an established early marker of children's language outcomes. In this longitudinal study, 42 parents completed the Music@Home questionnaire to capture their 6-12 month old infants' home music environments. Parents subsequently completed the MacArthur-Bates Communicative Development Inventory when their infants were 18- and 24-months of age as a measure of their infants' expressive vocabulary development. Generalized linear mixed-effects modeling revealed that infants' general home music environment and the amount parents sing to their infants at 6-12 months significantly predicted their infants' 18- and 24-month expressive vocabulary outcomes, even when accounting for other parental factors (parents' musicality, education levels, parental verbal responsivity, and parents' affective attachment). The model including parent singing demonstrated better fit than the model including the general home music environment. These findings highlight the importance of rich home musical activities, especially parent singing, as a correlate and potential facilitator of early vocabulary development. Findings also motivate further research on how enriched home music environments may serve as a potential protective factor for children at risk for developmental speech/language disorders.

items.title: Beyond the basics: Using nonlinear approaches to classical statistical tests to improve fit and interpretability.
items.abstract: Nonlinear models are less familiar to practitioners and can appear intimidating. However, nonlinear models often fit data better and, critically, may improve interpretability. Our previous work gave a simple introduction to nonlinear regression modeling, providing simple and straightforward examples and underscored the superiority of likelihood methods in obtaining confidence intervals. The current manuscript extends this introduction and shows how classic linear models - such as paired t-tests, analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), two-way ANOVA, and logistic regression - can benefit from using a nonlinear approach to fitting the data. Here we introduce, explore and discuss several of these approaches using important examples which highlight the benefits of the nonlinear methodology to the data analysis. As demonstrated herein, these benefits include (but are not limited to) providing additional insights into the process underlying the data, more appropriate model fit of the data, and more directly addressing the research questions. The provided R code can be adapted for use.

items.title: Psychotherapy as gendered participatory sense-making: An enactive analysis of patients' and therapists' experiences in Austrian private psychotherapy practices.
items.abstract: Research on gender in psychotherapy has largely conceptualized gender as a stable characteristic of therapists and patients, yielding inconsistent findings. Drawing on an enactive perspective, this study examined gender as a dynamic process of participatory sense-making. We conducted 40 semi-structured interviews with patients and psychotherapists in private psychotherapy practices in Austria, including matched patient-therapist dyads. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Perceived gender similarity often fostered familiarity, ease, and embodied understanding, whereas perceived gender difference created opportunities for reflection, learning, and new relational experiences. The significance of gender varied across therapeutic relationships and was frequently intertwined with other social factors, particularly age. Overall, gender emerged as a relational, embodied, affective, and context-dependent dimension of the therapeutic process rather than simply a stable characteristic of patients and therapists. These findings complement categorical approaches to gender by showing how its significance is enacted within therapeutic relationships. Therapists may benefit from attending to how gender becomes salient, remains backgrounded, or becomes intertwined with other relational meanings in specific therapeutic encounters.

items.title: Dynamic associations between impulsivity, craving, and co-use of alcohol, cannabis, and nicotine among young adults: A study protocol.
items.abstract: Relative to other age groups, young adults are at elevated risk for alcohol, cannabis, and nicotine use as well as their dual-use (i.e., use of alcohol with cannabis or nicotine) and tri-use (use of all three substances). Although impulsivity and craving are established risk factors for substance use, little is known about how these processes dynamically relate to dual-/tri-use in daily life. Prior research has largely examined impulsivity as a trait or aggregated across days, limiting understanding of momentary changes in impulsivity and craving surrounding substance use episodes. This study will use ecological momentary assessment (EMA) to examine dynamic associations among impulsivity, craving, and alcohol, cannabis, and nicotine use in 250 young adults (ages 18-25) who report past-month use of all three substances and recent dual-/tri-use. Following an in-person assessment of trait impulsivity, inhibitory control, and impulsive choice, participants will complete five smartphone-based assessments per day for 17 days. EMA assessments will capture five facets of state impulsivity (negative urgency, positive urgency, sensation seeking, perseverance, and planning), substance-specific craving, substance use and co-use, mood, location, and social context. Multilevel models will examine whether daily impulsivity and craving are associated with dual- and tri-use relative to alcohol-only use. Time-varying effect models will characterize changes in impulsivity and craving before, during, and after alcohol use initiation and determine whether concurrent cannabis and/or nicotine use alters associations. Moderation analyses will explore whether associations vary as a function of mood, social and environmental context, sex, racial-ethnic group, and baseline impulsivity. By capturing within-person fluctuations in impulsivity and craving in naturalistic settings, this study will clarify when and under what conditions these processes are associated with alcohol, cannabis, and nicotine dual-/tri-use. Findings will advance understanding of the temporal mechanisms underlying dual-/tri-use and may identify time-sensitive targets for prevention and intervention among young adults at elevated risk for substance-related harms.

items.title: The VaLuE Study: A Grounded Theory of What It Means to 'Value' the Lived/Live Experience of Mental Health Difficulties Amongst Clinical Psychology Doctoral Trainees.
items.abstract: Contextualised by a dearth of previous research and inspired by the British Psychological Society's position that lived experience of mental health (MH) difficulties should be both supported and valued, the VaLuE study investigated how current UK trainees on clinical psychology doctoral (DClinPsy) programmes understood what it means to value the lived/live experience of MH difficulties and how this can be achieved. Fourteen DClinPsy trainees partook in semi-structured interviews with transcripts being analysed via constructivist grounded theory. The model was latterly reviewed by these participants and a further three DClinPsy trainees. Grounded theory techniques within a social constructionist frame resulted in the VaLuE model (capitals standing for Valuing Lived Experiences), a relationally framed model which identified utilising as the key concept in determining whether lived/live experience of MH difficulties is valued. A further six interconnected concepts were identified as necessary to achieve utilising and build a supporting and valuing culture. These were: taking accountability, accommodating, role modelling, trusting, embracing, and integrating. Findings are contextualised in social identity and justice frameworks and recommendations for implementation are offered. Building a valuing culture requires intentional, continual, and purposeful action by all members of the clinical psychology community. The VaLuE model provides a framework with which DClinPsy programmes can progress towards this.

items.title: Stigma Reduction and Resiliency Training for First Responders (SRRT-FR): A Feasibility and Initial Efficacy Evaluation.
items.abstract: First responders, especially law enforcement officers (LEOs), frequently encounter individuals experiencing substance use disorders (SUDs). Previous research has documented that a greater understanding of SUDs promotes reductions in stigmatizing perspectives. The present study evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy of the Stigma Reduction and Resiliency Training for First Responders (SRRT-FR), a novel program designed to improve LEO interactions with community members exhibiting SUDs, while also promoting officers' professional well-being. One hundred and ten LEOs participated in SRRT-FR and completed pre-, post- (n = 77; 70% retention), and 4-month follow-up (n = 42; 38% retention) surveys. Statistically significant improvements were observed in role adequacy (ΔM = 1.69, p = 0.004, d = 0.31) and role support (ΔM = 0.74, p = 0.010, d = 0.27), and job satisfaction improved both immediately after training (ΔM = 2.72, p < 0.001, d = 0.62) and at follow-up (ΔM = 2.46, p = 0.009, d = 0.39). Professional self-esteem and role legitimacy did not significantly improve. CD-RISC scores declined immediately post-training (ΔM = -3.26, p = 0.006, d = 0.31) but slightly improved by follow-up, though not significantly. Qualitative feedback indicated the training was acceptable and valued, with participants noting increased knowledge of SUDs, improved communication strategies, and enhanced awareness of personal coping needs. Preliminary findings suggest that SRRT-FR is feasible and acceptable among LEOs and may modestly decrease stigmatizing perspectives and increase resiliency. Replication with larger samples and randomized controlled trials across first responder populations is warranted.

items.title: Methodological Framework for Integrating Large Military Data Sets to Assess Health Outcomes in US Military Deployers and Evacuees, 2001-2015.
items.abstract: The sustained military combat operations in Afghanistan and Iraq following the terrorist attack on America in 2001 have resulted in a new generation of military service members and veterans with unique long-term health needs. This study describes the methodology to construct and integrate large military data sets to enable future comparative analyses of physical and mental health outcomes among US military service members who served on active duty between 2001 and 2015. Research regulatory approvals and data use agreements were completed to obtain data from the population of >5 million service members who served on active duty between 2001 and 2015. To evaluate the physical and mental health outcomes, 4 cohorts were created that included service members who were or were not aeromedically evacuated out of the theater and those who did or did not deploy. Those who deployed and were evacuated for a psychiatric diagnosis were established as the reference cohort (n=9405). Then, cohorts matched for branch of service, sex, and birth year were constructed for those evacuated for a nonpsychiatric medical diagnosis (n=9223), who were not evacuated (n=9265), or who served but never deployed (n=9265). A multidisciplinary team optimized data set construction, demonstrating the feasibility of integrating large military data sets while addressing challenges such as data fragmentation and privacy compliance. This methodology provides a framework for future studies to evaluate long-term health outcomes and informs military health policy.

items.title: An Ecological Whole-Of-Food Systems Framework for Regulating Ultra-Processed Foods.
items.abstract: Ultra-processed foods (UPFs) are a leading contributor to diet-related chronic disease and socio-ecological harm. Despite increasing recognition of these impacts, regulatory responses remain fragmented, focused on isolated actions and individual behavior change, and often legitimize rather than challenge the power of UPF corporations. This study aims to identify and synthesize policy actions and regulatory measures to reduce the share of UPFs in population diets and control industry practices, using an ecological approach to regulation. We conducted a framework synthesis of academic and gray literature, guided by ecological regulation theory and three systems frameworks: the High-Level Panel of Experts food systems framework, Intervention Level Framework, and Food Systems Governance Principles. Data were coded by food system component, sub-component, and intervention level, and synthesized into a final framework. We identified 59 recommendations across four food system components (governance, supply chains, food environments, and systemic drivers) ranging from upstream paradigm shifts to downstream regulatory actions. The framework integrates four key principles of ecological regulation: ecological orientation, synergistic interactions, plurality of actors, and diversity of measures. Examples from Brazil, Chile, and Mexico illustrate their application in practice. This is the first synthesis to apply ecological regulation to food policy design, offering a systems-based alternative to conventional regulatory approaches. It supports the design of integrated, structural interventions to address the complex drivers of UPF proliferation and guide national and international policy responses.

items.title: TRPM8 channel blockers as a potential new pharmacological class for the treatment of migraine.
items.abstract: Migraine therapy has advanced in recent years, particularly with the emergence of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)-targeting drugs. However, acute treatment still faces limitations, especially in patients who are unresponsive to or unable to take triptans or gepants. Transient receptor potential melastatin 8 (TRPM8) is a polymodal-gated, nonselective cation channel that represents a promising target for the treatment of migraine supported by genetic, preclinical and clinical evidence. This review covers the evidence supporting an important role for TRPM8 in the pathophysiology of migraine and provides a detailed synopsis of the preclinical, pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic profiles of potential TRPM8-interacting compounds in clinical development for the treatment of migraine. PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched to August 2026 for TRPM8 and migraine, supplemented by 2026 congress abstracts and company disclosures. TRPM8 channel blockade has a mechanistically distinct approach from current therapeutics. A proof-of-concept and dose range finding Phase 2 study with elismetrep, a novel, oral TRPM8 blocker, provides supportive, although not definitive, evidence for TRPM8 blockers in migraine. Although the primary endpoint of 2-hour pain freedom was not statistically significant, numerically greater effects at 20 mg and nominally significant secondary-endpoint findings support further development.

items.title: Sexual dimorphism in morphological predictors of upper- and lower-limb strength in adult rugby players.
items.abstract: Sex differences in athletic performance extend beyond body size, encompassing morphology-strength relationships. To analyse sex-specific associations between body size and composition (body mass, fat-free mass [FFM], and thigh volume) and strength (hand grip strength and isokinetic knee extensor and flexor strength) in adult rugby players. 84 players (42 males) were assessed. Body composition was measured by air-displacement plethysmography, and thigh volume was estimated anthropometrically. Strength was measured by grip (kg) and isokinetic knee torque at 60°·s-1. Males were taller (178.3 cm), heavier (82.7 kg), and stronger (hand grip: 48.2 kg; knee extensors: 252 N·m). Females had a higher fat percentage (24.2% vs. 14.1%) and lower strength. FFM was the best predictor of peak torque in males (r ≈ 0.69 to 0.74); body mass correlated best (r ≈ 0.45 to 0.50) with peak torque in females. The hamstring-to-quadriceps ratio was, on average, 0.56 in both sexes. Strength determinants differ by sex in rugby players. FFM is the primary predictor of strength in males, whereas body mass is more relevant in females. These findings support the development of sex-specific training methods to optimise performance and potentially reduce injury risk.

items.title: Model-informed characterisation of the target therapeutic window for dexamethasone by quantitatively balancing foetal lung maturation and neurotoxicity in pregnant rats.
items.abstract: Dexamethasone, a first-line treatment for neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS), promotes foetal lung maturation whilst simultaneously inducing neurotoxicity in offspring. We aimed to define the therapeutic window of dexamethasone for the treatment of NRDS. Pregnant rats were given dexamethasone at 0.1 or 0.4 mg·kg-1 to simulate clinically equivalent prenatal dexamethasone exposure. Half of the rats were anaesthetised, and surfactant proteins A and B in foetal lungs quantified. A pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) model was developed to determine the minimum effective concentration. The remaining rats, delivered naturally, and their offspring underwent open-field testing. Messenger RNA sequencing of the foetal hippocampus was performed, and concentration-toxicity assays were conducted using H19-7/IGF-IR cells. Data were integrated with a maternal-foetal physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model to determine the maximum tolerated concentration. A clinical PBPK for dexamethasone in pregnant women was used to simulate a potentially optimal dosing regimen. The PK/PD model adequately characterised dexamethasone-induced foetal lung maturation and indicated a minimal effective concentration of 1.63 ng·ml-1. The offspring of PDE rats exhibited significant behavioural changes. mRNA sequencing analysis suggested that neurotoxicity was mediated via the Wnt pathway and renin-angiotensin system, with BDNF and CMA1 identified as potential biomarkers of neurotoxicity. Cell-based assays suggested a neurotoxic threshold concentration of 17 ng·ml-1. For a therapeutic window of 1.63-17 ng·ml-1, PBPK model simulations indicated that a reduced dose regimen of 2.5 or 3 mg every 8 h for six doses may represent an optimised therapeutic strategy. This model-informed precision dosing strategy provides a rational approach to optimising clinical dexamethasone dosing regimens.

items.title: Polygenic scores improve persistent smoking prediction over single variants and phenotypic factors.
items.abstract: Smoking is a leading cause of preventable death and illness. Genetically-informed precision interventions are feasible, but whether genetic risk for persistent smoking can be captured by high-risk single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) or requires comprehensive assessment using whole-genome polygenic risk scores (PRS) is unknown. This study compared discriminatory performance of a baseline model for long-term persistent smoking based on phenotypic predictors with models that (1) integrate phenotypic predictors with three well-characterized SNPs and (2) incorporate phenotypic predictors and PRS for smoking cessation. Data were from the Nurse's Health Study (NHS) and NHS II, two all-female, prospective cohorts that collected data every 2 years. Two independent data sources were used from baseline (1976 for NHS and 1989 for NHS II) and up to 2014 for NHS and 2015 for NHS II. Population-based, longitudinal cohort studies of nurses from 17 states in the United States. Female, baseline ever-smokers of European ancestry with whole-genome genetic data (NHS: n = 10 017; NHS II: n = 2793). Baseline models included phenotypic and other predictors influencing smoking behavior: age, year of follow-up, smoking intensity, menopausal status, hormone replacement therapy use, early initiation of smoking and body mass index (kg/m2). Additional genetic predictors for persistent smoking were estimated by (1) three well-characterized risk SNPs for smoking (CHRNA5 rs16969968, CYP2A6 rs56113850, DRD2/ANKK1 rs1800497) and (2) PRS. The primary outcome of the study was improvement in predictive performance as measured by the area under the receiver operating characteristics curve (AUC) between baseline models for long-term persistent smoking and models adding genetic risk with (1) risk SNPs and (2) PRS. Within NHS, the baseline model showed moderate predictive performance for persistent smoking with an AUC of 0.674. Adding SNPs showed similar performance (AUC = 0.675), whereas adding PRS statistically significantly improved discriminatory performance, raising the AUC to 0.730, a 5.7% [95% confidence interval (CI) = 5.4%-5.9%] improvement in prediction (AUC) over baseline models. Results were replicated in NHS II, where baseline and SNP models performed moderately with AUCs of 0.671 and 0.677, and adding PRS increased the AUC to 0.735, representing a 6.4% (95% CI = 5.9%-6.8%) improvement in prediction over baseline models. Among females of European ancestry, polygenic risk scores appear to enhance identification of individuals at high risk for long-term, persistent smoking compared with single well-known risk variants and phenotypic predictors. Combining genetic and phenotypic factors can improve risk stratification and precision intervention guidance for long-term smoking abstinence management.

items.title: Current Status and Epidemiologic Perspectives on Mite-, Flea-, and Louse-Borne Diseases in Korea.
items.abstract: This narrative review summarizes the epidemiology and public health relevance of mite-, flea-, and louse-borne infections in Korea. We combined English- and Korean-language literature with national surveillance data. Annual and monthly notifications of scrub typhus and murine typhus were summarized for 2001-2024, and mean annual regional incidence was assessed for 2015-2024 using population statistics. National surveillance recorded 149,303 scrub typhus cases and 660 murine typhus cases during 2001-2024. Scrub typhus showed a pronounced autumn peak and higher incidence in southern and southwestern regions. Murine typhus showed a recent increase in annual case notifications, reaching 60 cases in 2024, with heterogeneous regional patterns. Bartonella henselae infection has been documented in Korea, but its burden remains uncertain. Epidemic typhus and louse-borne relapsing fever have not been officially reported for several decades, although reemergence in vulnerable populations remains possible. Mite-, flea-, and louse-borne infections remain neglected components of the febrile illness landscape in Korea. Improved diagnostic awareness, strengthened surveillance, and continued collaboration are needed to better define their burden and to detect potential reemergence.

items.title: Inhalable IL-10 as an Aerosolized Therapeutic Approach to Acute Lung Injury in Mice.
items.abstract: Background:Acute lung injury (ALI) is a severe inflammatory condition with substantial morbidity and mortality, with no approved pharmacologic therapies targeting its underlying inflammatory pathways. Prior studies demonstrated that intratracheal interleukin (IL)-10 reduces lipopolysaccharide (LPS)- and organic dust-induced lung and systemic inflammation.Methods:The present study evaluated the aerosol performance and efficacy of nebulized IL-10 against a high-dose LPS-induced ALI model with comparisons to shock-dose dexamethasone (5 mg/kg, intraperitoneal injections). C57BL/6 male mice were challenged with LPS (5 mg/mL) and treated with low- (0.1 mg/mL), mid- (0.5 mg/mL), or high-dose (1 mg/mL) IL-10, or vehicle, all by nose-only aerosol inhalation (15-minute exposure duration), with euthanasia on day 2. Results:Aerosolized IL-10 exhibited a mass median aerodynamic diameter of 1.66 µm (geometric standard deviation 2.04). Pulmonary deposited doses were 5.5-5.7 µg/mouse for LPS and 10.4, 21.3, and 38.4 (ug/kg) for low-, mid-, and high-dose IL-10. LPS-induced weight loss (18.6%) was reduced by high IL-10 (8.4%) and dexamethasone (7.0%), with no significant difference between treatments. Increased lung weights (40.8%) following LPS challenge were significantly reduced by mid- and high-dose IL-10 and dexamethasone. LPS-induced airway total cell and neutrophil counts in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid were not reduced by either treatment. In contrast, IL-10 treatment produced dose-dependent reductions in LPS-induced pro-inflammatory mediators (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-12p70, IFN-γ, KC/CXCL1, MCP-1, and MIP-1α), with beneficial responses at the high IL-10 dose comparable to dexamethasone. Histopathology demonstrated dose-responsive reductions in LPS-induced peribronchovascular mixed cellular lung inflammation, significant at mid- and high IL-10 doses and comparable to dexamethasone.Conclusion:Overall, aerosolized IL-10 demonstrated aerodynamic properties consistent with deep lung penetration and dose-dependent efficacy at ≥21.3 µg/kg, achieving anti-inflammatory effects comparable with dexamethasone in this ALI murine model.

items.title: Anthropometry with a nutritional focus on motor function, hand-grip strength and subjectively assessed fatigue at diagnosis in Parkinson´s disease.
items.abstract: Altered anthropometry and nutritional status are associated with motor- and non-motor symptoms in patients with Parkinson´s disease (PD). To investigate if anthropometry can discriminate between low and high levels of motor symptoms, hand grip strength (HGS) and fatigue. Cross-sectional study including baseline data on newly diagnosed patients with PD prior to start of anti-Parkinson medication. Assessments of body composition, risk for malnutrition, fatigue severity scale (FSS) and motor symptoms using Unified Parkinson´s Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS III), including gait performance and ability to arise from chair and HGS were performed at diagnosis. Clinical characteristics and anthropometrical variables were compared between patients with or without motor symptoms and low or high level of fatigue or HGS. Logistic regression was used to examine the association between anthropometry and the odds of having motor difficulties or fatigue. Increased body mass index (BMI) was associated with difficulty arising from chair (OR 1.37, 95% CI 1.09, 1.72, p = 0.007). In addition, these patients had low intracellular water index, (5.2 (1.2) vs. 6.4 (0.7) p < 0.001) and fat free mass index (13.9 (2.3) vs. 15.8 (3.1), p = 0.005) and higher fat mass % (42.5 (7.2) vs. 40.2 (9.8), p = 0.024) compared with patients without difficulty. Patients with high FSS had higher UPDRS II (10 (4) vs. 8 (5), p < 0.001), higher BMI (27.9 (3.8) vs. 25.4 (5.7), p = 0.039) and larger calf circumference​ (37.5 (5.0) vs. 35.8 (4.1)), p = 0.045) than patients with low FSS. Low HGS was associated with low mid upper arm circumference (30.0 (4.0) vs. 32.0 (4.0), p < 0.007) and low calf circumference (35.5 (4.4) vs. 37.0 (4.8), p = 0.049), low fat free mass index (14.9 (3.1) vs. 16.0 (3.2)), intracellular water index (5.7 (1.7) vs. 6.4 (1.6), p = 0.004) and arm muscle area (25.5 (3.5) vs. 26.7 (4.3), p = 0.047) as compared with patients with high HGS. Anthropometry could be used to discriminate between level of motor function, HGS and perceived fatigue at diagnosis of PD. The amount of muscle mass and BMI were important when evaluating the clinical condition in patients with difficulty arising from chair or having low HGS as compared with normal function.

items.title: Feline intestinal organoids reveal cell type-specific tropism and antiviral responses to type II feline infectious peritonitis virus.
items.abstract: Feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV), a highly pathogenic feline coronavirus (FCoV), causes a nearly uniformly fatal disease in cats, yet its infection dynamics within the intestinal epithelium-the primary site of viral entry and replication-remain largely unresolved. Here, we report the first establishment of long-term, passageable three-dimensional (3D) feline intestinal organoids, including feline ileal organoids (fILOs) and feline colonic organoids (fCOs), which faithfully recapitulate the cellular diversity and architecture of the feline intestine and support infection by type II FIPV. Using this physiologically relevant platform, we demonstrate that FIPV infection induces profound epithelial remodeling in fCOs, characterized by a marked expansion of proliferative cell populations and depletion of differentiated epithelial lineages. High-resolution single-cell RNA sequencing of fCOs revealed pronounced cell type-specific viral tropism, with preferential infection of differentiated epithelial cells, particularly goblet and tuft cells, while stem and transit-amplifying cells exhibited relative resistance. This differential susceptibility was strongly associated with cell type-specific expression of host entry and trafficking factors, including aminopeptidase N (APN), TMPRSS2, and Niemann-Pick C1 (NPC1). Importantly, our organoid-based infection model recapitulated in vivo-relevant antiviral responses, enabling robust evaluation of therapeutic candidates and accurately reflecting the potent antiviral efficacy of GS-441524 and the neutralizing antibody 1AF10. Collectively, this study establishes a novel, scalable, and physiologically faithful feline intestinal organoid platform that provides unprecedented insight into type II FIPV epithelial tropism and pathogenesis, and represents a powerful preclinical tool for accelerating the development of effective antiviral and preventive strategies against feline infectious peritonitis.

items.title: Population structure, pathogenic potential, and antimicrobial resistance of Streptococcus suis serotype 16.
items.abstract: Streptococcus suis is an important swine pathogen with numerous serotypes, and different serotypes vary considerably in population structure, pathogenicity, and antimicrobial resistance. Serotype 16 is one of the serotypes reported to infect humans, yet its population structure, pathogenic potential, and resistance characteristics remain poorly understood. Here, we analyzed 303 serotype 16 strains from 13 countries and found high genetic diversity, clear geographical clustering, and three distinct phylogenetic groups. Notably, some serotype 16 strains exhibited high virulence in zebrafish and mouse models and strong cytotoxicity toward human lung adenocarcinoma and brain microvascular endothelial cells. Among the 107 isolates tested phenotypically, 99.07% were multidrug resistant and 39.25% were resistant to penicillin. Integrative and conjugative elements (ICEs) and prophages were identified as major vehicles associated with the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance genes. Remarkably, the vast majority of ICE‑carrying genomes (88.00%, 44/50) clustered within group 2-2, indicating that this group may have greater potential for ICE-mediated horizontal dissemination of antimicrobial resistance genes. In addition, ICEs from these strains showed high similarity to elements identified in a highly pathogenic human-derived S. suis strain and Streptococcus agalactiae, indicating potential cross-species genetic exchange. Together, these findings reveal substantial genetic diversity, pathogenic potential, and widespread multidrug resistance in S. suis serotype 16, underscoring the need for continued surveillance.

items.title: Decomposition of age-specific income-related health inequalities: mobility around the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic in Germany.
items.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic caused major societal disruptions that may have altered existing health inequalities. This study examines how income-related inequalities in physical and mental health in Germany changed between 2018 and 2020, and whether these changes were driven by income-related health changes or by health-related income changes. Data from the 2018 and 2020 waves of the German Socio-Economic Panel were used to analyze physical and mental health outcomes derived from the SF-12 questionnaire. Age-specific mean levels were estimated, and a varying concentration index was applied to estimate smoothed, age-specific measures of income-related health inequality for men and women and for households with and without children. Changes in inequality were separated into income-related health changes and health-related income changes using a mobility decomposition. Physical health declined significantly for working-age and older men, while remaining largely stable for women. Mental health decreased across most groups. The physical health advantage of higher-income individuals grew, while their mental health advantage shrank and disappeared among women in their 30s. Both shifts were driven by income-related health changes, while health-related income changes contributed significantly only to mental health inequality among women in their mid-30s. The pandemic period did not uniformly exacerbate income-related health inequality but shifted its social distribution. In a crisis that affected both health and income, individuals in poorer health largely kept their income position, at least in the short term, whereas lower-income individuals experienced comparatively larger declines in physical health.

items.title: Stakeholder perspectives on the regulation of homeopathy in Germany: a qualitative interview study and normative analysis.
items.abstract: Although homeopathy continues to be the one of the most popular types of alternative medicine in Germany, its regulation is increasingly being debated. In recent years, prominent players have spoken out in favour of removing the option of reimbursement by statutory health insurance companies while its continued reimbursed is strongly advocated by proponents. This study aims to explore key stakeholders' views about the current regulation of homeopathy in Germany. Semi-structured qualitative individual interviews were conducted between March and October 2023 with 28 participants from different groups, including statutory health insurance companies, German medical and pharmaceutical associations, State Medical Councils, homeopathic practitioners, and outspoken homeopathy critics. The transcripts were analysed using conventional content analysis. The current liberal regulation of homeopathy in Germany was seen as problematic by most participants. Representatives of health insurance companies shared that their companies' incentives to reimburse homeopathy are mainly due to strategic reasons (competitive advantage), while they remain sceptical of the actual effectiveness of homeopathy. Furthermore, there was a pragmatic acceptance of the use of homeopathy by health care professionals despite confidence in its effectiveness being low. There was a growing consensus towards the need to tighten the regulation of homeopathy in Germany. We argue that the current regulation of homeopathy in Germany is ethically inappropriate. Homeopathy should not be treated differently by law, but should instead be held to the same standards as other therapies. The special legal regulations regarding homeopathy should be removed to create uniformity and equality.

items.title: For emergency department patients with alcohol withdrawal syndrome, a comorbid mood disorder is associated with increased system utilization representing illness burden.
items.abstract: The impact of comorbid mood disorders on emergency department revisits and hospitalizations among patients presenting with alcohol withdrawal is not well understood. We compared ED revisits and hospitalizations among those patients with alcohol withdrawal and mood disorder to those without mood disorder. We included unique patients who presented to EDs in Vancouver, Canada, with a diagnosis of alcohol withdrawal. Structured chart reviews ascertained comorbidities and defined the presence of mood disorder based on documented diagnosis at or before the index visit. The primary and secondary outcomes were any ED visit or hospitalization in the subsequent year. We describe differences between patients using absolute difference and 95% confidence intervals [CI]. We identified 1010 unique patients; the median age was 46 (range 15-79), 73% were male, and 403 (40%) had a mood disorder. By 1 year, 78% of patients with mood disorders had at least one ED revisit, compared to 61% of patients without (difference 17% [11-22%]). Among patients with mood disorders, the median number of return visits was 3 [1-8] compared to 1 [0-5] for a patient with no mood disorder. By 1 year, 35% of patients with a mood disorder had ≥ 1 hospital admission versus 21% of patients without (difference 14% [8.5-20%]). Among patients with alcohol withdrawal, those with mood disorders had nearly double the number of ED visits and more frequently required hospital admission within 1 year. These findings underscore the need for targeted interventions for patients with alcohol withdrawal and mood disorders.

items.title: The Neighborhood-Level Association Between Renter Cost Burden and Fatal Opioid-Involved Overdoses, Chicago, IL, 2015-2023.
items.abstract: Housing insecurity, including homelessness and eviction, is linked to higher fatal overdose risk. However, the relationship between renter cost burden and fatal opioid-involved overdose remains unclear. This study examined the neighborhood-level association between renter cost burden and fatal opioid-involved overdoses across time in an urban setting. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of Chicago census tracts using locations of opioid-involved fatal overdoses from the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office, 2015-2023 (n = 8423). Renter cost burden, defined as the percentage of renter households spending ≥ 30% of income on housing, was obtained for Chicago census tracts from the American Community Survey. We used negative binomial regression to estimate the association between renter cost burden and severe cost burden (≥ 50%) and fatal overdose rate by year, controlling for neighborhood variables (e.g., income, segregation, and population density). We observed positive spatial autocorrelation, indicating spatial clustering of census tracts with a high proportion of cost-burdened renters and fatal overdose rates. We found consistent positive associations between fatal overdose rates and renter cost burden and severe cost burden over time, controlling for neighborhood demographics. For example, in 2023, each 10-percentage point higher proportion of cost-burdened renters was associated with a 9% higher fatal overdose rate (aIRR = 1.09, 95% CI [1.02, 1.17]). These findings support further investigation of the relationship between renter cost burden and fatal overdose and motivate studies using quasi-experimental designs to assess whether upstream housing interventions (e.g., rental assistance) may reduce fatal overdose risk.

items.title: Association of "Nonadherence" Documentation with Clinician Empathy and Clinic Dismissal: A Randomized Survey Experiment.
items.abstract: Designations of "nonadherence" are common in the electronic health record (EHR). While intended to convey information regarding patient behavior, such language may inadvertently shape clinician perceptions. However, the potential effects of such terminology on clinician attitudes and decisions remain poorly understood. To examine the impact of "nonadherence" documentation, with and without social context, on primary care clinicians' attitudes and management decisions. Randomized controlled vignette-based survey experiment. Five primary care practices across two US academic medical centers. We invited 703 primary care clinicians to complete a 15-item survey. Respondents were randomized to one of three otherwise identical clinical vignettes describing an adverse outcome that differed only in how medication adherence was documented: adherent, nonadherent, or nonadherent with accompanying social context. Self-reported empathy, judgment, and attribution of responsibility were compared across groups using Mann-Whitney U tests. Participants also indicated whether they would uphold or dispute a policy dismissing the patient from the clinic following missed appointments; relative risks (RRs) for dismissal were calculated. Among 233 respondents (167 with complete data), the "nonadherent" vignette elicited significantly lower empathy, greater judgment, and increased attribution of responsibility to the patient compared with the adherent control group. Inclusion of social context attenuated or reversed each of these effects. Adding social context also resulted in significantly lower risk of clinic dismissal among respondents shown a patient labeled as nonadherent. Labeling patients as "nonadherent" may influence clinician attitudes and increase support for punitive actions. Incorporating social context into nonadherence documentation may mitigate these effects. Attention to language in the EHR represents a potentially actionable strategy to promote more equitable and patient-centered care.

items.title: San Francisco's Shared Priority Pilot: An Interagency Initiative to Connect Shared Clients to Housing, Human Services, and Health Care.
items.abstract: The San Francisco County Shared Priority pilot was a collaboration between County public agencies and community partners to improve care for their shared clients experiencing homelessness and co-occurring substance use disorders (SUD) and mental illness. In this study, we evaluated the pilot's primary objectives of connecting Shared Priority clients with permanent supportive housing and intensive case management services. DESIGN AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a matched control analysis evaluating the Shared Priority pilot's objectives among its clients - unhoused individuals prioritized for supportive housing with both SUD- and psychoses-related diagnoses - and two matched control groups: (1) a "housing priority" group composed of unhoused individuals prioritized for supportive housing with either a psychoses-related or SUD diagnosis but not both and (2) a "behavioral health" group composed of unhoused individuals not prioritized for supportive housing with both a psychoses-related and SUD diagnosis. Our primary outcome was permanent supportive housing attainment and retention 16 months into the pilot. Secondary outcomes included intensive case management enrollment and health care utilization. Difference-in-differences estimations compared the average annual change in secondary outcomes in fiscal year 2018-2019 vs. 2019-2020. At 16 months, 95 Shared Priority clients (46.6%) attained permanent supportive housing, compared to 53 individuals (26.5%) in the housing priority control group, and 22 individuals (9.7%) in the behavioral health control group. Housing retention was > 96% in all groups. Shared Priority clients had increased case management engagement compared to both control groups; health care utilization did not differ. The Shared Priority pilot achieved its primary goals of connecting clients to housing and case management services, and, compared to similar individuals in our comparison groups, Shared Priority clients experienced greater success in engaging with these services. The pilot demonstrated the value of bringing together interdisciplinary teams from health, housing, and human services to serve clients with complex needs.

items.title: Achieving High Tuberculosis Treatment Completion Rates in a Student-Run Free Clinic Model: A Retrospective Observational Study.
items.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) is the leading infectious cause of death globally. HAVEN Free Clinic is a student-run free clinic that provides TB screening and treatment. To assess the feasibility of a student-run free clinic model for TB screening and treatment as well as evaluate patient retention through the cascade of care. Retrospective observational study using electronic medical record data. Patients who required TB screening between January 1, 2019, and February 1, 2025 (n = 742). Data were collected on rates of retention at each step of screening, diagnosis, and treatment. Logistic regression was used to assess whether age, gender, treatment regimen, or distance from clinic were associated with treatment completion. For patients who completed treatment, the TST/IGRA interpreter tool TSTin4D was used to estimate risk reduction for developing TB disease and disability. Forty-eight of the patients initiated on treatment successfully completed it for a treatment completion rate of 87.3%. As estimated using the TSTin4D tool, treatment completion was associated with an average relative risk reduction of 80.7% for developing TB disease in the next 20 years and an average relative risk reduction of 68.7% for long-term disability and death from TB disease. Age, gender, treatment regimen, and distance to clinic were not associated with treatment completion. A student-run free clinic model of TB screening and treatment is effective and has treatment completion rates exceeding standard benchmarks. Strengths of this model include focused scope and patient education. Opportunities for improvement include access to in-person interpreters and close follow-up with patients during their treatment course.

items.title: Exploring race and obesity in relation to multimorbidity and patient-reported health outcomes in breast cancer survivors.
items.abstract: The purpose of this exploratory study was to determine differences in multimorbidity, global mental health, and global physical health among breast cancer survivors (BCS) based on different race and obesity status groups. This study is a secondary analysis of the Facilitating Adaptive Coping with Fear of Recurrence Among BCS (FACing Fear) trial (NCT05364450) with a sample of 363 BCS. Participants were organized into four groups based on race (Black and White) and obesity status (BMI). Outcomes included total multimorbidity and the PROMIS Global Health mental and physical health subscales. Among White BCS, 41% had obesity compared to 61% of Black BCS. ANCOVA analyses tested differences between groups of BCS by race/obesity status. Group differences in multimorbidity and physical health were detected (F = 3.04, p = .030; F = 2.85, p = .038). White BCS with obesity reported greater multimorbidity (p = .046) than White BCS without obesity. Compared to White BCS without obesity, both groups with obesity reported significantly worse physical health (White with obesity: Mdifference = - 4.65, p < .001; Black with obesity: Mdifference = - 5.91, p = .002), with no differences between Black and White BCS with obesity. Obesity was related to significant negative impacts on multimorbidity and physical health, and Black BCS had higher rates of obesity.
