items.title: Global landscape of early-onset breast cancer: from understanding risk to precision prevention and cancer interception.
items.abstract: Early-onset breast cancer (EOBC), defined in this Review as breast cancer diagnosed before 50 years of age, accounts for a growing proportion of global breast cancer incidence and is associated with disproportionately unfavourable outcomes. Although inherited susceptibility contributes to EOBC risk, the rising incidence and persistent disparities that characterize EOBC cannot be explained by genetics alone; molecular subtype distribution, modifiable exposures and healthcare-related factors also affect presentation, response to treatment and outcomes. In this Review, we synthesize epidemiological trends, providing an overview of the inherited and multifactorial risk determinants, tumour subtype distributions and modifiable exposures that shape EOBC across populations. We examine why age-based screening paradigms do not fully capture EOBC risk and discuss approaches to risk-informed early detection and diagnosis, emphasizing the need for prompt histopathological confirmation and biomarker-guided care. We then address structural and healthcare-related barriers that constrain implementation of such an approach, including diagnostic capacity, pathology infrastructure, treatment affordability and financial toxicity. Finally, we propose a roadmap for the prevention, early diagnosis and interception of EOBC that integrates family history, germline testing, ancestry-aware risk models, pathology, treatment access and resource-stratified implementation. We argue that biological risk architecture must be aligned with healthcare systems that translate risk recognition into prompt, equitable and optimal management, including appropriately adapted treatment, ultimately improving outcomes for patients with EOBC.

items.title: Forced displacement is associated with health service delivery disruption beyond the effects of armed conflict.
items.abstract: Humanitarian emergencies test the resilience of global health systems, yet policy is constrained by limited empirical evidence on the magnitude and timing of service delivery disruptions. Here, we assess the association between measured childhood vaccination-as a proxy for health service delivery-and forced displacement, armed conflict, and natural disasters. Across 193 countries from 2000 to 2023, sudden increases in displaced populations were associated with declines in vaccination coverage of approximately 3 to 6 percentage points, persisting for 2 to 3 years before recovery. Dose-response analyses revealed a nonlinear relationship: coverage fell steeply at low displacement levels and plateaued at extreme exposure. Conflict intensity followed a similar nonlinear pattern that plateaued near 3000 annual battle-related deaths while mortality from natural disasters showed no detectable association with coverage. Displacement's association was largely independent of armed conflict, indicating that displacement may act as a distinct, additive shock rather than a proxy for violence.

items.title: Population-level characterisation of the human gut phageome and its association with microbial metabolites.
items.abstract: Bacteriophages, viruses infecting bacteria, are abundant in the human gut, but their population-level structure and metabolic associations remain unclear Here we present a foundational characterisation of the gut phageome using deep shotgun metagenomic data in a large population-based cohort (n = 1,069: TwinsUK). We assembled 116,740 non-redundant vOTUs of which 52.9% were predicted to be temperate and 47.0% virulent. Individuals harboured an average of 3,370 vOTUs, mostly at low abundances, exhibiting structured population-level co-abundance patterns with bacterial species including Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Blautia wexlerae. Phageome diversity was mostly driven by environmental factors, with modest heritable components. We detected 4 significant vOTU diet associations. Additionally, 6,572 phages were associated with short-chain fatty acids and secondary bile acids, identifying extensive population-level associations between phage-associated genomic variation and microbial metabolites. Over 100 vOTUs encoded auxiliary metabolic genes, while a distinct subset of phages encoded virulence-associated genes, including vacuolating autotransporter toxin (vat) and LPS glucosyltransferases (gtrA, gtrB, gtr) implicated in O-antigen modification and immune invasion, and showed consistent co-abundance patterns with bacterial species previously associated with opportunistic or pathobiont features. These results identify structured population-level associations between phage-associated genomic elements, bacterial communities, and microbial metabolites, motivating future experimental and mechanistic studies.

items.title: Strengthening Public Health Delivery of Eating Disorders Treatment: A Mixed-Method Formative Evaluation Informing Future Implementation in Community Mental Health Teams.
items.abstract: Eating disorders are mental illnesses associated with significant risk and wide-ranging client impacts. To facilitate timely access to care, recent initiatives propose implementing treatments across health services. To inform implementation strategy development, this study aimed to identify barriers and opportunities for delivering evidence-based treatments within public community mental health teams. This cross-sectional, developmental study used clinician and manager focus groups and surveys to inform future implementation strategies. Focus group guides and surveys were designed, and existing survey scales were administered. Reflexive thematic analysis and statistical methods were utilized. One hundred forty-one staff participated in focus groups and 140 completed surveys. Focus group themes included: (1) existing clinician capabilities differ across the workforce; (2) multiple factors impact clinician motivation to engage in treatment; and (3) organizational readiness, workforce capacity and clinician support are essential. Existing mental health skills and service models were enablers. Barriers included limited staffing, varied clinician capability and motivation, treatment complexity, illness and family factors, and access to training and support. Participants showed implementation readiness. Clinician willingness to provide treatment was high (CAMHS n = 34, 89%; AMHS n = 48, 77%), although reported adequacy of knowledge and skill in providing treatment was low (35%, n = 14 CAMHS; 21%, n = 13 AMHS). Adult clinicians reported lower confidence (p = 0.04) and competence (p = 0.004) in delivering eating disorders treatment. This study suggests community mental health teams offer a feasible setting for eating disorders evidence-based treatment implementation. Multi-faceted implementation strategies are required, including leadership, resources, building workforce capability, health provider collaboration, implementation support, monitoring, and evaluation.

items.title: How Mapping Data Capture in Western Australian Cardiac Rehabilitation Services Is Aligning With Change for Improving Access to Quality Care.
items.abstract: Cardiac rehabilitation cost-effectively reduces hospital readmissions and deaths from cardiovascular disease. There is no national approach to quality assessment and improvement in cardiac rehabilitation across Australia. Survey responses from 39 Western Australian (WA) cardiac rehabilitation services describe the current practices of data capture, management, and use, in addition to perceptions and adoption of the national quality indicators. Most services have access to an electronic system to collect data; however, a minority are still using paper only, and most are double-handling information, including paper and electronic processes. There are 14 different electronic systems being used, with electronic medical record and patient management systems being the most common types. The type of system being used is dependent on whether the service is public or private. There are no quality improvement platforms in use by WA cardiac rehabilitation services. Most services use their data for at least one reason; usually, they report patient progress to their general practitioner or other doctors. This was not uniform across all services. Most services were aware of the contemporary National Cardiac Rehabilitation Quality Indicators and described them as useful, yet they are not implemented. Several strategies to collect and implement the indicators were proposed by survey respondents. The heterogeneity in the way WA cardiac rehabilitation services collect and report data is not synonymous with assessing quality. Hence, recommendations for a consistent digital data capture process with pragmatic implementation and support from professional networks should be considered.

items.title: Reliability and Validity of a Culturally Adapted Short Food Literacy Questionnaire (SFLQ) in Japanese Community-Dwelling Older Adults.
items.abstract: Food literacy (FL) is essential for healthy diet of community-dwelling older adults to prevent frailty. This study aims to adapt culturally and revise the short food literacy questionnaire (SFLQ) to the Japanese context and to evaluate its reliability and validity. A paper-based questionnaire survey was conducted from October 2024 through February 2025 among 364 older adults aged ≥65 years. The questionnaire included a revised Japanese version of the SFLQ (rSFLQ-JP), healthy eating literacy (HEL), health literacy (HL, using HLS-Q12), eHealth literacy (eHL, using eHEALS), and dietary knowledge tests. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses indicated that 14 out of 16 items should be included in three subscales of the rSFLQ-JP. The Cronbach's α of the rSFLQ-JP was high (α = 0.91). rSFLQ-JP was correlated with HL (τb = 0.36), HEL (τb = 0.50), and eHL (τb = 0.25) using Kendall's τb. The median rSFLQ-JP scores were significantly higher in those who answered correctly on the dietary knowledge tests than in those who did not (Mann-Whitney's U tests, P < 0.01 for each test). These findings confirm the reliability and validity of the rSFLQ-JP, which can be used to assess the need for and effectiveness of nutrition education to improve older adults' well-being.

items.title: Carbohydrate quality and progression trajectories of cardiometabolic multimorbidity: a prospective cohort study with multi-omics analyses.
items.abstract: Carbohydrate quality is associated with cardiometabolic health, but its relationships with cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) progression and molecular and genetic characteristics remain unclear. To investigate associations of carbohydrate quality with CMM progression and explore potential multi-omics signatures, pathways, and genetic effect modification. We included 177,763 UK Biobank participants free of baseline cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs). Carbohydrate quality was assessed using correlation and principal component analyses. Multivariable Cox and multi-state models evaluated CMD incidence and CMM progression. Carbohydrate-associated proteomic and metabolomic signatures were derived for exploratory mediation analyses, and genomic data were used for gene-environment-wide interaction study (GEWIS). During a median 12.56-year follow-up, 37,527, 5,751, and 650 participants developed first, double, and triple CMDs, respectively. High- and low-quality carbohydrates showed opposing associations with CMM accumulation, strongest for ≥3 CMDs [HRs (95% CIs): 0.92 (0.86, 0.98) and 1.11 (1.05, 1.19), respectively]. In multi-state analyses, associations were particularly evident for progression from hypertension to comorbid T2D [HRs (95% CIs): 0.98 (0.96, 0.99) and 1.05 (1.03, 1.06), respectively]. Exploratory multi-omics mediation analyses yielded statistical mediation signals, with estimated pathway-level mediation proportions for T2D of 40.1% for PPAR signalling with high-quality carbohydrates and 36.2% and 36.4% for PI3K-Akt and MAPK signalling with low-quality carbohydrates. GEWIS identified candidate interaction loci with genotype-dependent differences in carbohydrate-CMD associations. High-quality carbohydrates were inversely associated with CHD onset among rs17589271 TT carriers but positively associated among GT/GG carriers [HRs (95% CIs): 0.95 (0.93, 0.98) and 1.22 (1.10, 1.35), respectively]. Low-quality carbohydrates showed a stronger association with progression from prior CMDs to comorbid T2D among rs144465069 AG/AA carriers [HR (95% CI): 2.09 (1.57, 2.78)]. Carbohydrate quality was differentially associated with CMM progression. Exploratory multi-omics and genetic analyses highlighted potential pathways and genotype-specific associations. These findings may inform future research on personalised nutritional strategies for cardiometabolic prevention.

items.title: Transcriptomic and metabolomic remodeling in HepG2 cells during continuous PFOA exposure.
items.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a persistent environmental contaminant, is associated with hepatic metabolic dysfunction, yet the molecular consequences of sustained low-concentration exposure remain poorly characterized. Here, we used a serial-passage HepG2 cell model under continuous 8 μM PFOA exposure and integrated RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) with targeted metabolomics to compare cells at the first (G1, 48 h) and seventh (G7, 14 d) serial passages. PFOA did not affect cell viability at 48 h but induced clear transcriptomic and metabolomic divergence from controls. At G1, 255 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and 53 differential smetabolites were identified, with enrichment in nucleotide metabolism, central carbon metabolism, lipid pathways, and ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters. At G7, 2102 DEGs and 74 differential metabolites were identified, with enrichment in glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, amino acid and one‑carbon metabolism, glycerolipid metabolism, and mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) signaling. Cross-stage comparisons revealed stage-dependent differences in shared metabolites and representative genes. Joint pathway analysis highlighted glycerolipid metabolism as a persistently perturbed node, whereas central carbon metabolism became increasingly prominent at G7. A biochemically constrained gene-metabolite network identified five candidate association axes preferentially detected at G7: fructose 1,6-bisphosphate (F1,6BP)-ALDOC, F1,6BP-PFKL, F1,6BP-PFKP, inosine-NT5E, and nicotinamide-SIRT7, suggesting a distinct metabolic state involving glycolytic regulation, lipid homeostasis, purine metabolism, and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+)-dependent signaling. Collectively, this study provides an integrative multi-omics framework for PFOA hepatotoxicity and identifies candidate molecular axes for functional validation.

items.title: Long-term trajectories of intrinsic capacity and risk of cardiometabolic multimorbidity and its subtypes in older US adults: A 19-year prospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Intrinsic capacity (IC) changes with aging, but the association between its long-term trajectories and subsequent cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) remains unclear. We examined the associations of long-term trajectories of IC with incident CMM and its subtypes among older US adults. Data were drawn from the Health and Retirement Study. Group-based trajectory modeling identified IC trajectories using five assessments across wave 3-7. Participants with CMM during this period were excluded. Incident CMM, defined as the coexistence of at least two of diabetes, heart disease, and stroke, was assessed over up to 19 years of subsequent follow-up. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Among 3707 participants, four IC trajectories were identified: very high-late decline (17.53%), high-gradual decline (45.59%), moderate-gradual decline (29.24%), and low-persistent decline (7.63%). During 33,744 person-years of follow-up, 638 participants developed CMM. Compared with the very high-late decline group, fully adjusted HRs were 1.53 (95%CI = 1.19-1.96), 1.75 (1.31-2.33), and 2.38 (1.61-3.52) for high-gradual decline, moderate-gradual decline, and low-persistent decline groups, respectively. Associations were observed across all three CMM subtypes, and generally persisted in sensitivity analyses, including alternative IC scoring approaches. Less favorable long-term IC trajectories were associated with higher subsequent CMM risk. Repeated IC assessments may provide useful information for identifying older adults at elevated cardiometabolic risk.

items.title: Atomic layer deposition of antigen-decorated phage-like particles as a platform for thermally stable, single-injection antiviral vaccines.
items.abstract: Overcoming barriers to the distribution, availability, and effectiveness of vaccines, are major public health challenges. For example, thermal instabilities of vaccines result in the need for strict cold-chain conditions during storage and shipping. In addition, many vaccines require the administration of multiple vaccine doses per individual for protective and durable immunity. In this study, we describe the combination of a SARS-CoV-2 receptor binding domain (RBD) lambda phage-like particle (PLP) vaccine platform with our spray-drying and atomic layer deposition (ALD) formulation to generate highly thermostable single-dose immunogens. We show that ALD formulated SARS-CoV-2 RBD PLP vaccines retain potent immunogenicity in mice following incubation for one month at temperatures up to 50°C. In addition, mice immunized with a single dose of ALD formulated SARS-CoV-2 RBD PLP vaccines developed SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibody responses similar to those induced by standard prime-boost regimens and were strongly protected against SARS-CoV-2 infection and disease. These data suggest that ALD-coated PLP-based vaccine formulations can address two critical barriers to effective deployment of antiviral vaccines-thermal stability and single-shot dosing.

items.title: Multigenerational neurotoxicity of the decabromodiphenyl ethane (DBDPE) in Caenorhabditis elegans: role of p38 MAPK / oxidative stress and protection by nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN).
items.abstract: Decabromodiphenyl ethane (DBDPE), an emerging brominated flame retardant, poses potential neurotoxic risks, yet its multigenerational effects and mechanisms remain unclear. Here, Caenorhabditis elegans was exposed to environmentally relevant concentration DBDPE (500μg / L) for 72h. DBDPE caused neurobehavioral deficits and damage to dopaminergic, cholinergic, glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons, accompanied by downregulation of dat-1, eat-4 and other neurotransmitter genes. These neurotoxic effects were transmitted from parental (P0) to F2 generation, but recovered by F3. Mechanistically, DBDPE elevated ROS, reduced mitochondrial membrane potential, activated p38 MAPK and induced DAF-16 / SKN-1 nuclear translocation. Notably, 500μM nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) partially reversed these alterations, restored mitochondrial function and blocked p38 MAPK activation. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that DBDPE at environmental levels induces multigenerational neurotoxicity via oxidative stress and p38 MAPK, and reveal NMN as a potential protective strategy, emphasizing the urgency of long-term risk evaluation and informing mechanism-based pharmacologic strategies.

items.title: Self-prompting small language models for privacy-sensitive clinical information extraction.
items.abstract: Clinically meaningful information in dental progress notes is largely locked in free text, and because the notes contain protected health information, extraction must run locally. We developed and evaluated a framework enabling locally deployable small language models (SLMs) to perform clinical named-entity recognition (NER) without transmitting clinical text or using external models. Using 1,200 annotated notes (200 training, 1,000-note gold-standard evaluation set) spanning 19 entity types, each candidate SLM generated, verified, refined, and evaluated its own entity-specific prompts, with self-prompt performance as a model-selection signal. Inference ensembled prompts across sentence-level Boolean screening and entity extraction. Selected models were adapted with QLoRA-based supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and direct preference optimization (DPO). Soft-match entity-level F1 was reported with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Additional analyses isolated ensembling, repeated the pipeline on six training-set draws, and benchmarked fine-tuned BioClinicalBERT. Across 10 SLMs, self-prompt performance ranked models concordantly with gold-standard performance (micro-F1 Kendall's τ = 0.78, p < 0.01) and more consistently than general benchmarks (IFEval, MMLU), but overestimated absolute F1 (0.884 versus 0.769 for Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct). SFT raised recall but cut precision; DPO restored precision, improving four of five models beyond base and SFT (non-overlapping CIs), while one collapsed. Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct with DPO performed best (micro-F1 0.863, 95% CI 0.852 to 0.873; macro-F1 0.836), though across six training draws its converged runs averaged 0.836 micro-F1 and one draw collapsed. Ensembling helped mainly after adaptation. BioClinicalBERT reached 0.868 micro-F1. Self-generated prompting with lightweight post-training supports privacy-preserving clinical NER using locally deployed SLMs. Self-prompt performance should rank models, not estimate accuracy, and DPO convergence should be verified before deployment. With accuracy near a supervised encoder, the framework's advantage is adaptability: an instruction-tuned SLM can add an entity through a self-generated prompt rather than retraining. It is domain-agnostic in principle, pending external validation.

items.title: Integrative medicine information on United States comprehensive cancer center websites: An environmental scan.
items.abstract: Integrative medicine (IM) in cancer care combines conventional treatments with evidence-based complementary therapies to address survivors' physical, psychosocial, and spiritual needs. Despite growing evidence supporting IM for symptom management and quality of life, awareness and access remain inconsistent. This study evaluated how National Cancer Institute (NCI)-designated comprehensive cancer centers communicate IM information on their publicly accessible websites. An environmental scan of 59 United States NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center websites was conducted in November 2025-January 2026. Two independent reviewers evaluated each website for the presence of predefined IM modalities, descriptions of modality benefits, website usability, and readability of extracted text. Thirty-three IM modalities were identified. The most frequently described were nutrition counseling/therapy (81.4%), yoga (71.2%), art therapy, exercise, and spiritual counseling (61.0% each). The level of detail in the descriptions of benefits varied considerably across modalities and centers. Navigation, usefulness, and information quality received moderate ratings. Most content exceeded recommended reading levels, with a mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 12.65. The communication of IM information varies across NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center websites. Improving specificity, usability, and readability of online IM content may enhance patient understanding, improve informed decision-making, and promote wider access to support services.

items.title: How to navigate infectious disease mathematical models: a guide for clinicians.
items.abstract: Infectious diseases are characterised by transmission between hosts, creating population dynamics that distinguish them from non-communicable diseases. Because these dynamics are difficult to measure empirically, mathematical models are used to capture them and evaluate interventions, including scenarios that would be impractical or impossible to study directly. Clinicians increasingly encounter such modelling studies in decisions about clinical practice and public health, and need to be able to understand and interpret them. To introduce fundamental concepts in infectious disease transmission modelling and provide practical guidance for clinicians to understand modelling studies and critically interpret their findings in clinical and public health contexts. This narrative review draws on peer-reviewed literature on infectious disease transmission modelling, using bacterial infections and interventions to reduce antimicrobial resistance (AMR) as illustrative examples. We propose a practical checklist to support the interpretation of infectious disease modelling studies. The checklist guides clinicians in understanding which clinical or public health question a model addresses, which assumptions and parameters shape the model, how uncertain the results are, whether the model and its results are valid, and what the results mean for clinical and public health. As with empirical studies, understanding how an infectious disease modelling study was conducted is essential for critically interpreting findings before applying them to practice. The proposed checklist offers clinicians a practical framework to do so.

items.title: Tnfaip2 Promotes the Antifungal Effects of Mannoprotein Against Cutaneous Candida albicans Infection by Enhancing NF-κB-mediated M1 Macrophage Polarization.
items.abstract: Mannoprotein (MP), a major cell wall component of Candida albicans (C. albicans), has been increasingly recognized for its immunomodulatory properties, especially in inducing macrophage polarization. However, the molecular determinants that mediate MP-driven macrophage antifungal immunity remain poorly defined. Transcriptomic and proteomic profiling was performed to identify key responsive factors involved in macrophage polarization and to elucidate the signaling mechanisms that support enhanced antifungal defense. Tnfaip2 was identified as a prominently upregulated host-response molecule. In a murine model of cutaneous candidiasis, MP administration markedly reduced epidermal damage and fungal burden, accompanied by enhanced M1 polarization, increased reactive oxygen species (ROS)/inducible NO synthase (iNOS) levels, elevated superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, increased Ca2+/Mn2+ influx, and augmented NF-κB activation, whereas Tnfaip2 knockdown elicited the opposite effects. In macrophages, MP engaged the C-type lectin receptor Dectin-3, and Dectin-3 knockdown attenuated NF-κB activation and Tnfaip2 induction, placing Dectin-3 upstream of the NF-κB-Tnfaip2 axis. In conclusion, MP upregulates macrophage Tnfaip2, a molecule associated with M1 macrophage polarization and antifungal activity. These findings suggest that Tnfaip2 represents a potential mechanistic node through which MP regulates macrophage function, providing a theoretical basis for the further exploration of MP in the management of cutaneous C. albicans infection.

items.title: Towards a definition of animal health for interdisciplinary health collaboration.
items.abstract: This paper proposes an initial definition for animal health. It argues that a definition needs to be applicable to all animals, to include all domains of health, to consider health as a dynamic state, and to be compatible with current uses of the term. Drawing on veterinary medicine and science, conservation, public health and human health literatures, it proposes an initial definition that, "Animal health is a dynamic state of physical, mental, social and ecological well-being." This definition is intended to encourage veterinary advocacy, inter-disciplinary collaboration, and ongoing evolution of the definition. Potential refinements to the definition are considered, reflecting debates about the definition of human health, for which this initial definition provides a basis.

items.title: Quantitative Modeling of Action-Potential-Driven Sodium Dynamics in Neurons: From Sodium Influx to Sodium MRI
items.abstract: Neuronal action potentials are accompanied by the influx of extracellular sodium ions (Na+) into axons through voltage-gated sodium channels. Repetitive neuronal firing can lead to activity-dependent increases in intracellular sodium concentration, which are subsequently reversed primarily through the Na+/K+-ATPase. Quantifying these dynamic changes provides a biophysical foundation for investigating neuronal activity using sodium (23Na) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). This mini-review examines the relationships among firing frequency, action-potential-driven sodium influx, and intracellular sodium accumulation, to establish a quantitative framework linking neuronal activity to sodium MRI. The potential sensitivity and limitation of conventional and compartment-sensitive sodium MRI for detecting activity-dependent sodium changes are also discussed. Keywords: Sodium MRI; neuronal firing; action potential; sodium influx; intracellular sodium concentration.

items.title: How the material world of the brain, as a complex system governed by intermittent dynamics, gives rise to the supposedly "immaterial" world of mental processes such as thought
items.abstract: In this paper, we argue that the brain is a complex dynamical system in a critical state similar to that of the 3D Ising model. We highlight several properties of the brain, including resonance phenomena within this critical state, long-range autocorrelations consistent with long memory, a hysteresis zone suggesting the presence of an as yet undetected "exotic" type of matter within the brain, and possible quantum phenomena within the microtubules of neural networks. The latter suggests that these structures exhibit a combined form of "logical superposition". In the proposed model, "AND" logic would require two distinct quantum states to be occupied simultaneously. The proposed "OR" logic allows any one of several quantum states to be occupied at a time. Moreover, we propose that kink and antikink solitons could mediate coupling between occupied quantum states in the microtubules and thereby contribute to pattern formation in neural networks. This mechanism may well be what gives the brain the flexibility to support complex thought and other cognitive functions.

items.title: Hebbian self-organization of monosynaptic reflexes in a biologically realistic multiarticular limb
items.abstract: Spinal monosynaptic reflexes depend on patterns of connectivity between muscle spindle afferents and motoneurons that should reflect musculoskeletal dynamics. One possibility is that the details of these circuits are specified genetically, but this requires an unlikely coevolution of musculoskeletal and neural elements. Here we show how biomechanical structure can determine the connectivity of self-organized spinal circuits. Using a neuromechanical model combining a multi-joint limb, proprioceptive feedback, and Hebbian plasticity driven by motor babbling, we find that biologically realistic connectivity emerges spontaneously when babbling is neither too sparse nor too frequent. This results in strong homonymous projections, weaker heteronymous projections among functional synergists, and very weak connections among antagonists. This outcome also depends on musculoskeletal morphometry. Heteronymous synergies form when proximal muscles are strongest---the characteristic gradient of mammalian limbs--whereas excessively strong biarticular muscles lead to unphysiological antagonist coupling. The mechanisms differ: homonymous connections arise from direct sensorimotor correlation during fusimotor coactivation by beta motoneurons, while heteronymous connections depend on multi-joint dynamics that emerge only after homonymous reflexes stabilize and increasing muscle strength generates multisegmental motion. Overall, this study provides a mechanistic basis for fetal sensorimotor development and generates testable predictions about the consequences of naturally occurring and experimentally induced variations.

items.title: Neural Circuit Architectural Priors for Rat Locomotion
items.abstract: Animals generate behavior through continuous interactions between their neural circuits, bodies, and environment. Embodied simulations study these interactions by testing neural circuit models in biologically realistic settings. Recent efforts have simulated diverse animals, and emerging work on biologically grounded neural architectures has begun to integrate circuit connectivity and single-unit dynamics from experimental data into artificial neural networks, introducing stronger inductive biases and closer mechanistic alignment with biology. How can we develop embodied simulations that enable the study of increasingly complex bodies and neural circuits? In this work, we address the challenge through coordinated advances in the simulated body, neural architecture, and training infrastructure. We introduce Rat v2, an efficient and flexible biomechanical body for simulating rat behavior. To control this body, we develop Rat NCAP, a biologically grounded neural architecture for locomotion based on mammalian spinal circuits that incorporates cell-type-specific connectivity and a novel flexor-extensor neuromechanical interface. To optimize circuit parameters, we develop GPU-accelerated simulation and training infrastructure. The model learns to locomote at different speeds and transition between gaits without imitation learning, producing locomotion statistics, kinematics, and cell-type-specific neural activity consistent with experimental data. Analyses reveal that the neuromechanical interface substantially affects trainability and gait quality, and in silico cell-type ablations reproduce known gait phenotypes and predict gait changes under graded perturbations. Together, these findings support the view that embodied simulations at an intermediate level of abstraction can simultaneously reproduce complex behavior and yield mechanistic insights into the neural circuits that generate it.

items.title: Hierarchical Control of Antiphase Synchronization in Biomorphic Spiking Neural Architectures for Locomotor Control
items.abstract: Central pattern generators (CPGs) provide a biologically inspired foundation for adaptive locomotor control, yet systematically characterizing their dynamic regimes in spiking neural networks remains challenging. This study introduces a framework for identifying and stabilizing antiphase synchronization in a biomorphic spiking CPG model embedded in a closed neuromuscular loop. A composite synchronization metric is developed, integrating phase coherence, amplitude balance, and temporal stability. Its performance is evaluated across systematically varied stimulation waveforms and synaptic configurations. Statistical analysis reveals that stimulation type dominates regime determination, with tonic drive yielding the most robust antiphase synchronization. Periodic inputs induce nonlinear saturation and context-dependent network routing. Although synaptic weights alone show limited discriminative power, they significantly modulate robustness within a given stimulation context, with reciprocal Ia interneuron connections emerging as key stabilizers. The proposed composite metric achieves robust antiphase detection, outperforming traditional phase-only measures while preserving biophysical interpretability. These findings establish a statistically validated, hierarchical modeling approach in which external drive defines the operating regime and targeted synaptic configurations fine-tune dynamic stability, providing actionable guidelines for closed-loop neuromechanical controllers and adaptive neuroprosthetic interfaces.

items.title: Lunar laser ranging analyses of NGLR-1 data with PEP and prospects for MPAc: towards one millimeter range precision
items.abstract: Since 1969, Lunar Laser Ranging (LLR) has provided critical data for investigating Earth-Moon dynamics, lunar internal structure, and tests of General Relativity (GR). However, the measurement precision of historical arrays (such as those from Apollo and Lunokhod missions) is inherently limited by laser pulse broadening induced by lunar librations. To overcome this limit, next-generation single Cube Corner Retroreflectors (CCRs) of large optical diameter have been developed to eliminate pulse dispersion, enabling LLR measurements to advance from centimeter-level precision down to the millimeter scale. In this work, we present a detailed analysis of LLR observations from NGLR-1 (Next Generation Lunar Retroreflector-1), the first single 10cm-diameter CCR deployed on the lunar surface. Carried out using the Planetary Ephemeris Program (PEP), this study investigates individual range measurements, normal points (NPs), residuals, and observational dispersion collected by the ground stations at Apache Point Observatory Lunar laser ranging station (APOL), Wettzell, and Grasse. The results: demonstrate the success of NGLR-1 in significantly enhancing time of flight measurement precision compared to legacy Apollo and Lunokhod retroreflector arrays; indicate similar good prospects also for ESA's MPAc laser retroreflector (MoonLIGHT with Pointing Actuators) to be launched in early 2027; pave the way for a new era of LLR observations and enhanced tests of GR, alternative gravity theories in general and improved lunar geophysics and geodesy.

items.title: Color Through Time: Distributions, Sparsity and Dominance in Western Painting
items.abstract: We investigate the evolution of color in Western painting using a large corpus of digitized artworks. Each painting is represented by its distribution over a fixed palette of colors in a perceptually uniform space. We compare the color distributions of historical periods and artistic movements through their Jensen-Shannon distances, and introduce two interpretable descriptors, sparsity and dominance, that quantify how many colors are used and how unevenly they are represented. We find a historical transition from dark, earthy palettes toward a broader and more saturated chromatic range, unfolding through distinct shifts from the nineteenth century onward. Periods evolve smoothly over time, whereas artistic movements display increasingly distinct chromatic signatures beyond chronology. In the sparsity-dominance plane, painting follows a two-stage historical trajectory, first broadening the range of colors used and later increasing color dominance. Comparison with natural images reveals distinct ways in which artistic palettes depart from nature, either through the colors they use or through how broadly and evenly those colors are distributed. Finally, two surveys on generated images show that judgments of harmonious color balance concentrate around two complementary regimes: many colors arranged in a strong hierarchy, or few colors used evenly.

items.title: RDX-Associated Hearing Loss: Expanded Variant Spectrum, Founder Effect, and Mechanistic Insights from Functional Assays.
items.abstract: Purpose Bi-allelic RDX variants are responsible for DFNB24, a type of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss. Due to its rarity, the mutational spectrum, genotype-phenotype correlations, and population genetics of this condition are not yet fully understood. Methods We performed exome or targeted panel sequencing, along with segregation analysis, and evaluated clinical data. We conducted minigene assays on three intronic variants, with canonical splice-site variants included as positive controls, and used molecular dynamics simulations to explore the predicted conformational effects of missense and in-frame deletion alleles. Additionally, we compiled a systematic review of all previously reported DFNB24 families. Results We identified 12 distinct bi-allelic RDX variants in 16 families, six of which were novel. Those affected experienced bilateral, prelingual, or early childhood onset of sensorineural hearing loss, with varying degrees of severity. Minigene assays demonstrated variant-specific activation of cryptic splice sites for all three intronic variants, generating frameshift transcripts predicted to result in loss of function. Exome-derived haplotype and founder-dating analyses identified two distinct shared ancestral haplotypes among the Iranian families. Probands homozygous for c.1076_1079del, an allele found in four unrelated families, shared a 2.44-Mb haplotype with a most recent common ancestor approximately 386 years ago (95% CI, 83.7-677.7 years), whereas the two probands homozygous for c.1729A>T (Families 14 and 16) shared a 7.88-Mb haplotype dating to approximately 99.9 years ago (95% CI, 24.3-521.1 years), indicating a single ancestral event rather than two independent observations. The systematic review showed that reported DFNB24 families were concentrated in Middle Eastern and South Asian populations. Conclusions This work significantly broadens the RDX mutational spectrum, improves genotype-phenotype correlations, and identifies a founder allele together with a second, more recently shared ancestral haplotype. These data represent the largest single cohort of people with RDX-associated hearing loss compiled to date.

items.title: Mirror Movements in a Child With a TUBB-Related Tubulinopathy: Expanding the Phenotypic Spectrum.
items.abstract: Congenital mirror movements (CMM) are involuntary contralateral movements that mirror intentional unilateral actions and are most commonly associated with pathogenic variants in genes such as DCC, NTN1, and RAD51. Tubulinopathies, caused by mutations in tubulin-encoding genes, are recognized contributors to abnormal motor pathway development; however, mirror movements have rarely been reported in association with TUBB-related disorders. We report a 6-year-old girl with normal development and bilateral mirror movements of the upper limbs who carries a de novo heterozygous TUBB variant, NM_178014.4:c.155A > G; p.(Asn52Ser), classified as likely pathogenic. Neuroimaging revealed corpus callosum dysgenesis, basal ganglia abnormalities, and brainstem hypoplasia, consistent with a tubulinopathy. This case expands the phenotypic spectrum of TUBB-related tubulinopathies and supports the role of tubulin dysfunction in corticospinal tract development and interhemispheric motor control.

items.title: Trinidadian Killifish (Anablepsoides hartii) From Streams With Parasitic Intestinal Nematodes (Camallanus cotti) Have Decreased Brain Size and Brain Cell Proliferation.
items.abstract: Trinidadian killifish ( Anablepsoides hartii ) live in streams that vary in the presence of parasites, competitors, and predators. This allows for ideal field studies on how biotic factors interact to affect fitness and morphology, including brain size and brain plasticity. Infection rates with parasitic gut nematodes ( Camallanus cotti ) are higher, and survival is lower in sites with competitors (guppies, Poecilia reticulata ) compared to sites without competitors. To assess the possible effect of parasite-induced changes in the brain as a factor contributing to this increased mortality, we collected killifish from streams varying in parasitic infection rates and competitors, and measured their brain mass and brain cell proliferation rate. Fish from streams with parasites had smaller brains and fewer newborn cells than fish from parasite-free streams. The association between parasites and reduced brain size was amplified in a stream that contained both parasites and competitors. Thus, parasite infection alone and in combination with competition appear to impact brain morphology of hosts and may influence host mortality.

items.title: Effects of Climate Change on the Population Dynamics of a Long-Lived Fish.
items.abstract: Population dynamics of long-lived species can be affected by environmental variation driven by climate change. Predicted climate changes in Western North America include a shift from snowmelt to rainfall driven runoff, increased stochasticity in runoff, and prolonged droughts. We used a matrix population model coupled with predicted changes in climate to project future population dynamics and persistence of a long-lived freshwater fish, June sucker ( Chasmistes liorus ). We evaluated population dynamics of June suckers under four likely climate scenarios: (1) increased stochastic variation in river flow, (2) increased amplitude in cyclic lake level variation from 1 m to 1.5 m, (3) a 0.5 m decline in average lake level, and (4) varying periods in cyclic lake levels from 30 years to 6 years. We also assessed population dynamics under combinations of these scenarios to determine the relative strength of effects. Increased stochasticity in river flow and declining lake level negatively affected population growth; whereas, greater variation in the amplitude of lake level and a decreased climate cycle frequency to 8-18 years positively affected population growth. Combinations of the three scenarios, not including lake level decline, resulted in overall positive population growth. Combining all four scenarios led to population decline, but not as severe as when only lake level decline was included. Stable lake levels and a sustained shorter climate cycle could promote positive population growth in June suckers despite ongoing climate change.

items.title: Long-Term Site Fidelity and Environmental Drivers of Short-Tailed Stingray (Bathytoshia brevicaudata) Occurrence in South Africa: Evidence From Decade-Scale Sightings Data and Photo-Identification.
items.abstract: Large coastal elasmobranchs face disproportionate extinction risk yet remain among the most data-deficient marine vertebrates globally. Photo-identification has emerged as a powerful non-invasive tool for studying individually recognizable species, though its application to batoids remains limited relative to sharks. This study applied decade-scale sightings data and photo-identification to characterize occurrence patterns, individual residency, and local abundance of the short-tailed stingray ( Bathytoshia brevicaudata ) at an aggregation site in Gansbaai, South Africa-a species for which site fidelity and population structure remain poorly characterized across most of its Southern Hemisphere range. Between 2014 and 2024, short-tailed stingrays were recorded on 1149 of 5730 standardized boat-based shark cage-diving trips, yielding 1351 sightings concentrated at a single shallow inshore site. A negative binomial generalized additive model identified sea surface temperature, depth, season, and time as significant predictors of occurrence, with sightings increasing above 15°C, peaking at 6-9 m depth, and displaying a bimodal seasonal pattern inconsistent with austral summer mating aggregations documented elsewhere in the species' range. Sightings increased markedly after 2017, coinciding with documented white shark displacement from the area. Photo-identification of dorsal spot patterns cataloged eleven individuals across 405 positive identifications, with residency spanning from single visits to near-decade repeated associations. An open population mark-recapture model estimated high apparent survival (0.95), moderate detection probability (0.76), and a super-population of eleven individuals with low annual recruitment. These results support the presence of a small, predominantly female, partially resident assemblage exhibiting long-term site fidelity embedded within a broader regional population. This study represents the first population-level assessment of short-tailed stingrays in South Africa and the longest continuous observational dataset on record of the species globally, demonstrating that shark cage-diving operations can serve as cost-effective, passive monitoring platforms for coastal elasmobranchs and validating photo-identification as a viable mark-recapture framework for batoids with naturally stable pigmentation patterns.

items.title: First Record of the False Catshark (Pseudotriakis microdon) From Lesser Antilles.
items.abstract: The false catshark, Pseudotriakis microdon , is the largest representative of a poorly known family of deepwater sharks and exhibits a patchy worldwide distribution. In this short note, we report the first record of P. microdon from Lesser Antilles. The female specimen, measuring approximately 310 cm in total length, was captured by an artisanal fisherman at a depth of 800 m off Martinique (14.5996° N, 61.1371° W). In addition to documenting this record, semi-directive interviews conducted with the fisherman who captured the specimen provided valuable ecological insights. Owing to a long-standing collaborative relationship, the fisherman reported many observations, suggesting that P. microdon may occur more regularly in the region. Given their life-history characteristics, deep-water sharks are generally considered particularly vulnerable to fishing pressure, making the collection of occurrence data through fisher-scientist partnerships especially important for their conservation.

items.title: Urban avian viromes reveal viral diversity of potential public health relevance across China.
items.abstract: Urbanization reshapes ecological interactions at the human-animal interface, yet how it structures viral diversity in urban avian communities remains unclear. Here, we present a pan-urban viromic analysis of avian samples collected across 22 cities in China. We identified 52,314 viral operational taxonomic units, broadly representing species-level viral clusters, revealing extensive and previously underexplored viral diversity. Viral richness varied markedly among cities, largely reflecting variation in bacteriophage diversity, whereas vertebrate-associated viruses showed a comparatively narrower diversity range. Network analyses revealed pronounced geographic structuring of avian viromes, with several cities sharing viral lineages with multiple other cities and acting as hubs of virome connectivity, linked by a core set of widely distributed viral families alongside substantial local heterogeneity. Sequence similarity and phylogenetic analyses showed that 63.1% (2994/4746) of vertebrate-associated viral sequences shared less than 80% similarity with their closest known references, including 65.6% (2718/4143) of DNA virus sequences and 45.8% (276/603) of RNA virus sequences, highlighting pervasive viral novelty across genome types. Further comparisons with reference sequences identified candidate associations with diverse annotated host taxa, including mammals and humans. Functional profiling of auxiliary metabolic genes revealed a highly skewed repertoire dominated by CysH (phosphoadenosine phosphosulfate reductase), a key enzyme in assimilatory sulfate reduction, suggesting that phages may modulate sulfur assimilation in infected bacterial hosts and potentially influence sulfur metabolism in urban bird-associated microbial communities. Together, these findings provide a nationwide view of the spatial organization, evolutionary diversity, and cross-host association patterns of viruses in urban birds, highlighting their role in shaping viral ecology in human-dominated environments.

items.title: Ecological Resilience Response of Radial Growth of Two Dominant Coniferous Tree Species to Drought in the Western Kunlun Mountains.
items.abstract: In the context of global climate warming, frequent extreme drought events pose a serious threat to the structure and function of forest ecosystems in arid and semi-arid regions. As a key ecological barrier in the inland arid areas of Asia, the Western Kunlun Mountains harbor coniferous forests whose drought adaptation mechanisms remain unclear. In 2024, tree core samples of the typical coniferous species Picea schrenkiana ( P. schrenkiana ) and the endemic species Juniperus jarkendensis ( J. jarkendensis ) were collected in the Western Kunlun Mountains. A standardized chronology was established based on tree-ring width data, and the growth-climate relationships and drought adaptation differences between the two species were systematically revealed via Partial correlation analysis, missing ring rate (MRR) calculation, and ecological resilience index. The results indicated that the missing ring characteristics of the two species differed significantly: the total missing rates of P. schrenkiana and J. jarkendensis were 2.523% and 4.093%, respectively, with 1961 identified as a common missing ring year for both. Correlation analysis indicated that the radial growth of P. schrenkiana was more sensitive to spring temperature and precipitation of the previous year ( p J. jarkendensis exhibited more significant responses to spring temperature and spring-summer precipitation of the current year ( p J. jarkendensis displayed lower resistance compared to P. schrenkiana, yet J. jarkendensis demonstrated higher recovery capacity following the drought; both species regained their pre-drought growth levels within 4 years post-drought. This study clarifies the key climatic limiting factors and drought adaptation strategies for coniferous growth in the Western Kunlun Mountains, thereby providing a scientific basis for regional historical climate reconstruction and adaptive management of coniferous forest ecosystems.

items.title: Forb Communities and Plant Functional Traits Differ Between Horse Grazed Pastures and Abandoned Fields in Northern Sweden.
items.abstract: Seminatural grasslands, created by traditional land use systems such as low-intensity cattle grazing, have high ecological value due to the occurrence of numerous plant species and their associated faunal communities. In Sweden, this habitat is threatened by both land abandonment and agricultural intensification. Low-intensity grazing by large herbivores could potentially benefit grassland-associated forb communities. The aim of this study was to compare the forb communities between horse-grazed pastures and abandoned fields in the boreal region of Northern Sweden. We surveyed forbs within 20 horse-grazed pastures and 20 abandoned fields, and compared community composition, diversity, and trait composition. Within the horse-grazed pastures, we analyzed the effect of grazing intensity, mowing frequency, and number of years grazed. The composition of the forb community differed between horse pastures and abandoned fields. Forb species richness tended to be higher in horse-grazed pastures, which were dominated by ruderal species associated with grazing, while forb communities in abandoned fields consisted mainly of competitive species. Eight species associated with semi-natural pastures were found, primarily within horse pastures. Forb species in horse pastures had a lower canopy height and seed mass, which are two known traits associated with grazing. On the contrary, the specific leaf area (SLA), a trait associated with tolerance to grazing, tended to be higher among the forbs of abandoned fields. The number of wind-pollinated species was lower in fields that were grazed for a longer time and a positive trend was shown for total forb species richness. Pastures with higher grazing intensity had lower seed mass. Synthesis : Horse-grazed pastures hosted ruderal, grazing-associated plant communities compared to abandoned sites which were dominated by strong competitors. Our results show that horse-grazed pastures host a plant community with short, small-seeded plants. The differences between field types indicate that horse grazing might be a potential restoration method to provide habitat for grazing-associated forbs which are disfavoured by land abandonment.

items.title: Novel Insights Into the Life History, Taxonomy, Host Use, and Biogeography of the Rare Ant Social Parasite Acromyrmex argentinus (Gallardo) comb. nov.
items.abstract: Ant inquiline social parasites are brood parasites of free-living ant species that exploit the social colony services of their hosts for survival and reproduction. To trace the convergent evolutionary origins of inquiline social parasitism in ants, it is important to decipher the parasites' life histories. Here, we report novel observations on the rare inquiline social parasite Pseudoatta argentina Gallardo. In addition, we inferred a mitochondrial phylogeny for 15 leaf-cutting ant species. The phylogeny demonstrates that P. argentina is deeply nested inside the genus Acromyrmex rendering the genus Acromyrmex paraphyletic. On the basis of morphological and phylogenetic evidence, we synonymize the genus Pseudoatta under the name Acromyrmex . Our field study confirms that Acromyrmex argentinus (Gallardo) comb. nov . is an obligate, workerless inquiline social parasite of Acromyrmex leaf-cutting ants. We show that A. argentinus is likely monogynous, host-queen-intolerant, and reproduces semelparously. Winged males of A. argentinus are gynaecomorphic, that is, queen-like, and male and female offspring mate with their siblings. Mitochondrial DNA barcodes reveal that A. argentinus is highly inbred across its distribution, which was either caused by a genetic bottleneck during speciation or resulted from sib-mating. Acromyrmex argentinus is a generalist parasite exploiting at least four free-living Acromyrmex species including A. ambiguus , A. crassispinus , A. heyeri , and A. lundii . Furthermore, A. argentinus is distributed throughout northern-central Argentina, southern Brazil, and Uruguay, which constitutes the largest known geographic distribution range of any inquiline social parasite in the southern hemisphere. We suggest that repeated host shifts may have facilitated the geographic range expansion of the social parasite. Although widely distributed, A. argentinus is locally rare infecting ~1% of the colonies in a host population. In summary, our study suggests that the morphological, behavioral, and life history characters associated with the inquiline syndrome evolved convergently in a mosaic fashion across the fungus-growing ants.

items.title: Shifts in Biomass Allocation and Trait Correlations Under the Combined Effects of Drought and Shade.
items.abstract: Biomass allocation in plants is mainly interpreted through two major theories: Allometric Partitioning Theory (APT) and Optimal Partitioning Theory (OPT). Under a specific environmental condition where drought and shade co-occur, biomass allocation can also be explained by trade-off, facilitation, and uncoupled hypotheses. These theories and hypotheses make contradictory predictions regarding the direction of biomass allocation to above- versus belowground organs. Because empirical support can be found for each of them, it remains unresolved which framework better explains biomass allocation strategies under combined effects of drought and shade. Moreover, we lack a unified understanding of how these frameworks may integrate. To test these five frameworks, we examined three Fagaceae species with contrasting tolerances: drought-tolerant Quercus pubescens , shade-tolerant Fagus sylvatica , and Castanea sativa with moderate shade and drought tolerance. We conducted a greenhouse experiment to detect seedling responses to simulated drought and shade using an experimental design controlling water-table gradients, light quality and quantity. We analyzed aboveground growth via LiDAR, aboveground/belowground biomass allocations, and resource acquisition strategies of these three species. We found that individual seedling responses were highly nuanced along continuous gradients, and no single theory and hypothesis adequately explained the observed biomass allocation. Moreover, we developed a novel decision chart that systematically links these disparate theories and hypotheses, rather than treating them as mutually exclusive frameworks.

items.title: Comparisons of Food Intake Rate Between Wild and Game-Farm Mallards From North America.
items.abstract: Domesticated in Europe, the game-farm mallard has been released throughout North America over the last century to supplement wild mallard populations and to increase harvest opportunities. Recent landscape genomic studies have revealed that releases have resulted in geographically widespread introgressive hybridization between game-farm and wild mallards. As a result, there is increasing concern about possible negative effects of artificially selected game-farm genes moving into wild mallard populations in North America. Given the known differences in bill morphology between game-farm and wild mallards, we hypothesized that the food intake rate would differ between game-farm and wild mallards. We studied food intake rates of wild-caught and game-farm mallards in captivity by providing these birds a representative range of food sizes that wild mallards would normally consume. We detected that game-farm mallards ingested food at about half the rate of wild mallards. Our results suggest that game-farm introgression could lead to maladaptive traits in wild mallards, but an understanding of how game-farm traits may influence the survival and reproduction of wild × game-farm mallard hybrids is needed.

items.title: Dietary Composition Is Associated with Tissue Metal Concentrations in Two Sympatric Bats.
items.abstract: Most bats are insectivorous predators, serving as sensitive bioindicators for monitoring environmental heavy metal pollution. However, the link between trophic niche characteristics and heavy metal contaminant accumulation in wildlife remains poorly quantified. Here, we combined DNA metabarcoding of the cytochrome c oxidase subunit I ( COI ) gene with tissue-based heavy metal analyses to investigate dietary composition and its relationship with tissue metal concentrations in 2 coexisting bat populations, Myotis chinensis (Chiroptera: Vespertilionidae; n = 4) and Rhinolophus sinicus (Chiroptera: Rhinolophidae; n = 5). The results revealed significant dietary differentiation between the 2 bat populations. R. sinicus exhibited a highly concentrated dietary composition, with Endoclita davidi (Lepidoptera: Hepialidae) accounting for more than 99% of the prey-assigned sequencing reads. In contrast, M. chinensis showed a more diverse prey taxonomic composition, with sequencing reads primarily assigned to dipteran insects (Muscidae and Chironomidae), along with some lepidopterans. Multivariate ordination analyses further supported clear dietary differentiation at both the prey genus and species levels between the 2 bat populations. Significant differences in heavy metal concentrations were also observed between the 2 sampled populations. Dietary composition was associated with individual-level mean Cu concentrations, while tissue-specific associations varied among organs. Our findings suggest associations between dietary composition and tissue metal concentrations in the 2 sampled bat populations.

items.title: Metabolic disease engineers the colorectal cancer ecosystem.
items.abstract: Obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D) increase colorectal cancer (CRC) risk, yet the mechanisms linking systemic metabolic dysfunction to carcinogenesis are usually considered independently. I propose that metabolic disease can act as an ecosystem engineer, altering the selective conditions in which neoplastic cells emerge and evolve. Nutrient availability, adipose dysfunction, metabolic-epigenetic coupling, immunometabolic rewiring, microbial remodeling, and bile acid metabolism interact across the colonic environment, redistributing metabolic fitness among epithelial, immune, and microbial populations. These interactions may establish a self-reinforcing ecosystem that favors metabolically adaptable clones and reduces constraints on their persistence. Metabolic dysfunction may thus alter which cellular populations can most effectively exploit available resources and evade antitumor surveillance. This hypothesis predicts that tumors with similar molecular characteristics may exist within biologically distinct environments according to the host metabolic state, and therefore could show differential responses to immune activity and therapy. Integrating systemic metabolic parameters, including adiposity distribution, insulin resistance, glycemic control, circulating metabolites, and microbial features, with molecular tumor classification could reveal distinct CRC ecological states and host-tumor dependencies. Such metabolic stratification could generate opportunities for personalized prevention and therapy by identifying vulnerabilities that remain obscured by current tumor-centric classification.

items.title: Designing psychiatric environments tailored to the needs of geriatric patients: spatial solutions in geriatric-psychiatric hospital wards that reduce stress and dissorientation.
items.abstract: Background The progressive aging of the population increases the demand for specialized psychiatric wards adapted to the needs of older adults. A particular challenge is designing spaces for patients with dementia, as environmental changes may cause disorientation, deterioration of mental condition, and increased behavioral disturbances. Properly designed therapeutic environments improve safety, support spatial orientation, and enhance psychological comfort. The aim of this study was to identify and analyze good design practices in geriatric psychiatric wards based on the principles of health-promoting architecture. Material and methods A narrative literature review was conducted, covering publications on healthcare architecture, environmental psychiatry, and therapeutic environment design, with particular focus on patients with dementia. Current guidelines, design recommendations, and practical solutions used in healthcare facilities were also analyzed. The study had a descriptive and comparative character. Identified architectural solutions were assessed using a qualitative comparative approach according to criteria related to health-promoting architecture, including spatial orientation, accessibility, environmental safety, sensory comfort, social interaction, and reduction of stress and behavioral symptoms. Results The analysis showed that clear functional layouts, spatial zoning, and intuitive wayfinding reduce disorientation and improve patient independence. Important elements include appropriate colors, visual identification features, natural lighting, contact with nature, and ergonomic and safe equipment. Communal spaces support social interaction, reduce isolation, and enhance therapeutic processes. These solutions may reduce stress, aggressive behaviors, and improve quality of care. Conclusions Designing geriatric psychiatric wards according to the needs of people with dementia supports treatment effectiveness and user safety. Integration of architectural knowledge with psychiatry and environmental psychology enables the creation of health-promoting environments. The findings may support modernization of existing wards and the design of new facilities, while indicating the need for further research on the impact of therapeutic environments on clinical outcomes and patient well-being in long-term psychiatric care settings for older adults. items.title: Prevalence and determinants of undetected and uncontrolled hypertension: findings from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging.
items.abstract: Background Hypertension awareness and control are widely used indicators of health system effectiveness, quality, and reach in managing chronic disease. This study estimated the prevalence of undetected and uncontrolled hypertension among middle-aged and older Canadian adults and examined the factors associated with each. Methods We analyzed cross-sectional data from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging (CLSA) for adults aged 45 years and older. Hypertension was identified from interviewer-administered blood pressure measurements or self-reported diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine associations with predisposing, enabling, and need factors. Results The prevalence of hypertension was 42.9%. Of those with hypertension, 17.2% were unaware of their condition, and 26.2% of those who were aware had uncontrolled blood pressure. Not having blood pressure measured in the previous year was strongly associated with undetected hypertension (OR 3.15, 95% CI 2.39-4.15) and was also associated with uncontrolled hypertension (OR 1.51, 95% CI 1.09-2.10). Not having seen a physician in the previous year was similarly associated with both undetected (OR 1.58, 95% CI 1.19-2.08) and uncontrolled hypertension (OR 1.35, 95% CI 1.03-1.77). Younger age and better self-rated general health were associated with undetected hypertension, with odds declining progressively as self-rated health worsened (poor vs excellent: OR 0.28, 95% CI 0.14-0.55). Older age and male sex were associated with uncontrolled hypertension. Conclusion Undetected and uncontrolled hypertension are common among middle-aged and older Canadians, consistent with gaps in access to primary care and routine screening. Undetected hypertension was most common among adults reporting excellent health, which suggests that care prompted by symptoms may miss a substantial share of cases. Future research should identify and evaluate system-level policies targeted to the populations most affected, including opportunistic and community-based blood pressure measurement.

items.title: Psychometric Validation of the German International Depression Questionnaire and the International Anxiety Questionnaire.
items.abstract: Background The International Depression Questionnaire (IDQ) and the International Anxiety Questionnaire (IAQ) are brief, ICD-11-aligned self-report instruments designed to assess depressive episodes and generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). While the initial validation study of the original English versions supported unidimensional structures, further cross-cultural validation is warranted. This study examined the psychometric properties of the German versions of the IDQ and IAQ among German-speaking adults. Methods A total of 710 participants completed an online survey including the IDQ, IAQ, and additional measures assessing depressive symptoms, anxiety, posttraumatic stress, and adjustment difficulties. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses assessed factorial validity. Internal consistency was evaluated using Cronbach's alpha. Convergent and discriminant validity were examined via partial correlations controlling for age and gender. Results Analyses supported a three-factor structure for the IDQ (essential, cognitive-affective, and vegetative symptoms) and a unidimensional structure for the IAQ, as two-factor solutions yielded very highly correlated factors. Both scales demonstrated good model fit and excellent internal consistency ( α = 0.90 for each scale). The IDQ showed the strongest correlations with depressive symptoms and negative automatic thoughts, while the IAQ correlated most strongly with measures of generalized anxiety. Lower correlations with posttraumatic stress and adjustment problems supported discriminant validity. Conclusions The results provide initial evidence that the German versions of the IDQ and IAQ are reliable and valid tools for assessing ICD-11 depression and generalized anxiety. The multidimensional structure of the IDQ supports theoretical distinctions between depressive symptom domains, whereas the IAQ appears best represented by a single generalized anxiety factor. Further replication and validation against external clinical criteria are needed to establish the clinical relevance of these factor structures.

items.title: Preparedness of osteopathic medical students to address vaccine hesitancy: training and confidence.
items.abstract: Context Vaccine hesitancy poses a growing threat to public health, contributing to measles resurgences and declining childhood vaccination coverage in the United States. Although physicians remain among the most trusted sources of vaccine information, formal training in vaccine communication is not consistently integrated into medical curricula. Osteopathic medical education emphasizes whole-person, patient-centered care, which closely aligns with the skills required for effective vaccine counseling. However, the preparedness of osteopathic medical students for vaccine-related communication has not been well characterized. Objectives This study aimed to assess osteopathic medical students' perceptions of their curricular preparation for vaccine-related communication, as well as clinical-year students' real-world experiences and confidence in addressing vaccine hesitancy during rotations. Methods A prospective cross-sectional anonymous online survey was administered via Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) to medical students enrolled in Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) programs across the United States. Participants were recruited through Student Osteopathic Medical Association (SOMA) communication channels and institutional listservs. The survey assessed demographics, clinical exposure to vaccine discussions, confidence in addressing vaccine hesitancy, curricular preparation, and perceived training needs utilizing 5-point Likert-scale items. Ordinal logistic regression and Welch's t tests compared preclinical (Osteopathic Medical Student [OMS]-1/2) vs. clinical (OMS-3/4) students, OMS-3 vs. OMS-4 students, and clinical vaccine discussion groups. Odds ratios (ORs) and p values were calculated on 95 % confidence intervals (CIs) between groups. Results A total of 1,415 osteopathic medical students completed the survey. Overall, 87.1 % reported no formal vaccine communication training, with 88.6 % of OMS1/2 students and 85.3 % of OMS3/4 students agreeing or strongly agreeing that vaccine communication should be formally included in their curriculum. Compared with preclinical students, clinical students were less likely to report adequate curricular preparation for addressing vaccine hesitancy (OR=0.67, 95 % CI [0.55, 0.81;] p Conclusions Osteopathic medical students recognize vaccine hesitancy as a routine clinical challenge, agree that additional training in counseling would be helpful, and although clinical exposure builds confidence, this may occur unevenly and without structured design; formal training would help build this competence earlier and more equitably. Evidence-based tools, including motivational interviewing, simulation, and standardized patient encounters, align closely with osteopathic principles of whole-person care. Integrating these approaches into required curricula represents a practical and necessary step toward preparing future physicians to navigate both vaccine-related conversations and difficult conversations effectively.

items.title: Birth position and tissue context influence Bipolar Cell translocation mode in the developing retina.
items.abstract: Neuronal translocation is essential for establishing functional tissue architecture in the developing central nervous system. While many of the cell-intrinsic mechanisms driving translocation have been identified, how these strategies adapt to dynamic developmental tissue changes remains less understood. Here, we address this question using retinal Bipolar Cells as a model as they are generated across unlaminated and laminated stages. This enables direct comparison of neuronal translocation modes and dynamics across development. We show that the mode of movement of Bipolar Cells changes depending on tissue lamination state. Bipolar Cells born before photoreceptor layer formation undergo directed, microtubule-dependent somal translocation as seen for other early born neurons. In contrast, later-born Bipolar Cells exhibit more passive and less directed displacement that seems to be mostly driven by collective tissue movements. Interference with tissue-wide movements reduces this displacement, while disrupting photoreceptor layer formation leads to directed translocation also at later developmental stages. Independent of strategy, cells achieve accurate laminar positioning. Together, this shows that tissue context can influence cell movement modes, a principle likely relevant across developing neural and other tissues.

items.title: GLP-1(9-37) Improves Left Ventricular Function in a Murine Model of Cardiac Pressure Overload by Promoting Mitochondrial Biogenesis.
items.abstract: Aim Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is an incretin hormone that is released in response to nutrient intake and inflammation. Its active form, GLP-1(7-37), binds to the GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R), but GLP-1 is rapidly degraded by dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) into GLP-1(9-37), which does not bind to the classical GLP-1R. Both peptides exhibit cardioprotective effects, although the underlying mechanisms are unclear and the role of GLP-1(9-37) remains poorly understood. Methods and results In this study, we investigated cardiac and metabolic effects of GLP-1(9-37) in a mouse model of cardiac pressure overload. LacZ and GLP-1(9-37) were overexpressed using an AAV vector system. While GLP-1(9-37) does not affect glucose metabolism, it mechanistically activates key metabolic regulators, as evidenced by increased AMPK and PGC1α signalling. This shift suggests an improvement in cellular energy balance and mitochondrial function under hypertrophic stress conditions. GLP-1(9-37) was also found to mitigate adverse cardiac remodelling. Treatment is associated with reduced septal thickness and decreased cardiac fibrosis, indicating attenuation of structural hypertrophy. Conclusions In summary, our data suggest a protective role of GLP-1(9-37) in pressure-overload-induced cardiac remodelling, which is associated with AMPK/PGC1α-signalling.

items.title: Interpretation of non-statistically significant results in randomised controlled clinical trials in rehabilitation: a cross sectional analysis.
items.abstract: Objectives To assess the prevalence of misinterpretation of non-statistically significant results, both in the abstract and in the article conclusions, in a sample of randomized controlled trials with non-statistically significant primary outcomes published in rehabilitation journals, and the reporting of the primary outcomes in accordance with the CONSORT Guidelines. Methods A cross-sectional analysis was conducted of all RCTs with non-statistically significant primary outcomes in five general rehabilitation journals with the highest Impact Factor, published between 2019 and 2023. The objective of this analysis was to assess the prevalence of misinterpretation of non-statistically significant results, both in the abstract and in the article conclusions, in a sample of RCTs with non-statistically significant results and reporting of primary outcomes according to CONSORT guidelines. Results The analysis included 31 trials. The most common interpretation of non-statistically significant results was the evidence of absence, both in the abstract (74.2%) and the article (58.1%). Only four (12.9%) studies in the abstract and five (16.1%) conclusions in the article suggested the correct interpretation as the absence of evidence. Adherence to CONSORT guidelines was moderate, with only 61.3% of trials reporting results summaries for each arm, effect size, and confidence interval. Discussions/conclusions There is a need for increased rigor in reporting and interpreting non-statistically significant results in rehabilitation trials. Evidence misinterpretations can adversely impact clinical decision-making and future research directions. Efforts should be made to promote accurate interpretation of statistical results, emphasize the importance of analyzing confidence intervals, and develop educational interventions to improve statistical literacy.
