items.title: Epigenetic modulation of the skeletal muscle methylome in a hind-limb unloading model.
items.abstract: Skeletal muscle exhibits remarkable plasticity, continually adapting to physiological and environmental stressors through coordinated transcriptional and epigenetic mechanisms. To our knowledge, this is the first study investigating the whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) of the gastrocnemius muscle of mice in a hind-limb unloading (HLU) model, to characterise genome-wide DNA methylation. HLU mice exhibited reduced gastrocnemius weight, consistent with muscle atrophy, impaired grip strength, and shorter wire hanging times. Histological analysis revealed smaller fiber sizes and fewer myonuclei per fiber, accompanied by a significant reduction in myonuclear domain (MND) size, suggesting compromised transcriptional support per nucleus. These structural and functional changes were accompanied by differential methylation of genes associated with anabolic and cytoskeletal pathways. Following quality control (coverage ≥ 10×; q < 0.01; methylation difference ≥ 25%), 6,892 differentially methylated regions (DMRs) were identified and annotated to genomic and functional features. HLU induced widespread CpG methylation remodelling, with 4,755 regions (69.0%) hypermethylated and 2,137 (31.0%) hypomethylated, indicating a genome-wide shift toward hypermethylation. Pathway enrichment analyses were performed to identify the biological relevance of methylation changes. Most DMRs were localised within promoter and gene-body regions, particularly across chromosomes 1, 7, and 11, which contain regulators of muscle metabolism, cytoskeletal organisation, and energy homeostasis. Hypermethylation of genes such as Atp6v1h, Sox17, and Rgs20 was associated with pathways involved in lysosomal function, angiogenesis, and G-protein signalling, potentially reflecting metabolic downscaling and reduced contractile demand. Conversely, hypomethylation of structural and cytoskeletal genes may support maintenance of mechanical stability and stress resilience. Enrichment of calcium signalling, MAPK, Rap1, Wnt, oxidative phosphorylation, and autophagy pathways underscores coordinated epigenetic regulation of contraction-metabolism and mitochondrial adaptation. Together, our findings suggest that HLU is associated with coordinated epigenetic and phenotypic remodelling in skeletal muscle, with CpG methylation representing a potential regulatory layer involved in adaptation to mechanical unloading.

items.title: Go With the Flow: Environmental Conditions Are Associated With Congruence Between eDNA Signals and Fish Communities in Small Lotic Ecosystems.
items.abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding is increasingly used to assess fish communities. However, how environmental and hydrological conditions are associated with the eDNA signal, and how it relates to local fish assemblages, remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether environmental drivers modulate the spatial congruence between eDNA signals and local fish assemblages by comparing qualitative and quantitative fish data derived from eDNA metabarcoding and electrofishing surveys at 17 sites across eight watercourses in central Italy. Expectedly, metabarcoding detected more species than electrofishing at most sampling sites, reflecting higher sensitivity to rare taxa. eDNA read counts showed a moderate relationship with both fish abundance and biomass, with stronger associations for the latter. However, the congruence between eDNA and electrofishing-derived community estimates varied along environmental gradients: while increased water discharge correlated with higher divergence between methods, temperature and oxygen showed the opposite trend. These results suggest that eDNA signals integrate both local and upstream biodiversity depending on hydrological and physicochemical conditions. Our findings support the high detection power of eDNA metabarcoding for characterizing fish communities in small rivers and suggest that the eDNA signal may integrate information from beyond the electrofished reach. More broadly, our study demonstrates that eDNA should be interpreted as an environmentally mediated signal rather than a direct proxy of local community composition. By linking variation in eDNA-community congruence to environmental gradients, this study provides a general framework for predicting when and where eDNA reflects the sampling area versus upstream biodiversity in flowing ecosystems.

items.title: Quantifying Methionine Requirements for Two Strains of Juvenile Nile Tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ) Fed Diets Containing Black Soldier Fly Larvae Meal.
items.abstract: This study investigated the optimal dietary methionine requirements of local and genetically improved strains of Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) fed diets with constant inclusion levels of black soldier fly larvae meal (BSFL). Six isonitrogenous (∿35% crude protein [CP]), isolipidic (∿11% crude fat) and isoenergetic (∿492 kcal gross energy/100 g) diets (D0.36, D0.96, D1.05, D1.15, D1.23 and D1.41) were formulated with graded levels of DL-methionine (0%, 0.67%, 0.77%, 0.87%, 0.97% and 1.17%, respectively) at the expense of carboxymethyl cellulose to give analysed methionine levels of 3.6, 9.6, 10.5, 11.5, 12.3 and 14.1 g/kg of diet, with a constant cysteine level of 4.2 g/kg. Thirty-five fish of each strain (4.08 ± 0.12 g) were randomly stocked in each 100 L plastic tank, with three replicate tanks per treatment, in a recirculating aquaculture system (RAS) and fed to apparent satiation twice daily for 84 days. There were significant effects of dietary methionine, strain and their interaction on all analysed parameters (p < 0.05), except survival rate and albumin levels. Significantly higher growth performance, feed utilisation, haemato-biochemical and antioxidant profiles were recorded with a methionine inclusion of 10.5 g/kg in the diet for the local strain and 11.5 g/kg in the diet for the improved strain (p < 0.05). Quadratic regression estimated optimum dietary methionine requirements at 9.08-9.64 g/kg of the diet for the local strain and at 9.13-9.55 g/kg of the diet for the improved strain, with a cysteine level of 4.2 g/kg. These findings suggest that aligning dietary formulations with strain-specific nutritional requirements is crucial for optimal fish performance, successful fish farming and sustainable aquaculture.

items.title: GPCR-Mediated Regulation of Cytochrome P450 Drives Sulfoxaflor Resistance in Aphis gossypii Glover.
items.abstract: Rapid evolution of insecticide resistance threatens agricultural productivity. While the fundamental molecular and biochemical mechanisms underlying resistance are well documented, the regulatory processes governing resistance-associated genes, particularly those involving signal-regulated transcription factors, remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated trans-regulation of cytochrome P450 genes associated with sulfoxaflor resistance in Aphis gossypii Glover. Our findings suggest that G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR)-associated signaling and cAMP response element binding protein contribute to resistance-associated P450 gene regulation. FISH and RT-qPCR demonstrate that DopR1 transcripts are enriched in the epidermis, and β-1A transcripts are enriched in the head. Molecular docking, heterologous expression, and biolayer interferometry assays demonstrate that DopR1 and β-1A participate in cellular recognition or response to sulfoxaflor and activate downstream cAMP signaling. Silencing DopR1 and β-1A reduced cAMP content, PKA activity, P450 enzyme activity, and resistance-related P450 expression, thereby enhancing aphid sensitivity to sulfoxaflor. Inhibitor-based suppression, pathway gene silencing, and dual-luciferase reporter assays implicated AC-2, AC-5, PKA-4, PKA-7, CRTC, and CREB in regulating critical resistance-related genes, especially CYP6CY19. Furthermore, functional validation using transgenic Drosophila melanogaster expressing CYP6CY13 and CYP6CY19 demonstrated increased sulfoxaflor tolerance. Collectively, these findings support a working model linking GPCR-associated signaling to the regulation of selected resistance-associated P450 genes in A. gossypii.

items.title: Self-Awareness and Career Decision-Making: Evidence From Adolescents in Arunachal Pradesh, India.
items.abstract: Career decision-making is an important developmental task during adolescence, yet evidence from geographically understudied regions remains limited. This study examined the associations between self-awareness and career decision-making among adolescents in Arunachal Pradesh, India. A cross-sectional school-based survey included 564 adolescents aged 14-19 years enrolled in secondary and higher secondary schools in the Itanagar Capital Region of Arunachal Pradesh, India. Participants completed standardized measures of self-awareness and career decision-making. They also completed open-ended questions on perceived strengths, career aspirations and sources of career guidance. Pearson correlations, simple and multivariable linear regression, and content analyses were used. Adolescents reported high self-awareness and career decidedness (r = 0.40, p< 0.001), but not with career indecision (r = -0.08). Self-awareness accounted for 15.8% with career decidedness in the bivariate model (R2 = 0.158, f2 = 0.19) and remained modestly associated after adjustment for gender, community, school type and age (β = 0.37, p < 0.001). Content analysis indicated that medical and technical professions were the most preferred career aspirations, while some adolescents reported uncertainty regarding their career interests. Many participants relied on parents and teachers for career guidance. Self-awareness showed a modest association with career decidedness and should be understood as one developmental resource operating alongside family, school and community influences. The findings contribute to adolescent career development in an understudied Indian context and highlight the importance of fostering self-awareness to support career decision-making.

items.title: Profiles of emotion regulation difficulties in the transition to menopause: a latent profile analysis.
items.abstract: The menopausal transition is associated with heightened psychological vulnerability, yet individual differences in emotion regulation (ER) during this period remain poorly understood. This study applied latent profile analysis to identify distinct ER difficulty profiles in women during menopause transition and examined attachment anxiety and avoidance as predictors of profile membership. A sample of 455 women aged 40-60 years at different stages of the menopausal transition (late reproductive, perimenopausal, and postmenopausal) participated in this cross-sectional study. Four profiles were identified: High ER Difficulties (11.2%), Moderate ER Difficulties (48.1%), Emotional Clarity Deficit (11.4%), and Low ER Difficulties (29.2%). Profiles differed significantly on depression, anxiety, stress, menopause-specific somatic and psychological symptoms, and personal burnout (all p < .001, with large effects), with one key exception: the Emotional Clarity Deficit profile did not differ from the Low ER profile on any outcome despite presenting the highest lack of emotional clarity scores in the solution. Attachment anxiety and avoidance both predicted membership in the High and Moderate ER profiles, whereas only attachment avoidance uniquely predicted the Emotional Clarity Deficit profile. These findings provide initial person-centered evidence of ER heterogeneity in the menopausal transition. The Emotional Clarity Deficit profile, which was statistically associated with attachment avoidance, represents a configuration not captured by severity-based approaches; however, its clinical significance and stability remain to be established through replication in independent samples and longitudinal research.

items.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: A Qualitative Study of Lived Experience Disclosure in the Workplace Among Eating Disorder Clinicians.
items.abstract: Background Up to half of eating disorder clinicians report personal lived experience of an eating disorder. However, there is limited research examining experiences of eating disorder clinicians' disclosure of an eating disorder in the workplace. We aimed to analyze qualitative responses about disclosure of an eating disorder in the workplace among eating disorder clinicians. Method Australian eating disorder health professionals responded online to an open-ended question where respondents (N = 103, 95.15% female, M age = 36.98 years) were asked about personal or colleagues' experiences of eating disorder disclosure in the workplace. Responses were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Four themes were developed through analysis: (1) stigma, prejudice, and discrimination; (2) supportive inclusivity, hope and understanding; (3) disclosure policy and practice uncertainty, and (4) disclosure agency and context. Responses highlighted negative assumptions made about a clinician's fitness to practice, from collegial interactions through to recruitment and supervision practices. Discussion Findings suggest that eating disorder clinicians with lived experience of an eating disorder report significant stigma and discrimination within the workforce. Results highlight the urgent need for the eating disorder sector to create psychologically safe workplaces, which has the potential to improve clinician and client wellbeing. Continued research into building a mentally healthy eating disorder workforce should include development of ethical practice guidelines to help supervisors, managers, and colleagues support clinicians with lived experience of an eating disorder.

items.title: Persistent Gaps in the Reporting, Representation, and Assessment of Sociodemographic Sample Characteristics in United States Eating Disorder Psychotherapy Trials: An Invited Interim Update.
items.abstract: Objective Present an interim update on the reporting and representation of sociodemographic data in eating disorder psychotherapeutic treatment trials in the United States from 2021 to 2026 and discuss challenges that arose during screening and data synthesis. Provide recommendations to improve trial reporting to facilitate ongoing systematic evaluation of representation. Method PRISMA guidelines for systematic reviews were followed. Eligible studies were randomized controlled psychotherapeutic eating disorder treatment trials in the efficacy or effectiveness stage with at least one US site published from 2021 to mid-2026. Two independent raters screened and extracted data. We calculated pooled estimates to evaluate representation. Results Our search yielded 1343 studies for screening; eight were deemed eligible. Screening challenges arose due to participant location ambiguity, lack of by-country demographic data, and ambiguity in intervention development stage. Trials were predominantly focused on young adult, female populations and disproportionately targeted binge-eating spectrum disorders and high weight. Sexual orientation and diverse gender identities were not assessed. We observed some indication of increased racial diversity, but Black participants remained markedly underrepresented. Discussion Representation estimates should be interpreted with caution due to small sample size. We observed some signals of progress in sociodemographic representation, but also continued areas of stagnation (e.g., age diversity). To facilitate future evaluation of sociodemographic representation, we provide recommendations for clinical trial conduct and reporting, including improved transparency in participant location and intervention stage.

items.title: Disordered Eating Attitudes and Behaviors in Individuals With BMI > 27 kg/m<sup>2</sup> Treated by Semaglutide: A 60-Week Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Objective To examine disordered eating attitudes and behaviors in individuals treated with semaglutide 2.4 mg or placebo for 60 weeks. Methods Individuals seeking obesity treatment (n = 120) randomized (3:2) to semaglutide or placebo, both with lifestyle intervention, were assessed at baseline and Weeks 20, 40, and 60. At each assessment, clinicians evaluated binge eating and eating disorder psychopathology (Eating Disorder Examination), and questionnaires measured loss of control (Loss of Control Over Eating Scale), drive for thinness [Eating Disorder Inventory (EDI)], body dissatisfaction (EDI and Body Satisfaction Scale), and mood (PHQ-9). Following multiple imputation, ANCOVAs compared the groups in change at each assessment, controlling for baseline. Results Mean reductions from baseline in loss of control, global eating disorder pathology, weight and shape concern, drive for thinness, and body dissatisfaction were significantly greater with semaglutide compared to placebo at several timepoints. The groups did not differ significantly in binge frequency reductions. However, participants reporting baseline binge episodes (n = 31) and those who had full or subthreshold binge-eating disorder (n = 18) were more likely to achieve abstinence with semaglutide compared to placebo. Reliable deteriorations in eating psychopathology, new onset of binge eating, and compensatory behaviors were rare, and symptom emergence did not seem higher with semaglutide. Discussion Semaglutide reduced eating disorder psychopathology and improved body image relative to placebo at 20 to 60 weeks of treatment for obesity management. Semaglutide also increased remission in those with binge eating. Disordered eating behaviors were rare but did occur, suggesting the need for periodic monitoring in at-risk individuals. Trial registration clinicaltrials.gov number NCT05548647.

items.title: Divergent effects of memory suppression on food reward evaluation: devaluation in normal-weight versus rebound in females with overweight/obesity.
items.abstract: Previous research has shown that satiety-related inhibition of food reward memory retrieval is a key process in appetite regulation, with impairments in this function promoting overeating and weight gain. Building on this literature, the present study examined whether externally cued active suppression of food-related memory retrieval via the Think/No-Think (TNT) paradigm can directly modulate subjective food reward evaluations, including liking and wanting, across individuals with varying body mass index (BMI) levels. Fifty-seven female university students, including those with normal weight and those living with overweight/obesity, completed a food-specific Think/No-Think task, wherein participants were instructed to actively retrieve certain food-related words while deliberately suppressing others. Self-reported measures of liking and wanting for each food item were employed to assess how memory suppression influences food reward evaluations. All participants, regardless of BMI status, demonstrated significantly lower recall accuracy for suppressed items compared to retrieved items ([-0.079, -0.031], p < 0.001) and baseline items ([-0.070, -0.018], p = 0.001). However, reward evaluations differed markedly. Individuals with healthy weight exhibited a significant reduction in wanting for No-Think items ([0.013, 0.426], p = 0.038), indicating successful devaluation. Conversely, participants with overweight or obesity exhibited heightened desire for suppressed items ([-0.324, -0.029], p = 0.021). Further analyses revealed that restrained eating behaviors mediated these divergent responses ([-0.589, -0.079], p = 0.011). Active memory suppression not only reduces food memory accessibility but also significantly devalues subjective food reward evaluations, particularly subjective wanting for food items. Maladaptive eating behaviors like dietary restraint appear to generate a "rebound effect" rather than devaluation. These findings suggest that memory suppression holds potential for regulating food responses and obesity-prevention interventions.

items.title: Cannabis Use Modalities and Their Associations with Cannabis Use Disorder Severity.
items.abstract: Cannabis continues to be the most common illicit substance used in the United States. Increases in cannabis use prevalence are associated with increases in cannabis use disorder (CUD) risk. With changes in legalization, potency, and social acceptability, very little research has examined the potential usage modalities and their association with CUD. The purpose of this study is to determine the classes of cannabis users and examine each class' probability of being associated with current CUD in an undergraduate sample. The sample included 431 self-identifying African American undergraduate students (Women = 71.70%) with a mean age of approximately 19.55 (SD = 1.64) years. After giving consent, participants were asked to complete an online self-reported survey, including the Daily Sessions, Frequency, Age of Onset, and Quantity of Cannabis Use Inventory (DFAQ-CU). The DFAQ-CU contains an item inquiring about the participant' primary cannabis consumption method. Upon completion of the online survey, participants were administered a semi-structured interview that included the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI). The MINI assesses psychological disorders, including CUD ( n = 144). Employing Latent Class Analysis, we identified three classes: 1) Unlikely Users ( n = 247), Joints/Blunts ( n = 159), and Multi-users ( n = 25). Multinomial regression analysis revealed that Joints and Blunt users were more likely to have mild, moderate, and severe CUD. Multiusers were also more likely to have mild or moderate CUD, with higher likelihood than their Joint/Blunt counterparts. The three-class model underscores the increased risk of CUD associated with multi-use and predominant joints/blunts usage.

items.title: Differential neural mechanisms of hypnosis and progressive muscle relaxation in reducing social anxiety symptoms.
items.abstract: Background Hypnosis (HYP) and progressive muscle relaxation (PMR) are effective for social anxiety disorder (SAD), but their neural mechanisms remain unclear. This study compared their effects on brain activity and connectivity during emotional face processing. Methods Forty-five participants with high social anxiety symptoms were randomized to HYP (n = 24) or PMR (n = 21) and assessed before and after 6 sessions using the Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale and fMRI. 23 matched healthy controls (HC) served as baseline controls. Brain activation and generalized psychophysiological interaction (gPPI) analyses were conducted. Results At baseline, SAD group versus HC showed higher LSAS scores, slower emotional face RTs, and reduced activation in occipital, postcentral, prefrontal/temporal regions, caudate, putamen, and thalamus. After intervention, both groups had lower LSAS scores. PMR increased RTs while HYP did not. HYP selectively decreased activation in the left superior frontal gyrus (lSFG) for negative stimuli and in the right superior temporal gyrus for neutral stimuli, whereas PMR showed no such effects. Both interventions reduced activation in the caudate, putamen, and thalamus. gPPI revealed that HYP increased lSFG-posterior cingulate cortex connectivity under negative stimuli, while PMR decreased this connectivity. Conclusions Both interventions alleviated SAD symptoms via limbic modulation; however, HYP more strongly targeted fronto-temporal regions and cognitive-attentional networks, suggesting partially distinct neural mechanisms from PMR. Clinical trials registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR1900022651).

items.title: Acute and Early HIV Infection Among Key Populations in Rwanda: A Multisite Cross-Sectional Study to Inform Targeted Testing and Case-Finding, 2025.
items.abstract: Acute HIV infection is highly transmissible yet often missed by antibody-only rapid tests. Rwanda adopted fourth-generation antigen/antibody (Ag/Ab) tests in 2016, but routine p24 antigen documentation remains limited, limiting acute/early infection estimates. This study characterized acute/early HIV infection among key populations, including female sex workers (FSW), men who have sex with men (MSM), and people who inject drugs (PWID), to inform targeted testing and prevention interventions. We conducted a cross-sectional study in 2025 across 25 health facilities in 12 Rwandan districts. Individuals aged ≥ 15 years with unknown HIV status from FSW, MSM, PWID, and adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) were recruited via snowball sampling. Structured RedCap questionnaires captured socio-demographic, behavioral, and HIV testing history data. HIV testing followed the national serial algorithm using fourth-generation Determine HIV Early Detect rapid tests; acute/early infection required p24 antigen positivity regardless of antibody status. Among 1341 participants (median age 25 years, interquartile range [IQR]: 21-30), 864 (64%) were FSW, 177 (13%) were MSM, 58 (4.3%) were PWID, and 242 (18%) were AGYW; 66% had only primary education and 55% resided in rural areas. In the prior 4 weeks, 52% reported multiple sexual partners and 35.5% reported consistent condom use. One-third (416, 32.8%) were aware of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), and 34.7% (141/406) had ever used it. Overall HIV positivity was 5.0% (67/1341); acute/early HIV infection yield was 0.45% (6/1341), with two-thirds of cases (4/6) among MSM, all from Kigali City. Half (3/6) of acute/early cases reported inconsistent condom use and none reported PrEP use. Acute and early HIV infections appear more common among MSM in Kigali, potentially associated with ongoing risk behaviors and low PrEP uptake, although this observation is based on a small number of cases. Priorities include strengthened acute HIV surveillance via fourth-generation and self-testing, rapid antiretroviral therapy (ART) initiation, and scaled-up tailored prevention, especially PrEP.

items.title: Diurnal Patterns of Accelerometer-Measured Physical Activity, Genetic Risk and Incident Obesity: A Cohort Study of 58 877 Participants.
items.abstract: To examine the associations of diurnal physical activity patterns with incident obesity and whether these associations vary by genetic susceptibility. This prospective study included 58 877 UK Biobank participants with accelerometer data. Functional principal component analysis (fPCA) was applied to derive diurnal physical activity (PA) patterns. Cox proportional hazards models were used to examine the associations of PA patterns with incident obesity and their interactions with a body mass index polygenic risk score (PRSBMI). During a median follow-up of 8.3 years, 1567 participants developed obesity. Four functional principal components (fPCs) accounted for 97.2% of the total variance. Greater overall activity (fPC1) was associated with lower obesity risk (HR per SD = 0.85, 95% CI: 0.80-0.89). After adjustment for total physical activity, greater central-daytime activity (fPC2) was also associated with lower risk (HR per SD = 0.93, 95% CI: 0.90-0.97). For fPC4, compared with a score of 0, HRs were 0.91 (95% CI: 0.83-1.00) at a score of 1 (greater morning and evening activity) and 0.92 (95% CI: 0.84-1.00) at a score of -1 (greater midday and overnight activity). The fPC1 association was similar across low, intermediate, and high PRSBMI levels (HR = 0.87 at each level). Our findings support prioritising overall physical activity for obesity prevention across levels of genetic susceptibility, while also considering greater concentration of activity during the daytime.

items.title: Trustworthy Crisis Mental Health Care: Key Values and Features.
items.abstract: Mental health crises are increasing in the United States. Local and national policy efforts have focused on increasing access to crisis services, but little attention has been given to the quality of services delivered, or their perceived trustworthiness by people who use them. While trust in health care has been well studied in general health care settings, there has been a gap in the context of crisis mental health care. This gap exists despite the central role of relationships in mental health care, the vulnerability of people experiencing crises, and the use of practices known to erode trust (e.g., involuntary hospitalization). Our aim was to develop a framework for conceptualizing values and features of trustworthy crisis mental health care. With ongoing consultation from an advisory board, we conducted seven semistructured 1.5-hour virtual focus groups with 27 adults with lived experience of crisis mental health care to understand how trust in services is shaped. Transcripts were analyzed abductively for emergent themes through a rigorous process of codebook development and validation. We identified four core values underpinning beliefs in a trustworthy crisis mental health care system (human connection, autonomy, transparency, and respect), and four supporting values (personalization, benevolence, competence, and access). A trustworthy crisis mental health care system that expresses these values would exhibit a range of features across relational, organizational, systems, and societal levels. Participants emphasized the need to invest in non-medical, alternative crisis models. A central tension in current services emerged between risk management (e.g., concern over liability and physical safety) and therapeutic benefit, undermining trustworthiness at all levels. Beliefs in trustworthy crisis mental health care are unique to this setting. While we have outlined values and features of trustworthy crisis services, future work is needed to identify appropriate strategies to operationalize these values, as well as ways to address salient tension points that compromise trustworthiness.

items.title: Maximizing the utilization and impact of the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI): A comprehensive guide to data handling and analytic strategies.
items.abstract: The Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) is a cohort study with publicly available resources intended to accelerate osteoarthritis research by providing harmonized clinical data, imaging, and biospecimens for 4,796 participants aged 45-79 years at enrollment, who were followed longitudinally for up to 16 years. OAI resources are distributed across three repositories: 1) the National Institute of Mental Health Data Archive (NDA; original visit data, millions of images, secondary image assessment, and biospecimen project data), 2) the database of Genotypes and Phenotypes (dbGaP; genome-wide association study data), and 3) the OAI biospecimen repository. The breadth and depth of the OAI's complex data architecture - spanning multiple repositories, nested studies, and longitudinal data files - are strengths. However, they also present challenges for investigators, particularly those new to the OAI. This manuscript provides a practical, methods-oriented guide to using OAI data and resources to lower barriers to OAI use, with the hope of accelerating discovery in osteoarthritis and related fields. We describe the study's design and its three repositories. We offer detailed guidance on dataset structure, file formats, naming conventions, key-merging variables, and missing-data codes. We address common analytic considerations, including the handling of data from image assessment projects, contingent variables, informative missingness, and subcohort-specific eligibility criteria. We provide recommendations for transparent reporting and reproducibility. We also describe how the OAI Collaborative Osteoarthritis Research Enterprise (OAI CORE) Knowledgebase, a National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS)-funded initiative designed to promote and facilitate the use of OAI resources, can assist users.

items.title: Exposure to multiple cephalosporins and central obesity among rural Chinese adults: A population-based biomonitoring study.
items.abstract: Cephalosporins are commonly used in human and veterinary medicine. Urinary biomonitoring can capture internal exposure from medical, dietary, and environmental sources. However, evidence on cephalosporin exposure and adiposity in adults remains limited so far. A population-based cross-sectional study included 1044 adults from three rural communities in Zhejiang Province, China, between May and June 2023. Twelve urinary cephalosporins were measured by solid-phase extraction coupled with ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. In a restricted sample of 918 participants, estimated daily intake (EDI) was calculated for 10 cephalosporins, and hazard quotients (HQs) and hazard indices (HIs) were calculated for six compounds as exploratory comparisons with available acceptable daily intake (ADI) benchmarks. Logistic regression models examined associations between cephalosporin detection and WHtR-defined central obesity, with BMI-defined obesity and WC-defined central obesity examined as alternative outcomes. Sensitivity analyses excluded participants with recent antibiotic use and extreme urinary concentrations, and separately those with chronic diseases. At least one target cephalosporin was detected in 383 participants (36.69%). WHtR-defined central obesity, BMI-defined obesity and WC-defined central obesity prevalences were 60.54%, 6.90% and 28.74%, respectively. In the restricted sample, cumulative EDI for the 10 included compounds was <0.01 μg/kg/day in 86.93% of participants, and cumulative HI for the six included compounds exceeded 1 in two participants (0.22%). In fully adjusted models, exposure to human-use cephalosporins (OR = 1.41, 95% CI: 1.07-1.86) and cumulative exposure to total cephalosporins (OR = 1.40, 95% CI: 1.06-1.84) were associated with WHtR-defined central obesity. The positive associations were generally consistent in sensitivity analyses. No corresponding associations were observed for BMI-defined obesity or WC-defined central obesity. Adults from rural communities were exposed to multiple cephalosporins, although overall exposure levels were low and screening indices for the six assessed compounds were below 1 for most participants in Zhejiang Province, China. Urinary exposure to cephalosporins was associated with higher odds of WHtR-defined central obesity.

items.title: High-Risk Mobility and Interruption in HIV Treatment Among Men in Malawi: Secondary Analysis of Two Randomized Controlled Trials.
items.abstract: Mobility is a key risk factor for interruption in HIV treatment (IIT). However, little is known about which aspects of mobility confer greatest risk (i.e., comprise high-risk mobility) and whether people prone to high-risk mobility can be identified prior to events. We conducted a secondary analysis of the IDEaL and ENGAGE trials (ClinicalTrials.gov #NCT04858243; #NCT05137210), which tested interventions to improve 6-month ART engagement among men living with HIV (MLHIV; ≥15 years old) not in care (i.e., ART naïve or missed refill by ≥ 28 days) in Malawi. We used baseline and endline (4-7 months post-enrollment) surveys and medical chart reviews of established ART clients experiencing IIT at enrollment who re-initiated ART during trials. We used Poisson regressions with random effects and receiver operator characteristic (ROC) curves to identify mobility characteristics most strongly associated with repeat IIT (≥ 28 days late for ART appointment during 6-month trial period) and to identify associated baseline characteristics. Of 1,119 men, 454 (41%) experienced repeat IIT; 314 (28%) took ≥ 3-night trips during the 6-month trial period. Trips ≥ 30 nights (aIRR 1.51, 95%CI 1.14-1.99, AUC 0.648) and lasting longer than expected (aIRR 1.50, 95%CI 1.15-1.96, AUC 0.653) best predicted repeat IIT (specificity 90%). No sociodemographic or pre-trial mobility variables were independently associated with high-risk mobility during the trial period. Mobility is a key risk factor for IIT among men in Malawi, and we found "high-risk mobility" to be trips ≥ 30 nights and/or that lasted longer than expected. We were unable to predict which men would experience high-risk mobility.

items.title: From the possible to the optimal: differentiable optimization of gene regulatory networks
items.abstract: Understanding the space of ``the actual and the possible'' regulatory architectures capable of realizing biological functions is one of the major challenges in biology. Optimization-based approaches can rationalize regulatory mechanisms from functional objectives and constraints, but their computational cost has limited them to finding individual solutions. Here, we introduce \texttt{jaxgrn}, a framework that combines differentiable programming with stochastic simulations of gene regulatory networks (GRNs) to optimize thousands of networks end-to-end on GPUs. Using morphogen-driven embryonic patterning as a case study, we optimize networks for domain formation and positional information, while varying constraints on input noise, boundary precision and scaling with system size. While recovering known archetypes for scaling, we find that varying the constraints organizes optimal solutions into qualitatively distinct regimes. When optimizing domain formation, we observe phenotypic convergence across a continuum of regulatory architectures, ranging from input-driven to feedback-driven networks. When optimizing positional information, solutions are initially phenotypically diverse despite moderate variation in regulatory architecture; imposing scaling drives both phenotypic and regulatory convergence of the optimized networks onto a few recurring regulatory architectures. Our systematic approach opens the door for variational systems biology in which changing functional constraints reshape the landscape of possible phenotypes and regulatory architectures.

items.title: Analysis choices can produce apparent rich-club differences: an Alzheimer's disease EEG case study
items.abstract: The weighted rich-club coefficient tests whether a network's most strongly connected nodes are preferentially interconnected. Its interpretation depends on two often-implicit choices that are easy to overlook: how the randomised comparison networks are constructed, and whether the hubs are re-identified in each comparison network or held fixed at those of the observed network. When hubs are defined by connection strength, these choices change what the coefficient actually tests. We examined how these choices affect inference using resting-state EEG from 20 people with Alzheimer's disease and 20 controls. Holding the data fixed, we compared four analysis pipelines, crossing two ways of building the comparison networks with the two hub choices, and ran a calibration study in which the same pipelines were applied to data constructed to contain no preferential hub coupling. An apparent eyes-open group difference in rich-club organisation appeared under only one of the four pipelines, the one combining a global weight reshuffle with re-identified hubs, and was absent under the other three. More tellingly, that same pipeline reported a group difference in 40% of cases where none was present, almost always higher in the Alzheimer's disease group, while the other three stayed near the expected 5%. This shows that the same data can support or dissolve an apparent rich-club difference depending on choices that are rarely reported. No single choice is universally correct, but reporting which were made, and why they fit the question being asked, is essential to interpreting the result.

items.title: Geometric tracking of a halo CME using full-circle wide-field views from PUNCH
items.abstract: We tracked the large, geoeffective halo coronal mass ejection (CME) of 2025-May-31 across the very wide field of view of the Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) mission, as a proof of concept for data-informed forecasting of CME arrival times at Earth. using simple point-and-click measurement of the front location as far as 47 degrees away from the Sun itself, we constrained an analytic "ludicrous ice-cream cone" geometric model with just three parameters: position angle, off-Earth-Sun angle, and propagation speed. We show that the model is sufficient to capture the bulk envelope of the CME, and also insufficient to capture the complexity of the CME's evolution. We generated simulated arrival-time forecasts for the CME by extrapolating the constant-velocity propagation to determine the time of impact with Earth. These "retro-forecasts" converged to within 30 +/- 15 minutes of the actual arrival time, 8 hours prior to arrival. The convergence was marked by a clear inflection point in the curve of predicted-arrival-time vs time-of-forecast. We conclude that continuous wide-field tracking is sufficiently powerful to enable even crude models to substantially improve arrival-time forecasting precision, and discuss future work required both to validate this single-event result and to extend it to more sophisticated analyses.

items.title: TOI-2665 b: A Highly Irradiated Giant in the Hot Neptune Desert
items.abstract: We report the confirmation of TOI-2665 b, a close-in sub-Saturn ($P=2.85$ days, $R_p=7.00_{-0.15}^{+0.16}~R_{\oplus}$) just inside the hot Neptune desert around a metal-rich G dwarf, observed by the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS). We make use of the Carnegie Planet Finder Spectrograph for precise radial velocity measurements to measure its mass with $13.5σ$ precision ($M_p= 57.0_{-4.2}^{+4.2} ~M_{\oplus}$). The low density of TOI-2665 b ($ρ_{p} \sim 0.9~\mathrm{gcm}^{-3}$) implies the existence of a significant gaseous envelope that has survived in the hot Neptune desert despite high irradiation ($S=1068~S_{\oplus}$), making it an intriguing target for understanding the formation and evolution of desert-dwelling giants. The relatively bright host star ($V=11.0$ mag, $J=9.8$ mag) and extensive atmosphere make TOI-2665 b a promising target for atmospheric characterization.

items.title: Contrasting tendencies in limb laterality relates to conspicuous coloration score in Dendrobatid poison frogs.
items.abstract: Predation is a major selective force shaping biological traits at multiple levels of organization, including laterality, the preferential use of one side of the body structures over the other. Poison frogs (Dendrobatoidea) provide an ideal system to investigate this relationship because they include species with contrasting antipredator strategies (crypsis, aposematism) and presumed predation risk. Because the right cerebral hemisphere is generally associated with rapid responses to threats (left-side body dominance), whereas the left hemisphere is linked to more analytical and goal-directed behaviors (right-side body dominance), we hypothesized that species with relatively high conspicuous coloration scores (proxy of visual warning signaling, one of the components of aposematism in dendrobatid frogs) would tend to be right-limb lateralized, whereas species with low coloration scores would tend to be left-limb lateralized. We conducted standardized laterality experiments in eleven dendrobatid species and examined the relationship between limb lateralization and species-level conspicuous coloration scores. Consistent with our prediction, species with higher coloration score exhibited a higher proportion of right-limb lateralized individuals in the forelimbs, whereas species with lower coloration score tended to show the opposite pattern. In contrast, no association was detected between coloration score and hindlimb lateralization. This discrepancy may reflect the distinct functional roles of the two limb pairs: in anurans, hindlimbs are highly specialized for locomotion and escape, whereas forelimbs participate in a broader range of behaviors associated with environmental assessment and decision making. Our findings provide the first comparative evidence that interspecific variation in a trait related to contrasting antipredator strategies may be associated with differences in forelimb lateralization among anuran species.

items.title: On the richness of metamaterials generated by recursive cell division
items.abstract: Scale-rich metamaterials are one member of a family of recursive cell divisions, which differ in which cell is cut, where the cut passes and at what angle. We characterise six members of this family through three network mappings, the cell tree, the dual graph of ligaments and junctions, and the frame graph of spans, and through their elastic-wave properties: the effective refractive index n, its isotropy and the band over which it holds. The dual-graph degree law, the mean degree and the age law of the ligaments hit by new ones are the same for every rule, so they cannot distinguish the materials. The cell tree and the cell shapes do differ, and one consequence of them explains the physics: the tail of long spans in the frame graph. With the longest spans as the length scale, the bending part of the inverse squared index follows a single power law across rules, densities and numbers of ligaments, and the same spans set the lowest local resonance and the band edge. The stretching part, which caps the index, is carried by the straight frame lines of the tiling rather than by the division. Random cut angles produce elongated cells and long spans, hence high index and a narrow band; cuts perpendicular to the long axis of the cell keep the cells compact, giving low index and a wide band. Cutting through the centroid instead of a random point bounds the split fraction between 4/9 and 5/9, which removes the area hierarchy without changing the index. The cut angle interpolates continuously between these limits, and the isotropy peaks where the ligament orientations become isotropic while the cells are still compact. In three dimensions the plate and strut divisions are stretching dominated and the index stays low for every rule.

items.title: Does a label survive the loop? A screen of necessary physical conditions for a self-measuring system, with a pre-registered test on fly connectomes
items.abstract: Theories that tie experience to a system that re-reads its own state rarely say what a physical substrate must supply for such a loop to run. We state necessary conditions as measurable bounds in one currency: the number of rounds, each one write, hold and re-read, that a written label survives.A floor follows from fundamental constants. Tier 1 asks whether a carrier can hold the label; it is the published quality-factor screen, restated in rounds and extended to a population code. Tier 2 bounds how many rounds a quantum resource survives in a loop that keeps a record. Tier 3 asks whether a network contains a compartment, a set of neurons that a random walk leaves more slowly than it mixes inside. Tier 4 compares what the loop and an outside observer can recover. We implement Tiers 3 and 4 on three connectomes of Drosophila. Exploration of two animals singled out the heading system of the ellipsoid body. Five criteria were then registered and run once on a third animal, and all were met with all connections counted. One was met narrowly, and two fail in that data set when connections of one or two synapses are removed, which we trace in part to synapse detection. As a population code the heading label holds about two bits for seven seconds. The screen can exclude substrates. Passing it is not evidence of experience.

items.title: Urban Ecology Compiler: An AI-Assisted Geospatial Framework for Compiling Natural-Language Planning Goals into Spatial Ecological Interventions
items.abstract: Urban ecological planning requires the integration of environmental information, spatial constraints, budget considerations, and competing sustainability objectives. However, translating high-level natural-language planning goals into geographically grounded and actionable ecological interventions remains a complex task. This paper presents the Urban Ecology Compiler, an AI-assisted geospatial decision-support framework that translates natural-language urban planning objectives into structured, spatially explicit ecological intervention plans. The framework combines large language model capabilities with geospatial data processing and environmental information to interpret planning objectives, evaluate spatial constraints, and generate intervention proposals within specified budget limits. It supports ecological planning objectives including flood resilience, urban greenery, heat reduction, and biodiversity enhancement. The system integrates geospatial technologies and data sources including OpenStreetMap, Copernicus Sentinel, Open-Meteo, and OpenElevation. Proposed interventions include green corridors, rain gardens, bioswales, permeable pavements, and other nature-based solutions. Spatial outputs are represented using GeoJSON and visualised through an interactive geospatial interface. The paper documents the system architecture, methodology, implementation, and experimental evaluation. An internal benchmark involving 200 compilations reports 94.2% valid GeoJSON generation. These results represent internal experimental evaluations and should not be interpreted as independent real-world validation. The framework is intended as a prototype for AI-assisted urban ecological planning and decision support. Its outputs are designed to support preliminary planning and exploration rather than replace expert assessment or field-based environmental validation. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Geospatial Decision Support, Urban Ecology, Large Language Models, GeoAI, Nature-Based Solutions, Sustainable Urban Planning, Environmental Planning, Spatial Optimisation, Climate Resilience.

items.title: NBD-F derivatization and rapid separation of catecholamines and their O-methylated metabolites using flow-gated micellar electrokinetic chromatography.
items.abstract: Catecholamines function as neurotransmitters and hormones in the brain and the sympathetic nervous system. Measurements of these compounds are important in neuroscience research, clinical diagnosis, and drug development. Their O-methylated metabolites, particularly metanephrine and normetanephrine, are established biomarkers used in the biochemical evaluation of pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas. The objective of this study was to evaluate 4-fluoro-7-nitro-2,1,3-benzoxadiazole (NBD-F) as the fluorogenic agent for the rapid separation and sensitive detection of these compounds using flow-gated capillary electrophoresis (CE). Experimental results showed that NBD-F in excess of the analytes readily reacted with amino and phenolic hydroxyl groups of catecholamines, resulting in fully NBD-substituted, tri-NBD derivatives. Similarly, the O-methylated metabolites of catecholamines were also fully NBD-substituted, forming di-NBD derivatives. These derivatives were separated with micellar electrokinetic chromatography (MEKC) within 80 s. Sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) in the sample solution might facilitate the derivatization of catecholamines, whereas SDS in the separation buffer enhanced fluorescence intensity of the derivatives. The limits of detection (LODs) were estimated to be 1.7 nM for dopamine and 1.3 nM for norepinephrine, representing an approximately 80-fold improvement over previously reported LODs obtained using the MEKC/NBD-Cl method. The method was further applied to the analysis of urine and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples to demonstrate its applicability. These results demonstrate the potential of the NBD-F/MEKC approach as a sensitive and rapid analytical method for catecholamines and their metabolites and as a useful biochemical tool for neuroscience research.

items.title: Sex, but not age, drives transcriptome-wide gene expression variation in a turtle with female-biased longevity.
items.abstract: Sexes frequently differ in life-history traits including body size, lifespan, and age at sexual maturity. Organismal aging, the progressive decline in physiological function and cellular resilience over time, is a central component of sex-specific life histories, yet the mechanisms driving sex differences in aging remain largely unresolved. Long-term mark-recapture efforts reveal a striking pattern of female-biased longevity in painted turtles (Chrysemys picta) (lifespan: males = 24 years, females = 48 years). This species exhibits temperature-dependent sex determination, and thus, provides a compelling system to test for the molecular underpinnings of sex-specific aging in the absence of sex chromosomes. Here, we assess how sex, age, and their interaction affect gene expression in the blood transcriptomes of wild adult painted turtles (N = 93) spanning the entire lifespan. We identified widespread gene expression differences between females and males (2,347 genes; 13.4% of all filtered genes). In contrast, only six genes showed significant linear relationships with age in both sexes. We also employed a machine-learning approach that identified distinct genes in each sex for which expression was predictive of age. Age-related gene expression patterns highlight both conserved molecular pathways with known roles in organismal aging (e.g., insulin/insulin-like signaling and target of rapamycin) as well as novel gene targets. These findings suggest sex-specific molecular processes may contribute to observed sex differences in demographic aging in this species. More broadly, this work underscores the need for future studies disentangling the environmental and developmental contributions to sex-specific survival trajectories in species with diverse sex determination systems.

items.title: A specialized microbiome enriched in nitrification and halogen cycling potential resolved from multi-omics investigation of a Caribbean suboxic and acidic marine sinkhole.
items.abstract: The Luymes Sinkholes, located on the Luymes Bank northwest of Saba, represent a unique marine environment characterized by distinct biogeochemical gradients. Most noticeable is an acidic (pH ≈ 6.25) and suboxic (O2 < 60 µmol/kg) submerged 'lake' at ~ 220 m depth exhibiting extreme deviations from standard oceanographic patterns, including elevated inorganic carbon, nitrate, and phosphate, and a lower temperature (20.3 ºC vs 26.4 ºC). To determine how the microbiome within the submerged acid lake adapted to these unique conditions, we collected 59 coupled samples of size-filtered (0.22 µm) planktonic microbes for shotgun metagenomics and solid-phase extracted dissolved organic matter for untargeted metabolomics from 21 stations at depths ranging from 2 to 600 m during a 10-day research cruise in December 2019. We identified a distinct microbial community within the submerged acid lake different from the non-acidic sinkholes, with increased abundances of Nitrospinota, Thermoproteota, Planctomycetota, and Actinobacteriota. We also found three enriched classes of dissolved compounds within the submerged acid lake: (1) large, (2) low-polarity, and (3) halogenated metabolites, including iodides and halobenzoic acids. Correlations between microbial taxa and metabolite classes show potential links between nitrifying archaea and halogenated compound cycling. We further supported these findings using the functional annotation of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) and protein clusters showing enrichment of nitrification and halogen cycling genes, suggesting the presence of specialized degradation and biosynthetic pathways, directly connecting microbial metabolism to the observed geochemical conditions. These findings demonstrate that the submerged acid lake contains specific microbially driven biogeochemical processes under acidified and low-oxygen conditions, providing a natural model for future extreme ocean acidification scenarios. With this multi‑omics approach, we were able to connect the microbial metabolism with this unique environment, thereby expanding our understanding of how both are interconnected. Video Abstract.

items.title: Ecological succession in Glomeromycota: How to know a hawk from a handsaw.
items.abstract: Arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungal communities in the roots of terrestrial plants present strong seasonal changes over the growing season, but the drivers and ecological consequences of those temporal dynamics remain poorly understood. We present and review here three competing, but not mutually exclusive, hypotheses about AM fungal seasonality. Each of them assumes a different controlling factor, namely plant host, intrinsic AM fungal dynamics, and climate, but they can all potentially explain seasonal trajectories, while simultaneously contributing invaluable insights on the functioning of arbuscular mycorrhizal systems. We synthesize evidence in support of and against each of these three hypotheses. We then summarize insights that could be gained from testing these hypotheses and propose experimental designs to disentangle their relative contributions to belowground seasonality. We therefore contribute a testable framework for designing multi-time-point metabarcoding studies to disentangle drivers of belowground seasonality.

items.title: Hemodynamic spectral signatures across vigilance states: a whole-night EEG/fNIRS investigation.
items.abstract: Sleep is accompanied by coordinated changes in neuronal activity and cerebral hemodynamics. However, cortical hemodynamic signatures across sleep stages remain poorly characterized, partly because most human electroencephalography (EEG)/functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies are limited in duration, rarely capture deep or Rapid-Eye-Movement (REM) sleep, have low sampling rate, or rely on a sleep-deprivation paradigm, which limits the generalizability of findings. Here, we combined whole-night polysomnography, EEG and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) in healthy young adults, as a bedside technology to monitor cortical hemodynamic fluctuations. We recorded fNIRS using an optimal, personalized, locally dense bilateral frontoparietal montage, alongside peripheral physiology recordings (respiration, photoplethysmography, mean arterial pressure). We computed oscillatory components of oxy- and deoxyhemoglobin (HbO-HbR) spectra across sleep stages using wavelet-based time-frequency analysis. Additionally, we analyzed within the same regions an independent sleep EEG-fMRI dataset (no REM recorded). Our results are suggesting that across frontal and parietal regions, slow-frequency (0.002-0.1Hz) power increased during N1 sleep in HbO and then progressively attenuated across N2 and N3 sleep, in HbO, HbR, and fMRI. REM showed a re-emergence of very-low-frequency power (<0.01Hz) in HbO and HbR. Higher-frequency oscillations (0.15-0.5Hz; overlapping respiratory-band) were selectively enhanced during NREM sleep (largest increase during N3) and returned toward wake-like levels during REM in frontal regions, with regional differences. Peripheral signals captured systemic physiology oscillations but did not reproduce the cortical stage-specific patterns. Together, our findings provide a cortical characterization of sleep-stage hemodynamic organizations that can serve as a reference for future mechanistic and clinical sleep studies.

items.title: From physical symmetry to aesthetic value: investigating symmetry-induced attractiveness enhancement with fMRI.
items.abstract: Facial symmetry contributes to perceived attractiveness, but how physical symmetry is linked to subjective aesthetic evaluation in the brain remains unclear. In this study, we used fMRI to examine BOLD responses to identity-matched symmetrical and asymmetrical faces while participants rated either facial attractiveness or facial symmetry. Behaviorally, symmetrical faces were rated as both more symmetrical and more attractive than asymmetrical faces, although the attractiveness enhancement varied across facial identities. To link the physical symmetry manipulation to subjective evaluation, we modeled two complementary measures: trial-by-trial raw ratings and identity-matched changes in ratings induced by the symmetry manipulation. The categorical contrast between symmetrical and asymmetrical faces identified left superior temporal/supramarginal activity during attractiveness evaluation, but this pattern was not confirmed by the direct task comparison. items.title: Climate Change Adaptaion Strategies And Biodiversity Conservation In Himachal Pradesh
items.abstract: Himachal Pradesh stands at a critical juncture where rapid development and climate pressures threaten its rich biodiversity. The state, positioned as a front-runner in India’s ecological policy experiments, has pursued innovative green energy agendas, community-driven conservation, and ambitious habitat protection measures. Despite this, however, a number of persistent issues such as habitat fragmentation, unregulated tourism, human-wildlife conflict, and disruptions brought about by climatic changes keep destabilizing the area’s fragile ecosystems. This paper examines some of the recent trends within environmental law, state policy measures, and civil society activism, their implications for conservation and sustainability. Much emphasis will be laid on emerging conservation measures such as the Green Energy State program, decentralization of renewable energy through solar panchayats, and resilience against climate change in forestry management. Through the assessment of these current challenges and emerging conservation measures, the importance of an integrated and multidisciplinary approach will become evident.

items.title: How to survive as mountain dwellers: palaeopathological study of European leopards
items.abstract: Abstract Previous morphofunctional analyses linked Pleistocene leopards from the eastern Pyrenees to rocky mountainous habitats, within a broader interpretation of European leopard ecology. Such environments are expected to increase exposure to falls, missteps and difficult landings during locomotion and prey capture. Here we develop the palaeopathological dimension of this interpretation by examining two pathological leopard ( Panthera pardus ) forelimb elements from Late Pleistocene European cave assemblages: a radius from Grotte de la Carrière, France, and a fifth metacarpal from Tut de Fustanyà, Iberia. External morphology and computed-tomography images reveal pronounced diaphyseal enlargement, irregular periosteal bone formation, cortical reorganization and persistent deformation, most consistent with remodeled fractures. Substantial reparative bone documents survival beyond the acute injury and through an extended phase of osseous repair. Comparisons with pathological leopards, lynxes, cave lions and saber-toothed felids support the diagnostic assessment and place these injuries within a broader record of skeletal trauma. We propose that the fractures reflect the mechanical risks of locomotion and hunting in steep, rocky terrain. The pathological evidence adds an individual life-history dimension to the postcranial adaptations previously recognized in European leopards. Integrating the lesions with the morphological and environmental evidence, we interpret them as potential traumatic consequences of the mountain-associated way of life proposed for European Pleistocene leopards. Their extensive repair also documents the capacity of injured individuals to survive within this demanding ecological setting.

items.title: The Forecasting Proficiency Test: A General Use Assessment of Forecasting Ability
items.abstract: Accurate predictions about the future are crucial for optimizing policy choices, but finding skilled forecasters is challenging. Prior work relied on forecasting tournaments to identify generalist "superforecasters" who made accurate predictions across domains, but these tournaments take months to complete and require large concurrent samples to compare performance among individuals. We solve these problems by developing a one-hour Forecasting Proficiency Test (FPT) that explains 75% of the variance in forecasters' accuracy about a wide variety of events. The FPT provides standardized percentile scores normed to a large (N=1,147) test development sample based on a combination of reusable real-world forecasting questions and standalone cognitive tests. Which questions and tests are included is highly customizable. Forecasting questions are the best predictors of forecasting proficiency, but cognitive tests help stabilize score distributions and facilitate score exchangeability across different custom test versions even as forecasting questions and resolution dates change. The FPT is primarily a practical tool for decision-makers who rely on accurate predictions to make decisions. However, it is based on one of the largest dedicated psychometric studies ever conducted on human forecasting, which also provides insight into the cognitive mechanisms that drive forecasting proficiency and guidance for future researchers interested in studying the psychology of forecasting.

items.title: Measuring Cognitive Demands in Professional Esports
items.abstract: Practice may improve certain cognitive skills more than others because those skills are called upon more frequently during an activity. Professional esports provides a means of measuring these demands during gameplay because match records capture the information available to players and their responses as events unfold. This study introduces the Telemetry and Replay Analysis of Cognitive Exposure (TRACE) framework, which measures seven dimensions of cognitive demand in professional esports. The analysis used records from 314 professional DOTA 2 matches, covering 558 distinct player accounts and approximately 2,184 player-hours of competition. TRACE defines four measures at the player level (cognitive control capacity, task switching, inhibitory control, and dynamic attention) and three measures at the team level (visuospatial working memory and updating, decision-making under uncertainty, and feedback learning). Hierarchical Bayesian models estimated each dimension in its original units and on a common percentile scale, accounting for differences among teams, matches, and hero-role combinations. By identifying comparable situations across matches, TRACE can quantify how often players encounter a given demand and how they respond when it arises. This transforms routinely recorded match replays into a source of large-scale behavioral data for cognitive psychology.

items.title: Introducing the One-Shot Download Task: Testing the validity of a new and simple measure of online pro-environmental behavior
items.abstract: AbstractMeasures of actual pro-environmental behaviour are increasingly in environmental psychology due to their increased ecological validity over self-report measures. Here we introduce a new such measure, the One-Shot Download Task (OSD), a brief online behavioural measure in which participants choose between incurring personal costs (completing a tedious task) or environmental costs (downloading unnecessary files associated with carbon emissions). Two studies were conducted (Study 1: N = 104; Study 2: N = 96) that assessed the OSD’s criterion validity by examining associations with measures of eco-anxiety, environmentally minded consumer behaviour and environmental attitudes, while Study 2 also tested whether social influence in the form of exposure to “watching eyes” stimuli increased pro-environmental choices in the task. It was found that OSD scores positively correlated with environmentally minded consumer behaviour and the Preservation dimension of environmental attitudes, but not with eco-anxiety or Utilization attitudes. Furthermore, participants exposed to watching eyes selected significantly more environmentally friendly options (higher scores on the OSD). These findings provide initial evidence for the validity of the OSD as a measure of actual pro-environmental behaviour, demonstrating expected relationships with established environmental constructs and sensitivity to social influence. Given its simplicity, low cost, and accessibility, the OSD offers a practical addition to the growing range of behavioural measures available to environmental psychological researchers, although further validation is warranted.

items.title: Perceived treatability is not evidence of diagnostic validity and benefit: A response to Hastings and Hahn on borderline personality disorder
items.abstract: Hastings and Hahn report that a borderline personality disorder (BPD) label can improve selected treatment beliefs among clinical psychology trainees. However, more favourable clinician expectations should not be interpreted as evidence that receiving the diagnosis benefits patients. Perceived treatability, treatment efficacy, treatment safety, and patient benefit are distinct constructs. This distinction is particularly important given documented negative effects associated with dialectical behaviour therapy and broader limitations in the systematic assessment and reporting of treatment-related harm in psychotherapy research. Hastings and Hahn's vignette design also presupposes rather than evaluates the legitimacy of the BPD construct and cannot address diagnostic bias, harms arising from classification, or the lived consequences of diagnosis and subsequent care. Their findings therefore demonstrate a change in selected clinician beliefs, not improved care or net patient benefit. Claims of diagnostic benefit require evidence addressing treatment safety, patient-defined outcomes, diagnostic validity and bias, and lived experience.

items.title: TO MONETIZE OR NOT: INFLUENCE OF INDIVIDUAL DIFFERENCES AND GENDER IN MONETARY VALUATION OF MEANINGFUL EXPERIENCES
items.abstract: Money is a universal measure of value that influences most decisions. For centuries, humans have used it to exchange goods and experiences. Research in psychology and behavioral economics, however, shows that there may be limits to what individuals are willing to exchange for money. This study examined the monetary values people assign to personal experiences, and whether willingness to engage in monetary valuation differs between males and females. Five hundred and twenty-nine participants completed an online survey in which they provided the minimum amount of monetary compensation it would require to complete ten separate hypothetical scenarios, with the option to refuse any task. The hypothetical tasks ranged from temporary restrictions and social isolation to public disclosure, loss of memories and permanent identity changes. Based on the results from previous economic decision-making studies, we hypothesized that females would refuse to price tasks more than males and that males would request higher compensation for priced tasks. We also hypothesized that permanent or identity-altering tasks would result in higher refusal rates than temporary ones in both genders. Whether resistance to monetary valuation is a consistent individual tendency was also examined. Our results showed that participants who refused to price one hypothetical task were more likely to refuse other tasks. While no gender differences were observed for any task regarding the monetary value requested, females refused significantly more tasks than males (4.43 vs. 3.17, p < .001). Refusal rates were highest for permanent or identity-altering tasks and lowest for temporary tasks. Lastly, refusal rates for loss of digital pictures/videos were nearly identical to losing contact with friends and family. Together, these findings suggest that monetary valuation involves two separate decisions: whether or not to assign a monetary value and, if so, how much to request. Individuals differ consistently in their willingness to engage in monetary valuation, and gender influences the decision to engage rather than with the amount requested.

items.title: Spontaneous emergence of action decisions and slow ramping in a deep brain-constrained model of frontotemporal areas
items.abstract: Abstract Humans are capable of voluntarily initiating actions that are spontaneous—not triggered by any sensory event in the immediate context. In such cases, how does the brain make a decision that the time to act has come? To investigate this question, we used a 6-area brain-constrained neural-network model to account for the neurophysiological and anatomical features of relevant areas of the cortex. To replicate the experimental settings under which volitional non stimulus-triggered button-presses are performed, we analysed the network activity in the absence of any “sensory” input: we observed spontaneous ignitions of previously-learned “perception–action” circuits (linking “visual” information to corresponding “hand/finger movement”) caused by the accumulation of noise within them, which we took as model correlates of self-generated decisions to act. The time to first spontaneous circuit ignition was then used to build a simulated waiting-time histogram. We found that, for select values of the parameters, the network autonomously “decided” to act (or to wait) in a way that accurately reflected participant behaviour under such conditions. Additionally, we found that when the model’s macroscopic behaviour matched that of participants, its microscopic activity prior to a spontaneous ignition event also reproduced the pre-movement slow ramping neural signal (the readiness potential, or RP) experimentally recorded using electroencephalography. Reproducing both behavioural and brain indices of spontaneous voluntary movements, the present brain-constrained architecture offers a neuro-mechanistic explanation of the emergence of endogenous action decisions in the human brain in the form of memory traces’ spontaneous ignitions. Our results also speak to the ongoing debate over the interpretation of the RP, suggesting that, rather than reflecting motor preparation (a decision outcome), the emerging RP is pre-decisional, with overt movement being the result of a distributed perception–action circuit spontaneous ignition.

items.title: A multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset with repeated experience sampling
items.abstract: The integration of electroencephalography (EEG) and functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) can be used to characterize temporal and spatial components of neural activity during unfolding mental experience. Here we introduce a multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset with measures of continuous behavior and spontaneous mental experience. Data components, organized in Brain Imaging Dataset Structure (BIDS) format, include fMRI, EEG with carbon wire loop sensors for artifact removal, continuous performance task responses, experience sampling ratings, and mental health surveys, from 24 healthy adults. Tasks included the gradual-onset continuous performance task and resting state with intermittent experience sampling of 13 unique thought dimensions (36 repetitions, including 468 total ratings, per participant). The same protocol was completed on two different days, yielding approximately 1.33 hours of simultaneous EEG-fMRI data per individual. The dataset may be used to explore the behavioral and experiential relevance of brain activity during the wakeful resting state. The dataset also provides a means to study the reliability of relationships between fMRI and EEG features across sessions within individuals.

items.title: Cognitive networks reconstruct mindsets about STEM subjects and educational contexts in high-schoolers, undergraduates, experts and their digital twins
items.abstract: Attitudes toward STEM develop from the interaction of conceptual knowledge, educational experiences, and affect. Here we use cognitive network science to reconstruct group mindsets as behavioural forma mentis networks (BFMNs). In this case, nodes are cue words and free associations, edges are empirical associative links, and each concept is annotated with perceived valence. We analyse BFMNs from $$N=981$$ observations spanning high school students, university students, and early-career STEM experts, alongside LLM (GPT-OSS) “digital twins” (group-level synthetic counterparts, not individual-level copies), prompted to emulate comparable profiles. Focusing also on semantic neighbourhoods (“frames”) around key target concepts (e.g., STEM subjects or educational actors/places), we quantify frames in terms of valence auras, emotional profiles, network overlap (Jaccard similarity), and concreteness relative to null baselines. Across student groups, science and research are consistently framed positively, while their core quantitative subjects (mathematics and statistics) exhibit more negative and anxiety-related auras, amplified in higher math-anxiety subgroups, evidencing a STEM-science cognitive and emotional dissonance. High-anxiety frames are also less concrete than chance, suggesting more abstract and decontextualised representations of threatening quantitative domains. Human networks show greater overlap between mathematics and anxiety than GPT-OSS. The results highlight how BFMNs capture cognitive-affective signatures of mindsets towards the target domains and indicate that these synthetic counterparts approximate cultural attitudes but miss key context-sensitive, experience-based components of human educational anxiety.

items.title: Development of a Digital Violence Prevention E-Module to Strengthen Harmonious Social Interaction among Elementary School Students
items.abstract: Abstract Violence in elementary schools in Indonesia is still a serious problem that hinders student development. This research aims to develop an E-Mode of Violence Prevention Education designed to strengthen the harmonization of harmonious life in the elementary school environment. This study uses a 4D development model which includes the Define, Design, Develop and Disseminate stages which involve the validation of experts, teachers and students in four elementary schools in Gorontalo Regency. The results of expert validation show that the E-Module meets the criteria of "very valid" with an average score above 85%. The limited trial showed that more than 85% of students rated the E-Module as practical, easy to use, and attractive. Data analysis through the Kolmogorov–Smirnov normality test showed that the pretest and posttest data were normally distributed (Sig.>0.05). The results of the paired samples t-test showed significant differences in students' knowledge, attitudes, and skills before and after the use of the E-Module (p = 0.001). The effect size calculation (Cohen's d) ranged from 1.34–1.86 with a very large category, which confirms the strong influence of the E-Module in improving the competence of violence prevention. Thus, this E-Module is valid, practical, and effective, and is able to be widely implemented as part of creating harmonious harmony of life in the elementary school environment.
