items.title: Power-law age-dependence supports phenotype-specific multistep architecture in MND.
items.abstract: Objective To determine whether age-specific motor neuron disease (MND) incidence is better described by power-law age-dependence, compatible with multistep architecture, or by an exponential model. Methods We analyzed curated Australian Motor Neuron Disease Registry data using age at symptom onset, clinical phenotype and Australian population denominators. The primary analysis modeled age-specific incidence across the 30-75-year range using 5-year age bands. Power-law and exponential Poisson models were compared using differences in Akaike Information Criterion (ΔAIC), with supplementary analyses across an expanded 20-90-year range and a restricted younger age range ( Results Across 2,556 patients in the primary analysis, the power-law model provided superior fit to the exponential model in the total cohort, with a ΔAIC of 60.06. The estimated power-law slope was 3.75, corresponding to 4.75 apparent steps. Power-law superiority was observed across clinical phenotypes, with the highest apparent step estimates in bulbar-onset ALS and flail arm syndrome, and the lowest in cervical-onset ALS and primary lateral sclerosis. Sensitivity analyses across expanded and restricted age ranges supported the primary findings. Conclusion In the Australian MND Registry cohort, power-law age-dependence provided a better fit to observed age-specific incidence than the exponential alternative. These findings are compatible with a multistep model of MND pathogenesis but do not establish a fixed sequence of discrete pathogenic events.

items.title: Delayed Delivery of Intranasal Insulin Partially Improves Recovery after Moderate Brain Injury in a Rat Model.
items.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) results in an acute period of increased glucose demand followed by sustained hypometabolism in the brain, associated with cognitive and physical deficits for which there are currently no treatments. We previously showed that administration of intranasal insulin (INI) within 4 h of a moderate TBI injury in rats using the controlled cortical impact (CCI) model significantly increased hippocampal glucose uptake and improved cognitive function. However, the therapeutic window for INI is currently unclear, so this study aimed to evaluate the effect of delaying treatment from 24 h to 28 days post-injury. Male adult Sprague Dawley rats were exposed to a moderate CCI injury followed by INI or saline treatment beginning 24 h, 14 days, or 28 days post-injury and continuing with daily administration for 14 days. We now show that initiation of INI at 24 h after CCI injury led to significant increases in 18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography measurements in the cortex and hippocampus at 2 and 10 days after initiation of treatment. Novel object recognition tests also showed that 24-h delayed INI administration significantly improved memory function at 2 days. However, unlike the more acute treatment, injured animals treated with INI at a delayed time demonstrated no significant difference in cognitive performance on the Morris water maze or motor function in the beam walk task. These data suggest that acute INI administration is optimal for improving outcome after moderate TBI, but delaying treatment to 24 h may still offer some benefit.

items.title: Etiology and geographic variation in acute symptomatic seizure management: An international vignette-based survey.
items.abstract: Objective Acute symptomatic seizures (ASyS) account for nearly half of new onset seizures, but evidence guiding management remains limited. We aimed to characterize international variation in ASyS management across common etiologies. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional, vignette-based survey through the International League Against Epilepsy national chapters (February to May 2025). Five etiology-based vignettes assessed clinical and electrographic ASyS scenario after ischemic stroke, traumatic brain injury (TBI), meningitis, hyponatremia, and alcohol withdrawal. Respondents who managed neonatal seizures completed a neonatal stroke vignette. We assessed antiseizure medication (ASM) initiation, duration after clinical ASyS, and continuous electroencephalography (cEEG) use. Interrespondent variability was quantified by normalized Shannon entropy (H'). Multivariable generalized estimating equations accounted for repeated responses. Results Among 963 respondents (92 countries), 62% recommended ASM initiation in clinical and 61% in electrographic ASyS scenarios. Overall ASM initiation variability was high (H' = .96), highest for alcohol withdrawal (H' = 1.0), followed by stroke (H' > .9), and consistently higher for electrographic than clinical ASyS. Etiology was the strongest driver of ASM initiation. Compared with stroke, ASM initiation odds were higher for TBI (odds ratio [OR] = 2.5, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 2.2-2.8) and meningitis (OR = 1.9, 95% CI = 1.7-2.2), and lower for hyponatremia (OR = .2, 95% CI = .2-.2) and alcohol withdrawal (OR = .5, 95% CI = .5-.6). Compared with Europe, initiation odds were higher in North America (OR = 2.7, 95% CI = 2.0-3.6), Asia-Oceania (OR = 2.4, 95% CI = 2.0-3.0), and Latin America (OR = 2.0, 95% CI = 1.5-2.7), but not Africa. These differences persisted after accounting for country income. Compared with stroke, the mean ASM duration was 3.2 months shorter for hyponatremia and .6 months longer for TBI. Alcohol withdrawal durations were polarized (41% discontinued at discharge; 20% continued >12 months). cEEG use was markedly higher in North America than Europe (OR = 11.3, 95% CI = 7.8-16.5). Among 291 neonatal respondents, 75% continued ASM beyond discharge. Significance ASyS management varies markedly, reaching near-maximal heterogeneity in several common scenarios. Although etiology drives decisions, geography and provider characteristics also influence care, underscoring an urgent need for randomized trials and international consensus guidance to harmonize care.

items.title: Ketogenic diet therapy in adolescents and adults with epilepsy: A scoping review of cognitive outcomes.
items.abstract: Objective The ketogenic diet treatment (KDT) is an established non-pharmacological treatment for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). However, rigorous research for seizure efficacy based on randomized controlled studies in adolescents and adults remains limited, and cognitive outcomes are rarely assessed using standardized measures. Methods This scoping review has mapped evidence on cognitive outcomes of KDT in adolescents and adults with epilepsy. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, PubMed and Embase were searched for studies published between 1986 and 2026. Eligibility for this review required inclusion of adolescents or adults with epilepsy receiving KDT and reporting cognitive outcomes. Results Of 951 records, 19 studies were included. Overall, KDT was associated with favorable seizure and cognitive outcomes, although reports of cognitive outcomes were generally subjective. Significance Rigorous research designs were scarce, and evidence remains limited; future studies should use stronger designs, larger samples, standardized cognitive assessments, and longer follow-up periods. Plain language summary Research shows that people with epilepsy often experience difficulties with the brain's ability to process information. While dietary treatments have been shown to be effective for seizure control, less is known about their effects on cognition. We reviewed published research examining cognitive outcomes in adolescents and adults with epilepsy following dietary treatment. Most studies suggested that these diets had a positive effect on aspects of cognitive functioning. However, the available evidence remains limited. More studies with better designs using well-established cognitive assessments are needed to better understand these effects.

items.title: Scalp high-frequency oscillations differentiate neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy with and without electroencephalographically confirmed seizures.
items.abstract: Objective Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) is a leading cause of neonatal seizures, but seizure detection is challenging when continuous electroencephalography (EEG) is unavailable and neonates undergo only a single routine EEG. Biomarkers derived from routine EEG may aid identification of neonates with seizures. We investigated whether scalp high-frequency oscillation (HFO) rates derived from the first eligible routine EEG (1) differentiate neonates with HIE with and without seizures; and (2) contribute to seizure classification alongside established clinical, neurophysiological, and imaging biomarkers. Methods We retrospectively analyzed routine scalp EEG recordings from 33 term neonates with HIE (17 with seizures, 16 without), obtained at a mean postnatal age of 4 ± 3 days. The mean analyzed EEG duration was 38 ± 14 min in neonates with seizures and 36 ± 20 min in those without. HFO rates in sleep segments were quantified using a validated automated detector. Results Scalp HFO rates were significantly higher in neonates with seizures than in those without (.12 ± .11 vs. .03 ± .02 HFOs/min/channel, adjusted p = .02). An HFO rate threshold of .07 HFOs/min/channel optimally discriminated neonates who had seizures from those who did not (area under the curve [AUC] = .81). HFO rates did not differ significantly according to HIE severity, therapeutic hypothermia, antiseizure medication response, EEG background activity, or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) abnormalities. Multivariable models incorporating HFO rate, EEG background activity, and MRI findings showed discrimination (AUC = .92, 95% confidence interval [CI] = .69-1.00 for logistic regression; AUC = 1.00, 95% CI = .75-1.00 for random forest), with HFO rate as the strongest contributor to seizure classification. Significance These findings support scalp HFO rate as a potential electrophysiological biomarker of seizure occurrence in neonatal HIE, complementary to EEG background assessment and MRI findings. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether HFOs can predict subsequent seizures.

items.title: Strengths and weaknesses in epilepsy training across residency programs in Italy: A multicenter survey by the Italian chapter of the Young Epilepsy Section (YES-I).
items.abstract: The objective of the study was to assess epilepsy-related services across Italian neurology and child neuropsychiatry residency programs, evaluate residents and early-career specialists' perceived strengths/weaknesses in epilepsy training, and identify unmet needs and expectations for improving residency programs and Young Epilepsy Section (YES)-Italy educational initiatives. A nationwide cross-sectional survey was conducted between January and April 2026 by a focus group of the YES-Italy Education Task Force. A structured questionnaire was distributed to neurology and child neuropsychiatry residents and specialists within 2 years of completing residency, assessing demographics, epilepsy-related services, self-perceived competencies, training strengths and limitations, and suggestions for improving residency curricula with YES-Italy educational activities. Descriptive statistics were used; group comparisons (neurology vs. child neuropsychiatry; residents vs. early-career specialists) employed the Mann-Whitney U test. The survey was completed by 150 participants. Epilepsy training was widely available (85.3%) but variable and often brief (<6 months). EEG training was mostly embedded within epilepsy rotation (32.7%), organized as a distinct brief rotation (<3 months; 33.3%), or not available (19.3%). Core epilepsy services were widely present (inpatient wards 82.7%; neurophysiology laboratories 93.3%), while other services were less common (such as epilepsy surgery). Marked variability in Status Epilepticus management emerged across centers. Participants perceived adequate competence for core clinical-diagnostic domains, but lower competence for EEG interpretation and complementary disciplines. Perceived competence was higher in chronic than in acute care. Child neuropsychiatrists reported greater competence in neuropsychology and genetics, neurologists in neuroimaging and acute management. Clinical rotations and multidisciplinary case discussions were major strengths, whereas lectures and direct teaching required improvement. Suggestions for the YES-I group highlighted improving EEG training, structured educational initiatives, access to courses, webinars, and scientific materials. This survey highlights substantial heterogeneity and weaknesses in Italian epilepsy training, particularly regarding EEG interpretation, complementary diagnostics, and acute management, underscoring the need for national standardization, multidisciplinary educational pathways, and strengthened educational initiatives.

items.title: Human foetal cortical slice cultures: A translational platform for studying early neurodevelopment.
items.abstract: The developing human neocortex is characterised by complex and dynamic changes in cellular architecture, neuronal organisation and activity. We previously described how human foetal cortical organotypic slice cultures, prepared from ethically sourced tissue could be used to investigate these processes. Cultures can be maintained for weeks, exhibiting features of the normal developing brain that are not replicated in current organoid models. Such cultures allow the possibility for experimental manipulation, for instance testing the effects of genetic mutations. Here we extend the characterisation of our model. We report that these organotypic cultures preserve the laminar organisation of the developing cortical wall and show considerable diversity of neuronal morphology. Employing bulk mRNA hybridisation for 794 genes (a "human neuropathology" gene panel), we identified consistent patterns of evolving gene expression between 0 and 14 days in vitro (DIV) across different tissue samples taken at 16-18 post-conceptional weeks (pcw). To put this in the context of the normal developmental pattern, we compared our data set with previously acquired tissue RNAseq data collected between 7-17 pcw (https://www.hdbr.org/expression). This indicated that many gene expression changes in vitro followed prior developmental trajectories, but others diverged strongly, including upregulated genes associated with responses to stress, and downregulated genes associated with the vascular function. This latter effect may reflect the redundancy of vascular development in culture. Notably, various genes associated with pre- and post- synaptic function, including both glutamate and GABA receptors, continued to be expressed strongly. Consistent with this, we observed spontaneous neuronal network activity in the subplate (SP) using targeted expression of the genetically encoded Ca 2+ indicator, GCaMPf6, to post-mitotic neurons. The frequency of neuronal Ca 2+ transients increased when blockers of either GABA A receptors or gap junctions were applied. Conversely, activity was significantly reduced by glutamatergic receptor antagonists and abolished by voltage gated sodium channel blockade. Neuronal Ca 2+ transients were triggered directly by focal application of glutamate in the SP and subventricular zone, whereas cortical plate neurons exhibited weaker responses. This was consistent with levels of immunoreactivity for glutamate receptor sub-units in these compartments. In conclusion, the organotypic cultures show functional synaptic networks, supported by continued expression of the relevant synaptic protein machinery. These data provide further validation of organotypic cultures as a model for investigating and manipulating the early prenatal development of human neocortex, a period that is otherwise difficult to study.

items.title: FlyAnatoView: Visualization of Drosophila Single-cell RNA-seq Datasets on Anatomographs.
items.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is a powerful approach for characterizing gene expression at single-cell resolution and identifying distinct cell populations within complex tissues. However, tissue dissociation disrupts the spatial relationships among cells, making it difficult to determine their original anatomical locations and interpret gene expression patterns in the context of tissue organization. To address this limitation, we developed FlyAnatoView (https://www.flyrnai.org/tools/rna_seq_base/web/svg_files/), a resource that projects scRNA-seq data onto anatomical diagrams of Drosophila melanogaster. By integrating gene expression data with anatomical representations, FlyAnatoView helps restore spatial context and enables users to explore expression patterns across tissues, organs, and cell types. This resource provides an intuitive way to connect transcriptomic profiles with anatomical structures, facilitating the interpretation and exploration of scRNA-seq datasets.

items.title: Transcriptomic Indicators of the Point of No Return in Leiocassis longirostris : Ecological Thresholds and Molecular Signatures of Failed Nutritional Transition.
items.abstract: The transition from endogenous yolk utilization to exogenous feeding is a critical developmental event in larval fish. Failure to complete this transition during starvation may lead to the point of no return (PNR). We conducted transcriptomic sequencing at eight developmental stages (F2, F3, F5, S5, F9, S9, F14, and S14/PNR) in Leiocassis longirostris larvae to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying nutritional transition and starvation-induced PNR. During normal development, the transition to the exogenous nutrition phase was characterized by a coordinated program encompassing translational activation, immune-barrier establishment, and enhanced nutrient utilization. In contrast, under starvation, larvae exhibited a progressive trajectory from adaptive compensation to systemic failure. Early starvation was marked by PPAR-mediated lipid mobilization and cell-cycle suppression to conserve energy. Upon reaching the PNR, the transcriptomic profile shifted toward terminal catabolism, characterized by significant proteasome activation and the catastrophic disruption of ECM-receptor interactions and focal adhesions, signaling a loss of tissue integrity. WGCNA identified a PNR-specific module enriched in programmed cell death and inflammatory signaling. We propose a mechanistic model for the PNR driven by necroptosis via the RIPK1-RIPK3-MLKL axis and persistent inflammation involving p65 and STAT3/6. Cross-sectional comparisons of the starvation and feeding groups revealed a progression from early adaptive metabolic signaling to terminal bioenergetic collapse and irreversible structural degradation. The PNR therefore represents a critical ecological threshold, with the identified pathways and genes offering candidate indicators of larval feeding success and survival potential.

items.title: Factors associated with Anaplasma phagocytophilum PCR positivity and seropositivity in horses in Europe (2022-2025).
items.abstract: Equine granulocytic anaplasmosis (EGA) is caused by Anaplasma phagocytophilum and mainly transmitted by Ixodes persulcatus complex ticks, particularly I. ricinus in Europe. The study aimed to investigate factors associated with PCR positivity and seropositivity in horses. Equine samples from across Europe submitted to a laboratory between January 2022 and December 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) results on EDTA blood and serology using immunofluorescence antibody test (IFAT) on serum or plasma were included. Multiple logistic regression analysis was performed, in which horses were grouped in different age categories. Of 2,753 horses tested by PCR, 358 (13.0%) were positive. In the multivariable model, PCR positivity was associated with season, sampling year, European region, age category, sex, and horse type classification. The strongest seasonal effect was observed in winter, with lower odds compared to spring (OR=0.033, P 18 years (OR=1.640, P<0.001), and in heavy horses compared with warmbloods (OR=2.740, P<0.001). Descriptively, PCR-positivity was highest in summer and lowest in winter; adjusted pairwise comparisons confirmed significantly lower odds in winter compared with the other three seasons, in accordance with tick activity patterns. Further significant differences between different seasons were not noted. The increasing seropositivity with increasing age can be interpreted as higher risk for pathogen contact during life. Horse type-associated differences may reflect unmeasured differences in management, housing conditions, and vector exposure rather than intrinsic biological susceptibility. Given the multi-host ecology of A. phagocytophilum and the zoonotic potential of some genetic variants, equine infections are relevant from a One Health and All-species perspective.

items.title: Shifting schedules: phenology of insects in cities.
items.abstract: Cities have the potential to profoundly alter insect phenology, with potentially cascading ecological effects through disrupted species interactions. After surveying the literature, existing studies of urban insect phenology show strong biases towards observational studies of the timing of the presence and abundance of pollinators in temperate regions. Even with this focused scope, results are highly variable among studies and do not show the often predicted trend towards earlier spring phenology observed in better studied taxa. Understanding this variation in phenology will require the use of experimental studies such as transplant and common garden experiments to identify both the urban environmental changes and subsequent biological processes (such as phenotypic plasticity and evolution) that cause these changes. Thus, there are abundant opportunities for further research into the effects of urbanization on insect phenology, which will in turn improve our understanding of the effects of our growing cities on insect diversity.

items.title: A multimodal model integrating microscopic images and fractal dimension for characterizing the granulation process of aerobic granular sludge.
items.abstract: Reliable identification of aerobic granular sludge (AGS) granulation stages can support cultivation monitoring and operational adjustment. We collected 231 microscopic images and particle size measurements from three sequencing batch reactors operated at influent chemical oxygen demand concentrations of 250, 500, and 1000 mg/L. Growth, stabilization, and disintegration were labeled according to consecutive-day changes in median particle diameter (ΔD 50 ). Agreement between expert consensus and threshold-based labels was 88.31% (Cohen's κ = 0.823). Fractal dimension (FD) was calculated by box counting at 20, 40, and 80 pixels to characterize two-dimensional spatial occupancy of sludge foreground. Conventional machine learning, numerical-feature, image-only, image-numerical fusion, and vision-language models were compared. Trained models were evaluated using leave-one-reactor-out cross-validation across five training runs, with an 80:20 training-validation split in the two remaining reactors. FD was higher and less variable during stabilization (1.644 ± 0.082) than during growth (1.587 ± 0.087) or disintegration (1.580 ± 0.114). Adding FD increased the macro-averaged F1 score of ResNet34 from 0.866 to 0.905 and reduced confusion between stabilization and disintegration. ResNet34FD-Gated achieved the highest mean accuracy (0.919 ± 0.012) and Macro-F1 (0.920 ± 0.012). Input permutation analysis identified microscopic images as the dominant information source for stage classification. Integrating FD with microscopic images and particle size improved stage identification under laboratory conditions, although external validation remains necessary.

items.title: Metagenomic insights into regulatory effects of micro-aerobic conditions on microbial metabolism during hydrolytic acidification of printing and dyeing wastewater.
items.abstract: Micro-aerobic hydrolysis and acidification (MAHA) is a promising pretreatment for printing and dyeing wastewater (PDW), yet the role of dissolved oxygen (DO) in regulating hydrolysis-acidification performance and microbial functions remains poorly understood. In this study, laboratory-scale reactors treating synthetic PDW were operated under four DO ranges to investigate changes in reactor performance, microbial communities, and metagenomic functional potential. A DO of 0.1-0.3 mg/L achieved the best overall performance, with an apparent decolorization efficiency of 77.0 ± 7.5 %, a BOD 5 /COD ratio of 0.58 ± 0.029, and a COD removal efficiency of 41.4 ± 5.5 %. Acetate was the predominant volatile fatty acid (VFA), whereas VFA accumulation decreased with increasing DO. Microbial community analysis revealed distinct community structures under different DO conditions, with several potential hydrolytic and organic matter-transforming genera enriched at 0.1-0.3 mg/L DO. Metagenomic analysis further indicated enhanced functional potential for central carbon metabolism, electron transfer, redox cofactor metabolism, and aromatic compound transformation under this condition. Notably, azo-reductase-related genes did not increase concomitantly, suggesting that the improved apparent decolorization was likely associated with broader community-level functional potential rather than enrichment of a single azo-reduction gene. Overall, maintaining DO at 0.1-0.3 mg/L was associated with enhanced apparent decolorization, providing operational insights for further optimization of MAHA under the investigated conditions.

items.title: Accumulation of rubber-derived chemicals from shoe sole abrasion in urban pedestrian zones.
items.abstract: Rubber derived chemicals (RDCs) are widely investigated in tire related environments, but their presence and accumulation in pedestrian zones remain poorly understood. We conducted a large-scale survey of 32 RDCs in pedestrian dust across 44 cities in China, which included detailed investigations of four functional zones in Guangzhou and dust from different floors of a single building. RDCs were widely detected, with total concentrations ranging from 136 to 1,380 ng/g across surveyed cities. Although the ∑RDC concentrations did not significantly differ among broad geographic regions, their chemical composition showed spatial differentiation, with p-phenylenediamine derivatives (PPDs) exhibiting stronger geographic variation. For example, mean concentrations of N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (6PPD) were approximately 117 ng/g in South China and 2 ng/g in Central China. In Guangzhou, living areas had the highest mean ∑RDC concentration (4,380 ng/g), and RDC concentrations decreased with floor level and increased with pedestrian density (R 2 = 0.619, p < 0.05). Commercial shoe soles contained diverse RDCs (mean ∑RDCs: 25,400 ng/g), the mean ∑RDC concentration in leather shoes (36,700 ng/g) is twice that of sneakers (17,900 ng/g), and their chemical profiles aligned with those found in pedestrian dust. It is estimated that China's annual shoe sole wear particle and RDC emissions are 174,000 and 4.17 tons, respectively. These findings support that shoe sole abrasion represents an overlooked diffuse source of RDCs in urban pedestrian environments, extending the environmental footprint of RDC pollution beyond the conventional focus on tire wear.

items.title: Carbon cycling and ecological functions of cultivated and natural macroalgae/seagrass in tropical coastal waters: Insights for blue carbon resource management in Hainan Island.
items.abstract: As important primary producers in marine ecosystems, macroalgae and seagrass play a key role in carbon sequestration and environmental restoration, but comprehensive assessments in tropical island regions are still insufficient. The present study took the Eucheuma gelatinae cultivation area in Haiwei Bay, Changjiang, and the Sargassum polycystum bed and Enhalus acoroides seagrass meadow in Gaolong Bay, Wenchang, Hainan Island, China as research objects to explore the carbon dynamics and environmental benefits of macroalgae and seagrass during the growth and decomposition stages, and estimate their carbon sequestration potential. The study found that large-scale cultivation of E. gelatinae significantly improved water pH and dissolved oxygen (DO), reduced chlorophyll a (Chl a), and absorbed phosphorus (P) nutrients. Compared with the Sargassum bed, DO and pH were 4.31% and 0.47% higher, respectively; compared with the seagrass meadow, they were 27.73% and 1.48% higher, respectively. In terms of organic carbon dynamics, E. gelatinae was particularly effective in increasing dissolved organic carbon (DOC), while Sargassum beds and seagrass meadows had more advantages in releasing particulate organic carbon (POC). In terms of carbon sequestration capacity, Sargassum exhibited higher carbon sequestration capacity than E. acoroides and E. gelatinae, and a similar trend was observed in the ability to absorb nitrogen (N) nutrients. Over the past 15 years, the cultivation of Sargassum and E. gelatinae in China has shown considerable carbon sequestration potential. The total organic carbon fixed and stored by macroalgae (C TS ) reached 452,900-466,900 tons and 121,300-126,000 tons, respectively, and the carbon removed by macroalgae harvest (C SH ) made a significant contribution of Sargassum and E. gelatinae cultivation. However, cultivation carbon sources (C si ) offset 36% and 31% of C TS , respectively. The cultivation of both also produced significant ecological benefits in absorbing heavy metals and removing N/P nutrients. Decomposition experiments showed that E. gelatinae and S. polycystum decomposed relatively quickly, while E. acoroides decomposed slowly but had strong carbon enrichment capacity. In conclusion, Sargassum has outstanding carbon sequestration capacity; E. gelatinae is conducive to water restoration; seagrass meadows need to be strengthened for protection. Combined deployment of the three macrophyte types can build a complementary tropical coastal system integrating habitat remediation and long-term carbon storage. The present study provides a theoretical basis for the resource enhancement and ecological assessment of macroalgae and seagrass, and contributes to blue carbon resource management and marine ecological restoration.

items.title: Removal performance and putative degradation mechanisms of bisphenol A in bioretention cells.
items.abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA) is a typical endocrine-disrupting pollutant. It can enter receiving waters through urban stormwater runoff and pose potential risks to aquatic ecosystems. Bioretention cells are widely used stormwater control measures for urban runoff and can retain and transform organic pollutants. However, the removal performance and mechanisms of BPA in bioretention cells remain unclear. In this study, two bioretention cells were constructed. BPA removal under different influent concentrations was investigated. The main removal zone and transformation process of BPA were also analyzed. The results showed that BPA removal by the bioretention cells exceeded 70%, with the main removal occurring in the upper filter media layer. Both filter media adsorption and microbial processes contributed to BPA removal. Several transformation products in the bioretention cells were putatively identified by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS), including monohydroxylated BPA, 4-hydroxyacetophenone, 3-oxohexanedioic acid, and other intermediates. Together with the metagenomic results, these products suggest that BPA may undergo initial oxidation, side-chain cleavage, intermediate transformation, and ring-opening processes in bioretention cells. These findings provide a scientific basis for BPA control in urban stormwater runoff.

items.title: Warming reduces grassland biomass gains from precipitation and biodiversity in arid Central Asia.
items.abstract: Aboveground biomass (AGB) is a key component of the carbon cycle and an important indicator for sustainable grassland management, particularly under climate change. However, the nonlinear and threshold-dependent responses of AGB to climatic factors and species richness (SR) remain poorly understood, especially in arid Central Asian grasslands. Here, we aimed to quantify the effects of mean annual precipitation (MAP), mean annual temperature (MAT), and plant SR, including their interactions and thresholds, on grassland AGB across diverse ecological zones in Xinjiang, China. Using extensive field data, we applied threshold regression and mixed-effect models to assess how MAP, MAT, SR, and their interactions influence AGB across alpine, temperate, and transzonal grasslands. Our results indicated that AGB varied significantly across grassland types (P < 0.05), ranging from 23.35 ± 1.36 g m-2 to 312.50 ± 16.57 g m-2. Relationships between AGB and MAP, MAT, and SR were nonlinear and shifted beyond specific thresholds unique to each grassland type. While MAP and SR generally promoted AGB, MAT did not. In water-limited temperate grassland, increasing MAP strengthened the positive effect of SR on AGB, whereas in alpine and transzonal grasslands, this SR effect weakened along the MAP gradient. Across all grassland types, higher MAT both directly reduced AGB and weakened the positive effects of MAP and SR. Our findings highlight that warming indirectly reduces AGB by suppressing the beneficial effects of precipitation and biodiversity. Accounting for these interactive and threshold effects is crucial for accurately predicting climate change impacts on grassland ecosystems.

items.title: Iron-Dependent Siderophore Production via NRPS-Independent Pathways in Pedobacter.
items.abstract: Recent genome mining studies have revealed substantial biosynthetic potential for specialized metabolites in the phylum Bacteroidota, particularly NRPS-associated pathways. However, canonical NRPS-encoded metallophore biosynthetic gene clusters appear poorly represented, leaving iron acquisition strategies in this phylum largely unexplored. We therefore investigated NRPS-independent siderophore biosynthesis as an alternative route and examined its iron-responsive regulation in the environmental genus Pedobacter. Comparative genome mining identified multiple putative NRPS-independent siderophore (NIS)-associated biosynthetic gene clusters across Pedobacter genomes, and Pedobacter cryoconitis PAMC 27485 was selected for experimental validation. Cultivation under iron-limited and iron-supplemented conditions, combined with transcriptional analysis, UHPLC-HRMS metabolomics, and GNPS molecular networking, revealed iron-responsive siderophore production. Genes within a candidate NIS-associated cluster were induced under iron limitation and repressed upon iron supplementation. Consistent with this transcriptional response, a family of related metabolites accumulated specifically under iron-limited conditions. Targeted MS analysis detected both apo and Fe-bound forms, supported by characteristic mass shifts and Fe-associated isotope patterns. Isolation and NMR-based structure elucidation confirmed three lipidated cyclic imide hydroxamate siderophores, named flavolipid imides A-C. These findings demonstrate that the scarcity of canonical NRPS metallophore pathways in Bacteroidota does not imply limited iron acquisition potential but instead highlights NIS-dependent siderophore biosynthesis as an alternative strategy. By linking genome-encoded biosynthetic potential, iron-responsive transcriptional regulation, and structurally validated siderophore production, this study expands our understanding of iron acquisition in Bacteroidota and establishes Pedobacter as a promising system for discovering cryptic metallophore pathways.

items.title: Genomic epidemiology of CHIKV during the largest outbreak in Mainland China - implication for CHIKV intervention.
items.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) has caused recurrent epidemics across tropical and subtropical regions globally. In 2025, Guangdong, China, experienced the largest documented CHIKV outbreak in mainland China, with 23,464 reported cases across all 21 prefecture-level cities. We conducted integrated epidemiological, genomic, and phylodynamic analyses to investigate the outbreak's origins, transmission dynamics, and CHIKV lineage evolution. The Guangdong strain belongs to the East/Central/South African (ECSA) genotype, Middle African lineage (ECSA-MAL) - one of several CHIKV lineages co-circulating globally in 2025; a long internal branch separates ECSA-MAL from previously sequenced relatives, indicating substantial surveillance gaps in endemic regions. Phylodynamic analysis using a local molecular clock model estimated that the viral introduction occurred within a narrow window in early April 2025 (95% HPD: March 26-April 12), suggesting a 2.5-month period of cryptic transmission prior to detection. The prolonged silent phase aligns with vector dynamics: the Mosquito Ovitrap Index in the outbreak town of Beijiao, Foshan, stayed low in April (3.0) before surging to 9.0 through July - consistent with suppressed early transmission followed by seasonal amplification. Human migration from the two epidemic epicenters was moderately associated with the spatial distribution of cases (Spearman ρ around 0.5), while mosquito ecology may constrain spatial spread. Phylowave analysis on global circulating strains identified 33 lineage-defining mutations across 14 sublineages, concentrated in NSP3, E1 and E2. Four of these have been experimentally validated as adaptive mutations. This study demonstrates the critical need for enhanced genomic surveillance during pre-peak months and underscores the importance of monitoring adaptive mutations across diverse ecological regions.

items.title: Assessing the potential of the invasive decapod crustacean Percnon gibbesi as a sentinel of coastal water quality in Mallorca, Western Mediterranean.
items.abstract: Marine coastal sites in the Mediterranean are under long-term anthropogenic pressure, intensified by tourism and xenobiotic release. Globalisation has also facilitated the spread of invasive species, including crustaceans. Here, the alien crab Percnon gibbesi, established along the Balearic coast (Mallorca), was evaluated as a potential sentinel species at three sites representing contrasting anthropogenic influence: Port Adriano (n PAD = 10) and Portals Vells (n POV = 13), higher anthropogenic influence, and Alconàsser (n ALC = 10), lower anthropogenic influence. Microplastic (MP) abundance, morphology, and polymer composition in surface waters (n = 3 per area) were used as indicators of anthropogenic pressure rather than direct measures of organismal exposure. Biomarkers related to immune function, moulting, detoxification and antioxidant defences were analysed in hepatopancreas, haemolymph, eyes, muscle and gills. In vitro assays assessed the sensitivity of two metabolic enzymes to environmentally relevant xenobiotics. MP abundance increased from Alconàsser (37.3 ± 4.2 MPs L⁻ 1 ) to Portals Vells (68.0 ± 7.2 MPs L⁻ 1 ) and Port Adriano (103.3 ± 10.4 MPs L⁻ 1 ), with significant differences among all sites (p ≤ 0.008). Fibres predominated (69.5%), while PP, LDPE and HDPE were the main polymers. Biomarker responses showed spatial patterns consistent with MP abundance and overall anthropogenic influence, suggesting an association with anthropogenic pressure rather than direct causality. Immune, moulting-related and antioxidant biomarkers showed the strongest responses at more influenced sites, whereas detoxification and neurotoxicity markers showed no consistent spatial patterns. Lipid peroxidation was unchanged (p = 0.45), consistent with maintained oxidative balance. Multivariate biomarker profiles differed significantly among sites, with the greatest separation between Alconàsser and Port Adriano (PERMANOVA, R 2 = 0.367, adjusted p = 0.004). Complementary in vitro assays showed that several plastic-associated xenobiotics inhibited detoxification enzymes, whereas moulting-related ones were unaffected. These findings support P. gibbesi as a candidate sentinel species for monitoring anthropogenic pressure in Mediterranean coastal waters, although further studies integrating chemical analyses and controlled exposures are needed.

items.title: Giant Sequoia (Sequoiadendron giganteum) Foliar Distillate Elicits Sex-Biased Attraction by the Western Cedar Bark Beetle (Phloeosinus punctatus) in Laboratory Assays.
items.abstract: Giant sequoia (Sequoiadendron giganteum) is a globally recognized cultural resource and recreational attraction that is listed as 'endangered' on the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List. In recent years, the western cedar bark beetle, Phloeosinus punctatus, has been implicated as a contributing factor in giant sequoia crown dieback and mortality of mature trees weakened by drought stress and severe wildfire. However, semiochemical options for monitoring and potentially managing P. punctatus populations are presently unavailable. To address this, we evaluated orientation behavior of P. punctatus to a steam-extracted distillate prepared from giant sequoia branches using Y-tube olfactometry. During olfactometry assays, 45% of adult beetles chose the distillate while 22.5% oriented towards the control arm (32.5% made no choice). Multinomial contrasts indicated that females oriented toward the distillate, whereas males exhibited no preference. Results from gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) found the volatile headspace of the distillate to be primarily (> 90%) composed of monoterpenes along with lesser proportions of oxygenated monoterpenoids and relatively non-volatile phenylpropanoids (< 10%), several of which are documented kairomones for conifer-associated insects. Likely kairomones for P. punctatus, the role of females as the host-seeking, pioneering sex, and the potential for giant sequoia distillate and synthetic terpene standards to support monitoring across the natural range of the host tree are discussed.

items.title: Flicker Fusion Camouflage: A Mechanistic Framework for Motion-Induced Concealment.
items.abstract: Flicker fusion camouflage (FFC) challenges the view that movement necessarily compromises camouflage by proposing that rapid movement can render contrasting patterns perceptually blurred. FFC emerges from interactions among pattern geometry, locomotion, observer visual processing, and environmental context. This framework provides testable predictions for determining when motion can enhance rather than compromise animal concealment.

items.title: Late-season cooling and local sensitivity shape blue ring formation in northern Fennoscandian Scots pine.
items.abstract: Blue rings (BRs) are wood anatomical anomalies formed by incomplete lignification of latewood tracheids and provide a direct record of disruptions during the final stages of wood formation. Because lignification is temperature sensitive, BRs offer a unique opportunity to investigate how short-lived cooling events affect xylem development. However, the timing of cooling-induced lignification failure and how local site conditions influence BR formation remain poorly understood, particularly at high-latitude treelines where wood formation operates close to thermal limits. Using paired 300-year Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris L.) chronologies from two northern Fennoscandian treeline sites approximately 250 km apart, we present the first direct comparison of BR formation between neighbouring populations exposed to broadly similar regional climatic forcing. BR frequency was consistently higher at Värriö (Finland, 67°N) than at Iškoras (Norway, 69°N), despite strong synchrony in major BR years and a coherent long-term decline in BR occurrence at both sites. BRs largely disappeared from Iškoras after the early twentieth century, whereas they persisted at Värriö. Daily temperature analyses suggest an association between BR formation and short-lived late-season cooling, with the largest observed differences between BR and non-BR years occurring around mid-September. However, differences in BR frequency between sites were not fully explained by the available measures of cold exposure. Instead, our findings are consistent with the hypothesis that BR formation depends on the temporal alignment between cooling events and a vulnerable phase of latewood lignification, potentially contributing to site-specific differences in sensitivity to cooling. Consequently, similar cooling events may trigger lignification failure in one population but not another, leading to different anatomical responses under comparable regional climate forcing. Our findings suggest that local controls on wood formation dynamics may mediate how climatic forcing is translated into anatomical responses, highlighting developmental timing as a potential control on tree sensitivity to short-term temperature variability at the northern climatic limit of Scots pine.

items.title: Upper-tail hydraulic stress and cumulative exposure respond differently to future climate forcing in Populus euphratica.
items.abstract: Hydraulic stress varies not only in magnitude but also in how long stressful conditions persist, yet these temporal dimensions are rarely considered together when projecting tree carbon-water responses to climate change. We combined field measurements with an hourly hydraulic-stomatal optimization model for 33 Populus euphratica trees across four riparian-to-desert plots in the Ebinur Lake Basin, China. Historical simulations covered 2013-2025 and future simulations 2065-2077 under four Shared Socioeconomic Pathway (SSP) scenarios. Model performance was evaluated against 198 matched observations per variable for assimilation, transpiration, stomatal conductance, and leaf water potential (R2 = 0.591-0.670). Historical simulations separated upper-tail hydraulic stress from cumulative exposure. Large trees at the river-proximal D1 plot had the smallest hydraulic safety margins, highest 95th-percentile stem vulnerability-curve-predicted percentage loss of conductivity (VC-PLC q95), and longest duration with VC-PLC ≥12% (PLC12 duration), whereas small trees at the desert-margin D4 plot accumulated the greatest integrated hydraulic burden. Rankings based on minimum hydraulic safety margin agreed moderately with upper-tail and duration metrics but showed little correspondence with integrated burden (Spearman ρ = 0.058). Integrated burden was also much more closely associated with cumulative carbon gain (ρ = -0.874) than either the upper-tail hydraulic safety margin or VC-PLC q95. Under future forcing, integrated hydraulic burden increased in all 11 site × size groups under SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5, while deterioration in upper-tail hydraulic metrics remained limited to relatively few groups. Cumulative carbon gain increased in 43 of 44 group × scenario contrasts and transpiration in all 44. Thus, greater future carbon and water fluxes can coexist with increasing hydraulic exposure. Distinguishing hydraulic intensity from cumulative exposure may therefore help explain how riparian trees sustain carbon and water fluxes as climatic forcing strengthens.

items.title: The correlation between reproductive initiation and remodeling of the TSH-DIO2-T3 axis in Daurian ground squirrels (Spermophilus dauricus).
items.abstract: Seasonal reproduction in mammals is regulated by complex neuroendocrine mechanisms, with the TSH-DIO2-T3 axis considered a common regulatory pathway. The Daurian ground squirrel (Spermophilus dauricus), an important model species for hibernation physiological ecology in China, exhibits seasonal reproduction and fat-storing hibernation. However, its laboratory standardization is limited by unclear hibernation-related reproductive mechanisms and unstable breeding success. In this study, we investigated seasonal variations in gonadal status, sex hormone concentrations, hypothalamic protein expression, and pituitary TSHβ levels in male and female Daurian ground squirrels across pre-hibernation, hibernation, and breeding stages. Results demonstrated that reproductive activation began during hibernation, with females initiating earlier than males. Thyroid-stimulating hormone cells in the pituitary showed seasonal differences: thyrotropin β expression increased during reproductive activation, while chromogranin A dominated in non-breeding seasons. Hypothalamic TSHR, DIO2, and kisspeptin levels changed in patterns consistent with the conserved seasonal reproduction pathway model. These findings describe key hypothalamic dynamics associated with reproductive initiation during hibernation and provide a data reference for post-hibernation laboratory breeding of this species.

items.title: Adult predation shapes brain evolution in guppies (Poecilia reticulata).
items.abstract: Predation is a powerful evolutionary force shaping many traits of prey species. As the brain is the neural substrate of all behaviours, including essential anti-predator actions, its morphology is expected to be directly shaped by predation. However, while correlative evidence supports this relationship, causal evidence of predation driving brain morphology is currently lacking. Here, we investigated how predation pressure changes brain morphology in guppies (Poecilia reticulata) from replicated artificial selection lines for adult predation survival. We found that after three generations of selection, predation-selected females likely evolved relatively larger brains compared to control fish. In males, while brain size was not affected by predation selection, predation lines showed relatively larger olfactory bulbs. These results demonstrate that predation can directly shape the evolution of brain morphology, remarkably fast and in a sex-specific manner. Comparing our findings to those from natural populations with divergent predation pressures allows us to disentangle the direct predation effects from the indirect ecological effects of high predation pressure that drive brain evolution.

items.title: Plant-soil feedbacks and seed dispersal through space and time: toward an integrative framework.
items.abstract: Background Plants can modify soil microbial communities and nutrient conditions, creating soil legacies that influence the performance of future plants and generate plant-soil feedbacks (PSFs). These legacies are often studied at local scales, whereas seed dispersal and germination determine where and when offspring encounter them. Integrating these processes is essential for understanding how local soil interactions influence plant recruitment and broader ecological dynamics. Scope We develop an integrative framework linking PSF with seed dispersal through space and time by matching seed distributions with the spatial extent of soil legacies and seed persistence and germination timing with legacy duration. Negative PSF reduces subsequent plant performance, whereas positive PSF enhances it. Under negative PSF, spatial displacement or delayed germination may reduce exposure to harmful legacies; under positive PSF, the same shifts may reduce access to beneficial legacies. The framework integrates classical spatial escape mechanisms, including Janzen-Connell distance-dependent escape from enemies near conspecific adults, with temporal escape through delayed recruitment, while considering reciprocal effects of dispersal on PSF and shared ecological drivers. An illustrative synthesis of 216 species identifies candidate cross-species associations: greater spatial dispersal tends to be associated with more positive PSF, whereas longer seedbank persistence tends to be associated with more negative PSF, and the dormancy association weakens after phylogenetic control. These observational patterns do not resolve causal direction. Conclusions By connecting soil legacies with seed movement and timing, this framework provides a mechanistic basis for understanding how local belowground interactions contribute to coexistence, succession, invasion, and restoration. Rather than assuming a universal PSF-dispersal relationship, the framework shows that recruitment outcomes depend on how seed movement and germination timing match the spatial extent and temporal persistence of soil legacies. Embedding PSF in a spatiotemporal context clarifies how local soil legacies scale up through recruitment to shape population and community dynamics.

items.title: Cognitive-behavioral conjoint therapy for posttraumatic stress disorder: A systematic review of outcomes, mechanisms, and clinical applications.
items.abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with interpersonal dysfunction, and including loved ones in treatment may benefit both PTSD symptom reduction and relationship functioning. Cognitive-behavioral conjoint therapy (CBCT) for PTSD is a manualized, trauma-focused psychotherapy delivered in a dyadic format, typically to an individual with PTSD and their intimate partner. We replicated and extended a systematic review published in 2020 to incorporate several studies published since then. Procedures for this preregistered systematic review were consistent with PRISMA guidelines. We identified 50 reports representing 41 unique studies: 19 main outcome studies (i.e., five randomized controlled trials [RCTs], four of which were published after the previous review; 12 uncontrolled trials; and two naturalistic outcome studies), 17 secondary analyses, and five ongoing RCTs. Overall, these studies indicate that CBCT for PTSD and its adaptations improve PTSD symptoms. Findings were mixed for relationship satisfaction, co-occurring psychiatric symptoms, and partner accommodation. Baseline relationship satisfaction moderated effects of CBCT for PTSD on relationship outcomes; partner accommodation and social support moderated PTSD outcomes. Adaptations designed to increase efficiency, accessibility, and potency include alternative formats of treatment delivery, modified content, and pharmacological augmentation. The evidence base for CBCT for PTSD has grown rapidly in recent years, but methodological limitations, including small sample sizes, insufficient evidence from well-controlled trials, lack of generalizability of samples, and limited evidence of mechanisms of action, remain. Several ongoing studies were designed and will be well-positioned to address these limitations.

items.title: The mental cost of urban living: neighbourhood deprivation, income, and depressive symptoms in Germany.
items.abstract: Objective This study investigates the established associations between neighbourhood socioeconomic deprivation, household income, and depressive symptoms in Germany, and assesses whether these associations differ across settlement structures. Building on the person-in-environment framework, we understand mental health as an emergent outcome of the interplay between individuals and their environments. Method We analysed cross-sectional data from the nationally representative German Health Update 2019/2020 wave of the European Health Interview Survey (GEDA 2019/2020-EHIS) ​ (N = 20,773). Depressive symptoms were measured using Patient Health Questionnaire-8 (PHQ-8). Polynomial regression models tested linear and quadratic associations of neighbourhood deprivation (German Index of Socioeconomic Deprivation, GISD) with depressive symptoms, and their interaction with household income quintiles. Whether settlement type (cities, urban, rural and sparsely populated counties) moderated these associations was tested explicitly using nested interaction models. Results Higher neighbourhood deprivation was associated with increased depressive symptoms, with a significant quadratic term indicating disproportionately higher symptom severity in highly deprived areas. Household income was inversely associated with depressive symptoms, though its moderation of the deprivation association was only partially supported. Settlement type significantly moderated the deprivation-depression association: the quadratic association was strongest in cities and attenuated, or shifted towards a concave pattern, in less densely populated settlement types. This settlement-related moderation was additionally associated with income, particularly in urban and rural counties, and less consistently in sparsely populated areas. Conclusions The psychological burden of socioeconomic deprivation is not uniform, but differs systematically by settlement context and, less consistently, by individual income. These associations were most pronounced, and most clearly evident, in major cities. Addressing mental health inequalities linked to neighbourhood deprivation may therefore benefit from strategies tailored to settlement-specific conditions, alongside broader efforts aimed at individual socioeconomic resources.

items.title: Perceived housing quality and emotional distress among refugees living in camps: a cross-sectional study in Eastern Germany.
items.abstract: Background Housing quality as a key social determinant of health has received growing attention in public health research. Asylum seekers and refugees in European countries are frequently housed in institutionalized, camp-like facilities. These facilities are often characterized by overcrowding and limited privacy, safety, and autonomy. Such conditions constitute an important post-migration stressor and may be a particularly relevant determinant of mental health. This study aimed to examine the association between multiple dimensions of perceived housing quality and emotional distress among refugees living in camps in Eastern Germany. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study among asylum seekers and refugees living in 16 camps across three federal states in Eastern Germany. Data were collected via a multilingual online survey; fieldwork took place in June and July 2025, and the survey remained accessible until the end of August 2025. As the primary outcome, we assessed emotional distress using the cross-culturally validated Refugee Health Screener-13 (RHS-13) as an indicator of common mental disorders in refugee populations. In addition, we assessed perceived housing quality using multidimensional indicators as well as relevant sociodemographic covariates. To examine associations between housing quality and emotional distress, we fitted multivariable linear regression models with housing quality indicators as exposures and the RHS-13 sum score as the outcome. First, each housing quality indicator was included separately in single-indicator regression models, which were adjusted for prespecified sociodemographic variables. We then included multiple indicators across different housing quality dimensions simultaneously in the main model, which was also adjusted for sociodemographic variables. Results Most participants scored at or above the cutoff for emotional distress (79%; RHS-13 ≥ 11), with nearly half scoring in the severe-distress range (48%; RHS-13 ≥ 25). Most assessed housing quality indicators showed associations with emotional distress when examined separately in adjusted single-indicator regression models. When multiple indicators across multiple housing quality dimensions were included simultaneously in the adjusted main model, safety, lighting conditions, autonomy, and feelings of boredom or imprisonment within the refugee camp remained associated with emotional distress, whereas crowding, frequent transfers between camps, and region did not. Conclusions Perceived housing quality is closely associated with emotional distress among refugees living in Eastern German camps. Psychosocial and institutional dimensions of housing quality appear particularly relevant to emotional distress. Housing policies for refugees in European countries should therefore consider not only the physical structure of housing but also its psychosocial and institutional dimensions, such as safety, autonomy, and daily-life restrictions, when addressing mental health inequalities in this population.

items.title: Case Study on Nursing Pain Interpretation and Residents' Ability to be Understood.
items.abstract: Introduction In long term care [LTC], the high prevalence of painful illnesses and dementia contributes to complex care needs and challenging pain management. What further complicates matters for residents in this context is the inability to be understood. Purpose In addition to not being understood in the expression of their pain, many residents with a cognitive impairment will exhibit behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia [BPSDs]. Pain indicators may then resemble BPSDs and be interpreted and treated as such. Little is known about this interpretation and subsequent interventions by nurses. Design To explore the management of pain in the LTC context, a single-site retrospective case-study was conducted in a Canadian province using a predefined list of indicators drawn from validated observational pain assessment instruments and the pain literature. Methods These indicators guided the review of residents' charts by abstracting data from nursing documentation and medication administration records. Nursing interpretation of symptoms, as documented in their notes, as either pain or behavior, as well as their actions, were examined. Also explored were associations between the resident's ability to be understood and the nursing interpretation of their symptoms. Results The analysis discovered that many symptoms were more likely to be interpreted as behavior versus pain. Furthermore, a relationship was discovered between the resident's ability to be understood and the interpretation of some symptoms as behavior versus pain. Conclusions and clinical implications Recommendations are made to better support nurses with this important yet challenging role of pain and behavior interpretation with residents who cannot be understood.

items.title: Evaluation of a clinician and lived experience peer worker co-led suicide prevention aftercare program: A non-randomized controlled trial of Next Steps.
items.abstract: Objective Evidence is lacking for the effectiveness of suicide prevention aftercare programs incorporating the lived-experience peer workforce. A non-randomized controlled trial evaluated Next Steps, a community-based clinician and peer-worker co-led aftercare program for individuals following a suicide-related emergency department presentation. It was hypothesized that compared to treatment-as-usual controls, participants will be less likely to have a repeat suicide-related presentation to an emergency department, have lower rates of re-presentations to the emergency department, and be associated with fewer all-cause deaths, in a 12-month follow-up. Method The study included 81 participants and 1412 controls. Re-presentation to an emergency department was analyzed using a Kaplan Meier plot, rates of re-presentation were analyzed using a negative binomial regression, and all-cause mortality was analyzed using Chi-square and Fisher's exact tests. Results No significant differences between participants and controls were found on suicide-related re-presentation (29.6% and 19.8%, respectively), or rates of re-presentation (p = 0.333). No deaths were recorded in the intervention group compared to 17 deaths in controls (1.2%), with the null hypothesis retained. Conclusions Next Steps did not demonstrate superiority over treatment-as-usual following a suicide-related emergency department presentation. The program offers a viable alternative to treatment-as-usual and one that involves the lived-experience workforce in implementation. Further research of peer involvement in aftercare programs is strongly indicated, and a gap remains in evidence of effectiveness at the level of controlled research trials.

items.title: Early caregiving adversity is associated with elevated pro-inflammatory gene expression during adolescence.
items.abstract: Background Early life adversity (ELA) is thought to increase risk for poor health outcomes, in part through induction of a persistent pro-inflammatory phenotype. Though ELA has been consistently associated with elevated circulating markers of inflammation in varied adult populations, meta-analytic work has found mixed links between ELA and circulating protein markers of inflammation in adolescents, leaving the pathways by which the adult inflammatory phenotype emerges unclear. Here we examined whether alterations in pro-inflammatory and Type I interferon (antiviral) gene expression in circulating immune cells (the Conserved Transcriptional Response to Adversity; CTRA) might provide a more sensitive measure of ELA-linked phenotypes in adolescents. Methods We assessed pro-inflammatory (NF-κB) and anti-viral (Interferon Response Factor) transcription factor activity and downstream gene expression in peripheral blood samples from 18 internationally adopted youth who had experienced previous institutional caregiving (a profound form of ELA) and 34 comparison, non-adopted youth. Results Consistent with the CTRA, relative to comparison youth, youth with a history of ELA showed elevated pro-inflammatory (NF-κB) and decreased antiviral (IRF) transcription factor activity. We found no group differences on a priori downstream gene expression composites. Differentially expressed transcripts were preferentially derived from CD16 + and CD16- monocytes, responsible for coordinating the early inflammatory stages of immune responses. Conclusions These findings confirm ELA-linked inflammatory gene regulation in circulating blood cells during adolescence. Compared to plasma protein measures, functional genomic (RNA) measures of inflammation may provide more sensitive, early indexes of developmental trajectories of inflammation following adversity, prior to emergence of an adult ELA-linked inflammatory phenotype associated with disease.

items.title: <sup>1</sup>H MRS reveals impact of early adversity and age on neurometabolic profiles in women.
items.abstract: Exposure to early-life stress (ELS), including neglect or abuse, is known for its detrimental effects on brain health. This study investigated how ELS interacts with chronological age to impact on brain metabolism in middle-aged women using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy ( 1 H MRS) at 3 T. High-quality spectra from the hippocampus (HC) and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) from 75 women, including 53% with ELS exposure before puberty, were analyzed. Generalized additive models assessed non-linear effects of ELS severity and chronological age on neurometabolites related to neuroinflammation and neurotransmitter cycling. Significant interactions emerged for myo-inositol (Ins) in both regions and glutamine (Gln) in the PCC, where greater ELS severity was linked to age-related increases in Ins and Gln concentrations. These results were robust when additionally controlling for symptoms of depression, anxiety, and PTSD, as well as SES, education, menopause status, and smoking. The observed patterns suggest that ELS exposure before puberty, at the older age range, is associated with glial and glutamatergic alterations that are indicative of neuroinflammation, potentially reflecting vulnerability to adverse brain health outcomes.

items.title: Longitudinal multimodal MRI correlates of subclinical insomnia symptoms and depressive mood in young adults.
items.abstract: Background Insomnia symptoms and depressive mood often change together in young adults, but their longitudinal associations with diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS), an indirect index of perivascular-space diffusivity, and within-limbic functional connectivity remain unclear. Methods 308 university students (233 women; age 19.0 ± 0.9 years) completed the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS), diffusion MRI, and resting-state fMRI at baseline and after 1.7 ± 0.5 years. Associations among change scores were tested with permutation-based general linear models with false discovery rate correction, followed by exploratory indirect-association models. Results ISI and SDS increased slightly (dz = 0.16 and 0.20), whereas DTI-ALPS and within-limbic connectivity decreased (dz = -0.59 and - 0.26). Greater ISI increases were associated with larger DTI-ALPS decreases (β = -0.31, 95% CI [-0.42, -0.21]). DTI-ALPS decreases were associated with decreases in within-limbic connectivity (β = 0.17 [0.05, 0.28]) and increases in SDS (β = -0.13 [-0.25, -0.02]); connectivity decreases were associated with SDS increases (β = -0.18 [-0.29, -0.07]). Full models, including covariates, explained 4-16% of the variance in change. The serial indirect association was small (β = 0.0052, 95% CI [0.0004, 0.0133]). An indirect association was also observed in the reversed model. Temporal precedence was not established. Conclusions In a nonclinical cohort, modest changes in insomnia symptoms and depressive mood covaried with changes in DTI-ALPS and limbic connectivity. These are candidate imaging correlates of subclinical symptom variation and should not be generalized to insomnia disorder or major depressive disorder.

items.title: Effects of Androstadienone on Women's Preferences for Male Facial Skin Color: The Moderating Role of Intrasexual Competition.
items.abstract: Previous studies have shown that androstadienone (AND) can influence women's preferences for male facial shape cues, but it remains unclear whether this effect extends to other visual dimensions of male faces, such as facial skin color. The present study examined whether exposure to AND influences women's preferences for male facial skin color and whether this effect is moderated by intrasexual competition. Eighty-three women completed a two-session within-subject experiment in which they were exposed to AND and a placebo solution on two consecutive days. In each session, participants completed a two-alternative forced-choice task using male facial stimuli manipulated along three CIE L*a*b* dimensions: lightness, redness, and yellowness. For each dimension, participants chose the face they perceived as more attractive in a long-term mate-choice context. Participants preferred increased redness and increased lightness in both conditions, whereas increased yellowness was selected below chance only in the AND condition. A trial-level binomial generalized linear mixed-effects model showed that AND selectively enhanced preference for increased lightness, whereas no significant AND effects were observed for redness or yellowness. This lightness-specific effect was moderated by intrasexual competition: AND increased preference for lightness primarily among women with lower levels of intrasexual competition, but not among women with higher levels of intrasexual competition. These findings suggest that AND may selectively modulate mating-related facial preferences across specific visual dimensions and that its effect depends on women's baseline competitive orientation.

items.title: Frontocentral theta oscillations bias perceptual judgments of ambiguous visual causality.
items.abstract: Human perceptual decisions frequently rely on incomplete, ambiguous sensory inputs resolved prior to stimulus onset. Prior electrophysiological work confirms pre-event frontocentral ERP components predict ambiguous visual causal judgments, yet the spectrotemporal signatures of spontaneous oscillatory biases remain uncharacterized. Frontocentral theta signals proactive cognitive control, but whether pre-event theta oscillation modulates high-order causal inference independently of stimulus-locked ERPs remains untested. Thirteen volunteers (16 recruited, 3 excluded) completed a staircase-calibrated Michotte launching task with 64-channel EEG recorded. Time-frequency decomposition, permutation tests, and ERP-subtraction controls isolated pre-coincidence oscillatory patterns distinguishing causal bouncing and non-causal streaming percepts under PSE level. Elevated pre-coincidence Fz theta power robustly biased observers toward causal reports, showing a negative linear relationship between theta magnitude and streaming response ratios. The theta bias survived single-trial ERP removal, proving oscillatory signals carry predictive information distinct from known ERP markers. These findings imply frontocentral theta pre-allocates anticipatory cognitive resources to support intuitive causal reasoning, separating theta's executive regulatory function from alpha's modulation of basic sensory awareness. This study constructs a novel spectrotemporal framework explaining how spontaneous frontal oscillations sculpt ambiguous causal perception.

items.title: Does the mirror have magic? The moderating role of self-awareness intensity on sharing behavior in 3- to 6-year-old children.
items.abstract: This study examined whether theintensityof self-awareness induction moderates sharing behavior in 3- to 6-year-old children. Two experiments employed distinct sharing paradigms. Experiment 1 used a dictator-game sticker-sharing task. Experiment 2 used a balloon-sharing task. Both adopted a between-subjects design that crossed three self-awareness conditions with two age groups. The three conditions were: anenhanced mirror-selfcondition (mirror plus self-relevant cues), amirror-selfcondition (mirror only), and a control condition (no mirror). The two age groups were 3-4 years and 5-6 years. The results showed that, in both tasks, children in theenhanced mirror-selfcondition shared significantly more than those in the control condition. In the balloon task, they also shared significantly more than those in themirror-selfcondition, whereas themirror-selfand control conditions did not differ. Meanwhile, children aged 5-6 years shared significantly more than those aged 3-4 years across both tasks. Among the 3- to 6-year-old preschoolers studied here, these findings indicate that the reliability of the mirror-self effect may depend on thestrengthof self-awareness induction. Higher-intensity self-awareness induction appears to more reliably promote prosocial behavior in preschoolers. The results support the continuity hypothesis of objective self-awareness theory, help resolve prior inconsistencies regarding the stability of mirror effects, and offer empirically grounded implications for fostering prosocial development.

items.title: The Perceived Suitability of Digitally Delivered Impulse-Focused Techniques in Binge Eating: A Qualitative Intervention Development Study.
items.abstract: Objective Impulsivity and inhibitory control difficulties are key mechanisms in binge eating behaviour in individuals with eating disorders. Digital interventions targeting these mechanisms are primarily developed for weight loss rather than the specific psychological and clinical needs of the population with binge eating, creating a gap in treatment. This study explored lived experience perceptions of digitally delivered impulse-focused techniques to inform future intervention development. Method Fourteen participants (2 males, 12 females) were recruited via social media for online semi-structured interviews. Participants viewed a short demonstration video of an existing impulse-focused dietary change intervention (ImpulsePal) and discussed the perceived suitability of its techniques for binge eating contexts. Data were analysed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis. Results Three overarching themes were generated regarding the perceived suitability and potential risks of digitally delivered impulse-focused techniques; designing for accessibility, personalisation, and supportive communication; and unmet needs extending beyond impulse management, including connection, reflection, and self-awareness. Initial Guiding Principles for future digital intervention development in binge eating contexts are presented. Conclusions With careful adaptation, an impulse-focused intervention like ImpulsePal could complement existing support pathways, but further development and feasibility testing are required before wider testing or use in people with binge eating.

items.title: Surprised Facial Expressions Strengthen Memory for Neutral Pictures Irrespective of Task Demands.
items.abstract: Facial expressions are crucial in social interaction. Previous studies have consistently demonstrated that positive and negative facial expressions affect memory for relevant faces and even other stimuli in different tasks. However, little is known about the role of surprised facial expressions on memory processes. Therefore, the present study aimed to investigate whether surprised facial expressions influence memory for emotional stimuli in different task demands. To address this issue, participants were presented with surprised or neutral facial expressions together with positive, negative or neutral pictures. Moreover, participants were asked to memorize the pictures or to indicate the emotional content of the pictures or the facial expression. Subsequently, participants completed an old/new recognition task regarding the pictures. Results showed that surprised facial expressions, as compared to neutral ones, resulted in better recognition of neutral pictures, irrespective of task demands. Surprised facial expressions also enhanced recognition of positive and negative pictures when the task involved facial expression processing, although this broader effect was not significantly different from that effect when facial expressions were task-irrelevant. These findings highlight the role of surprised facial expressions on memory for other stimuli.

items.title: A Pilot Study of the Neural Activation Associated with Convergence Subtypes in Individuals with Convergence Insufficiency.
items.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this pilot investigation was to assess the neural correlates of convergence eye movement subtypes in individuals with convergence insufficiency using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Methods Data were gathered from six individuals with convergence insufficiency. Brain activation was assessed using fMRI while subjects made convergence eye movements in response to stimuli that primarily led to changes in: (1) accommodative convergence (monocular viewing through a -2.00 D lens), (2) proximal convergence (monocular viewing of Difference-of-Gaussian (DOG) targets at different distances) and (3) disparity convergence (step increases in the disparity of a random dot stereogram). Results Areas of brain activation were dependent on the convergence stimulus. Subjects with convergence insufficiency showed substantial activation in the frontal lobes and in other areas associated with visual attention in the accommodative convergence and proximal convergence conditions. In the disparity condition, brain activation was primarily found in the occipital cortex. Conclusion These results suggest that activation seen in fMRI studies with convergence eye movements is dependent on the stimulus used to induce convergence. In the accommodative and proximal convergence conditions, brain activation was greater in areas associated with visual attention. In the disparity convergence condition, brain activation was primarily found in the occipital cortex.
