items.title: An Intrapersonal Network Approach to Acute Symptom Dynamics After Sport-Related Concussion.
items.abstract: Background Post-concussion presentations are heterogeneous, characterized by various nonspecific self-report symptoms. Historically complete rest was the standard recommendation for concussion care, but with relatively high rates of persistent symptoms, active domain-specific interventions have been popularized. Determining which intervention is warranted can be difficult when concurrent psychological and preexisting health factors exacerbate injury-related sequelae. Objectives We sought to apply within-person network analysis to an observational study to characterize temporal patterns in acute symptoms. Methods Participants were 403 collegiate student-athletes from the Concussion, Assessment, Research, and Education Consortium with sufficient data on the Sport Concussion Assessment Tool, Third Edition. We used seven serial symptom evaluations immediately post-injury to estimate intrapersonal partial correlation networks and derive centrality frequency and in-/out-strength magnitudes. Contemporaneous networks represent within-day symptom associations with undirected edge weights; temporal networks represent day-to-day symptom associations with edge weights directed temporally from t to t + 1. Results Sadness (mean [M] = 0.99) and more emotional (M = 0.96) were the most central symptoms in the contemporaneous network. For the temporal networks, fatigue/low energy (M = 0.53) and feeling slowed down (M = 0.47) had the greatest in-strength, while confusion (M = 0.84) and neck pain (M = 0.78) had the greatest out-strength. Conclusions After concussion, nonspecific cognitive complaints are common across presentations despite substantial heterogeneity in central symptoms. Vestibulo-ocular and cervicogenic symptoms frequently elicit next-day symptomatology and are associated with increased risk for persistent symptoms, though evidence-based treatments exist. Cognitive-/fatigue-related symptoms are likely to be exacerbated by other sequelae, highlighting the importance of active management and an early, graded return to physical activity that encourages symptom habituation.

items.title: Interventions to reduce perinatal suicidality: a global systematic review.
items.abstract: Introduction Perinatal suicidality (suicidal thoughts, behaviours, plans and attempts) is a risk factor for suicide. Evidence on interventions to reduce perinatal suicidality remains limited. This systematic review examined the effectiveness of non-pharmacological interventions to reduce suicidality in perinatal women. Methods This review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251081528). Seven databases were searched from 2010 to December 2025. Interventions assessing a reduction in perinatal suicidality as a primary, secondary, or safety monitoring outcome were included. Two reviewers independently screened articles. A narrative summary was compiled. Risk of bias was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Results Six studies were included: 5 randomised controlled trials (3 individually randomised, 1 cluster, 1 noninferiority) and 1 historical controlled trial. Three studies investigated suicidality as a primary or secondary outcome, and three studies collected suicidality data for safety monitoring. Of these, two investigated multidisciplinary community health programmes, and one evaluated a behavioural activation therapy. Two studies showed a reduction in suicidality, and one showed a significant reduction at 3-4 months postpartum, but not at 7-8 months. Three studies assessed suicidality as safety monitoring. These studies investigated eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing therapy, a practice-level intervention incorporated into obstetric practices, and an electronic mindfulness-based intervention. These studies were not adequately powered to assess a reduction in suicidality. Discussion Few studies have investigated suicidality as a primary or secondary outcome. Although some health system level and psychological interventions were associated with a reduction in suicidality, robust evidence from interventions specifically designed to reduce perinatal suicidality is needed.

items.title: Gifts for the dead: Maya children's developing theory of mind and their participation in Día de los Muertos.
items.abstract: To better understand the nature of Theory of Mind (ToM) and the cultural dynamics of its development, developmental research should consider new approaches to investigate its use in context. This study sought to understand how participation in Day of the Dead, a holiday involving both real and unseen minds, may involve ToM. Participants in this study were 50 indigenous Tzotzil Mayan children (range = 5-11 years, 46% female) and their caregivers. It was predicted that children with greater ToM would score higher in a gift-giving task where the object was to give a pretend spirit its preferred gifts. Children who passed a classic false-belief task were more likely to give the spirit its preferred gifts. Data were collected in June 2023.

items.title: Identifying voices using confidence judgments under deadline pressure.
items.abstract: Voice identification from categorical lineups can be error-prone. We tested whether Brewer and colleagues' radical alternative to categorical face lineups also improves classification accuracy for earwitnesses. This procedure requires witnesses to rate, under deadline pressure, how confident they are that each lineup member matches their memory of the perpetrator. Participants ( N = 803) attempted to identify a perpetrator from a categorical voice lineup, a confidence-based voice lineup with deadlines, or one without deadlines. Consistent with the findings of Brewer and colleagues, classification accuracy was higher for confidence-based procedures than for categorical lineups. Aligning with this result, discriminability, i.e., the ability to distinguish innocent from guilty suspects, was also higher in confidence-based than categorical lineups. We found some evidence that, for voice identification, it is beneficial to omit deadline pressure; time may support the formation of stable voice representations. Overall, our findings support the conclusion that confidence-based voice procedures are better able to identify guilty suspects than traditional categorical procedures.

items.title: Anxiety sensitivity as a transdiagnostic factor in paediatric chronic pain and sleep disturbances: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Objective This systematic review sought to highlight what is known about paediatric anxiety sensitivity (AS), chronic pain, and sleep disturbances, with the goal of improving theories on chronic pain and sleep and identifying novel areas for intervention. Methods PubMed, SCOPUS, and PsycINFO were searched through June 2026. Inclusion criteria: samples aged 0-18, assessed AS in relation to either chronic pain, sleep, or both, and were accessible in English. Of the 26 articles that met inclusion criteria, nine examined AS and sleep and 17 examined AS and chronic pain. No articles examined all three variables in concert. Results Higher AS was associated with worse sleep quality and efficiency, longer sleep onset latency, and insomnia symptomatology. AS was also related to worse pain outcomes, particularly fear of physical arousal, and may relate to the development and maintenance of chronic pain. Conclusions This systematic review highlights what is known about AS and sleep disturbances and AS and chronic pain in paediatric samples. No articles have been published examining these variables together. A theoretical model is proposed suggesting that AS may be an important target in clinical interventions with the goal of improving both paediatric chronic pain and sleep problems.

items.title: Ethnicity- and gender-based social stressors and parental socialization in Korean Chinese adolescent adjustment.
items.abstract: Although extensive research has documented the adverse effects of social stressors, such as ethnicity- and gender-based discrimination, on adolescent development, much of this work has focused on Western contexts. This survey study was conducted with 267 Korean Chinese adolescents (59% female; M age = 15.24 years, SD age = 1.66, age range: 12-18 years), examining how three forms of perceived discrimination linked to adolescents' psychosocial and academic adjustment, as well as the roles of parental socialization practices. Perceived discrimination by South Koreans, but not by Han Chinese, was linked to more depressive symptoms and delinquency. Gender nonconformity teasing was associated with more depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation. Parental cultural socialization was associated with lower suicidal ideation and delinquency and higher school attachment. Parental gender norm socialization was positively associated with school attachment. These findings underscore the negative implications of ethnicity- and gender-based discrimination, highlight the positive developmental correlates of parental cultural socialization, and suggest that parental gender norm socialization might serve a context-specific adaptive function.

items.title: Assessing book-length reading comprehension through knowledge structures.
items.abstract: Background Book-length reading requires readers to continuously maintain, update and integrate information across extended texts. However, traditional comprehension assessments of book-length reading provide limited insight into readers' ability to organize textual information globally. Aims The present study examined whether knowledge structures can be used to assess students' comprehension of book-length texts and to evaluate the cross-genre applicability and diagnostic value of this approach. Methodology Knowledge-structure representations were collected from 209 students after they read a narrative novel or an expository science book. Bayesian regression models were used to predict reading comprehension. Additional comparisons were conducted to examine differences in knowledge structures between students with different levels of comprehension. Results Knowledge structures measured by semantic networks predicted book-length text comprehension in both genres. At the same time, the knowledge structures constructed by students after narrative reading tended to reflect a sequence-based structure organized by temporal and causal relations, whereas those constructed after expository reading tended to reflect a hierarchy-based structure organized by logical relations among concepts. In addition, high-performing readers constructed networks with higher transitivity and clustering coefficient, and greater similarity to the expert reference network, indicating stronger structural organization. Low-performing readers' networks showed weaker or more fragmented organization and lower similarity to the expert reference network. Conclusions This study extends the assessment based on knowledge structure to book-length reading and shows that semantic networks can capture the structural quality of students' understanding after extended reading. This approach offers a promising framework for diagnostic assessment and targeted reading instruction.

items.title: Factors Associated With Satisfaction and Perceived Change Among University Students After Implementing Care Practices to Address Psychological Distress.
items.abstract: Introduction Entering university symbolizes a sudden transition for most students, who are faced with an unfamiliar environment, new demands, and adaptations associated with individual and collective expectations regarding entry into higher education, which may be linked to the onset of psychological distress. Objective To analyze the factors associated with the repercussions of satisfaction and perceived change among university students after implementing care practices to address psychological distress. Method A cross-sectional study involving 540 students from a public federal university in Brazil. The assessment was conducted using the Patient Satisfaction with Mental Health Services Scale and the Perceived Change Scale. The analysis included descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression models, with p Results Higher scores for satisfaction and perceived change were associated with participation in activities such as Circle Dance and psychological counseling, as well as with sense of belonging to the campus. In contrast, students who self-identified as Indigenous, of "Other" gender, in their fourth year of study and those who required housing assistance and social services had lower mean scores on the scales. Conclusion Participating in care practices promotes well-being and adaptation. However, initiatives must account for the pre-existing vulnerability of minority and socioeconomically disadvantaged groups, whose continued enrollment requires ongoing institutional support.

items.title: A cross-study single-cell atlas reveals heterogeneous transcriptional states in PMA-differentiated THP-1 cells.
items.abstract: THP-1 cells are widely used to model human monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation, yet the transcriptional states associated with the labels "undifferentiated" and "differentiated" may vary among studies. We uniformly reprocessed six public THP-1 single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets comprising 149,648 cells from two studies of undifferentiated cells and four studies of PMA-differentiated macrophage-like cells. A Harmony-based joint embedding was used for visualization, while state-associated expression was interpreted primarily through effect sizes and consistency across datasets because differentiation status was confounded with study background and cells were not independent biological replicates. The two undifferentiated sources shared high S100A8, S100A9, LYZ and VCAN expression. In contrast, differentiated datasets retained these markers to different degrees, demonstrating that the "differentiated" label did not denote a uniform transcriptional state. Undifferentiated cells also contained proliferative, interferon-responsive and inflammatory sub-states. Two independent bulk RNA-seq time courses showed progressive induction of CD14 after PMA exposure. Exploratory in-house bulk expression, immunostaining and nuclear morphometry were directionally consistent with a monocytic THP-1 phenotype but were not treated as replicated validation experiments. These results provide a cross-study reference for assessing THP-1 state heterogeneity and support direct measurement of differentiation markers in each experiment rather than reliance on protocol labels alone. items.title: Estimating PM<sub>2.5</sub> Concentration in Ho Chi Minh City Using Sentinel-5P and Machine Learning on Google Earth Engine (GEE).
items.abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) pollution poses serious public health risks in Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC), Vietnam, where monitoring infrastructure is limited to only four certified stations. This study integrates Sentinel-5P atmospheric composition products, ERA5 meteorological reanalysis, and MODIS-derived parameters within the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform to capture both primary and secondary PM 2.5 formation processes. Four machine learning (ML) models were compared: multiple linear regression, random forest, gradient boosting, and XGBoost. The XGBoost model achieved the best predictive performance (R² = 0.784, MAE = 2.53 µg/m³), enabling spatially continuous PM 2.5 mapping across the city. The estimated annual mean concentration of 21.55 ± 0.92 µg/m³ exceeded the WHO air quality guideline (5 µg/m³) by a factor of approximately 4.3, confirming widespread exposure to hazardous levels. This scalable framework supports pollution monitoring and public health risk assessment in conditions of changing urban green space and thermal environment for the former HCMC.

items.title: Fentanyl Concentrations in Vancouver's Unregulated Opioid Supply after Drug Decriminalization: A Controlled Interrupted Time-Series Study.
items.abstract: In January 2023, the province of British Columbia, Canada, implemented a 3-year pilot to decriminalize personal possession of selected drugs below a cumulative threshold of 2.5 g. Concerns arose that pressure to carry less and remain under the legal limit could result in increased concentrations of the potent opioid fentanyl in unregulated opioids. We sought to examine if the onset of decriminalization was associated with changes to the average fentanyl concentration in unregulated opioids in the city of Vancouver. Using drug checking data from Vancouver and the jurisdictional control of Toronto, Ontario, we performed a controlled interrupted time-series analysis modelling the monthly ratio of median fentanyl concentrations in opioid samples (Vancouver divided by Toronto) as a single series over a 4-year period (February 2021 to February 2025). Across the study period, 20,331 drug checking samples were available from Vancouver and 3,145 from Toronto. At the time of policy implementation, the Vancouver-Toronto concentration ratio was estimated to immediately decrease by 0.68 (95% CI - 1.72-0.37, p = 0.20), though the result was not statistically significant. Similarly, there was no significant difference in the monthly rate of change in the ratio before versus after decriminalization (0.06, 95% CI - 0.05-0.17, p = 0.27). Multiple sensitivity analyses indicated robustness of results. Fentanyl concentrations in both cities followed aligned temporal patterns and the relative trajectory of fentanyl concentrations between Vancouver and Toronto did not meaningfully diverge following decriminalization. Findings suggest that decriminalization was unlikely to have altered the strength of the unregulated opioid supply.

items.title: What Traditional Assessments Miss: A Perspective on Invisible Assets in Community Health.
items.abstract: Community needs assessments (CNAs) have historically taken a deficit approach that reveals gaps in resource allocation and distribution, while not giving the same attention to the strengths that communities possess. Asset mapping has challenged that practice but remains underutilized as a necessary component in community health assessments. This perspective paper argues for pairing participatory asset mapping with CNAs to capture the emic perspectives. Additionally, this paper defines invisible assets, discusses why they matter for under-resourced communities, and the factors that contribute to their development. Rather than relying solely on tangible resources, systemic disinvestment compels these communities to develop alternative survival strategies. Traditional assessments miss this, generating an incomplete picture of community health by underemphasizing informal, place-based, community-driven solutions. Standardizing the identification of invisible assets shifts assessments toward strength-based models, guiding policymakers, public health professionals, and funding to reinforce existing local capacity rather than disrupting beneficial systems communities have already established.

items.title: Cost-effectiveness of respiratory syncytial virus vaccines in post-marketing settings: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory infections, hospitalizations, and deaths, particularly among infants and older adults worldwide. This study aims to summarize cost-effectiveness evidence by pooling incremental net benefit (INB) estimates of marketed RSV vaccines. Methods In this review, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through November 20, 2025. Grey literature and reference lists were also searched. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted separately for older adults and infants. Potential sources of heterogeneity were explored using population-specific subgroup analyses and univariable meta-regressions. Results Of the 17 studies included in the systematic review, 11 contributed to the primary meta-analysis and one additional study to sensitivity analysis only. Among older adults, the pooled INB was USD 105.05 [95% confidence interval (CI): USD 41.89-168.21; I 2 = 93.2%]. For infants, the pooled INB was USD 5.81 (95% CI: USD - 35.44-47.07; I 2 = 89.4%). In the European subgroup, the pooled INB among older adults was USD 123.63 (95% CI: USD 41.23-206.02; I 2 = 89.4%), while that for infants was USD 15.00 (95% CI: USD - 4.33-34.34; I 2 = 43.4%). Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses showed robust pooled INBs among older adults, whereas infant estimates were sensitive to study exclusion. Conclusions At the thresholds used in the included studies, RSV vaccination might be cost-effective for older adults in post-marketing settings, while the evidence for maternal vaccination remained inconclusive. Descriptive findings suggested that age- and risk-based targeting in older adults and seasonal maternal vaccination may yield higher INB estimates. Substantial between-study heterogeneity warrants cautious interpretation of the pooled estimates and highlights the need to consider local epidemiology and implementation conditions when developing RSV vaccination policies.

items.title: When It All Falls On the Physicians: A Qualitative Study of Physician Workforce Changes Post-Dobbs in Four States With Abortion Bans.
items.abstract: Objectives We aimed to explore how abortion bans in four highly restrictive states affected physician workforce dynamics among physicians of diverse specialties after the Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization decision. Methods The Medical Integrity Initiative conducted in-depth interviews with physicians in Alabama, Idaho, Oklahoma, and Tennessee, states with strict abortion bans and severe legal penalties for physicians. Participants included specialists in emergency medicine, maternal-fetal medicine, medical genetics, obstetrics, oncology, and reproductive endocrinology and infertility. We used stratified and snowball sampling and conducted interviews via Zoom from July to October 2024. Grounded theory methodology informed the inductive approach to data analysis. We began with open (descriptive) coding and followed it with axial (interpretive) analysis. Results Thirty-two physicians across all specialties reported new challenges following the Dobbs decision. We identified the following overarching themes: 1) heightened liability concerns, 2) shifting burden of care onto academic hospitals, 3) added advocacy responsibilities, 4) emotional strain and ethical dilemma of leaving the state, and 5) increased challenges regarding workforce size and workload. Challenges that participants described included colleagues' exodus, difficulty recruiting providers and trainees, and labor and delivery unit closures. Many reported that they considered leaving their state. Participants expressed a desire for their institutions to support evidence-based clinical practice. Conclusion Physicians experienced changes in workforce composition and responsibilities following the Dobbs decision. Collective action and robust occupational, legal, and mental health support from their institutions and medical societies might enable physicians to safely stay and sustainably advocate in states with abortion bans.

items.title: Azole resistance in Aspergillus series Nigri and possible link with environmental selection route.
items.abstract: Background Resistance to medical azoles has been well investigated in Aspergillus fumigatus, which is primarily driven by exposure to azole fungicides. Azole resistance selection in other Aspergillus species remains understudied. We investigated azole resistance selection in Aspergillus series Nigri. Methods 165 clinical series Nigri isolates were collected from Dutch and Belgian hospitals and 77 environmental isolates were obtained from air and other environmental sources, including known hotspots for azole resistance selection. Isolates were screened for resistance to medical azoles and selected fungicides using the EUCAST microbroth dilution reference method. Epidemiological cut-off values were used to identify non-wildtype isolates. All isolates were subjected to whole-genome sequencing, and global sequence databases were used for population genomic analyses. Clinical information was collected for azole-resistant isolates. Findings Aspergillus tubingensis was the dominant species lineage among the clinical isolates (120/165, 72·7%), whereas species of the A. niger lineage were more frequently identified in environmental samples (55/78, 70·5%). Overall A. tubingensis isolates showed higher minimum inhibitory concentrations than A. niger isolates; 27 clinical isolates (17·0%) showed a non-wildtype phenotype for medical azoles as well as 24 of 78 (30·8%) environmental isolates. Sequencing revealed a worldwide distribution of multiple clonal groups. Cross resistance between medical azoles and azole fungicides was observed in A. tubingensis lineage isolates, which were recovered from hotspots, air and patient samples. Pan-azole resistant A. tubingensis was recovered from five mould-active azole-naïve patients, including a patient with proven invasive aspergillosis. Interpretation Our study shows azole resistance in A. tubingensis lineage isolates and evidence that supports environmental resistance selection. Population genomics indicate a risk of global migration of resistant clones in A. tubingensis. Next to confirmative studies regarding black aspergilli, mycobiome analysis of hotspots are needed to identify potential selection of intrinsic or acquired resistant fungal species that may cause infections.

items.title: Emergencies at Sea: Sudden Death on Cruise Ships For the BELTRAN Study (BaskEtbaLl and soccer sTadiums: Registry on Automatic exterNal defibrillators).
items.abstract: Sudden death on cruise ships represents a rare but critical public health and medical concern, occurring in a uniquely resource-limited, geographically isolated environment, with delayed access to definitive hospital care. This narrative review aimed to synthesize current evidence on the incidence, causes, circumstances, and response systems related to sudden death on cruise ships, and to examine the medical, logistical, legal, and public health frameworks relevant to these events. A literature search of PubMed, MEDLINE, and EMBASE was conducted using terms related to sudden death and cruise ships, with inclusion of English-language studies from 2010 to 2025. Results suggest that sudden death on cruise ships is rare, with reported mortality estimates of approximately 1.8 deaths per 100,000 cruise passengers. Research highlights that deaths occurring among passengers are predominantly due to natural causes, especially cardiovascular disease, including myocardial infarction and cardiac arrest. Factors such as delayed diagnosis, limited onboard diagnostic capacity, and barriers to timely evacuation have been noted to contribute to preventable mortality. However, deaths occurring among crew are predominantly due to traumatic deaths, particularly falls overboard, and suicide, which calls for increased safety measures and better mental health support for crew. Substantial variability remains in standards for onboard medical response, including accessibility of automated external defibrillator (AED) availability, cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training, and emergency preparedness. Overall, the findings highlight the need for stronger cardiac emergency protocols, broader AED deployment, enhanced crew training, improved telemedicine and medevac coordination, and regulatory frameworks to reduce preventable deaths at sea.

items.title: Using hip-worn accelerometer non-wear time to assess sleep duration and sleep midpoint.
items.abstract: We sought to validate non-wear time of accelerometers worn on the hip for all waking hours as an estimate of sleep duration and midpoint. If valid, this may allow research studies to leverage previously collected physical activity data for sleep research. In 2019-2023, 21,325 Cancer Prevention Study-3 participants (mean age 58 years, SD=9.8) were provided a hip-worn accelerometer and sleep diaries for a week. Time in bed (TIB) was defined as the duration of non-wear time between two consecutive wear days (e.g. wear on Monday and Tuesday correspond to Monday night sleep). A total of 17,855 participants had at least 3 weekday and 1 weekend sleep measurements. Bland-Altman plots compared TIB and midpoint calculated from accelerometer non-wear and from sleep diaries. Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated for TIB to assess convergent validity, and a Two One-Sided Test (TOST) was calculated for midpoint to assess equivalence (± 15 minutes). Participants were mostly non-Hispanic white (87%) and female (77%). On average, TIB was 41.1 (SD=44.6) minutes longer on weekdays (r = 0.72) and 41.3 (SD=61.0) minutes longer on weekend days (r = 0.67) compared to sleep diary. Accelerometry sleep midpoint was 1.3 minutes earlier compared to diary on weekdays and 1.6 minutes later on weekends (TOST p-value < 0.01). TIB calculated from non-wear time of hip accelerometry demonstrated convergent validity with sleep duration assessed from sleep diary. Midpoint based on non-wear time was equivalent to sleep diary.

items.title: Polystyrene nanoplastics enhance the environmental persistence and toxic effects of chlortetracycline by inhibiting its photodegradation.
items.abstract: Beyond their effects on fate of antibiotics in aquatic environments, nanoplastics (NPs) can also influence photodegradation and biological hazards of antibiotics, which remain poorly understood. This study demonstrated that PS NPs can suppress chlortetracycline (CTC) photodegradation, with decreasing photodegradation rate constant from 0.0132 to 0.0110 min ‒1 . In detail, the PS NPs inhibited direct photodegradation pathway of CTC via light-shielding effects and inhibitory effect of PS-DOM, while concurrently promote indirect photodegradation through reactive species generated (eg., O 2 •- , •OH, 1 O 2 and 3 PS*). Accordingly, the PS NPs yielded distinct transformation products, some of which exhibited toxicity significantly exceeding that of the parent compound, thereby causing severe toxicity effects, as manifested by growth inhibition and elevated intracellular ROS levels toward E. coli. Notably, such suppression of CTC photodegradation by PS NPs was also observed in different natural waters, where it was even more pronounced, as reflected by photodegradation rate constant decreasing from 0.0132 to 0.0052 min ‒1 . Consequently, the PS NPs could significantly enhance both the environmental persistence and toxic effects of CTC in natural waters, thereby aggravating its ecological risks. Ultimately, this study suggests that the coexistence and combined effects of nanoplastics should be carefully considered when assessing the fate and ecological risks of antibiotics in aquatic environments.

items.title: Time-series modelling and forecasting of acute watery diarrhoea (AWD) in the Gaza Strip before and during the war in October 2023.
items.abstract: Objectives This study aims to evaluate the temporal consistency and plausibility of manually collected data on acute watery diarrhoea (AWD) consultations reported by UNRWA staff based in Gaza and Cairo relative to the historical surveillance baseline. Further, the study aims to show the impact of the war in the Gaza Strip that began in October 2023 and the massive forced displacement of the Gaza population from Rafah governorate on the shape of the AWD curve. Study design We used epidemiological modelling with time-series analysis and forecasting. Methods Negative Binomial Regression was chosen based on the results of over-dispersion test. We obtained data prior to the war from UNRWA's electronic health system, while the health team (HT) collected data during the war manually during the war, and the Gaza office in Cairo audited them. We used October 7, 2023, and the Rafah mass incursion in late May (Epidemiological week 22) as cut-off points for forecasting. Results The regression model showed good reliability in trend prediction, though confidence declined during the war. Decomposition revealed a hump-shaped trend between 2023 and 2025, with descriptive seasonality and notable white noise. The model adequately addressed overdispersion in the weekly counts but did not completely capture their short-term temporal correlation. The outbreak prediction model showed an exponential rise in cases at the onset of the war. Forecasts exhibited similar trends between observed and predicted data before and after the cut-off points. Conclusions The analysis supports the accuracy and credibility of the reported data during the catastrophic humanitarian conditions and acknowledges the efforts of UNRWA Gaza HT. Time series analysis is a robust method for evaluating and interpreting humanitarian data.

items.title: Preparing nurse scientists to translate evidence into policy impact.
items.abstract: Background Nurse scientists generate evidence that could meaningfully shape health policy, yet many nurse scientists are not explicitly prepared to translate research into policy impact. Purpose and methods This invited paper builds on the authors' keynote presentation at the 2025 State of the Science Conference on Preparing Nurse Scientists to Create Policy Change. Using examples from nursing science and the lead author's career trajectory, we discuss strategies for translating evidence into policy impact and introduce career cartography as a framework for intentionally building careers that advance such impact. Throughout, we use the term policy impact to refer broadly to the ways evidence influences agendas, decision-making, implementation efforts, organizational practices, public discourse, and legislation. Stakeholder engagement refers to meaningful involvement of individuals and groups affected by an issue, as well as those positioned to act on the evidence, including community members, practitioners, organizational leaders, advocates, and policymakers. Discussion Nurse scientists can increase their potential for policy impact by intentionally aligning training, research, relationships, and dissemination activities with long-term policy goals. Seeking experiences in policy, advocacy, community, and interdisciplinary settings can strengthen the skills, relationships, and confidence needed to translate evidence into policy impact. Career Cartography provides a framework for identifying and leveraging these opportunities throughout a career. Conclusion Preparing nurse scientists for policy impact requires intentional career mapping, stakeholder engagement, and communication strategies that position evidence to inform policy and practice.

items.title: Developmental pathways of online grooming victimisation: Understanding adolescent vulnerability.
items.abstract: Adolescents increasingly engage with digital environments as a central part of their daily lives. While digital environments offer valuable opportunities, they also expose young users to risks, such as online grooming, a manipulative process in which adults build deceptive relationships with minors for sexual exploitation. Recent policy debates in Europe have reignited concern over the need to regulate adolescents' Internet use, especially given their developmental vulnerabilities. This study aimed to identify psychological, behavioural, relational, and contextual factors associated with online grooming victimisation in adolescents and to explore how these vulnerabilities vary across developmental stages, informing prevention strategies. Data were collected from 240 Portuguese adolescents aged 12-19 in schools in Porto, Portugal. A quantitative cross-sectional design was used. Online grooming victimisation was coded as a dichotomous outcome based on reported grooming-related experiences. Individual, relational, behavioural, and victimisation factors were analysed. Descriptive analyses, group comparisons, and binary logistic regression models were conducted for the overall sample and separately by developmental group. Three predictors of online grooming victimisation emerged: risky online behaviours (OR = 1.21; 95% CI[1.10, 1.33]; p < .001), gender (OR = 2.49; 95% CI[1.22, 5.06]; p = .012), and (cyber)bullying (OR = 2.21; 95% CI[1.19, 4.10]; p = .012). Age-stratified models showed developmentally contingent vulnerability: early adolescence involved behavioural exposure, experiences of (cyber)bullying, and gendered vulnerability, whereas in later adolescence, risk was associated with risky online behaviours. Prevention should adopt age-sensitive approaches addressing behavioural exposure, victimisation, and gendered vulnerability.

items.title: A practical evaluation of finite-sample BOIN calibration and Bayesian smoothing in phase I dose finding.
items.abstract: We evaluated an asymmetric loss-based BOIN boundary and a monotone Bernstein estimator. The boundary preserved lookup-table operation but did not improve correct selection uniformly in seven monotone scenarios. It reduced overdose selection relative to BOIN, aBOIN, and gBOINS in six. Its accuracy depended on MTD position and overdose aversion. Bernstein selection reduced accuracy in most scenarios, especially for middle and high MTDs. Reference MCMC showed that importance-sampling error did not explain these losses. Target-based elimination eventually removes a repeatedly sampled MTD when toxicity exceeds the target. An upper-equivalence-bound threshold avoids this asymptotic conflict but not finite-sample elimination. Standard BOIN should remain the default. The loss-based boundary is justified only when the protocol prespecifies overdose avoidance and calibration shows an acceptable tradeoff. The Bernstein estimator is not recommended in its present form.

items.title: Recent Advancements in Bio-Derived Fuels: Technological Pathways and Data-Driven Intelligence.
items.abstract: Bio-derived fuel refers to biofuels produced from organic materials originating from biomass or biowaste, industrial byproducts, municipal wastes, and animal effluents. To date, no single technology utilizes biomass and biowaste effectively to maximize bioenergy generation, as these technologies are at varying levels of technical and economic maturity. This review critically compares direct combustion, pyrolysis, transesterification, fermentation, and anaerobic digestion, together with mechanical, physicochemical, chemical, and biological pretreatment methods. Technologies of converting biomass and biowaste into bioenergy were critically evaluated based on conversion efficiency, processing time, energy density, emissions, technological maturity, and economic feasibility. Conventional and modern technologies for bio-derived fuels were reviewed in terms of processing time, energy density, emissions, and cost. Biorefinery and bio-derived fuel properties were compared with those of non-renewable fuels. The review highlights advanced approaches for process optimization, bioreactor stability, and bio-product improvement. Integrated biorefineries capable of co-processing multi-biomass and biowaste represent key future opportunities for producing multiple fuels and value-added co-products.

items.title: Dietary Clostridium butyricum NCU-02 and Its Postbiotic Butyrate Ameliorate Autism Spectrum Disorder-like Symptoms: Involvement of Hippocampal Oxidative Stress Modulation.
items.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition closely linked to gut microbiota dysbiosis and gut-brain axis dysfunction, yet effective dietary interventions remain limited. This study evaluated the therapeutic potential of Clostridium butyricum NCU-02, a probiotic candidate, and its sterile supernatant in a valproic acid (VPA)-induced mouse model of ASD, with emphasis on their postbiotic properties. Both treatments significantly ameliorated core ASD-like behaviors, attenuating repetitive marble-burying by over 35% and restoring social novelty preference to near-control levels (p < 0.05 for both). These interventions were associated with improved intestinal barrier integrity, upregulated tight junction proteins (ZO-1 and occludin), and suppressed colonic and hippocampal pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α). Metabolomics profiling identified butyrate as a key differential metabolite, with butyrate levels elevated by approximately 1.3- to 2.5-fold following interventions (all p < 0.05 vs. M group). Correlation analyses further linked butyrate elevation to activation of the hippocampal GPR109A/AMPK/Nrf2 pathway and reduction of oxidative stress markers. Collectively, these findings suggest that C. butyricum NCU-02 and its sterile supernatant are associated with protective effects against ASD-like symptoms, and that the postbiotic metabolite butyrate may contribute to these benefits through dual modulation of gut homeostasis and neuroprotective signaling. A sodium-butyrate comparison group reproduced several of these effects, indicating that exogenous butyrate is sufficient to reproduce several of these effects, although the present design does not establish butyrate as a necessary mediator for the live-strain effects. These findings position butyrate, and butyrate-producing probiotics, as promising candidates for dietary intervention in neurodevelopmental disorders.

items.title: Association between Brain Amyloid Status and Cognitive and Physical Performance in Older Adults with Frailty Criteria: Longitudinal Data from the CogFrail Study.
items.abstract: Background The impact of cerebral amyloid pathology on cognitive and functional decline may differ with age. Evidence linking brain amyloidopathy to physical decline remains limited and inconsistent. This study investigated the association between brain amyloid status and cognitive and physical decline in (pre)frail older adults with cognitive impairment. Methods This longitudinal analysis used data from the CogFrail study. Brain amyloid pathology was assessed using amyloid-positron emission tomography (visual reading). Linear mixed-effects models examined differences over a two-year follow-up between amyloid-positive and amyloid-negative participants in cognitive, functional, and physical trajectories. Cognitive and functional outcomes included the Mini-Mental State Examination, the Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes, the Activities of Daily Living Index, and a neuropsychological battery, while the physical domain was assessed using handgrip strength, chair rise time, gait speed, and the Short Physical Performance Battery. Results Among 199 participants (mean age 82.3 ± 4.8 years; 65.3% women), 108(54.3%) were amyloid-positive. Amyloid-positive participants experienced greater decline in the Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (β = 0.30, 95% CI 0.10-0.49; p = 0.003, log-transformed) and the Mini-Mental State Examination (β = -1.62, 95% CI -2.74 to -0.49; p = 0.005). No significant longitudinal differences were observed between groups in the Activities of Daily Living Index, neuropsychological outcomes, or physical performance measures. Conclusion Amyloid pathology assessment may help differentiate cognitive trajectories in cognitively impaired (pre)frail older adults. Greater cognitive decline in amyloid-positive participants was not associated with greater loss of independence or additional physical decline over time. Trial registration NCT03129269.

items.title: From Consumption to Harm: Socioeconomic Inequalities and Recovery Models in Addiction.
items.abstract: Introduction Socioeconomic inequalities shape substance use (SU) and treatment utilisation across Europe. However, substance-use prevalence and treatment admissions may show different socioeconomic distributions. Spain offers a valuable setting to examine these regional patterns using national data sources. Methods We conducted an ecological, cross-sectional analysis across the 17 Spanish autonomous communities, integrating data on SU, treatment admissions, income and mental health indicators (2022-2024). Socioeconomic inequalities were quantified using the slope index of inequality and the concentration index. Ordinary least-squares models assessed associations between income and SU prevalence or treatment admission rates, and spatial autocorrelation was evaluated. Results Alcohol use in the past 30 days showed a positive income gradient (slope index of inequality 6.29 percentage points; +1.25 percentage points per €1,000; p<0.001), as did cannabis use in the past 12 months. In contrast, daily tobacco smoking was more prevalent in lower-income regions. More than 70% of publicly recorded SUD treatment admissions occurred in regions within the lowest-income terciles, and treatment-admission rates decreased by 8.9 admissions per 100,000 inhabitants for each €1,000 increase in income (p=0.015). Significant but weak negative spatial autocorrelation was observed. Conclusion Spain shows opposing socioeconomic gradients in regional substance-use prevalence and publicly recorded treatment admissions. Alcohol and cannabis use were more common in higher-income regions, whereas treatment-admission rates were higher in lower-income regions. These population-level patterns should be interpreted cautiously because public surveillance does not comprehensively capture private-sector treatment.

items.title: Cultural Adaptation of an Intervention Guide for a Non-pharmacological Palliative Care Intervention for People With Advanced Dementia: A Multi-Stakeholder Process Preparatory to the International In-Touch Trial.
items.abstract: Effective, internationally transferable interventions for people with advanced dementia are needed to enhance consistent, high-quality care and quality of life. The international In-Touch project includes a cluster randomised controlled trial of an intervention to improve the quality of life for people with advanced dementia within nursing homes. A structured cultural adaptation process is crucial to ensure the In-Touch intervention retains core principles while improving local feasibility and acceptability, thereby enabling a clear assessment of fidelity. Here, we detail the cultural adaptation of the 'In-Touch Practical Guide for Nursing Home Staff' to enhance its feasibility, usability, and relevance across nursing homes in seven European countries. A structured cultural adaptation process, inspired by the ADAPT framework, was guided by an international team of experts, including individuals with lived experience, and dementia and palliative care researchers. Within-country group interviews were conducted in the Czech Republic, Ireland, Italy, Poland, Portugal, the Netherlands and the UK with three key participant groups: (1) nursing home staff familiar with intervention components, (2) nursing home staff unfamiliar with the intervention, and (3) family carers of people with advanced dementia. Participants ( n = 97) evaluated the guide's clarity, cultural appropriateness, and feasibility. Cross-country consensus is presented here, with key themes including the need to simplify the guide to improve usability, ensure accessible language for all staff levels, and introduce discussion of flexibility in session length, structure, and available spaces to align with nursing home routines. Clearer guidance was needed on the roles of volunteers and family members. The guide was refined into a single, adaptable version, optimising its cultural relevance, usability, and practicality across diverse European settings. This collaborative adaptation process led to a culturally sensitive guide optimised for use in the In-Touch trial across Europe. The outlined methods can help adapt other interventions for future international palliative care research.

items.title: Infant Linear Anthropometry at 6 Months Following Maternal Moringa oleifera -Royal Jelly Compared With Multiple Micronutrient Supplementation: A Follow-Up Study With Exploratory Gut Microbiota Analyses.
items.abstract: BackgroundMaternal nutrition during pregnancy may influence infant growth, while the developing gut microbiota may represent an additional biological correlate of early-life nutritional status. Evidence comparing food-based maternal supplementation with multiple micronutrient supplementation (MMS) in relation to infant linear anthropometry remains limited.ObjectiveTo compare 6-month linear anthropometric outcomes between maternal Moringa oleifera enriched with royal jelly (MRJ) and MMS groups and to explore associations between selected gut bacteria and length-for-age z-score (LAZ).MethodsThis 6-month follow-up included 88 infants (MRJ, n = 42; MMS, n = 46) from a randomized maternal supplementation trial. Infant length and LAZ were compared using linear regression, with additional adjustment for birth length. Stunting was examined descriptively. Five prespecified bacterial genera were quantified by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction, and their associations with LAZ were explored using multivariable regression.ResultsAfter adjustment for birth length, no significant differences were observed between MRJ and MMS in infant length (β = -0.24 cm; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.35 to 0.87; P = .66) or LAZ (β = 0.11; 95% CI, -0.36 to 0.59; P = .64). Stunting occurred in 4.8% and 15.2% of infants, respectively. Higher Clostridium (β = -0.114; P = .02) and Lactobacillus (β = -0.163; P = .03) abundances were associated with lower LAZ in adjusted exploratory analyses.ConclusionsLinear anthropometric outcomes at 6 months did not differ significantly between the MRJ and MMS groups. Higher Clostridium and Lactobacillus abundances were cross-sectionally associated with lower LAZ and require confirmation in longitudinal studies.

items.title: Pharmacological modulation of the striatal mGluR5-NR2B association attenuates L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia in 6-OHDA lesioned parkinsonian rats.
items.abstract: Objective: The clinical utility of L-DOPA is severely limited by the development of L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia (LID). Although metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5) antagonists alleviate LID, the underlying molecular mechanisms, particularly those involving striatal glutamate receptor crosstalk, remain incompletely understood. Methods: Adult female Sprague-Dawley rats with unilateral 6-OHDA lesions were randomized into Sham, PD, LID, MTEP, and MK-801 groups (n=6/group). L-DOPA/benserazide was given twice daily for 14 days, with MTEP or MK-801 30 min before each dose. AIMs, open-field activity, striatal mGluR5-NR2B co-immunoprecipitation, PKC/MEK/ERK phosphorylation, and c-fos/Pdyn mRNA were assessed. Behavioral and molecular data were analyzed by mixed models, ANOVA, or Kruskal-Wallis tests. Results: We observed aberrant elevation of the mGluR5-NR2B interactions in the striatum of 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA)-lesioned parkinsonian rats exhibiting LID. Administration of the mGluR5 antagonist MTEP or the NMDA receptor antagonist MK-801 reduced the co-immunoprecipitated association, reduced the synaptic association of mGluR5 with NR2B, and markedly attenuated LID severity. Mechanistically, the decoupling of these receptors was accompanied by decreased ERK1/2 phosphorylation, reduced PKC protein expression, and decreased L-DOPA-induced c-fos and prodynorphin mRNA levels. Furthermore, abnormal involuntary movement (AIM) scores significantly correlated with the extent of NR2B-mGluR5 interaction and downstream signaling activation. These findings suggest that increased mGluR5-NR2B association is associated with LID and may contribute to its expression. Conclusion: The therapeutic efficacy of MTEP or MK-801 is likely mediated by reducing this receptor interaction and downstream signaling, highlighting a potential molecular target for LID treatment.

items.title: Cohabiting microbes can impact one another's mutation rates creating a mutational eco-evo feedback loop
items.abstract: Eco-evolutionary feedbacks are typically thought to require an ecological change driving Darwinian selection. However, ecology can drive other evolutionary mechanisms too. In many microbial species mutation rates are elevated at low population density, mediated by nutrient availability and reactive oxygen species (ROS). These findings from monoculture populations led us to hypothesise that the presence and density of a cohabiting species will also affect mutation rates. Using Escherichia coli as a focal species we explore the mutational effects on both parties of co-culture with either Enterococcus faecalis or Pseudomonas aeruginosa. These species co-occur in multiple clinical settings and have different abilities to degrade ROS. In both co-culture systems we find evidence that the presence of a stronger ROS degrader reduces mutation rates in the weaker ROS degrading species. At the same time increasing population density of the weaker ROS degrader increases mutation rates in the stronger ROS degrading species. Simultaneous mutation rate estimation in co-cultured species raises multiple experimental challenges addressed here. Despite these challenges, we find evidence for a novel form of eco-evo feedback in which the environment shapes the supply of mutational variation to the population. This in turn feeds back to alter the chance of evolutionary rescue for one species or another during a subsequent environmental change. Such effects potentially matter not only for our fundamental understanding of the interplay between ecology and evolution, but for the treatment of polymicrobial infections in which rates of resistance evolution may be altered by the cross-species mutational effects of cohabiting species.

items.title: Seed dispersal in a Landscape of Fear: a review of rodent foraging decisions under predation risk.
items.abstract: Rodents play a dual role in plant regeneration, acting both as seed predators and dispersers. Their foraging decisions are shaped by the trade-off between food acquisition and predation risk, a dynamic conceptualized within the Landscape of Fear framework. Despite numerous studies, the role of perceived predation risk across the multiple stages of rodent-mediated seed dispersal remains poorly understood. We reviewed 168 studies to investigate how risk perception influences rodents' foraging behaviour and the consequences for seed dispersal. We identified five major take-home messages. (1) The influence of perceived predation risk has been investigated unevenly across the seed dispersal process, with foraging site selection being the best-understood stage; (2) perceived predation risk can be easily manipulated, facilitating the interpretation of small mammals behavioural responses; (3) rodents mainly modify their decisions according to indirect cues of predation risk (e.g., vegetation cover and illumination), whereas direct cues have weaker and more variable effects; (4) outcomes of seed selection under predation risk are inconsistent, reporting both species-specific feeding habits and context-dependent strategies; (5) the majority of studies lacked individual identification of animals, potentially undermining data independence and possibly introducing bias. We argue that future research should adopt experimental designs that simultaneously address risk perception (and the various factors affecting it) and seed dispersal (across its multiple stages), as well as incorporating individual-level predictors. Such approaches are crucial to elucidate how fear shapes the outcome of rodent-plant interaction and, ultimately, ecosystem functioning.

items.title: When do students seek AI help? Exploring within-person and between-person differences
items.abstract: Research on student AI use typically asks who adopts these tools, treating use as a stable trait. Yet students face a fresh decision at every problem. We examined how much AI use reflects stable individual differences and how much varies within a student across tasks. Undergraduates (N = 398) at two institutions completed 30 quiz trials, choosing on each trial to answer independently, consult an AI chatbot, or rely on an AI-generated answer. Students rated their topic expertise before each decision; cognitive abilities, AI attitudes, and demographics were also measured. Choices were analysed with Bayesian multilevel multinomial logistic regression. With moderately reliable AI, about half the variance in AI use reflected stable individual differences (intraclass correlations of 41% for chatbot use, 48% for full reliance); the remainder varied within individuals across trials. Self-assessed expertise accounted for this within-person variation: students sought help primarily when they felt unknowledgeable. Fluid intelligence predicted more chatbot consultation but less full delegation. Male students and those with more favourable AI attitudes delegated more readily. AI use is better described as adaptive help-seeking than as a fixed trait. Interventions targeting metacognitive calibration may prove more effective than blanket policies assuming uniform use.

items.title: Current and future climatic suitability of Sonchus arvensis and Xylella fastidiosa under climate change scenarios
items.abstract: Abstract Invasive species and plant diseases threaten global food security and the health of plants. Species Distribution Models (SDMs) were utilised to pinpoint areas of highest suitability for Sonchus arvensis and Xylella fastidiosa in both current and future scenarios, considering possible climate change, and to determine the primary environmental factors affecting the suitability of these species. We apply the maximum entropy algorithm to forecast future conditions for 2050 and 2070, utilising the SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios. Sonchus arvensis has an initial 10,190 records and Xylella fastidiosa has an initial 1195 records. The best model for S. arvensis (RM = 2; FC = LQH) gave TSS = 0.58 and Boyce = 0.94. The best model for X. fastidiosa (RM = 5; FC = H) gave TSS = 0.62 and Boyce = 0.97. The primary variables in the selected model were Bio1 (average yearly temperature) and Bio12 (yearly rainfall). For S. arvensis , forecasts suggest a decrease in favourable regions throughout the eastern United States, Europe, and South Asia across all scenarios analysed. Concurrently, an expansion in climatically suitable area is projected in southern Alaska, eastern Canada, northern Europe, and central Asia. For X. fastidiosa , the species occurrence is confined to a particular region in the Middle East. At the same time, growth is anticipated in the western and northern regions of the United States, northern Europe, and both western and eastern Asia.

items.title: Optimizing nitrogen balance in facility cultivation for higher productivity and lower environmental losses under excessive N fertilization
items.abstract: Vegetable production under greenhouse often leads to severe nitrogen (N) surplus, driven largely by intensive fertilizer application and frequent nutrient supplementation to maintain higher crop yield, which holds significantly higher nitrogen input levels than that of paddy and upland fields. Less than half of N applied is absorbed by the crops, while the remaining half is surplus, causes numerous ecological issues, including increased N 2 O emissions and NH 3 volatilization, eutrophication, contamination of drinking water, damaging crop productivity. This study evaluated the effects of varying nitrogen (N) fertilization levels-low (238 kg N ha -1 ), medium (337 kg N ha -1 ), and high (720 kg N ha -1 ) on crop productivity, N uptake efficiency, and environmental losses in the facility-cultivated fields. Nitrogen inputs and outputs were quantified to determine the N balance and evaluate its potential implications for crop growth and the N losses. The N balance in facility cultivation varied from -20 to 301 kg N ha -1 depending on nitrogen input levels, primarily depending on the amount of nitrogen fertilizer applied. As N input increased, emissions of N 2 O and NH 3 to the atmosphere were also increased, while nitrogen leaching into water systems was also increased remarkably. Total yield significantly declined by 20% in the high N treatment compared to lower N applications levels, and NUE was decreased with decreasing N input. In conclusion, excessive nitrogen fertilization in facility cultivation systems poses a potential threat crop productivity, disrupt nitrogen balance and accelerate environmental concerns. These findings highlight the importance of optimizing nitrogen fertilization and maintaining a balanced N budget to minimize environmental N losses while ensuring sustainable crop production and long-term ecological sustainability of facility cultivations.

items.title: Global patterns of radial growth-structural heterogeneity relationships in forests
items.abstract: Classical theory predicts that environmental improvement intensifies competition and increases forest structural heterogeneity (variation in tree radial size). Whether warmer and wetter conditions drive convergence in stress-dominated regions remains unknown. Using a global tree-ring dataset ( > 900 sites, > 55,000 cores) with mixed-effects and mediation models, and accounting for Taylor’s law, we show that the negative growth–structure correlation is widespread, but its absolute slope increases along the stress gradient and becomes non-significant in low-stress regions (warm low-altitude, South Temperate, and tropics). Climate-to-structure pathways shift from growth-mediated in stress-dominated regions to non-significant in low-stress regions, with mediation strength increasing from temperate to alpine zones. On the Tibetan Plateau, warmer and wetter conditions are associated with homogenization via enhanced radial growth and reduced climate sensitivity. These findings challenge the classical expectation that environmental improvement inevitably increases structural heterogeneity, revealing a shift from stress-driven convergence to decoupling under low stress and providing a unified framework for predicting forest responses to climate change. Climate change can reshape forest size structure. Using tree rings from > 900 sites, the authors found warming and wetter conditions reduce tree-size inequality in high-stress regions but have little effect in low-stress forests.

items.title: deepSTRAPP : An R package to assess trait‐ and range‐dependent diversification dynamics over time
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding how diversification dynamics interact with species traits and geographical distributions over time remains a central challenge in macroevolution and biogeography. Yet the timing of these associations is rarely tested explicitly: existing approaches often focus on present‐day trait–rate relationships, or summarize over the whole history of a clade, overlooking variations in historical processes acting over deep evolutionary timescales. We introduce deepSTRAPP , an R package for assessing trait‐ and range‐dependent diversification across any temporal interval. deepSTRAPP models the evolution of traits or ranges independently of diversification rates on time‐calibrated phylogenies, extracts inferred values at user‐defined time steps and performs semi‐parametric STRAPP (Structured Rate Permutations on Phylogenies) tests based on block‐permutation to identify time windows in which diversification rates varied with species attributes. It handles continuous, categorical and biogeographic data, and includes visualization tools to explore the evolution of traits, ranges, diversification rates and the significance of their associations through time. Applied to empirical datasets, deepSTRAPP provided critical new perspectives to macroevolutionary questions inaccessible to currently available methods. It uncovered significant state‐dependent dynamics confined to restricted time windows that whole‐tree analyses overlooked, and tempered conclusions about present‐day associations that did not extend substantially back through evolutionary time. By explicitly testing for temporal variation in trait‐ and range‐dependent diversification, deepSTRAPP provides a robust framework to disentangle the relative contributions of past versus recent processes in shaping biodiversity patterns across broad phylogenetic and temporal scales.

items.title: From Multidimensional Biodiversity Patterns to Conservation Features in Systematic Conservation Planning
items.abstract: Systematic conservation planning (SCP) provides a rigorous framework for addressing conservation prioritization by combining explicit objectives, conservation features, representation targets, costs, and implementation constraints. In this article, we advocate incorporating multidimensional indices into the determination of planning-unit weights or soft penalties. Rather than directly treating the spatial patterns of multidimensional biodiversity as features within the SCP framework, this approach ensures that areas with high local genetic, phylogenetic, or functional diversity values are explicitly favored among solutions achieving comparable species targets.

items.title: Grizzly Bear Use and Selection of Ski Resorts
items.abstract: Like other anthropogenic disturbances, ski runs are both a potential source of forage and increased mortality risk for grizzly bears (Ursus arctos). To better understand how grizzly bears select for and use ski runs we assessed grizzly bear selection for ski runs, differences in use of ski areas between age-sex classes, and differences in use during nocturnal and diurnal periods. We hypothesized that bears would select for ski runs, however, due to social hierarchy between age-sex classes, the lower social classes (e.g., subadults or females) would predominately use ski runs and the area around ski lodges. We also hypothesized that to minimize risk of human interactions, use would be highest during nocturnal periods. To test the selection hypothesis, we used resource selection function (RSF) models that were developed using GPS collar data collected from 22 grizzly bears living near three ski resorts. Next, we tested for a difference in the distance of age-sex classes to ski runs and lodges and during diurnal versus nocturnal periods. Grizzly bears selected for ski runs in spring and summer. Adult females preferred to be closest to ski runs while adult males appeared to distance themselves from ski runs. Subadult males were located closer to ski lodges, while adult males were located the furthest. These results suggest ski runs provide grizzly bear habitat, but higher quality and/or more secure habitat is available elsewhere. Finally, bears were on average closer to ski lodges during nocturnal periods as compared to diurnal; however, the average difference was very small. Our results suggest that management actions implemented in the National Park and at ski resorts may be changing grizzly bear behavior as compared to previous studies. Successful management of recreational facilities to mitigate effects to grizzly bears is increasingly important as recreational facilities expand in popularity and footprint.

items.title: Spatial pattern variations in AI-generated urban park layouts under retained urban constraints
items.abstract: How generated urban park layouts respond to different conditional spatial constraints remains unclear. There are three research gaps in current research: (1) Most studies examine individual spatial elements separately and provide limited comparisons among different retained constraint types; (2) Existing park cases differ in site conditions, making it difficult to compare constraint-related spatial responses under comparable conditions; (3) How combined retained constraints modify the spatial responses associated with individual constraints remains unclear. To address these problems, we construct a constraint-conditioned comparative generative framework for urban park layouts: (1) First, establish a common environmental baseline condition and construct single- and multi-constraint generation conditions by progressively introducing internal roads, building footprints, and water bodies; (2) Secondly, use conditional GANs to generate park layouts under different constraint conditions; (3) Finally, evaluate the generated layouts using 15 Spatial Pattern Indicators and use statistical comparisons and effect-size estimation to characterize spatial responses across constraint conditions. The research results show that: (1) Differences among single-constraint configurations were most pronounced in the connectivity of walkable spaces and landscape pattern, particularly in RCC, ED, and SHEI. (2) Indicator sensitivity varied across constraint types, with some indicators showing limited responses under individual constraints but greater responses under selected combined conditions. (3) Responses to combined constraints depended on the baseline configuration, with some additional constraints producing limited changes under already constrained conditions.

items.title: Lithium, Environmental Impacts and High Andean Salt Flats in Argentina, Bolivia and Chile. An Integrative Review of Scientific Literature
items.abstract: This article reviews scientific literature on lithium mining's environmental impacts in Argentina, Bolivia, and Chile's salt flats, analyzing the period 1975-2024. The literature splits into two views: an optimistic one promoting lithium as vital for energy transition and global markets, and a critical one warning of irreversible damage to fragile ecosystems and local lifestyles. Despite growing socio-environmental interest over 50 years, knowledge gaps persist, the information on socio-environmental impacts is dispersed, with different levels of depth and rigor, and with uneven data distribution and capabilities among these countries. Chile’s Salar de Atacama, heavily researched due to mining influence, shows major impacts on water, biodiversity, and communities, yet lithium extraction continues despite insufficient data for responsible management. Additionally, much of this information does not reach local territories, and the treatment of impacts perceived by local communities remains limited, exacerbating inequalities. Unless significant innovations are made, the extraction of lithium salts from high Andean salt flats is paradoxically accelerating the socio-environmental degradation of these fragile ecosystems.

items.title: Evaluating the sustainability of shrimp aquaculture in Vietnam: stakeholder perceptions across production intensification systems
items.abstract: Purpose This study examines stakeholder perceptions of the importance of 21 sustainability themes across 4 Vietnamese shrimp farming systems. It also assesses associations between respondent characteristics and a separate ranking of perceived system sustainability. Design/methodology/approach Using the Sustainability Assessment of Food and Agriculture Systems (SAFA) Guidelines, 94 respondents each rated 21 themes across 4 systems, yielding 84 ordinal ratings per respondent. Questionnaires were administered in person to 56 respondents and completed online by 38. Theme-specific Friedman tests accounted for repeated observations, with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across 21 omnibus tests and, separately, 126 paired Wilcoxon comparisons. Cumulative-link mixed models provided an ordinal sensitivity analysis. Ridge-penalised multinomial regression examined the separate ranking outcome. Findings Differences across systems were supported for 18 of the 21 themes after adjustment for multiple testing. Corporate ethics, rule of law and biodiversity showed no supported omnibus differences. Super-intensive farming generally received the highest ratings for the importance of addressing sustainability issues. These ratings concern perceived priorities rather than measured performance. First-rank counts were 27, 7, 5 and 55 for super-intensive, intensive, semi-intensive and extensive/improved extensive/integrated systems, respectively. Age and self-reported knowledge were positively associated with selected ranking contrasts. These associations provide secondary evidence because two outcome categories were small. Research limitations/implications The purposive sample comprised 52 consumers, 36 business stakeholders and 6 experts. Its size and composition limit generalisation. Survey mode, fixed question order, unmeasured familiarity with production systems, concentrated high ratings and seven uniform response profiles may have influenced the findings. Sparse ranking categories limit prediction and practical interpretation of the multinomial model. Social implications Promoting sustainable shrimp farming systems also aligns with MARD’s approved “Sustainable aquaculture development plan in the Mekong Delta to 2030” (Decision No. 3550/QÐ-BNN-TCTS, August 2021), which aims to develop regional aquaculture sustainably. Originality/value The study applies the SAFA themes to comparisons of shrimp farming systems rated by the same stakeholders. By distinguishing the importance assigned to individual issues from an overall sustainability ranking, it explains how these two forms of judgement contribute different evidence to sustainability assessment.

items.title: Floristic and Bioecological Analysis of Saxifraga L. Species Growing in the Territory of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic
items.abstract: The present study examines the floristic composition, ecological characteristics, geographical distribution, phenology, and potential utilization of species of the genus Saxifraga L. (Saxifragaceae) occurring in the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic. The work is based on floristic literature, taxonomic sources, field observations conducted during 2024–2026, and comparison with updated nomenclatural information. Nine of the fourteen Saxifraga species reported for Azerbaijan were identified as occurring in Nakhchivan. The species are concentrated mainly in rocky habitats, crevices, stony slopes, subalpine meadows, and alpine belts. Ecological analysis classified five species as xerophytes, two as mesophytes, and two as xeromesophytes. The taxa were assigned to five areal classes, with Caucasian, European mountain, and Front Asian mountain elements predominating. The expanded interpretation emphasizes the relationship between species distribution, altitude, substrate lithology, slope exposure, and microclimatic variability. The study also outlines scientifically justified prospects for rock-garden design, ecological restoration, phytomelioration, ex situ conservation, and bioindicator research. The proposed scientific novelty lies in integrating floristic, ecological, chorological, and applied-conservation perspectives into a single regional framework, while identifying priorities for future population-genetic, molecular-taxonomic, and climate-resilience investigations.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE APPLICATIONS FOR IMPROVING PRONUNCIATION SKILLS OF AUTISTIC PATIENTS: A CRITICAL REVIEW
items.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a developmental disorder and individuals with ASD experience challenges in social relation, communication, as well as speech articulation. Many children with ASD have significant difficulty pronouncing words properly, presenting difficulties with learning at school and communicating in day-to-day situations. Recently, AI has demonstrated high potential and application value in many therapeutic and educational applications, speech and pronunciation training among others. AI systems typically integrate speech recognition, text-to-speech synthesis, automatic feedback and interactive learning environments. However, even with this progress, the existing solutions still have limitations such as limited vocabulary, lack of real-time interaction and poor adaptation to different dialects and cultural backgrounds. In this paper, a review of AI techniques that have been proposed to enhance pronunciation skills in children with ASD is offered. The review included 44 peer-reviewed articles obtained from Scopus database. We indicate current research trends, reflect existing gaps, and propose directions toward the development of more adaptive, inclusive, and cultural responsive AI-pedestal pronunciation training tools for improving communication skills and quality of life in children with ASD

items.title: Determination of the helium volume mixing ratio in Saturn’s atmosphere from a future atmospheric probe: methodology and uncertainty analysis
items.abstract: Abstract We present a methodology for determining the helium (He) volume mixing ratio (VMR) in Saturn’s atmosphere from measurements obtainable by a future atmospheric entry probe equipped with a tunable laser spectrometer (TLS) implementing wavelength modulated spectroscopy. The approach derives the He abundance as the residual of the total atmospheric pressure after accounting for molecular H 2 , CH 4 , and a small but unknown abundance of remaining trace gases. H 2 is measured via its electric quadrupole absorption lines near 2.1 μ m and CH 4 via its fundamental v 3 band near 3.3 μ m using a multi-bounce optical cavity of 10 m total path length. We develop closed-form analytical expressions for the He VMR and its propagated uncertainty, treating the trace gas contribution as a one-sided systematic bias and the measurement uncertainties on pressure, temperature, H 2 number density, and CH 4 number density as independent random errors. We demonstrate that the uncertainty budget is dominated overwhelmingly by the fractional measurement precision on the H 2 number density. For a representative probe sounding with conditions within the TLS measurement chamber at T = 200 K and P = 10 4 Pa, the total fractional uncertainty on the retrieved H 2 number density is approximately 1.2% for a single-line, single-measurement retrieval, comprised of a noise-limited contribution of ~0.33% (TLS minimum detectable fractional absorption of 10 -4 over a 10 m path), a HITRAN line-strength contribution of ≲1%, a mixture-dependent line-shape contribution of ~0.5%, and a path-length contribution of < 0.1%, combined in quadrature. With three-line profile-fit retrieval, the total error reduces to 0.8–1.1%, well within the ≲2.4% threshold needed to meet an absolute He VMR random uncertainty requirement of ≤0.02. The corresponding absolute He VMR uncertainties are $${\sigma}_{{f}_{\text{He}}}$$ ≈0.010 (single-line) and 0.007–0.009 (multi-line). These results confirm the viability of the TLS approach for He abundance determination and identify the HITRAN H 2 line-strength uncertainty and mixture-dependent line-shape physics (the latter not reducible by pre-flight calibration) as the leading systematic contributors to the residual He VMR uncertainty budget.
