items.title: hilldiv3: a unified Hill-number framework for neutral, phylogenetic and functional diversity analysis in R
items.abstract: 1. Hill numbers provide a coherent family of diversity measures that can incorporate phylogenetic relatedness and functional trait dissimilarity, but applying them consistently across neutral, phylogenetic and functional diversity, and across measurement, partitioning and (dis)similarity, still requires combining several packages with incompatible conventions. 2. We present hilldiv3, an R package that provides per-sample diversity, nested multiplicative partitioning across scales for all three diversity types, bounded (dis)similarities and pairwise matrices, diversity profiles, evenness and redundancy, and the allocation of Hill power sums and dissimilarities to taxa or taxonomic sets. 3. hilldiv3 directly supported all twelve benchmarked combinations of operation and diversity type, and built pairwise (dis)similarity matrices 15-820 times faster than hilldiv2 and hillR, with up to two orders of magnitude less memory. We showcased the package by analysing Microflora Danica data (360 samples, 5,518 genomes, eight habitats), demonstrating that neutral, phylogenetic and functional diversity turned over at very different rates between habitats, and a near-constant Actinomycetota share concealed opposing shifts of two orders. 4. By deriving every metric from the same Hill-number formulation, hilldiv3 makes neutral, phylogenetic and functional results directly comparable, and lowers the barrier to rigorous diversity analysis of community-ecology and high-throughput sequencing data.

items.title: Marsupial fossil tracks reveal Eocene arboreal life in Antarctica.
items.abstract: Antarctica is the only continent where land mammals are extinct today. Before the Eocene-Oligocene boundary (>38 million years ago), however, the "white continent" had a much milder climate that sustained a diverse fauna of terrestrial mammals. Several discoveries of fragmentary Eocene fossils suggest that Antarctica acted as a land bridge connecting South America to Australia, most notably marsupials. However, fossil mammals are scarce and restricted to a single location-Seymour Island. Here we present two well-preserved fossil tracks which are the second Antarctic fossil mammal outside Seymour Island and the oldest fossil tracks assigned to an opossum-like animal in the Cenozoic. They were found in the Fossil Hill Formation on King George Island (lower-middle Eocene) and exhibit possible opposable thumbs, suggesting an arboreal behavior observable in microbiotheriid and some extant didelphid marsupials living in South America today. They further coincide in time with the rise of scansorial lifestyle in several mammalian lineages. This ichnologic record offers a more comprehensive look into the dispersion and ecology of mammals through the Early Cenozoic of Antarctica, evidencing that small arboreal marsupials inhabited the South Shetland Islands during the Eocene. In addition, the new finding indicates that Antarctica was not merely a corridor, but a rich habitat of dense and productive forest canopies during the middle Eocene.

items.title: Lessons in ecophysiology from the model sea anemone Nematostella vectensis: a review and future directions.
items.abstract: Ecophysiology seeks to understand how the environment affects organismal processes and shapes performance. Here, we synthesize >20 years of research that explores ecophysiology using a cnidarian model, the starlet sea anemone (Nematostella vectensis). Studies using N. vectensis as a model have employed field, laboratory and computational approaches, and have commonly entailed characterizing the responses of the anemones to biotic and abiotic environmental perturbations, including pathogens, heat, hypoxia, xenobiotics and more. These investigations have encompassed life stages from embryo through adult, with readouts spanning biological scales from gene to population. As a whole, this research has expanded our knowledge of how the environment influences processes such as phenotypic plasticity and stress acclimation, reproduction and early development, and immunity and host-microbe interactions. In this Review, we synthesize this knowledge and discuss major questions in each of these research areas, highlighting insights gained from studies using N. vectensis as a model organism. We also identify open questions for future research and discuss considerations for ecophysiology-focused laboratory experiments that are particularly relevant to the use of N. vectensis as a model. Overall, continued investigations in ecophysiology making use of N. vectensis hold promise to better equip society to meet the challenges of rapid environmental changes, pollution and emerging pathogen-based diseases.

items.title: A systematic review of EC number prediction algorithms based on reaction chemical structures.
items.abstract: Motivation Enzymes catalyse most of the metabolic reactions in living organisms. The functional characterization of enzymes is critical to understand the metabolic processes involved in different fields such as biotechnology, nutrition, ecology, and drug development. The Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers provide a hierarchical framework for classifying enzymatic reactions, linking gene and protein sequences to biochemical transformations. However, the incomplete annotation of biochemical reaction databases limits the accurate representation of metabolism of living organisms. Results To address this gap, several computational methods have been developed to predict EC numbers from reaction chemical structures, broadly classified into reaction similarity-based and machine/deep learning approaches. We systematically review these tools, comparing their performance predicting EC numbers from different databases, and assessing their robustness across enzyme classes. We also apply these methods to predict EC numbers from drug metabolism reactions, highlighting their potential to improve functional annotation of uncharacterized metabolic pathways. Availability and implementation All the necessary data and code to reproduce the results of this manuscript are available within https://github.com/PlanesLab/ECNumberPrediction GitHub repository and in Zenodo https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22957403. Supplementary information Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

items.title: Recognizing and Mitigating Reference Bias in Population Genomics.
items.abstract: Most population genomic analyses require mapping sequence reads to a reference genome. Mapping to a single reference introduces reference bias, defined as either low-quality read mapping or downstream analytical distortions arising from biased mapping. Although reference bias has been repeatedly documented, its consequences remain insufficiently understood. Its impacts are particularly relevant in biodiversity genomics, where heterospecific references are commonly used to analyse entire clades. Here, we survey the literature to document where reference bias occurs, its sources, and its impacts, focusing on population and biodiversity genomics. We identify five major classes of reference-inference bias impacts: distortions in population genetic inference; alterations to phylogenetic inference; structural variant detection; RNA expression analyses; and gene presence-absence variation. Critically, the direction and magnitude of these impacts are inconsistent across studies, suggesting that generalisations are premature. Reference bias is primarily driven by evolutionary divergence between the reference genome and the mapped samples, and is further aggravated by analytical and biological factors. We suggest several mitigation strategies, including divergence-aware filtering, tool benchmarking, and standardised reporting of reference bias. In the longer term, we advocate expanding reference genome diversity and adopting pangenome-based alignment across taxa.

items.title: Seasonal differences in the sound detection ability of Arctic cod, Boreogadus saida.
items.abstract: Human activities are rapidly altering marine ecosystems, with increasing vessel traffic elevating underwater sound levels worldwide. Polar regions are particularly vulnerable, as declining sea ice has expanded access to the Arctic Ocean. Arctic cod (Boreogadus saida) is a key species that spawns under sea ice, yet its hearing ability remains entirely uncharacterised. Understanding how this species detects sound is essential for assessing the potential impacts of rising anthropogenic sound. Here, the detection sensitivity of spawning and non-spawning Arctic cod was evaluated using auditory evoked potentials (AEPs). Both groups were most sensitive to frequencies below 200 Hz when assessed using sound pressure. However, particle motion sensitivity differed markedly: spawning fish showed peak sensitivity at 400 Hz, whereas non-spawning fish were most sensitive near 90 Hz. Overall, Arctic cod exhibited significantly enhanced hearing sensitivity and an expanded detectable frequency range during spawning compared with non-spawning individuals. These results provide the first evidence of seasonal differences in auditory plasticity in a broadcast-spawning fish and highlight the potential vulnerability of Arctic cod spawning behaviour to increasing anthropogenic sound in a rapidly changing Arctic environment.

items.title: Statistical fragility in the meta-analytic evidence base of animal cognition: a meta-meta-analytic reappraisal.
items.abstract: How reliable is the meta-analytic evidence base in animal cognition? We conducted a pre-registered second-order meta-analysis of 28 published meta-analytical papers, comprising 48 eligible models and 5740 effect-size observations from primary studies. We assessed statistical power, Type M magnitude error, and Type S sign error at both primary-study and meta-analysis levels. Because these quantities depend on the assumed underlying effect, we compared the results based on uncorrected pooled effects, a regression-based bias correction, and a sensitivity analysis using a bias-robust fixed-effect model incorporating a within-study variance-covariance matrix (FE+VCV). At the primary-study level, estimated power was low under all three empirically estimated effect proxies: 17.4%, 9.0%, and 13.4%, respectively. Type M and Type S errors were also sensitive to the assumed effect and correction method. Power increased when larger externally specified effects were assumed, confirming that these quantities are conditional on the assumed effect. Meta-analysis-level results were generally more favourable but also sensitive to analytical choices. The evidence base was concentrated in experimental rodent studies of learning and memory, limiting field-wide generalisation. These findings support improving study design and reporting within the represented literature while expanding meta-analytic coverage across taxa and cognitive domains.

items.title: An interbehavioral account of culture can guide the formulation of therapeutic demands: the case of eating disorders
items.abstract: Abstract Behavior analysts frequently discuss the importance of addressing culture in psychotherapy, identifying demands such as gender-based violence, discrimination-related distress, and eating disorders as culturally loaded. A persistent epistemological tension accompanies these discussions: how to distinguish the psychological and cultural levels of analysis without severing the relation between them. This paper argues that interbehaviorism offers a way of addressing that tension, not by choosing between the two levels but by specifying what each consists of within a single field-theoretic logic. The argument is developed through eating disorders, a demand whose onset and course are well documented as sociocultural and which carries one of the highest mortality rates among mental disorders. Two complementary routes are examined. The first, following Kantor’s cultural psychology, locates culture within the psychological field by treating the foods, bodies, and evaluations to which clients respond as bearing institutional stimulus functions. The second treats the client–therapist interaction itself as a referential sociocultural event, in which both participants adjust to a shared referent through conventional forms of responding. Three implications for clinical practice follow: culture becomes identifiable within the session rather than inferred about it; the institutional functions operating for the therapist require analysis alongside the client’s; and therapeutic change can be described as the establishment of conventional functions between them.

items.title: Forty Years of The Legend of Zelda : A Scoping Review of Game Design, Computation, Culture, and Play
items.abstract: Over four decades, The Legend of Zelda has evolved from a landmark action-adventure series into a recurring object of research across game studies, computer science, musicology, cultural studies, psychology, education, and related fields. This article presents a scoping review and structured survey of Zelda-related research across the franchise’s 1986–2026 history, examining how the series has been studied as a designed system, cultural artifact, interactive narrative, audiovisual environment, player-community object, and computational testbed. Following a PRISMA-ScR-informed process with duplicate screening and full-text eligibility assessment, 93 studies were included in the final synthesis: 52 Core scholarly studies, 40 complementary scholarly/grey-literature studies, and one complementary critical/industry record. The literature is strongly recent and unevenly distributed: 65 included studies were published from 2020 onward, while 44 explicitly address either Ocarina of Time or Breath of the Wild. Narrative and worldbuilding constitute the largest thematic area, whereas technology remains comparatively underrepresented as a primary research topic. In contrast, Zelda dungeon structures have become established computational objects for procedural content generation, formal modeling, and mixed-initiative design research. A sensitivity analysis restricted to the 52-study Core scholarly corpus preserved the principal distributional patterns, indicating that the main mapping conclusions are not driven by complementary evidence. Across the reviewed traditions, a recurring pattern is the interaction among spatial design, player agency, audiovisual feedback, narrative, and increasingly interoperable game systems. The survey identifies gaps in longitudinal analysis, technical research, visual studies, localization, empirical player research, and computational models of modern three-dimensional Zelda environments, positioning the franchise as a distinctive longitudinal case for studying the relationships among game design, technology, culture, computation, and play.

items.title: Between theory and practice: Patients' experiences of payment in private psychotherapy.
items.abstract: Objective: This study explored how payment shapes patients' subjective experiences in private psychotherapy, including perceptions of commitment, treatment value, and relational dynamics with the therapist. Method: Semi-structured depth interviews were conducted with 28 adults in private therapy and analyzed using iterative thematic content analysis. Results: Five themes were identified: (i) payment shapes expectations for rapid results and therapist competence, licensing what patients feel entitled to expect; (ii) ambiguity in time-money rules creates perceived unfairness, transparency mattering more than strictness; (iii) value is weighed against alternatives and reinforced by therapist flexibility, patients constructing competing measures of worth; (iv) payment strengthens commitment and limits access, two outcomes of one ongoing calculation; and (v) discussing and handling money in-session triggers discomfort, exposing relational dynamics that usually remain implicit. Across themes, direct discussion of payment was typically confined to its practical logistics, and participants did not report instances in which its relational meaning was subsequently addressed and worked through in treatment. Conclusions: Despite theoretical recognition of money's relational significance, payment's relational meaning is rarely addressed directly in practice, generating misunderstandings, perceived unfairness, and frame violations-revealing a theory-practice gap and underscoring the need for greater attention to financial issues in training and supervision.

items.title: Short-term culture and hormone secretion analysis of prepubertal testicular tissue.
items.abstract: Lay summary Some boys with cancer or blood diseases may have a small piece of testicular tissue frozen before they start treatment, with the hope of preserving future fertility. In this study, testicular tissue from 59 boys aged 0.7 to 14.3 years was kept in a laboratory dish for a short time after biopsy. We measured whether the tissue could still release testosterone and other hormones that support germ cells that will make sperm in adulthood. The tissue of was able to release hormones after being transported from the operating room to the laboratory premises and, in some cases, even after previous chemotherapy. Hormone release was linked to the child's age and to previous treatment with a type of chemotherapy known to damage fertility. It was not clearly linked to the number of germ cells in the tissue. This suggests that hormone producing testicular cells may remain active even when germ cells are reduced. These tests may help assess tissue quality before future fertility treatments.

items.title: Development and Internal Validation of a Two-Year Prognostic Risk Index for Functional Decline in Adults Aging with HIV.
items.abstract: Introduction People with HIV (PWH) are at risk for functional decline and disability due to a complex interplay of factors, yet longitudinal studies of everyday functioning in this population are lacking. To identify individuals at risk for functional decline, we developed an internally validated, point-based prognostic risk index. Methods 742 PWH were assessed in the CNS HIV Anti-Retroviral Therapy Effects Research (CHARTER) study at five visits over two years. To select predictors of self-reported functional dependence, a binary logistic regression was performed using Akaike information criterion-guided backward stepwise selection. Model performance, discrimination, and calibration were assessed. The final model was internally validated by bootstrapping and optimism corrected. Risk index scores were generated using adjusted beta coefficients and a risk score cut-off was determined. Results Baseline predictors of functional dependence included elevated depressive symptoms, thrombocytopenia (platelets Conclusions A combination of demographics, fine motor skills, depression, and medical conditions predict functional decline. Additional studies examining external validity of the index in large, age-diverse samples of PWH with functional impairment are required before deployment in clinical settings.

items.title: 6- and 12-month test-retest score reliability and practice effects of the NIH Toolbox Cognition Battery in older Black adults with subjective cognitive decline.
items.abstract: Objective: The NIH Toolbox Cognition Battery (NIHTB-CB) is increasingly used for cognitive assessment. However, its test-retest reliability estimates over clinically meaningful intervals are understudied in older Black adults. This study examined the reliability and practice effects of NIHTB-CB composite and subtest scores over 6- and 12-month intervals in older Black adults with subjective cognitive decline. Methods: Participants were 44 community-dwelling older Black adults with subjective cognitive decline ( M age = 71.4 years, SD = 4.9; M education = 16.1 years, SD = 2.1; 93% women) who completed baseline and 6-month testing and N = 29 participants (93% women) completed 12-month testing. Intraclass correlation coefficients evaluated the reliability of uncorrected standard scores and fully corrected T-scores. Paired-samples t tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction assessed mean-level change, and Bland-Altman plots evaluated agreement. Results: At 6 months, composite-level reliability was good for Total Cognition (ICC = .76-.78) and Crystallized Cognition scores (ICC = .82-.87), and moderate for Fluid Cognition scores (ICC = .69-.72). Subtest-level reliability was more variable, with lower reliability for List Sorting and Picture Sequence Memory scores. At 12 months, significant mean improvements were observed across several composites and subtest fully corrected scores. These changes demonstrated medium paired-samples effect sizes (| d z | = 0.51-0.58). 12-month follow-up reliability estimates remained strong for composite scores, particularly for Crystallized Cognition. Conclusion: NIHTB-CB composite scores showed generally good longitudinal reliability over 6-12 months among older Black adults with subjective cognitive decline. Variable subtest reliability and possible 12-month practice effects warrant cautious interpretation when monitoring change over time.

items.title: Acute effect of moderate and higher cognitive demand HIIT on cognition in early adolescents: a cross-over trial.
items.abstract: Background High-intensity interval training (HIIT) is a potential physical activity opportunity to be integrated into educational settings for adolescents, yet little is known about the acute cognitive effects of varying cognitive load. We examined the effects of school-based HIIT involving moderate or higher cognitive demand on adolescents' acute cognitive performance. Methods Within-subject, crossover design with two HIIT conditions completed between 7-14 days apart. Adolescents (aged 11-14) completed two, four-minute HIIT bouts, designed with either moderate or higher cognitive demand. Before and after each condition, adolescents completed four brief cognitive tasks from the Mobile Monitoring of Cognitive Change platform to assess processing speed, visuospatial working memory, and response inhibition. Results Participants (N.=25) were a mean of 13.0 years-old (Standard deviation [SD] 0.8), 39% girls, and 39% overweight or obese. We observed significant time-by-condition interaction effects for visuospatial working memory (P=0.015) and processing speed (P=0.026). Visuospatial working memory worsened following higher cognitive demand HIIT (sum error distance of 18.2 pre to 28.5 post), while it improved following moderate cognitive demand HIIT (20.6 to 18.1). Processing speed reaction time improved more following moderate cognitive demand HIIT (765.7 milliseconds [ms] to 555.6 ms), compared with higher cognitive demand HIIT (716.9 ms to 703.8 ms). Conclusions The HIIT condition designed with moderate cognitive demand was associated with more favorable improvements in visuospatial working memory and processing speed compared with HIIT involving higher cognitive demand in this sample of adolescents. The overall results suggest that layering additional cognitive demands on top of HIIT exercises may attenuate acute cognitive benefits of higher-intensity physical activity, but additional studies are needed to confirm these preliminary findings.

items.title: Adaptation and psychometric evaluation of the long and short forms of the yearning in situations of loss scale in a Turkish sample.
items.abstract: Background: Yearning, the intense longing for the deceased loved one, is a hallmark symptom of prolonged grief disorder. Objective: The aim of this study was to adapt the Yearning in Situations of Loss Scale (YSL) into Turkish and to examine the psychometric properties of its long (YSL) and short forms (YSL-SF). Method: Data were collected from 500 participants used for exploratory factor analysis and an additional 445 participants for confirmatory analyses. In the data analyses, construct validity was evaluated through exploratory factor analysis and confirmatory factor analysis, and convergent, discriminant, and incremental validity evidence was examined. Internal consistency was evaluated using item-total correlations and Cronbach's alpha coefficients. In addition, item analysis was conducted to evaluate item difficulty and discrimination parameters. Furthermore, measurement invariance of the YSL-SF was tested between Turkish ( N = 201) and American ( N = 95) samples using multigroup confirmatory factor analysis, and cross-cultural comparability of the construct was evaluated. Results: The findings provided evidence supporting the validity and internal consistency of the Turkish YSL and YSL-SF, both of which demonstrated a one-factor structure. The short form also showed measurement invariance across Turkish and American samples, supporting its suitability for cross-cultural comparisons. Conclusion: The Turkish versions of YSL and YSL-SF demonstrated good psychometric properties, supporting their use in the assessment of yearning following bereavement.

items.title: Internet-delivered self-help acceptance and commitment therapy for family carers of people with dementia (iACT4CARERS): a mixed-methods process evaluation of reach and recruitment.
items.abstract: Objectives A mixed-methods process evaluation was conducted alongside a randomised controlled trial of iACT4CARERS, an eight-session, online, self-help Acceptance and Commitment Therapy intervention with minimal therapist support for family carers of people with dementia. The study examined the reach of the intervention and factors influencing recruitment to inform equitable implementation. Methods Demographic data from 565 screened carers and interviews with 30 referrers across UK health services were analysed. Results The screened sample was predominantly aged 50-79 years (82.5%), female (77%), and White (91.7%). Five themes were identified: referrers' coordinated referrals, mutual motivation, and community outreach supported engagement; referrers' trust-building, tailored communication, and timely approaches facilitated participation; carers' time constraints and referrers' assumptions about older carers' digital skills influenced recruitment; proactive outreach was important for engaging ethnic minority carers; and cultural perceptions of mental health created barriers to participation. Conclusions The sample was broadly comparable with previous estimates of the UK dementia carer population. For the equitable implementation of interventions such as iACT4CARERS, coordinated recruitment across health, social care, and voluntary organisations, alongside centralised intervention delivery, may be critical. Outreach can be further strengthened by enhancing referrers' communication and empowerment skills, including challenging assumptions about older carers' digital abilities.

items.title: High-resolution spatiotemporal estimates of total and wildfire PM 2.5 in the contiguous United States, 2018-2024: Implications for population exposure and mortality burden
items.abstract: Wildfire smoke has become an increasing public health concern in the contiguous United States (CONUS). Previous studies have provided high-resolution estimates of either total PM2.5 or wildfire-related PM2.5 during the past two decades, but few have focused on the most recent wildfire-intensive years, and jointly estimated both to quantify wildfire contributions to total PM2.5 exposure. This study developed a high-resolution machine learning framework to estimate daily 1-km concentrations of total and wildfire-related PM2.5 across the CONUS from 2018 to 2024. This framework incorporates chemical precursors and wildfire smoke density as predictors and relies on publicly accessible data sources enabling future updates. The model achieved high performance with cross-validated R2 of 0.72 and 0.89 for daily and annual estimates, respectively. Elevated total PM2.5 concentrations were observed along the west coast and in several metropolitan areas across the CONUS. Wildfire smoke contributed substantially to total PM2.5 concentrations during major wildfire years, accounting for approximately 35% of PM2.5 along the west coast in 2020, and over 25% in the eastern U.S. in 2023. Wildfire-related PM2.5 mortality accounted for 20% of PM2.5-attributable deaths along the west coast in 2020 (30 times that in 2019), and 24% in the northeastern U.S. in 2023 (14 times that in 2019). These findings highlight the growing role of wildfire smoke as a major driver of total PM2.5 exposure and associated health risks in both western and eastern U.S., underscoring the need for sustained nationwide public health interventions to reduce wildfire smoke exposure.

items.title: Biodegradability of Polyethylene Plastics by Individual and Co-cultured Bacterial Isolates
items.abstract: Abstract The extensive dependence on polyethylene-based products has contributed to their persistence in the environment, accounting for about 64% of global plastic waste and posing serious ecological and public health risks. Conventional disposal methods such as incineration and landfilling further intensify pollution, emphasizing the need for eco-friendly alternatives. This study explores the biodegradation of polyethylene plastics using bacteria isolates obtained from soil samples collected across three sites in Kumasi, Ghana. Degradation efficiency was assessed through weight loss analysis and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) to determine changes in the polymer functional groups. Response Surface Methodology (RSM) was employed to evaluate the effect of pH, temperature, and incubation time on bacterial growth and degradation process. A total of eleven bacterial isolates were identified using Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption Ionization-Time of Flight Mass Spectrometry (MALDI-TOF), with Bacillus cereus being the most prevalent. Optimization analysis revealed that temperature, pH and incubation time significantly influenced degradation, with optimal conditions predicted at 25°C, pH 9- and 21-days incubation respectively. Co-cultures demonstrated higher degradation efficiency than single isolates, supported by elevated laccase activity indicating synergistic enzymatic interactions. FTIR analysis showed polymer modification, showing changes in asymmetric and symmetric C-H stretching peaks in all treatments except Bacillus cereus. In conclusion, the results demonstrate that co-cultured microbes enhance polyethylene degradation through metabolic cooperation and increased enzyme activity, highlighting the potential of microbial synergy as a sustainable strategy for plastic waste management.

items.title: The Impact of Unrestricted Transportation Passes on HIV Treatment and Service Outcomes: Results from a Randomized Controlled Trial among Unstably Housed People Living with HIV
items.abstract: Abstract Background Unstably housed people living with HIV (PLWH) face barriers to achieving and maintaining viral suppression. Transportation instability limits access to medical care and supportive services. Prior research has proposed transportation passes as a potential intervention. However, the effectiveness of this approach has not been evaluated. Methods This prospective randomized controlled trial recruited 146 unstably housed PLWH from a community-based organization serving PLWH in a Midwest city. Participants randomized to the intervention group received an unrestricted public transit pass for 6 months, while the control group retained their current benefits. Surveys administered at baseline and six-month follow-up assessed housing and transportation instability and quality of life. Viral load lab results and social service utilization were extracted from administrative databases. Results Logistic regression found no evidence of an effect of the intervention on the study’s primary outcome of viral suppression (OR .97; 95% CI: 0.47–2.01; p=.942) across multiple missing-data approaches. Models accounted for baseline indicators. Most secondary outcomes, including meals served, stable housing, employment, and quality-of-life scores, also showed no evidence of an effect. However, in a negative binomial model, the intervention affected the frequency of engagement with case management services, with the intervention arm having an estimated rate of recorded follow-up case management contacts 2.24 times that of the control arm (95% CI, 1.03 to 4.88; p = 0.042). Furthermore, stable housing and employment at follow-up clustered strongly in the intervention group (ratio of ORs: 48.9; p = .004). Conclusion Many supportive services are geared toward stabilizing PLWH experiencing homelessness to help them achieve and maintain viral suppression. However, transportation access is an oft-overlooked structural determinant of health. This study finds no evidence of a direct clinical effect of transportation passes during the follow-up period. Increased engagement with case management, though, is valuable and is associated with long-term health and stabilization benefits. The increased service engagement might warrant the relatively low cost of $16 per participant per month. The increased service engagement and exploratory stabilization findings suggest mechanisms by which transportation access might have clinical benefits at longer follow-up periods. Trial Registration The trial was prospectively registered with clinicaltrials.gov NCT06483152 on July 3, 2024.

items.title: “You cannot travel one hundred metres without finding such alcohol”: community perspectives on the availability of alternative alcohol products since the ban of alcohol sachets in Malawi and Uganda
items.abstract: Abstract Background Malawi and Uganda banned alcohol sachets in 2017 and 2019 respectively, to reduce alcohol availability and affordability and protect population health, particularly young people and the most vulnerable. However, the unintended consequences of those bans, particularly the use of alternative alcoholic products, is under-researched. Methods This qualitative study draws on 18 community focus group discussions conducted across both countries (nine per country; n = 159) between 2023 and 2024, in the districts of Wakiso and Gulu (Uganda), and Blantyre and Zomba (Malawi). Participants included adult men and women, in- and out-of-school young males and females, traditional leaders, teachers, and health workers. Data were analysed thematically. Results While participants considered the sachet bans effective, they perceived this effectiveness as temporary. All groups, from both countries, confirmed alternative products, which seem to be both newly emerging substitutes and existing products used as replacements. These included small bottles of recorded high-strength spirits (≤ 220ml) and unrecorded homebrews, sold by variable measures according to demand and purchasing power. Affordability of these products was mentioned in most groups. Community members expressed that these substitute products are widely available and sometimes sold without age verification. In both countries, this was viewed as leading to increased consumption and harm. Conclusion Sachet bans in Malawi and Uganda produced significant changes in the alcohol market rather than meaningful reductions in alcohol availability. Without understanding the market more fully and comprehensive legislation, banning a single product (such as sachets) is unlikely help to protect public health in the longer term.

items.title: Challenges in Collecting LGBT+ Health Data in Primary Health Care in Minas Gerais, Brazil
items.abstract: Abstract Background: This study aimed to understand the obstacles involved in recording data on sexual orientation and gender identity in the individual registration form of the eSUS system in two municipalities in the central region of Minas Gerais, Brazil. Understanding these barriers is essential, as this registration process enables the identification, reception, and qualified follow-up of the LGBT+ population within Primary Health Care (PHC). Results: A qualitative, cross-sectional study was conducted, involving 42 semi-structured interviews with health professionals and administrative assistants working in PHC, analyzed using content analysis. The results revealed barriers related to three thematic axes: Professional Limitations, Lack of Institutional Integration, and Tensions Between the Family-Community Model and LGBT+ Identification. These axes unfold into issues such as lack of training and non-recognition of the importance of collecting this data. Conclusions: These findings show that the difficulty in collecting such information is not merely a technical problem, but a reflection of how LGBT+ people continue to be marginalized within health institutions, despite advances in public policies aimed at equity.

items.title: Mobile phone use while driving and associated factors: an observational study in Córdoba, Argentina.
items.abstract: Objective Mobile phone use while driving (MPWD) is a growing road safety concern. This observational study explores handheld MPWD and associated factors in the city of Córdoba, Argentina. Methods A total of 117,799 vehicle drivers were observed in different areas, road types, time slots, and days of the week. The data collection period spanned from June 2023 to June 2024. Data were collected on vehicle type, driver's sex, estimated age group, driving speed (measured via gun radar), and handheld mobile phone use. Factors associated with handheld mobile phone use (yes/not) were analyzed using a multiple logistic regression model. Results The observed percentage of mobile phone use was 4.6%. The logistic regression results indicate higher usage among young adult drivers (18-24 years), delivery motorcycle riders, and those driving light and heavy cargo vehicles. Additionally, mobile phone use was more prevalent on weekdays and during afternoon hours, compared to the morning. Greater use was also noted on major urban roads rather than local streets, and during periods of lower traffic count. On average, drivers using mobile phones traveled at lower speeds. Conclusions MPWD was linked to human, environmental, and situational factors. Drivers seem to regulate when and where they use their phones and exhibit risk-compensatory behaviors, such as reducing speed. Young drivers and those who drive for work should be priority targets for prevention campaigns.

items.title: Causal Machine Learning for Treatment Effect Heterogeneity: Interpretation, Benchmarking, Validation.
items.abstract: Causal machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising approach for predicting individualized treatment effects and advancing precision medicine, moving beyond the limitations of conventional one-variable-at-a-time subgroup analyses of randomized trials. A recent benchmarking study by Chen and colleagues evaluated several causal ML learners across two large trials and concluded that current methods do not yet demonstrate reliable performance for clinical application. While such applied methodological investigations are valuable, this conclusion warrants a more nuanced examination. Multiple independent research groups have successfully applied causal ML across respiratory medicine and critical care, identifying clinically meaningful treatment effect heterogeneity that prior subgroup analyses had not resolved, although these applications have methodological limitations and do not yet establish that the detected heterogeneity is robust across internal and external validation. We outline four sequential and iterative dimensions central to credible causal ML analyses: choice of learner, model training with cross-fitting, internal validation using calibration-for-benefit and rank-weighted metrics, and external validation aligned with the original causal question. With careful methodological execution, causal ML holds considerable promise for personalized treatment decisions and warrants continued development; dismissing the field prematurely risks overlooking a powerful tool for personalized treatment decisions.

items.title: Landfill microplastic research in Asia (2013-2025): Bibliometric insights into trends, contributors, and emerging hotspots.
items.abstract: Landfill-derived microplastics (MPs) are an emerging environmental concern in Asia. Although MP pollution has received increasing scientific attention, the regional knowledge structure, leading contributors, and emerging hotspots of landfill MP research in Asia remain limited and fragmented. This study addresses this gap through a bibliometric analysis of landfill MP research in Asia from 2013 to 2025. A total of 1992 records were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection using a fuzzy logic search strategy. Bibliometric indicators and network-based methods were employed to examine publication growth, document types, country and institutional contributions, subject area distribution, author collaboration, and keyword co-occurrence patterns. The results reveal a rapid expansion of this research field, with annual publication output increasing from 3 records in 2013 to 491 records in 2025. The compound annual growth rate was 52.53%, with a model fit of R 2 = 0.58. Research articles accounted for 38.56% of the dataset, whereas articles represented 37.76%, indicating a relatively narrow gap between empirical and synthesis-based studies. China, India, and Malaysia became the top contributor countries. Malaysia exhibited a high level of collaboration at the author level, whereas China published a high level of research at the institutional level. The largest subject area was environmental science with 1356 publications. Keyword analysis revealed the key emerging hotspots: landfill leachate, risk assessment, bioplastics, circular economy, and health risks. The novelty of the study is that it is the first study focused in Asia that considers publication tendencies, scientific contributors, thematic evolution, and research gaps in a single bibliometric context. Thus, this study serves as a regional evidence base to help facilitate collaboration, enhance field-based monitoring, and inform future risk assessments, management, and policy development for landfills in Asia.

items.title: Beyond frictionless access: a testable downstream accountability framework for the WHO pathogen access and benefit-sharing annex.
items.abstract: The World Health Organization (WHO) Pandemic Agreement depends on a workable Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) annex that can reconcile rapid pathogen sharing with equitable access to pandemic-related benefits. This viewpoint presents a testable downstream accountability proposal rather than a description of agreed PABS rules. Article 12 already establishes the PABS system, requires the annex to address traceability, provides for legally binding contracts with participating manufacturers, and sets a target for WHO access to 20% of real-time production during a pandemic emergency. The proposal developed here adds an operational downstream trigger, persistent provenance identifiers, pass-through contractual duties, transparent compliance review, and pooled allocation. Routine public-health and non-commercial scientific access would remain rapid and low-friction, and obligations would arise when documented PABS use enters defined product-oriented, intellectual-property, regulatory, licensing, manufacturing, or commercial activity. Persistent identifiers would document provenance, not legal causation, while pooled benefit sharing would avoid sequence-by-sequence valuation. The model also acknowledges unresolved questions of legal authority, national access and benefit-sharing law, allocation governance, non-participating manufacturers, and political acceptability that require negotiation and prospective testing.

items.title: Investigating Incivility in Prelicensure Nursing Education: A Narrative Review of Faculty-to-Student Incivility.
items.abstract: Aim The aim of the study was threefold: 1) synthesize current research in undergraduate nursing education surrounding faculty-to-student incivility in the classroom setting, 2) construct a conceptual definition of faculty-to-student incivility, and 3) identify potential gaps in the current literature for future research purposes. Background Each dynamic of incivility in undergraduate nursing education has unique qualities that must be investigated. Faculty-to-student incivility can be identified in behaviors that negatively impact students' ability to progress through the program. Method A narrative review was performed on relevant articles from 2018 to the present across five databases. A thematic analysis was performed. Results Four key categories were identified in 14 articles: types of incivility, causes of incivility, consequences of incivility, and strategies to mitigate incivility. Conclusion Faculty-to-student incivility is an ongoing issue with profound consequences affecting student retention and the nursing profession. Addressing incivility through faculty education and institutional policies must be promoted.

items.title: Broadening global health knowledge: epistemic pluralism through Asian philosophical traditions.
items.abstract: Global health continues to operate largely within a biomedical epistemological framework that, while effective in addressing acute disease and advancing clinical care, remains limited in responding to complex challenges such as mental health, chronic illness, and persistent inequities. These limitations are not merely technical but reflect deeper epistemic constraints in how health and care are conceptualised. This article argues that selected Asian philosophical traditions, often interpreted through the lens of orientalism, offer an under-recognised resource for rethinking global health. Drawing selectively on Taoist, Confucian, and Buddhist traditions, we highlight how principles of relationality, adaptability, and compassion provide alternative foundations for understanding health beyond the absence of disease. These traditions offer distinctive conceptualisations of relationality, compassion and well-being that can be placed in dialogue with contemporary biomedical and public-health approaches. While contemporary global health systems have increasingly incorporated practices such as mindfulness-based interventions, this integration has often occurred without engagement with their broader philosophical and epistemological implications. Recognising these perspectives and their potential for integration has important implications for global health practice, including reorienting medical education toward reflective and relational competencies, strengthening person-centred and community-engaged care models, and addressing knowledge hierarchies that marginalise ancient philosophical traditions. Reimagining global health therefore requires moving beyond unidirectional knowledge transfer toward a more pluralistic and dialogic framework, in which diverse traditions contribute to more holistic, equitable, and contextually responsive health systems.

items.title: Dental solid waste management and associated environmental impacts in Australia: A mini-review.
items.abstract: Over the past century, global warming has become a major environmental issue. The healthcare sector, particularly the dental industry, has been responsible for generating significant amounts of solid waste, and consequently creating greenhouse gas emissions contributing to global warming. This mini-review collates evidence on the current global literature and Australian policy landscape on Australian dental solid waste management and associated environmental impacts. It involved a rapid literature review of global academic and grey literature and Australian policies on the management of dental solid waste. Seven academic articles, eight grey literature articles and three Australian policies were included for review. Key findings were tabulated and thematically coded into headings adapted from the 2018 Australian National Waste Policy framework for solid waste management. Solid waste generation should be reduced through actions such as oral health promotion and caries prevention activities, digitisation of dental administrative processes and streamlining of clinical processes. Waste management system design is important, including waste segregation and proper design of disposal and recycling systems. Knowledge sharing and staff education can help activate behavioural change towards the management of solid waste. Focusing on environmental sustainability, product stewardship and reducing single-use plastics and packaging can also improve solid waste management. Not all waste can be avoided in dentistry, and dental organisations should have alternative strategies to manage solid waste. Strong leadership and governance to support solid waste management strategies can ensure that organisations approach solid waste management at the highest level possible, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and their impact on climate change.

items.title: Toward a Definition and Differentiation of Secondary Traumatic Stress, Vicarious Trauma, Post-Traumatic Stress, and Compassion Fatigue in Relation to First Responders: An Integrative Literature Review.
items.abstract: This integrative review focuses on the psychological effects of direct and indirect exposure to trauma among first responders (firefighters, police investigators, police officers, paramedics, ambulance workers). The aim of this study is to provide conceptual clarification of the various terms used: secondary traumatic stress, vicarious trauma, compassion fatigue, and post-traumatic stress disorder. For this study, six databases were consulted: PsycINFO/ARTICLE; PubMed/Medline; Web of Science; Cochrane; Cairn; ScienceDirect, up to January 2026. To be included, articles had to be published in peer-reviewed scientific journals and concern an adult and professional population. Data extraction followed PRISMA guidelines, and 76 studies were included. Two researchers participated in data extraction and ensured the quality of the articles. The main results revealed conceptual porosity maintained by symptomatic overlaps and the limitations of measurement tools, often designed for other professional categories. The analysis also highlights the central role of organizational constraints in the emergence of trauma, the importance of considering the nature of exposure, cumulative burden, personal experience, and professional role in the study of traumatic responses. Finally, this review calls for exposure to trauma among first responders to be viewed as a public health issue.

items.title: Preparing for the future, feeling better now: Old-age financial preparation and psychological well-being in pre-old-age Korean adults.
items.abstract: Objectives Population aging has made old-age financial preparation increasingly consequential, yet it is typically indexed by a single measure that does not distinguish among the forms it takes. Drawing on Conservation of Resources theory and the institutional and normative structure of retirement in Korea, we examined associations between within-person changes in financial preparation and two distinct dimensions of subjective well-being among pre-old-age Korean adults. Methods Using seven biennial waves (2011-2023) of the Korean Retirement and Income Study (9,887 person-waves; 2,389 individuals), we estimated individual fixed-effects regressions examining associations between old-age financial preparation and depressive symptoms, measured using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D), and life satisfaction, adjusting for key time-varying covariates. Results Within-person transitions into preparation were associated with a 1.02-point lower CES-D score and a 0.11-point higher life-satisfaction score on a 5-point scale (both p Discussion Old-age financial preparation appears to function as a within-person psychosocial resource related to both evaluative and affective dimensions of well-being. These divergent patterns suggest that the scope and adequacy of preparation matter differently for depressive symptoms and global life evaluations, potentially informing pension policy and financial-planning interventions in aging societies.

items.title: Heart Failure in Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity: From Mechanisms to Clinical Management.
items.abstract: Anthracyclines remain a cornerstone therapy for haematological malignancies and solid tumours, but their use is limited by cardiotoxicity, ranging from asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction to overt heart failure (HF). The risk increases with cumulative doxorubicin-equivalent exposure exceeding 250-300 mg/m2, although susceptibility varies substantially according to patient characteristics, pre-existing cardiovascular disease, genetic predisposition, and modifiable risk factors. Clinically overt HF occurs in ∼6-9% of patients, while subclinical cardiac dysfunction develops in up to 18%. The pathophysiology is multifactorial, involving interconnected mechanisms that disrupt cardiomyocyte homeostasis and promote endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, fibrosis, and adverse remodelling. Yet evidence connecting molecular mechanisms with long-term HF outcomes in humans remains incomplete. Risk stratification, incorporating clinical variables, cardiac biomarkers, echocardiography and, when appropriate, cardiac magnetic resonance enables earlier recognition of cardiac dysfunction. Trials of preventive neurohormonal treatment and statins have produced heterogeneous results, often relying on imaging rather than clinical HF endpoints. Once cardiac dysfunction develops, prompt initiation of foundational HF treatment and multidisciplinary decisions on cancer therapy are essential. Early detection and prompt initiation of HF therapies may reverse myocardial dysfunction, whereas delayed recognition is associated with a poorer treatment response and prognosis. This narrative review integrates current evidence on the mechanisms, risk stratification, surveillance, prevention, and management of anthracycline cardiotoxicity and HF, while highlighting gaps in knowledge, emerging therapeutic strategies, and future directions for clinically meaningful, risk-guided research.

items.title: Child grant receipt and birth registration in Nepal: evidence from the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey.
items.abstract: Background In Nepal, a child grant program was introduced in 2009 to improve education and nutrition among disadvantaged children under the age of five while linking grant eligibility to birth registration as part of efforts to strengthen civil registration and vital statistics systems. Objective This study examined whether child grant receipt was associated with birth registration. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of data from the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey. The outcome was whether a child's birth had ever been registered with civil authorities. The main explanatory variable was whether the child had ever received a child grant. Child age, sex, maternal education, ethnicity, household wealth quintile, and province were included as covariates in multivariable logistic regression models. Results Among 5,064 included children, 72.8% had a reported registered birth. Registration was higher among children reported to have received a grant than among nonrecipients (93.6% versus 65.9%). Children reported to have received a grant had higher adjusted odds of registration than nonrecipients (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.75; 95% CI 5.14 to 8.85). Registration was 71.8% among children whose mothers had no education, 68.3% for grades 1 to 8, and 77.0% for education above grade 8. Conclusions Child grant receipt was strongly associated with reported birth registration. Links between social protection and birth registration should be accompanied by accessible registration services and support for families facing documentation barriers.

items.title: Photovoice as contributing to resiliency among trans women experiencing individual and intersecting HIV and anti-trans stigma in madhesh province, Nepal.
items.abstract: Trans women in low-income countries face high risk for HIV and poor care outcomes, often due to pervasive anti-trans and HIV-related stigma. We implemented a Photovoice intervention to explore how intersecting forms of stigma shape the lives of trans women in one of the Terai districts of Nepal and to examine how participation in the project influenced social support and community connectedness. Using a participatory mixed-methods design, fourteen trans women participated in two Photovoice workshops, completed pre- and post-intervention surveys, and engaged in photo documentation, journaling, group discussion, and interviews. Participants described experiences of internalised and familial stigma, economic exclusion, diminished family support, and social marginalisation, with photographs illustrating how stigma influenced daily life, livelihood, mobility and well-being. Following the intervention, most participants reported greater community connectedness, defined as increased feelings of interpersonal connection, emotional support, and engagement with other trans women and peer networks. These changes were reflected in participants reporting greater outreach to peers, increased emotional openness, and stronger support from relationships developed during the project. Photovoice effectively fostered social support and collective resilience, highlighting the need for structural interventions to improve HIV prevention, treatment, and wellbeing outcomes.

items.title: Arousal state fluctuations destabilize speech intelligibility in older adults
items.abstract: Understanding speech in noisy, multi-talker environments is fundamental for social communication but becomes increasingly challenging as we age. Age-related hearing loss reduces audibility and degrades speech encoding, yet these deficits do not fully explain the momentary lapses in speech understanding that frustrate real-time communication. Here, we tested whether brain state fluctuations immediately before speech onset predict forthcoming speech recognition errors in older listeners. We measured the accuracy, speed, and consistency of speech recognition in 183 adults aged 18-76 years (103 female) using a brief, trial-based multi-talker listening task while tracking pupil dynamics before and during speech presentation. Prestimulus pupil-linked arousal predicted trial-level speech recognition in older, but not younger, adults, independent of hearing status, cognitive load, and task accuracy. In adults over 50 years of age, lower and higher extremes of prestimulus pupil size were associated with less accurate and slower responses, producing a striking inverted-U relationship between prestimulus arousal and forthcoming behavioral performance. Older adults exhibited lower extremes of pupil-linked arousal that were specifically associated with greater self-reported difficulty listening in everyday life. By contrast, stimulus-evoked pupil dilation during speech encoding, a measure of listening effort, did not predict trial-level performance at any age. These findings identify prestimulus pupil-linked arousal as a hidden marker of forthcoming lapses in speech intelligibility in older adults. When considered alongside conventional measures of peripheral hearing status in mixed-effects regression models, these measures provide a more complete accounting of biological changes underlying speech intelligibility deficits that frustrate social communication in older adults . Significance statement As we age, following a conversation in crowded environments becomes more difficult and frustrating, even when hearing tests appear normal. This study shows that fluctuations in arousal level (measured through prestimulus pupil size) are tightly linked to fluctuations in the speed and accuracy of speech processing in adults over 50 years of age. Changes in arousal state regulation uniquely accounted for the moment-to-moment variations in speech intelligibility and were more closely associated with self-reported listening challenges than other conventional measures. These findings highlight the contribution of brain-wide arousal systems to real-world listening challenges and identify a straightforward measure that could be used to more comprehensively assess and potentially improve speech understanding in social settings.

items.title: A concurrent working memory task disrupts motor performance but preserves adaptation during dexterous object manipulation
items.abstract: Abstract Dexterous everyday actions such as grasping and lifting objects rely on precise sensorimotor control and are often performed under concurrent cognitive demands. This study examined how cognitive load induced through a verbal working memory task affects sensorimotor integration in anticipatory adaptation during object manipulation. Participants adapted to an asymmetrical mass distribution by generating compensatory moments at object lift onset, with the aim of minimising object roll. Sensorimotor adaptation performance and grip force modulation were assessed under both single-task (motor only) and dual-task (motor plus working memory) conditions. Results showed that cognitive load led to longer reaction times and increased grip forces, indicating cognitive-motor interference consistent with previous literature. Crucially, however, the trajectory of the adaptation to the novel object dynamics remained robust even under high cognitive load. This resilience suggests that the core processes of error-driven, trial-by-trial motor adaptation which hinge on salient, task-relevant visual and haptic feedback, are relatively immune to the disruptive effects of concurrent working memory demands.

items.title: Symmetry as a common origin of hierarchical emergence and abstraction
items.abstract: Many systems of interest exhibit nested emergent layers with their own rules and regularities, and our knowledge about them seems naturally organized around these levels. How do such hierarchical structures arise, and why should observers track these hierarchies so closely? This paper proposes symmetry as an answer to both questions. By combining principles from information theory, group theory, and statistical mechanics, it is shown that dynamical processes that are equivariant with respect to a symmetry group give rise to multiple emergent macroscopic levels arranged according to the algebraic structure of the symmetry. The same symmetries shape the Bayesian beliefs of an observer with only partial access to the system, yielding a matching hierarchy of “abstract” beliefs that can be updated autonomously at different levels of resolution. These ideas are illustrated in Hopfield networks, where familiar macroscopic quantities emerge from known symmetries, and in Boolean models of gene regulation, where symmetries are instead found from the dynamics. The computational advantages provided by symmetry are showcased in Ehrenfest diffusion and epidemic modeling, where abstract beliefs enable Bayesian inference over exponentially large state spaces. These results identify symmetry as a sufficient mechanism for hierarchical emergence and—at the same time—for the capacity of abstract beliefs to mirror the systems they track, making feasible inferential problems that would otherwise be intractable.

items.title: Children with developmental language disorder show selective impairments in low-frequency neural tracking of speech
items.abstract: Neural tracking of slow temporal modulations in speech supports extraction of the prosodic and syllabic structure thought to be critical for language acquisition by Temporal Sampling (TS) theory, yet whether these automatic cortical tracking mechanisms are altered in children with developmental language disorder (DLD) remains unclear. We recorded MEG while children with and without DLD listened to a story, and quantified source-level lagged speech-brain coherence and frequency-specific cortical functional connectivity across bilateral cortical regions. As expected a priori by TS theory, children with DLD showed significantly reduced coherence in the 0.9–2.5 Hz range associated with prosodic information in the story, spanning bilateral auditory and speech-related cortex. The strongest regional group differences were in left supramarginal gyrus ( p < 0.001) and right inferior frontal gyrus ( p = 0.001). In the 2.5–5 Hz range, linked to syllabic-rate modulations in the story, children with DLD showed reduced coherence in right temporal regions (all p < 0.02). Stronger low-frequency speech-brain coherence was associated with better language performance, indicating that individual differences in cortical speech tracking were behaviourally meaningful. No reliable differences were observed at higher modulation rates (5–9 Hz or 12–40 Hz). Exploratory functional connectivity analyses did not reveal network-level group differences that were robust across ROI time-series extraction methods. These findings indicate that atypical low-frequency neural tracking of speech is functionally relevant to language outcomes in DLD.

items.title: Theory of mind predicts conversational success in early right hemisphere stroke recovery
items.abstract: Those living with right hemisphere damage (RHD) often struggle with engaging in aspects of conversation that require understanding what a speaker means. There is growing evidence that conversation relies on deducing the speaker’s perspective, an ability known as theory of mind (ToM). However, whether individual differences in conversation after RHD relate to ToM deficits is unknown. Here, we related individual differences in conversational success to ToM in 31 speakers during the early stages of RHD (median 5 days post-stroke) in comparison to 16 age- and education-matched controls. We measured conversational success as the number of differences identified between two images while participants conversed with study coordinators. A non-verbal false belief task measured ToM abilities. Baseline cognitive tasks assessed visual inattention, inhibitory control/visual selective attention and working memory. Linear mixed-effects modeling revealed that the ToM ability to explicitly infer others’ perspectives while managing conflict with one’s own reliably predicted conversational success (β = 0.42, p = .023; β’s = 0.44 − 0.64 across sensitivity models). Adding false belief ToM substantially increased model fit (ΔR 2 = 0.115, Cohen’s f 2 = 0.15), independent of baseline cognitive abilities and demographic factors. These findings provide the first empirical evidence in unilateral RHD that the ability to reason about a partner’s knowledge and manage conflict with one’s privileged perspective is critical for successful conversation. Results support theoretical models of ToM as a cognitive basis for everyday conversation. The clinical implications underscore the importance of socio-cognitive screening and ToM-based interventions to enhance communication outcomes in stroke rehabilitation.

items.title: Day-to-Day Variation in Perceived Causal Networks: A Feasibility Study in Two Psychiatric Settings
items.abstract: Abstract Purpose The network approach conceptualizes psychopathology as a system of causally interacting problems of living. Longitudinal Perceived Causal Networks (L-PECAN) is a self-report method designed to capture day-to-day variability in patients’ perceived causal relations between problems. We examined the feasibility of an L-PECAN procedure in two clinical settings and explored within-person variability in perceived causal network structures. Methods Patients in two psychiatric clinics first completed an L-PECAN training week using a generic item list. Personalized items, including contextual factors, were then formulated and used subsequently for a minimum of three weeks. Feasibility was evaluated via recruitment rates and adherence. Within-person variability was examined using saturation and drift analyses. Results Eight patients completed the protocol. Median daily completion times ranged from one to eight minutes. Participants largely perceived their personalized problems as being caused by their other problems. Some causal relations were perceived consistently across days, but overall network structures showed substantial day-to-day variability. Conclusions An L-PECAN procedure incorporating a training week and personalized nodes appeared feasible in the university clinic, whereas uptake and adherence indicated greater implementation challenges in specialist psychiatric care. The method provides a structured way to examine day-to-day variability in perceived causal problem networks. Further research is needed to establish feasibility across clinical populations and to evaluate validity and clinical utility.

items.title: Personalized to Persuade: The Effects of Contextualization and Warmth on Trust and Reliance in Conversational AI
items.abstract: Conversational agents tailor explanations to users’ backgrounds and interests, a strategy we refer to as contextualization. While personalization is an established persuasive lever in politics and marketing, its effect in everyday tasks, where users lack prior knowledge, remains unclear. We report a 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment (N = 380) testing how contextualization and conversational warmth shape the persuasiveness of, and reliance on, an AI assistant that argues against expert recommendations. Contextualization and warmth each reduce persuasiveness, yet their combination restores it through a crossover interaction. Behavioral reliance is high in every condition and invariant to conversational design. Trust predicts both outcomes but mediates neither. AI literacy decouples attitude from behavior: more literate users report lower trust, yet are more persuaded and more likely to abandon the expert position.

items.title: Enacting Constructive Conflicts with AI Agents to Enhance Reconsideration among Novice Interaction Designers
items.abstract: Generative AI agents are increasingly used in interaction design to facilitate ideation, often following their own internal reasoning. These interactions tend to expand the design space. Our work explores an antagonistic role for design agents, prompting designers to engage with stakeholder tension. We built an antagonistic AI agent and examined the agent’s influence in a between-subjects experiment with 45 design students across three conditions: Self Reflection (unsupported review of the design proposal), Stepwise Guidance (written prompts that walk designers through a constructive-conflict framework), and Interactive Engagement (an AI agent that enacts the constructive-conflict framework interactively by synthesizing stakeholder pushback). The latter two conditions share the framework but differ in whether it is self-enacted or agent-enacted. Results show that, compared with Self Reflection, both the Stepwise Guidance and Interactive Engagement groups reported significantly higher self-reconsideration and made more improvements to their design proposals. Compared with Stepwise Guidance, the antagonistic agent introduced more conflictual perspectives, and participants in the Engagement condition generated and discarded more ideas. These findings suggest that an interactive agent that surfaces stakeholder pushback can support concrete design revision while keeping designers engaged with divergent perspectives.

items.title: Neighborhood Exposome at Birth and Trajectories of Epigenetic Age Acceleration Across Childhood
items.abstract: Importance Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) has been linked to increased disease risk in adults, yet its developmental trajectories and early-life neighborhood determinants remain poorly understood. Objective To examine whether there are associations between the neighborhood exposome at birth and EAA trajectories from early childhood through adolescence. Design, Setting, and Participants This longitudinal cohort study used data from Project Viva, a prebirth cohort that enrolled pregnant women in eastern Massachusetts from April 22, 1999, to July 31, 2002. Participants included 570 children with available peripheral blood DNA methylation data, complete neighborhood characteristics, and complete covariates. Data were analyzed from August 19, 2024, to August 21, 2026. Exposures Neighborhood exposome profiles at birth derived from 22 census tract–level characteristics across 4 domains (area deprivation, social fragmentation, population density, and environmental quality) using self-organizing maps. Main Outcomes and Measures EAA was calculated at 3, 8, and 13 years of age using the Horvath, Skin & Blood, and Wu epigenetic clocks. Trajectories were identified using latent class linear mixed models. Associations between neighborhood profiles and EAA trajectories were estimated using multinomial mixed models. Results Among 570 children (mean [SD] age at early childhood, 3.2 [0.4] years; 305 [53.5%] male), 3 EAA trajectory groups (stable, increasing, and decreasing for the Horvath and Skin & Blood clocks or low-baseline for the Wu clock) and 3 neighborhood profiles were identified. Compared with profile 1 (suburban, lowest adverse exposures [n = 278]), children born into profile 2 (urban, high residential instability and single-person households, and highway proximity [n = 168]) had greater odds of increasing EAA for the Wu clock (adjusted odds ratio, 1.67 [95% CI, 1.03-2.69]). Profile 3 (urban, high socioeconomic deprivation and pollution [n = 124]) showed no associations. Conclusions and Relevance In this longitudinal cohort study, birth into neighborhoods characterized by high residential instability and single-person households and highway proximity was associated with increasing Wu EAA trajectories across childhood. These findings suggest that early-life neighborhood conditions, encompassing both social and physical environmental factors, may represent targets for interventions aimed at reducing long-term disease risk. Further research is needed to clarify the implications of these findings for later health and prevention.

items.title: Fairness, agency, and algorithms: AI in Greek higher education linguistics
items.abstract: The swift expansion of AI in higher education has not been matched by a clear understanding of its effective application within linguistics education, especially in Greece, where the technology is viewed as a means to advance social and economic development. This research undertakes a thorough exploration of AI integration in Greek higher education linguistics through a utilitarian perspective, centering on the experiences of instructors. It aims to shed light on the advantages and obstacles linked to AI adoption, with particular emphasis on issues of fairness and student agency. The study’s goals include examining educators’ experiences with AI tools, identifying perceived contributions to fairness and student empowerment, and uncovering the limitations and difficulties involved. Drawing on semi -structured interviews and focus group discussions, insights will be collected from fourteen technologically adept language educators. The ensuing thematic and discourse analyses will engage with these issues and highlight strategies to strengthen teaching practices. Ultimately, the study seeks to inform policymakers, practitioners, and stakeholders of the profound influence of AI on education, while enriching the academic conversation on this subject and proposing actionable ways to enhance teaching and learning in Greek higher education linguistics.

items.title: Believability and conditional inference in mathematics undergraduates: a replication and extension
items.abstract: Abstract This paper replicates a study in which Alcock et al. (2026) found that content influences first-year mathematics undergraduates’ evaluations of conditional inferences . Alcock et al. reported that these students responded more normatively to inferences from highly believable (true) mathematical conditionals than from conditionals with other mathematical, everyday, or abstract content. We replicated this work with a larger and more diverse sample, finding a similar overall believability effect and evidence that some individual differences in the original study were due to recent teaching. We extended the work by relating conditional inference responses to prior performance in mathematics and to students’ cultural backgrounds, finding that better mastery of more mathematics is associated with better rejection of invalid affirmation of the consequent inferences and that students with English as a first language responded more normatively than students with Chinese as a first language, especially for modus tollens inferences. We consider limitations to generalisability, and argue for the importance of replicating effects of all kinds, not only those linked to teaching interventions.
